  - Mipmaps: `mipmaps/generate` default `false` `[BIN]`; keep off (mipmaps with nearest sampling produce shimmering on scaled pixel art `[UNV-4.3]`).
  - Camera: `Camera2D` has no pixel-snap member `[BIN]`; `position_smoothing_enabled` default `false` `[BIN]`. Sub-pixel camera positions therefore rely on `snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel`. `physics/common/physics_interpolation` (default `false`) and `Node.physics_interpolation_mode` exist `[BIN]`, and lights/occluders are interpolable `[BIN]`; whether interpolation plus snapping removes 60 Hz camera judder: `[UNV-4.3]`, spike test with a moving crewmate carrying a shadow beam.
  - `Viewport.sdf_scale` default `SDF_SCALE_50_PERCENT` `[BIN]` — the SDF built from `sdf_collision` occluders is half-res; irrelevant unless shaders read the SDF.
  
  **Integer-scale table (arithmetic).**
  
  | Base | 1920×1080 | 2560×1440 | 3840×2160 | Notes |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | 640×360 | 3× | 4× | 6× | integer everywhere |
  | 960×540 | 2× | 2.67× — letterbox to 2× or fractional | 4× | fails 1440p |
  | 1920×1080 | 1× | 1.33× — fails | 2× | fails 1440p; 9× the pixels to draw and light |
  
  **What it limits.** Sprite resolution and the beam-edge look are coupled. Rendering the world at base resolution keeps every rotated segment, cone edge and shadow edge on the pixel grid (good for 5.4's grid-snapped look, cheap) but renders the hero #1 cone edge as stair-steps of scale size; rendering at window resolution with integer-scaled sprites gives smooth cones and shadows at full cost and lets rotated rig segments and the fringe fall off the pixel grid. Whether Light2D resolves at the viewport's render size: `[UNV-4.3]`, spike step 2.
  
  **Recommendation — one combined architecture (reconciles flag 3 and this item).**
  - Root viewport: project `stretch/mode = canvas_items`, `aspect = keep`, `scale_mode = integer`, base `viewport_width/height = 640×360`. The root carries only the HUD `CanvasLayer` and the `SubViewportContainer`, so HUD text renders at window resolution and is outside the world's glow by construction.
  - World: a `SubViewport` sized 640×360, `use_hdr_2d = true`, `use_debanding = true`, `snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel = true`, `canvas_item_default_texture_filter = NEAREST`, inside a `SubViewportContainer` with `stretch = true` so the container scales it by the root's integer factor.
  - The spike's A/B: keep the SubViewport at 640×360 for pass A (lights at base res); for pass B set the SubViewport's `size` to the window size and `size_2d_override = 640×360` with `size_2d_override_stretch = true` `[BIN]` — logical 640×360 coordinates, sprites integer-scaled, lights and shadows computed at window resolution — without flipping any project setting. Whether `size_2d_override` behaves that way is `[UNV-4.3]`; it is the test.
  - Project-wide texture filter `0` (NEAREST) regardless, mipmaps off. `960×540` is recommended against on the 1440p failure alone; 1×-native only if the AD accepts 9× lighting cost and 9× drawing time.
  
  ## 4. Per-client hallucination filter and the 5.5 fringe shader
  
  **Constraint / feasibility.**
  - Unlit pass: `CanvasItemMaterial.LIGHT_MODE_UNSHADED` `[BIN]` or `render_mode unshaded` in a `canvas_item` shader (`Shader.MODE_CANVAS_ITEM` `[BIN]`; the render-mode keyword is `[UNV-4.3]`). An unshaded CanvasItem receives no Light2D contribution and, not being a Light2D, emits none — "casts no light" holds by construction.
  - Per-viewer: the fringe is a material/uniform on the *local* client's view of the crewmate, driven by `CanvasItem.set_instance_shader_parameter` `[BIN]` from a presentation-only script that reads replicated sanity state and never writes it. Rule for Section 8 and the control manifest: **presentation scripts may read simulation state and may only write to CanvasItem / Material / Light2D properties; they never call into gameplay or networking.** A player never sees their own fringe because the local script skips the local avatar.
  - Outline shader: sample the albedo alpha at ±1, ±2 texels and paint `#B07BE6` where own alpha is 0 and a neighbour is opaque — hence the 2-px padding rule (flag 6). Breathing 4–6 s via `TIME` on alpha only, never on width or position (2.9: no tempo change). Width is "2 px at sprite resolution": in the base-res SubViewport that is automatic; in pass B the shader needs the integer scale as a uniform.
  - Beam-edge fringe: the beam is a Light2D texture, not a CanvasItem, so it has no edge to outline. Author one edge-mask sprite per beam shape (4 small unshaded textures) drawn at the hand point with the beam's rotation. Cost: 4 textures, one extra draw per fringed crewmate.
  - Glow interaction: keep fringe luminance below `glow_hdr_threshold` (flag 3). Order: fringe sprite drawn as a child **behind** the body (`show_behind_parent` `[BIN]`) so it never covers the sprite's own pixels.
  - Own-sanity filter (stages 1–3): a `canvas_item` shader on the `SubViewportContainer` (it already holds the world as a texture), or — if the world is not in a SubViewport — a full-screen pass on a `CanvasLayer` above the world and below the HUD reading the screen via `BackBufferCopy` `[BIN]` (or the screen-texture hint, `[UNV-4.3]`). Stage-2 "false reach" is an unshaded additive cone sprite, not a Light2D — it tints but reveals nothing because unlit geometry is already black. Stage-2 "shadow with no occluder" is an unshaded dark polygon. None of these touch `LightOccluder2D`, `Light2D` or simulation nodes.
  - Shader count: fringe, iridescence-per-segment, full-screen filter, pipe-flow scroll, ambient-floor material. Enable the Shader Baker (4.5 `[REF]`; "not using it" is listed as a common mistake in `current-best-practices.md`) so these do not hitch on first use.
  - Multiplayer scope: up to four clients each run their own filter; there is no server-side rendering so "per-client" is free. NOT SOURCEABLE — anything about the networking model; this is presentation only.
  
  **What it limits.** One extra unshaded draw per fringed crewmate and one full-screen pass for the filter — negligible against the 1000-draw budget. The real constraints are flag 3 (glow) and flag 6 (padding).
  
  **Recommendation.** Build the fringe first in the spike (it is the cheapest proof that unshaded-per-viewer works), then the filter as a SubViewportContainer shader. Write the "presentation never writes simulation" rule into the control manifest.
  
  ## 5. Horror segment rigs — quantised rotation, stepped playback
  
  **Constraint.**
  - `Skeleton2D`, `Bone2D`, `SkeletonModificationStack2D` and the `SkeletonModification2D*` set (CCDIK, FABRIK, LookAt, Jiggle, TwoBoneIK, PhysicalBones, StackHolder) all exist in 4.7.2 `[BIN]`. There is **no** `SkeletonModifier2D` `[BIN]`; the 4.6 IK rework in REF (`SkeletonModifier3D`) is 3D-only. `Skeleton2D` exposes `execute_modifications`, `set_bone_local_pose_override` `[BIN]`.
  - Skeleton2D is built for `Polygon2D` mesh skinning (`Polygon2D.skeleton`, bone weights `[BIN]`), which deforms textures — the opposite of a grid-snapped look. Plain `Sprite2D` children under a `Node2D` hierarchy need no skeleton at all.
  - Rotation of a nearest-filtered sprite in the base-res SubViewport lands on the base pixel grid (stair-stepped edges, which *is* the grid-snapped look); at window resolution it leaves the grid. `[UNV-4.3]` for the mechanism; spike step 2 confirms it.
  
  **What it limits.** Stepped playback is a script decision, not an engine feature: pose only every N physics ticks (12 fps = every 5th tick at 60 Hz) and quantise each segment angle to 360/24 = 15° (or 360/16). IK modifications run continuously, so if Skeleton2D IK is used, call `execute_modifications` manually on the stepped tick and write the quantised result back — more plumbing than it saves.
  
  **Recommendation.** Manual rig: a `Node2D` per limb chain with `Sprite2D` segments (tapering, round joint caps for overlap), a GDScript procedural animator (creep / unfold / snap signatures, per-instance seed) stepped at 12 fps with 15° quantisation, segments ordered by `z_index` for joint overlap, the iridescence band as a `ShaderMaterial` on each segment with a per-instance phase uniform (`set_instance_shader_parameter` `[BIN]`). Reserve Skeleton2D + FABRIK only for the filament-rider type if a limb must reach a world point; even then, quantise after solving. If pass B (window-res lighting) wins, pre-rotate segment sprites at import into 24 angle variants (tool step; at T=32 that is ≈ 60 cells × 24 × 4096 × 12 ≈ 70 MB, still fine) or keep horrors in a base-res SubViewport. Silhouette test per 5.4 on rest / reach / move poses captured from the rig, not from sheets.
  
  ## 6. Draw-call shape — TileMapLayer, Y-sort, HUD layer
  
  **Constraint.**
  - `TileMapLayer.rendering_quadrant_size` default `16` `[BIN]`: tiles are grouped into 16×16-cell quadrants, each quadrant drawn as a batch per material/texture `[UNV-4.3]`. A 20×11-tile view touches ≈ 4 quadrants → ≈ 4 draws for a floor layer.
  - Y-sort: `CanvasItem.y_sort_enabled` (default `false`) `[BIN]`, `TileMapLayer.y_sort_origin`, `TileData.y_sort_origin` `[BIN]`. Enabling Y-sort on a TileMapLayer makes it sort per cell with its siblings and is known to break quadrant batching `[UNV-4.3]` — potentially one draw per cell (≈ 220 for a full view). NOT SOURCEABLE as a 4.7.2 number; spike measures `RENDER_INFO_DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME` with Y-sort on and off.
  - 2D batching: `rendering/2d/batching/item_buffer_size = 16384`, `uniform_set_cache_size = 4096` `[BIN]`. Batching merges consecutive items that share texture, material, blend mode and light state `[UNV-4.3]`; a CanvasTexture page is one such texture, so three-sheet pages batch exactly as single textures do.
  - `CanvasLayer` (`layer`, `follow_viewport_enabled`) `[BIN]`; `RenderingServer.CANVAS_LAYER_MIN/MAX` `[BIN]`. Light2D and CanvasModulate act on their own canvas, so a HUD CanvasLayer is unlit and un-ambiented `[UNV-4.3]`. Glow is not per-canvas (flag 3) — hence the SubViewport in item 3.
  - `z_index` range ±4096 `[BIN]`.
  
  **What it limits.** 3/4 oblique needs actors to sort against wall faces and props, which forces Y-sort on the layer containing those — the single largest draw-call multiplier in the scene. Floors never sort against actors and must stay off Y-sort.
  
  **Recommendation (target shape against the 1000 budget).**
  
  | Layer | Node | Y-sort | Expected draws |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | Floor | `TileMapLayer` (CanvasTexture page: dialect floor) | off | ≈ 4 |
  | Floor trails/stains | `TileMapLayer` or sprites, shared page | off | ≈ 4–20 |
  | Wall faces, props, actors, horror rigs | one Y-sorted `Node2D` parent containing a `TileMapLayer` (walls/props) plus actor scenes | on | measure: 50–300 |
  | Wall top caps | `TileMapLayer`, `z_index` above actors | off | ≈ 4 |
  | Pipes + emissive overlay | `TileMapLayer` (shared pipe page) + unshaded additive sprites | off | ≈ 10–40 |
  | Lights | `PointLight2D` nodes | — | 0 extra draws, shadow passes extra (measure) |
  | Fringe / hallucination | unshaded sprites + 1 full-screen pass | — | ≤ 10 |
  | Particles (dust, mist, venting) | `GPUParticles2D` (`fixed_fps` default 30 `[BIN]`) | — | 1 per emitter, ≤ 12 emitters |
  | HUD | `CanvasLayer` in the root viewport (world in SubViewport) | off | ≈ 20–60 |
  
  Plenty of headroom if Y-sort stays confined to one layer. If the measured Y-sorted layer exceeds ~300, split wall faces into a non-sorted layer with per-row `z_index` bands (tile rows become z bands; actors pick the band by their feet). Particle LOD: `GPUParticles2D.amount_ratio` `[BIN]` scaled by distance from the beam, `visibility_rect` set tightly; proposed caps: dust-in-beam ≤ 300 total, mist ≤ 64 per trail, venting ≤ 128 per vent, ≤ 12 live emitters.
  
  ## 7. Importer constraints and recommended import preset
  
  **Constraint.** `ResourceImporterTexture` options and defaults `[BIN]`: `compress/mode = 0`, `compress/high_quality = false`, `compress/lossy_quality = 0.7`, `compress/normal_map = 0`, `compress/channel_pack = 0`, `mipmaps/generate = false`, `mipmaps/limit = -1`, `process/fix_alpha_border = true`, `process/premult_alpha = false`, `process/normal_map_invert_y = false`, `process/size_limit = 0`, `process/channel_remap/* = identity`, `detect_3d/compress_to = 1`, `roughness/mode = 0`, `svg/scale = 1.0`. The dump has no constants for this class, so the *meaning* of each integer (`compress/mode 0 = Lossless`, `detect_3d/compress_to 0 = Disabled`) is `[UNV-4.3]` — confirm in the Import dock during the spike. `ResourceImporterTextureAtlas` exists (`atlas_file`, `crop_to_region`, `import_mode`, `trim_alpha_border_from_region = true`) `[BIN]`. Project-level: `rendering/textures/lossless_compression/force_png = false` `[BIN]` (lossless .ctex uses WebP-lossless internally `[UNV-4.3]`; no quality loss either way). Normal-map Y convention for 2D lights: NOT SOURCEABLE — which direction green points; spike test: a sphere normal map lit from top-left must highlight top-left, otherwise set `process/normal_map_invert_y = true` in the preset. 4.7 draws `CanvasItem` lines without an antialiasing feather `[REF]` — irrelevant to sprites, but it rules out `draw_line` / `draw_polyline` for hairlines and filaments: those are sprites.
  
  **What it limits.** `ResourceImporterTextureAtlas` with `trim_alpha_border_from_region = true` would eat the 2-px fringe padding and would pack albedo independently of normal/specular — do not use it. Pack externally, once, with one layout for all three sheets.
  
  **Recommended preset (set as Import Defaults for `texture`, then per-folder overrides).**
  
  | Option | Albedo | Normal | Specular | Light / beam textures | UI |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | `compress/mode` | lossless (`0` `[UNV-4.3]`) | lossless | lossless | lossless | lossless |
  | `mipmaps/generate` | false | false | false | false | false |
  | `process/fix_alpha_border` | true | false | false | true | true |
  | `process/premult_alpha` | false | false | false | false | false |
  | `process/normal_map_invert_y` | false | spike-determined | false | false | false |
  | `detect_3d/compress_to` | disabled (so a stray 3D use never VRAM-compresses) | disabled | disabled | disabled | disabled |
  | `process/size_limit` | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1024 | 0 |
  | Texture filter (project `default_texture_filter`) | 0 NEAREST | inherits via CanvasTexture | inherits | LINEAR allowed on the light texture only (`PointLight2D.texture` is sampled by the light, not the item; `[UNV-4.3]`) | NEAREST |
  
  Source-file rules for Section 8: PNG, RGBA8, sRGB; normal sheets RGB8 with the spike-determined Y; specular sheets 8-bit grey; cells with ≥ 2 px transparent padding on every side; sheet dimensions multiples of the cell size; one `layout.json` per page shared by the three sheets; hairlines, filaments and seams are sprites, never runtime line draws. Naming (project `snake_case`): `<set>_<page>_albedo.png`, `<set>_<page>_normal.png`, `<set>_<page>_specular.png`, e.g. `crew_body_01_albedo.png`; light textures `beam_<shape>.png`, `pool_<kind>.png`; segments `horror_<type>_seg_<n>.png`; overlays `crew_overlay_<kind>.png`.
  
  ## Spike measurement plan (lighting spike, first spike per Section 1)
  
  1. Print `RenderingServer.get_current_rendering_driver_name()` and `get_current_rendering_method()` `[BIN]` — settles flag 7a.
  2. One room (20×11 tiles, Foundry kit placeholders, CanvasTexture floor/walls) in the item 3 SubViewport architecture. Pass A: SubViewport 640×360 scaled ×3. Pass B: SubViewport at window size with `size_2d_override = 640×360`, `size_2d_override_stretch = true` `[BIN]`. Confirm where Light2D resolves (flag 4) and compare beam-edge look and frame time.
  3. Sweep shadow lights 0→8 with PCF5 and occluders 0→300 (per-tile vs merged); record frame time and `RENDERING_INFO_TOTAL_DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME` `[BIN]` at each step; find the knee.
  4. Sweep non-shadow lights 0→32 overlapping the floor; record the per-item light cap behaviour.
  5. Y-sort on/off on the wall layer; record draw calls.
  6. Normal-map Y and CanvasTexture-over-region/TileSet sampling checks; confirm importer enum meanings in the Import dock.
  7. Ambient floors 0 / 1 / 2 / 3 / 8 % with and without `hdr_2d` + debanding, SDR output; screenshot and histogram Graphite vs Void Steel (flag 1).
  8. Fringe shader on one crewmate, glow on; confirm no bloom at `glow_hdr_threshold = 1.0` (4.6 glow rework `[REF]` — do not reuse older tuning).
  9. Compatibility branch: repeat 2–4 once, record which features are missing (NOT SOURCEABLE until run).
  10. Record `RENDERING_INFO_TEXTURE_MEM_USED` and `VIDEO_MEM_USED` `[BIN]` against the item 2 estimate; enable the Shader Baker `[REF]` and note first-run hitching before/after.
  
  ---
  
  Notes for the orchestrator: (a) the pinned reference was silent on every 2D topic asked, so I supplemented it with the installed binary's own class dump — every such fact is tagged `[BIN]` and limited to names/defaults/constants; (b) two REF-vs-BIN discrepancies (Windows driver default, 4.7 stretch defaults) are flagged rather than resolved; (c) the seven flags at the top are the items where the art direction's asks (0–3 % ambient floors, many shadow-casting fixtures, glow-excluded fringe/HUD, 960×540 or 1×-native base) are likely to exceed budget or need a trade-off the art-director must decide.

  # Section 8 (Asset Standards) — Engine-constraint half, technical-artist
  
  Working copy (durable, session scratchpad): `C:\Users\dasbl\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\D--the-synaptic-sea-2d\e887ccb9-1186-40d9-9566-5eacccbd9b44\scratchpad\section8-engine-constraints.md`. The 4.7.2 class dump I used as a primary source is at `C:\Users\dasbl\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\D--the-synaptic-sea-2d\e887ccb9-1186-40d9-9566-5eacccbd9b44\scratchpad\doctool\doc\classes\`. No project files were written. Full markdown follows.
  
  ---
  
  Scope: Godot 4.7.2, Forward+ (reversible to Compatibility), Windows, 2D HD pixel art, 3/4 oblique. Budgets from `project.yaml` / orchestrator: 60 fps, 16.6 ms, 1000 draw calls/frame (2D default, to tune after profiling), 4 GB memory ceiling. No min-spec GPU or VRAM figure exists in `D:\the-synaptic-sea-2d\project.yaml` — NOT SOURCEABLE — min-spec GPU / VRAM budget; the 4 GB figure is a memory ceiling, not VRAM.
  
  ## Sourcing legend (applies to every claim below)
  
  | Tag | Meaning |
  | --- | --- |
  | `[REF]` | Stated in `docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md`, `modules/rendering.md`, `breaking-changes.md`, `current-best-practices.md` or `deprecated-apis.md`. |
  | `[BIN]` | Read from the installed editor itself: `Godot_v4.7.2-stable_mono_win64_console.exe --headless --doctool` run 2026-10-25 into the session scratchpad. The dump's `<description>` tags came back empty, so `[BIN]` sources **existence, types, defaults, enum values and constants only** — never behaviour or cost. Importer option *meanings* (which integer is "lossless") are not in the dump. |
  | `[UNV-4.3]` | Training-era (≤ 4.3) knowledge, not confirmed by REF or BIN. Used only where a concrete spike test is named alongside it. May have changed in 4.5–4.7 — verify against the reference docs before relying on it. |
  | `NOT SOURCEABLE — <what>` | Neither REF nor BIN says it, and I will not guess. The spike measures it. |
  
  Recommendation to the orchestrator: the pinned `modules/rendering.md` contains no 2D lighting, CanvasTexture, stretch, snap or importer content at all. The `[BIN]` facts below are worth folding into it (I do not write that file).
  
  ## Flags for the orchestrator (trade-offs the art direction must hear)
  
  1. **Ambient floors of 0–3 % cannot carry the "dark has a floor" rule in 8-bit SDR output.** Ambient as a canvas multiply (`CanvasModulate` `[BIN]`) gives Graphite mid `#2A303A` × 0.02 ≈ 0.8/255 and Void Steel `#0B1018` × 0.02 ≈ 0.2/255 — both quantise to black. 4.1's "hull still darker than true black" exists only where ambient is high enough to separate them (≈ 6–8 % for a 2-step gap). Nuance: with `hdr_2d` on, the multiply happens in linear space and is re-encoded to sRGB on output `[UNV-4.3]`, which lifts darks a step or two — the conclusion is directional, and spike step 7's histogram decides. The arithmetic assumes SDR output; `display/window/hdr/request_hdr_output` exists (default `false` `[BIN]`) and should stay off through the spike. Options: raise the floors; keep the floors but add a material-level `max(albedo × ambient, floor_tint)` on hull materials so unlit hull never drops below Void Steel; enable `rendering/viewport/hdr_2d` (default `false` `[BIN]`) plus `use_debanding` (default `false` `[BIN]`). The AD chooses which; I recommend option 2 plus HDR 2D.
  2. **"Many tungsten fixtures" (2.3) with true occlusion is the state most likely to break the frame.** Shadow cost scales with shadow-casting lights × occluder polygons (mechanism `[UNV-4.3]`, number NOT SOURCEABLE). The bible already describes stable-state shadows as "soft, nearly directionless" — that is the licence to make fixtures **non-shadow** lights and reserve shadow-casting for beams (≤ 4), the alarm beacon and at most one deployable in view. This matches the direction rather than cutting it. If the spike shows even that over budget, Section 1 says cut emitters before occlusion — see item 1's budget shape.
  3. **Glow is a per-viewport post pass; no single CanvasItem can be excluded from it.** Consequences: (a) the violet fringe must stay below `glow_hdr_threshold` (default `1.0` `[BIN]`) or it blooms and reads as emission — a principle 3 violation; (b) "HUD excluded from glow" requires either HUD luminance below threshold or the world rendered in a `SubViewport` `[BIN]` with the HUD in the root viewport. I recommend the SubViewport (it also gives integer-scale control, item 3). Also: glow was reworked in 4.6 — it now runs before tonemapping with screen blending `[REF]` — so no 4.3-era glow tuning transfers; the threshold test in spike step 8 is the only number to trust.
  4. **Base-resolution choice is a 9× lighting-cost lever, not only an art choice.** If the world renders at base resolution (640×360 = 1/9 of 1080p pixels), lights, shadows and the beam edge are computed there and the beam's hard edge becomes a 3-px stair-step at 1080p. If the world renders at window resolution with integer-scaled sprites, the beam edge is smooth and lighting costs 9× the pixels. Whether Light2D is evaluated at the viewport's render size (so that a 640×360 SubViewport lights at 640×360) is `[UNV-4.3]`; it is the first thing the spike must confirm, because the whole budget hangs on it. Integer-scale table in item 3: only 640×360 scales to integers at 1080p, 1440p and 4K.
  5. **"Normal maps are generated, not drawn" (5.7) is half true.** A flat albedo has no height; a Sobel on albedo yields garbage normals. Each sheet needs a painted height/mask pass (2–4 grey levels, fast but not zero) from which normals are generated by tool. Budget it as roughly 20–30 % of the albedo drawing time, not 0 %.
  6. **The 2-px fringe "outside the contour" needs 2 px (at sprite resolution) of transparent padding in every frame cell** or the outline clips at the cell edge. This is an atlas-packing rule (item 7) and a tool-pipeline rule (padding must survive trim-on-import).
  7. **Two REF-vs-BIN conflicts to verify on line one of the spike.** (a) `rendering/rendering_device/driver.windows` default is `"vulkan"` `[BIN]` while REF says D3D12 is the Windows default since 4.6 — print `RenderingServer.get_current_rendering_driver_name()` `[BIN]` at startup. (b) `display/window/stretch/mode` default is `"disabled"` and `aspect` `"keep"` `[BIN]` while REF says new 4.7 projects default to `canvas_items` / `expand`; `D:\the-synaptic-sea-2d\project.godot` has no `[display]` block, so write the stretch settings explicitly rather than inheriting a default nobody can name.
  
  ---
  
  ## 1. 2D lighting — PointLight2D / DirectionalLight2D, shadows, occluders, normal/specular
  
  **Constraint (what exists, 4.7.2).**
  - `Light2D` (base): `energy`, `color`, `blend_mode` (`ADD` / `SUB` / `MIX`), `shadow_enabled` (default `false`), `shadow_filter` (`NONE` / `PCF5` / `PCF13`), `shadow_filter_smooth`, `shadow_color`, `range_item_cull_mask`, `shadow_item_cull_mask`, `range_z_min/max` (±1024), `range_layer_min/max` `[BIN]`.

Hard cap `RenderingServer.MAX_2D_DIRECTIONAL_LIGHTS = 8` `[BIN]`.

  **Constraint / feasibility.**

  - Outline shader: sample the albedo alpha at ±1, ±2 texels and paint `#B07BE6` where own alpha is 0 and a neighbour is opaque — hence the 2-px padding rule (flag 6). Breathing 4–6 s via `TIME` on alpha only, never on width or position (2.9: no tempo change). Width is "2 px at sprite resolution": in the base-res SubViewport that is automatic; in pass B the shader needs the integer scale as a uniform.
  - Beam-edge fringe: the beam is a Light2D texture, not a CanvasItem, so it has no edge to outline. Author one edge-mask sprite per beam shape (4 small unshaded textures) drawn at the hand point with the beam's rotation. Cost: 4 textures, one extra draw per fringed crewmate.

  - Own-sanity filter (stages 1–3): a `canvas_item` shader on the `SubViewportContainer` (it already holds the world as a texture), or — if the world is not in a SubViewport — a full-screen pass on a `CanvasLayer` above the world and below the HUD reading the screen via `BackBufferCopy` `[BIN]` (or the screen-texture hint, `[UNV-4.3]`). Stage-2 "false reach" is an unshaded additive cone sprite, not a Light2D — it tints but reveals nothing because unlit geometry is already black.   **Constraint.**

I recommend the SubViewport (it also gives integer-scale control, item 3). Also: glow was reworked in 4.6 — it now runs before tonemapping with screen blending `[REF]` — so no 4.3-era glow tuning transfers; the threshold test in spike step 8 is the only number to trust.
4. **Base-resolution choice is a 9× lighting-cost lever, not only an art choice.** If the world renders at base resolution (640×360 = 1/9 of 1080p pixels), lights, shadows and the beam edge are computed there and the beam's hard edge becomes a 3-px stair-step at 1080p. ## 1. 2D lighting — PointLight2D / DirectionalLight2D, shadows, occluders, normal/specular

**Constraint (what exists, 4.7.2).**

Hard cap `RenderingServer.MAX_2D_DIRECTIONAL_LIGHTS = 8` `[BIN]`.

- Directional lights: effectively zero use in a 3/4-oblique interior; cap is 8 anyway `[BIN]`.

- Emissive loops: "every running loop glows" cannot mean one PointLight2D per pipe segment. Emission (the pipe itself glowing) and illumination (the pipe lighting the floor) are different costs.

| Emissive loops that illuminate | ≤ 8 non-shadow lights (machinery nodes, not pipes) | Counted inside the 24 |
| Glow | ≤ 3 of `MAX_GLOW_LEVELS = 7` `[BIN]` | Each level is a downsample pass |

## 2. Texture memory and atlas limits

**Constraint.**
- `Image.MAX_WIDTH = MAX_HEIGHT = 16777216` `[BIN]` is the Image class cap, not the GPU's. GPU maximum texture dimension: NOT SOURCEABLE — hardware/driver limit for D3D12/Vulkan; the common 16384 is `[UNV-4.3]` hardware knowledge. Rule: no page larger than 4096×4096 regardless.
- Pairing normal/specular with albedo: one `CanvasTexture` per atlas page holding `diffuse_texture`, `normal_texture`, `specular_texture` `[BIN]`. All three sheets must share one identical layout (same cell positions), because the normal and specular are sampled with the albedo's UVs. `Sprite2D.region_enabled` / `hframes` / `vframes` `[BIN]`, `AtlasTexture.atlas` (typed `Texture2D`, so a CanvasTexture is assignable) `[BIN]`, `TileSetAtlasSource.texture` (typed `Texture2D`) `[BIN]`. Whether region / AtlasTexture / TileSet sampling over a CanvasTexture reads the normal and specular channels correctly: NOT SOURCEABLE — verify in the spike with one normal-mapped tile and one atlas-region sprite under a moving light.
- Compression: pixel-art albedo and normals must stay lossless (VRAM compression smears hard edges and normals). `compress/mode` default `0` `[BIN]`; that `0` means "Lossless" is `[UNV-4.3]` (verify in the Import dock). Memory is therefore uncompressed RGBA8 = 4 B/px per sheet. A greyscale specular PNG may import at 1 B/px (`[UNV-4.3]`); assume 4 B/px worst case.
- Alternative pairing: a `ShaderMaterial` sampling three `sampler2D` uniforms works without CanvasTexture but forfeits the built-in light path; keep CanvasTexture as the default and reserve shaders for the fringe and iridescence.

**What it limits.** Not memory — see the arithmetic. It limits *atlas page count* (every page is three textures and a batch break) and *authoring time* (three sheets per drawn sheet).

**VRAM estimate.** Section 8 owns tile size; the bible gives ratios only (crewmate ≈ 1.1 T, wall face 1.5 T). Assumption: a 20 × 11.25-tile field of view at every candidate, so T = 32 / 48 / 96 px. Frame cell for characters = 2T × 2T (figure + tool/pack overhang + 2-px fringe padding). Bytes per cell = px × 12 (three RGBA8 sheets). Formula: `MB ≈ cells × cell_px × 12 / 1 048 576`.

| Set | Cells (T² units) | 640×360, T=32 | 960×540, T=48 | 1×-native 1920×1080, T=96 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Characters, 5.7 full vision (≈ 430 images × 4 T²) | 1 720 T² | ≈ 21 MB | ≈ 47 MB | ≈ 190 MB |
| Environment, 6.3 full vision (≈ 360 pieces × 3 T² static + 12 animated nodes × 8 frames × 6 T² + trails ≈ 180 T²) | ≈ 1 900 T² | ≈ 23 MB | ≈ 52 MB | ≈ 210 MB |
| Environment, MVP (≈ 110 pieces + 3 nodes + trails) | ≈ 650 T² | ≈ 8 MB | ≈ 18 MB | ≈ 72 MB |
| Atlas padding/waste (+25 %) | — | +11 MB | +25 MB | +100 MB |
| Beam/light textures (4 shapes + pools, ≤ 1024², L8 or RGBA8) | — | ≤ 20 MB | ≤ 20 MB | ≤ 20 MB |
| Render targets: HDR-2D colour RGBA16F + glow chain (+⅓) at render res | — | 2–3 MB at 640×360 / 22 MB at 1080p | same | 22 MB at 1080p, 88 MB at 4K |
| Shadow atlas 2048² | — | ≤ 16 MB (format NOT SOURCEABLE) | same | same |
| **Full-vision total, order of magnitude** | | **≈ 100 MB** | **≈ 190 MB** | **≈ 650 MB** |

Reading: all three fit any plausible discrete GPU and the 4 GB memory ceiling. VRAM does **not** decide the base resolution; lit-pixel count (item 3) and drawing time (×9 pixels per frame at 1×-native) do. Pipe flow patterns should animate by UV scroll in a shader rather than by frames, which is why the environment row counts pipes as single frames.

**Recommendation.** Atlas pages 2048×2048 (16 MB per sheet, 48 MB per CanvasTexture triple); 4096 only for the T = 96 case. Cells per 2048 page: 1024 at T=32, 441 at T=48, 100 at T=96 — the whole 5.7 character set fits one page triple at T=32, two at T=48, five at T=96. One page triple per dialect kit, one for the shared set, one for characters. Pack once with a layout file, emit three sheets from it.

## 3. Pixel-perfect rendering

**Constraint.**
- Stretch: `display/window/stretch/mode` (`disabled` default `[BIN]`; values `canvas_items`, `viewport`), `aspect` (`keep` default `[BIN]`), `scale`, `scale_mode` (`fractional` default; `integer` exists — `Window.CONTENT_SCALE_STRETCH_INTEGER = 1`) `[BIN]`. Base size: `display/window/size/viewport_width/height` (defaults 1152×648 `[BIN]`).
- Sub-viewport route: `SubViewport.size`, `size_2d_override`, `size_2d_override_stretch`, `render_target_update_mode` `[BIN]`; `SubViewportContainer.stretch` (default `false`), `stretch_shrink` (default `1`) `[BIN]`. Per-viewport `use_hdr_2d`, `snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel`, `snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel`, `canvas_item_default_texture_filter`, `msaa_2d`, `use_debanding` `[BIN]`.
- Snapping: `rendering/2d/snap/snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel` and `snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel`, both default `false` `[BIN]`. `gui/common/snap_controls_to_pixels` default `true` `[BIN]`.
- Filter: project default `rendering/textures/canvas_textures/default_texture_filter = 1`, which under `Viewport.DefaultCanvasItemTextureFilter` is **LINEAR** (`NEAREST = 0`) `[BIN]`. The project is currently blurry by default; the preset must set `0`. `CanvasItem.texture_filter` default `0` = `TEXTURE_FILTER_PARENT_NODE` `[BIN]`, so one project-level change propagates to every item. `CanvasTexture.texture_filter` is typed `CanvasItem.TextureFilter` with default `0` = `PARENT_NODE` `[BIN]`, so it inherits too; set it explicitly to `NEAREST` (= `1` in that enum `[BIN]`) only on pages that must never inherit a different parent filter.
- Mipmaps: `mipmaps/generate` default `false` `[BIN]`; keep off (mipmaps with nearest sampling produce shimmering on scaled pixel art `[UNV-4.3]`).
- Camera: `Camera2D` has no pixel-snap member `[BIN]`; `position_smoothing_enabled` default `false` `[BIN]`. Sub-pixel camera positions therefore rely on `snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel`. `physics/common/physics_interpolation` (default `false`) and `Node.physics_interpolation_mode` exist `[BIN]`, and lights/occluders are interpolable `[BIN]`; whether interpolation plus snapping removes 60 Hz camera judder: `[UNV-4.3]`, spike test with a moving crewmate carrying a shadow beam.
- `Viewport.sdf_scale` default `SDF_SCALE_50_PERCENT` `[BIN]` — the SDF built from `sdf_collision` occluders is half-res; irrelevant unless shaders read the SDF.

**Integer-scale table (arithmetic).**

| Base | 1920×1080 | 2560×1440 | 3840×2160 | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 640×360 | 3× | 4× | 6× | integer everywhere |
| 960×540 | 2× | 2.67× — letterbox to 2× or fractional | 4× | fails 1440p |
| 1920×1080 | 1× | 1.33× — fails | 2× | fails 1440p; 9× the pixels to draw and light |

**What it limits.** Sprite resolution and the beam-edge look are coupled. Rendering the world at base resolution keeps every rotated segment, cone edge and shadow edge on the pixel grid (good for 5.4's grid-snapped look, cheap) but renders the hero #1 cone edge as stair-steps of scale size; rendering at window resolution with integer-scaled sprites gives smooth cones and shadows at full cost and lets rotated rig segments and the fringe fall off the pixel grid. Whether Light2D resolves at the viewport's render size: `[UNV-4.3]`, spike step 2.

**Recommendation — one combined architecture (reconciles flag 3 and this item).**
- Root viewport: project `stretch/mode = canvas_items`, `aspect = keep`, `scale_mode = integer`, base `viewport_width/height = 640×360`. The root carries only the HUD `CanvasLayer` and the `SubViewportContainer`, so HUD text renders at window resolution and is outside the world's glow by construction.
- World: a `SubViewport` sized 640×360, `use_hdr_2d = true`, `use_debanding = true`, `snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel = true`, `canvas_item_default_texture_filter = NEAREST`, inside a `SubViewportContainer` with `stretch = true` so the container scales it by the root's integer factor.
- The spike's A/B: keep the SubViewport at 640×360 for pass A (lights at base res); for pass B set the SubViewport's `size` to the window size and `size_2d_override = 640×360` with `size_2d_override_stretch = true` `[BIN]` — logical 640×360 coordinates, sprites integer-scaled, lights and shadows computed at window resolution — without flipping any project setting. Whether `size_2d_override` behaves that way is `[UNV-4.3]`; it is the test.
- Project-wide texture filter `0` (NEAREST) regardless, mipmaps off. `960×540` is recommended against on the 1440p failure alone; 1×-native only if the AD accepts 9× lighting cost and 9× drawing time.

## 4. Per-client hallucination filter and the 5.5 fringe shader

**Constraint / feasibility.**
- Unlit pass: `CanvasItemMaterial.LIGHT_MODE_UNSHADED` `[BIN]` or `render_mode unshaded` in a `canvas_item` shader (`Shader.MODE_CANVAS_ITEM` `[BIN]`; the render-mode keyword is `[UNV-4.3]`). An unshaded CanvasItem receives no Light2D contribution and, not being a Light2D, emits none — "casts no light" holds by construction.
- Per-viewer: the fringe is a material/uniform on the *local* client's view of the crewmate, driven by `CanvasItem.set_instance_shader_parameter` `[BIN]` from a presentation-only script that reads replicated sanity state and never writes it. Rule for Section 8 and the control manifest: **presentation scripts may read simulation state and may only write to CanvasItem / Material / Light2D properties; they never call into gameplay or networking.** A player never sees their own fringe because the local script skips the local avatar.
- Outline shader: sample the albedo alpha at ±1, ±2 texels and paint `#B07BE6` where own alpha is 0 and a neighbour is opaque — hence the 2-px padding rule (flag 6). Breathing 4–6 s via `TIME` on alpha only, never on width or position (2.9: no tempo change). Width is "2 px at sprite resolution": in the base-res SubViewport that is automatic; in pass B the shader needs the integer scale as a uniform.
- Beam-edge fringe: the beam is a Light2D texture, not a CanvasItem, so it has no edge to outline. Author one edge-mask sprite per beam shape (4 small unshaded textures) drawn at the hand point with the beam's rotation. Cost: 4 textures, one extra draw per fringed crewmate.
- Glow interaction: keep fringe luminance below `glow_hdr_threshold` (flag 3). Order: fringe sprite drawn as a child **behind** the body (`show_behind_parent` `[BIN]`) so it never covers the sprite's own pixels.
- Own-sanity filter (stages 1–3): a `canvas_item` shader on the `SubViewportContainer` (it already holds the world as a texture), or — if the world is not in a SubViewport — a full-screen pass on a `CanvasLayer` above the world and below the HUD reading the screen via `BackBufferCopy` `[BIN]` (or the screen-texture hint, `[UNV-4.3]`). Stage-2 "false reach" is an unshaded additive cone sprite, not a Light2D — it tints but reveals nothing because unlit geometry is already black. **Constraint.**

**What it limits.** Stepped playback is a script decision, not an engine feature: pose only every N physics ticks (12 fps = every 5th tick at 60 Hz) and quantise each segment angle to 360/24 = 15° (or 360/16). Resolved above — use as-is; `--review` overrides `review_mode`. No block →
defaults in `.claude/docs/config-resolution.md`.

# Map Systems


When this skill is invoked:

## Parse Arguments

Two modes:

- **No argument**: `/map-systems` — Run the full decomposition workflow (Phases 1-5)
  to create or update the systems index.
- **`next`**: `/map-systems next` — Pick the highest-priority undesigned system
  from the index and hand off to `/design-system` (Phase 6).


See `.claude/docs/director-gates.md` for the full check pattern. Individual gate definitions live in `.claude/docs/director-gates/[gate-id].md` — the spawned agent reads its own gate file; do not read it in the parent session.


Every `AskUserQuestion` call follows `.claude/docs/automation-modes.md`
(collaborative asks always · guided major-only · autonomous logs and proceeds;
`automation_always_ask` categories always prompt). In collaborative mode the
system list, dependency, priority and write approvals are separate questions:
each waits for its answer before the next step runs.

**`docs.density`** — it controls per-section *depth*, where `workflow`
controls which sections exist. `modes.rigor` sets both together; set
`docs.density` explicitly to vary depth alone: `terse` (the default, via `rigor: minimal`) = one-line system descriptions;
`balanced` = a brief paragraph per system + dependency notes (`rigor: standard`);
`thorough` = full system-by-system rationale + relationship analysis. Apply it to
every section you author.

> **Where the per-system prose goes.** `templates/systems-index.md`'s Systems
> Enumeration is a fixed-column table with no description column, so at
> `balanced` and `thorough` the prose belongs in `## Overview` — one short
> paragraph per system at `balanced`, plus relationship analysis at `thorough` —
> and in the `## Dependency Map` layer notes. **Do not add a column to the
> enumeration table** — it is a fixed contract in
> `.claude/docs/templates/systems-index.md`, and its consumers
> (`/design-system` §6 and §7, `/create-epics`) are written against the columns it
> defines. Widening it is a schema change, not a formatting choice.
>
> **How the consumers actually read it.** Nothing parses this table
> positionally. The two scripts that mention `systems-index.md`
> (`gdd-structure-check.sh:51`, `review-scope.sh:40`) match it **by filename** in a
> `case` statement and parse no columns at all; the two skills key on the
> **`Category` column by name** (`design-system:229`, `:780`). So `Category` is
> the column that must never be renamed or dropped, and the table stays a fixed
> contract because every consumer is written against the set of columns the
> template defines.
> At `terse`, the table plus a one-paragraph `## Overview` is the whole output.

**`workflow`** (see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`):
- `full` / `standard` — required before `/design-system` (systems must be mapped
  before per-system GDDs are authored).
- `minimal` — not required (the game brief replaces the systems index). Can
  still be run voluntarily.

---

## Phase 1: Read Concept (Required Context)

Read the game concept and any existing design work. This provides the raw material
for systems decomposition.

**Required:**
- Read `design/gdd/game-concept.md` (at `minimal`, read `design/game-brief.md`
  instead) — **fail with a clear message if neither is found**:
  > "No game concept found. Run `/brainstorm` first to create one, then come back
  > to decompose it into systems."

**Optional (read if they exist):**
- Read `design/gdd/game-pillars.md` — pillars constrain priority and scope
- Read `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — if exists, **resume** from where it left off
  (update, don't recreate from scratch)
- Glob `design/gdd/*.md` — check which system GDDs already exist

**If the systems index already exists:**
- Read it and present current status to the user
- Use `AskUserQuestion` to ask:
  "The systems index already exists with [N] systems ([M] designed, [K] not started).
  What would you like to do?"
  - Options: "Update the index with new systems", "Design the next undesigned system",
    "Review and revise priorities"

---

## Phase 2: Systems Enumeration (Collaborative)

Extract and identify all systems the game needs. This is the creative core of the
skill — it requires human judgment because concept docs rarely enumerate every
system explicitly.

### Step 2a: Extract Explicit Systems

Scan the game concept for directly mentioned systems and mechanics:
- Core Mechanics section (most explicit)
- Core Loop section (implies what systems drive each loop tier)
- Technical Considerations section (networking, procedural generation, etc.)
- MVP Definition section (required features = required systems)

### Step 2b: Identify Implicit Systems

For each explicit system, identify the **hidden systems** it implies. Games always
need more systems than the concept doc mentions. Use this inference pattern:

- "Inventory" implies: item database, equipment slots, weight/capacity rules,
  inventory UI, item serialization for save/load
- "Combat" implies: damage calculation, health system, hit detection, status effects,
  enemy AI, combat UI (health bars, damage numbers), death/respawn
- "Open world" implies: streaming/chunking, LOD system, fast travel, map/minimap,
  point of interest tracking, world state persistence
- "Multiplayer" implies: networking layer, lobby/matchmaking, state synchronization,
  anti-cheat, network UI (ping, player list)
- "Crafting" implies: recipe database, ingredient gathering, crafting UI,
  success/failure mechanics, recipe discovery/learning
- "Dialogue" implies: dialogue tree system, dialogue UI, choice tracking, NPC
  state management, localization hooks
- "Progression" implies: XP system, level-up mechanics, skill tree, unlock
  tracking, progression UI, progression save data

Explain in conversation text why each implicit system is needed (with examples).

### Step 2c: User Review

Present the enumeration organized by category. For each system, show:
- Name
- Category
- Brief description (1 sentence)
- Whether it was explicit (from concept) or implicit (inferred)

Then use `AskUserQuestion` to capture feedback:
- "Are there systems missing from this list?"
- "Should any of these be combined or split?"
- "Are there systems listed that this game does NOT need?"

**At `collaborative`** — iterate until the user approves the enumeration.
**At `guided`** — ask once, apply the answer, and proceed; do not loop.
**At `autonomous`** — do not ask. Record the enumeration and its inferred systems
via `log_decision` and proceed.

> **The loop needed an exit that does not depend on being asked.**
> `automation-modes.md:56` defines `autonomous` as *"No `AskUserQuestion`"*, so a
> loop terminating on "the user approves" has no termination path there at all.
> Same class as Step 5b, one level up: that was an unconditional *write* gate,
> this is an unconditional *control-flow loop* around the question.

---

## Phase 3: Dependency Mapping (Collaborative)

For each system, determine what it depends on. A system "depends on" another if
it cannot function without that other system existing first.

### Step 3a: Map Dependencies

For each system, list its dependencies. Use these dependency heuristics:
- **Input/output dependencies**: System A produces data System B needs
- **Structural dependencies**: System A provides the framework System B plugs into
- **UI dependencies**: Every gameplay system has a corresponding UI system that
  depends on it (but UI is designed after the gameplay system)

### Step 3b: Sort by Dependency Order

Arrange systems into layers:
1. **Foundation**: Systems with zero dependencies (designed and built first)
2. **Core**: Systems depending only on Foundation systems
3. **Feature**: Systems depending on Core systems
4. **Presentation**: UI and feedback systems that wrap gameplay systems
5. **Polish**: Meta-systems, tutorials, analytics, accessibility

### Step 3c: Detect Circular Dependencies

Check for cycles in the dependency graph. If found:
- Highlight them to the user
- Propose resolutions (interface abstraction, simultaneous design, breaking the
  cycle by defining a contract between the two systems)

### Step 3d: Present to User

Show the dependency map as a layered list. Highlight:
- Any circular dependencies
- Any "bottleneck" systems (many others depend on them — these are high-risk)
- Any systems with no dependents (leaf nodes — lower risk, can be designed late)

Use `AskUserQuestion` to ask: "Does this dependency ordering look right? Any
dependencies I'm missing or that should be removed?"

**Review mode check** — apply before spawning TD-SYSTEM-BOUNDARY:
- `solo` → skip. Note: "TD-SYSTEM-BOUNDARY skipped — Solo mode." Proceed to priority assignment.
- `lean` → skip (not a PHASE-GATE). Note: "TD-SYSTEM-BOUNDARY skipped — Lean mode." Proceed to priority assignment.
- `full` → spawn as normal.

**After dependency mapping is approved, spawn `technical-director` via `Agent` using gate TD-SYSTEM-BOUNDARY (`.claude/docs/director-gates/td-system-boundary.md`) before proceeding to priority assignment.**

Pass: the dependency graph (each system → what it depends on), layer assignments, bottleneck systems, and any circular dependencies with their proposed resolutions.

Present the assessment. If REJECT, revise the system boundaries with the user, show the revised dependency map, and only then move to priority assignment. If CONCERNS, note them inline in the systems index and continue. If NOT ASSESSED [missing input], it is not an APPROVE: name what was missing, then supply it and re-run the gate, or continue with `TD-SYSTEM-BOUNDARY: NOT ASSESSED — [input]` noted in the index draft.

---

## Phase 4: Priority Assignment (Collaborative)

Assign each system to a priority tier based on what milestone it's needed for.

### Step 4a: Auto-Assign Based on Concept

Use these heuristics for initial assignment:
- **MVP**: Systems mentioned in the concept's "Required for MVP" section, plus their
  Foundation-layer dependencies
- **Vertical Slice**: Systems needed for a complete experience in one area
- **Alpha**: All remaining gameplay systems
- **Full Vision**: Polish, meta, and nice-to-have systems

### Step 4b: User Review

Present the priority assignments in a table. For each tier, explain why systems
were placed there.

Use `AskUserQuestion` to ask: "Do these priority assignments match your vision?
Which systems should be higher or lower priority?"

Explain reasoning in conversation: "I placed [system] in MVP because the core loop
requires it — without [system], the 30-second loop can't function."

**How to phrase the reasoning** — this governs what you *say*, not a column you
write. Neither table has a `Why` column: Systems Enumeration is
`# / Name / Category / Priority / Status / Design Doc / Depends On`, and
Recommended Design Order is `Order / System / Priority / Layer / Agent(s) /
Est. Effort`. The rationale lives in the conversation above and, for anything
the user should still see after the session, in the index's `## Overview`
paragraph. Do not invent a column for it.

Mix technical necessity with player-experience reasoning. A purely technical
justification — "the damage system needs damage math" — is insufficient on its
own when the system directly shapes what the player feels. Good reasoning names
both, and cites the pillar it serves:
- "Required for the core loop — without it the player's main choice has no
  consequence (Pillar [N]: [pillar name])"
- "This is where [system]'s identity is established — the stat definitions here
  are what make it feel different from [the sibling system]"
- "Foundation for every later economy decision — the player must understand
  costs before any of the choices built on top of it mean anything"

> **Fill the brackets from *this* project.** The bracketed slots are not
> decoration. Worked examples from another genre (a tower-defense "Ballista's
> punch-through identity… what makes it feel different from Archer", "Pillar 2:
> Placement is the Puzzle") get reproduced verbatim by a run against a different
> game, which then carries that game's vocabulary instead of its own.

**Review mode check** — apply before spawning PR-SCOPE:
- `solo` → skip. Note: "PR-SCOPE skipped — Solo mode." Proceed to Step 4c.
- `lean` → skip (not a PHASE-GATE). Note: "PR-SCOPE skipped — Lean mode." Proceed to Step 4c.
- `full` → spawn as normal.

**After priorities are approved, spawn `producer` via `Agent` using gate PR-SCOPE (`.claude/docs/director-gates/pr-scope.md`) before writing the index.**

Pass the gate's fields from the index: the full vision scope (every system in the index), the MVP definition (the MVP tier's systems), the scope tiers (system count per milestone tier, with estimated implementation volume — system count × average complexity), the stated project timeline as the timeline estimate, and team size.

Present the assessment. PR-SCOPE answers REALISTIC / OPTIMISTIC / UNREALISTIC.
If UNREALISTIC, offer to revise priority tier assignments before writing the
index. If OPTIMISTIC, show the producer's suggested adjustments and ask whether to
apply them to the tiers before writing; if the user declines, note them and
continue. If NOT ASSESSED [missing input] — often the team size or timeline — it
is not a REALISTIC: name what was missing, then supply it and re-run the gate, or
continue with `PR-SCOPE: NOT ASSESSED — [input]` noted in the index draft.

### Step 4c: Determine Design Order

Combine dependency sort + priority tier to produce the final design order:
1. MVP Foundation systems first
2. MVP Core systems second
3. MVP Feature systems third
4. Vertical Slice Foundation/Core systems
5. ...and so on

This is the order the team should write GDDs in.

---

## Phase 5: Create Systems Index (Write)

### Step 5a: Draft the Document

Using the template at `.claude/docs/templates/systems-index.md`, populate the
systems index with all data from Phases 2-4:
- Fill the enumeration table
- Fill the dependency map
- Fill the recommended design order
- Fill the high-risk systems
- Fill progress tracker (all systems "Not Started" initially, unless GDDs already exist)

### Step 5b: Approval

Present a summary of the document:
- Total systems count by category
- MVP system count
- First 3 systems in the design order
- Any high-risk items

**At `automation: collaborative`** — ask: "May I write the systems index to
`design/gdd/systems-index.md`?" Wait for approval. Write the file only after
"yes."

**At `automation: guided`** — a **new** index gets the same "May I write …?"
question, because `.claude/docs/automation-modes.md` has `guided` ask "May I
write?" for new files. When the index already exists, present the summary above,
name the destination (`design/gdd/systems-index.md`), and write the update without
waiting for an explicit "yes". Say what you wrote afterwards.

> **Keep this line scoped to its mode.** `automation-modes.md` says `guided`
> *"proceeds after a short summary, does not wait for explicit yes"* and asks
> "May I write?" *"for new files only"*, and this skill's own Collaborative
> Protocol section is scoped to `collaborative`. An unconditional "wait for
> approval" here collides with both.

**Review mode check** — apply before spawning CD-SYSTEMS:
- `solo` → skip. Note: "CD-SYSTEMS skipped — Solo mode." Proceed to Step 5c.
- `lean` → skip (not a PHASE-GATE). Note: "CD-SYSTEMS skipped — Lean mode." Proceed to Step 5c.
- `full` → spawn as normal.

**After the systems index is written, spawn `creative-director` via `Agent` using gate CD-SYSTEMS (`.claude/docs/director-gates/cd-systems.md`).**

Pass: systems index path; game pillars and core fantasy — from `design/gdd/game-concept.md`, or at `minimal` the pitch and "what they feel" line of `design/game-brief.md`, which has no pillars; the priority tier assignments for every tier (MVP / Vertical Slice / Alpha / Full Vision); and the high-risk and bottleneck systems from the dependency map.

Present the assessment. If REJECT, revise the system set with the user before GDD authoring begins. If CONCERNS, show them and use `AskUserQuestion`: `Revise the system set` / `Accept — record them in the index` / `Discuss further`. On *Revise*, rework the affected systems with the user and ask again before re-writing the index. On *Accept* — the option names the edit, so choosing it is the ask — record them in the systems index as a `> **Creative Director Note**`
placed **directly beneath the `## Priority Tiers` table**, naming the tier each
concern applies to — e.g. `> **Creative Director Note** (MVP): …`.
`templates/systems-index.md` has a Priority Tiers *definition table*, not a
section per tier, so there is no "top of the tier section" to write to — do not
direct the writer to one. If NOT ASSESSED [missing input], it is not an APPROVE
(`.claude/docs/director-gates.md`): name what was missing, then supply it and
re-run the gate, or ask before recording `> **Creative Director Note**:
CD-SYSTEMS NOT ASSESSED — [input]` in the same place.

### Step 5c: Update Session State

After writing, create `production/session-state/active.md` if it does not exist, then update it with:
- Task: Systems decomposition
- Status: Systems index created
- File: design/gdd/systems-index.md
- Next: Design individual system GDDs

**Verdict: COMPLETE** — systems index written to `design/gdd/systems-index.md`.
If the user declined: **Verdict: BLOCKED** — user did not approve the write.

---

## Phase 6: Design Individual Systems (Handoff to /design-system)

This phase is entered when:
- The user says "yes" to designing systems after creating the index
- The user invokes `/map-systems [system-name]`
- The user invokes `/map-systems next`

### Step 6a: Select the System

- If a system name was provided, find it in the systems index
- If `next` was used, pick the highest-priority undesigned system (by design order)
- If the user just finished the index, ask:
  "Would you like to start designing individual systems now? The first system in
  the design order is [name]. Or would you prefer to stop here and come back later?"

Use `AskUserQuestion` for: "Start designing [system-name] now, pick a different
system, or stop here?"

### Step 6b: Hand Off to /design-system

Once a system is selected, invoke the `/design-system [system-name]` skill.

The `/design-system` skill handles the full GDD authoring process:
- Gathers context from game concept, systems index, and dependency GDDs
- Creates a file skeleton immediately
- Walks through all 8 required sections one at a time (collaborative, incremental)
- Cross-references existing docs to prevent contradictions
- Routes to specialist agents for domain expertise
- Writes each section to file as soon as it's approved
- Runs `/design-review` when complete
- Updates the systems index

**Do not duplicate the /design-system workflow here.** This skill owns the systems
*index*; `/design-system` owns individual system *GDDs*.

### Step 6c: Loop or Stop

After `/design-system` completes, use `AskUserQuestion`:
- "Continue to the next system ([next system name])?"
- "Pick a different system?"
- "Stop here for this session?"

If continuing, return to Step 6a.

---

## Phase 7: Suggest Next Steps

After the systems index is created (or after designing some systems), present next actions using `AskUserQuestion`:

- "Systems index is written. What would you like to do next?"
  - [A] Start designing GDDs — run `/design-system [first-system-in-order]`
  - [B] Run `/gate-check systems-design` — the Concept → Systems Design gate; offer this only while `project.stage` is still Concept

**Direction: *What You Light, You Can Read***

### The Rule

> **Light is a resource you spend. Inside it, every machine states its condition. Outside it, the dark is honest.**

**How to use it.** When two visual choices both seem fine, ask three questions in order. The first answer that separates them decides the choice.
1. Does one of them make the player *spend* something (light, power, attention) to learn what they see?
2. Does one of them put the information *in the world* (a moving part, a medium, a trail) instead of on top of it?
3. If the player is lied to here, will the lie leak the sane palette?

**Why this works as a tie-breaker.** It is one sentence with three clauses that map to three kinds of decision: lighting, state display, and truth. Almost every art question lands in one of those. It also keeps the art workload honest. The main cost sits in the 2D lighting pipeline rather than in sprite-state count, so the rule favors cheap, systemic answers (a light, a hue, a trail) over expensive bespoke ones (a new animation per state).

**Alternatives considered.**
- *"The Dark Is the Default"* alone. It gives strong mood but nothing to say about how a lit machine should look, so it would leave the Satisfactory-style legibility to chance.
- *"Every Pipe Is a Sentence"* alone. It gives strong legibility but treats light as free, which would erase Pillar 3 (The Web Watches).
- The hybrid keeps both. Legibility is the reward and darkness is the price.

### Principle 1: Darkness Is Honest; Light Is a Decision
**Serves Pillar 1, The World Never Lies** (Pillar 3 benefits secondarily).

Rooms are not fogged, they are *unlit*. Geometry always exists, and any source reveals it exactly as it is. The visible-world edge is the real edge of a real light, never a mask. The physical radius your light actually reveals is a fixed anchor and never lies. Even at low sanity, the hallucination layer may add things but may not move that boundary.

**Rationale.** Pillar 1 says the physical world is ground truth and only instruments and perception can be wrong. A vignette or fog-of-war mask is an interface lying about the world, and it would give the sanity system nothing to betray. True occlusion gives the player a reliable baseline. A hallucinated shadow with no occluder is then frightening *because* occlusion is normally trustworthy. It also makes light a decision, since each lamp is a visible cost with a visible reach.

**Design test.** When a vignette or fog-of-war mask competes with true 2D occlusion from light sources with hard falloff, choose the true occlusion.

**Alternative rejected.** A soft ambient-reveal radius around the player. It is cheaper to build and reads well, but it makes the player the light source for free, which erases the spend-light economy.

### Principle 2: Inside the Light, State Lives in the Sprite, Not the Icon
**Serves Pillar 2, Dread Before Chaos** (and Pillar 1, since the physical world carries the truth).

Every system has a visible moving part and a visible medium (a rotor, a fluid, a filament). Failure renders as a trail in the loop's own hue: puddle, frost, scorch, mist, drip. A trail is also a tell. Every breach is preceded by a perceivable escalation, and that escalation is drawn *in the world*, so a careful player can read it. Hue coding is always redundant with shape and pattern (flow chevrons, pipe diameter) so it stays readable for colorblind players.

**Rationale.** Pillar 2 needs tells a careful player could have caught. A banner is read once and dismissed, but a frosting elbow can be seen to worsen from across the room. This is the Satisfactory lesson: watching a machine work is its own reward, and failure can be diagnosed by following the eye along the pipe. Resource loops keep their hue everywhere they appear (working proposal: O₂ cyan, power amber, coolant ice-blue, fuel orange-red, integrity neutral grey), so a hue is a vocabulary the player learns once.

**Design test.** When a status LED or a "COOLANT LOW" banner competes with a turning rotor with visible fluid or a frosted elbow with a drip, choose the rotor and the elbow.

**Alternatives rejected.**
- A world-space icon layer on every system. It is cheap, but it reads as an interface and it gives the hallucination system an easy, un-physical target.
- Heavy per-state sprite sets. They are too expensive for a solo developer, so state should come from shared hue, trail and motion systems instead.

### Principle 3: Emission Is Exposure
**Serves Pillar 3, The Web Watches.**

Running loops glow in their own hue. With power off, the ship is lit only by what is still running. Every loop you run is a lantern the web can see. The web itself has no hue of its own and appears only in your light, as oily iridescence under direct illumination. Deeper rings do not change hue. They lower ambient light and raise the iridescence.

**Rationale.** Pillar 3 says Attention is shown in the world, never as a hidden meter, and that restraint is a real strategy. Making light, power use and visibility the *same thing visually* means going dark is a legible tactical choice, not a menu setting. Tying the web's appearance to the player's own light also makes the web's presence feel like a consequence of the player's choices, which supports the "dread is feeling it come" hinge. Keeping hue constant across depth keeps the loop vocabulary from Principle 2 reliable at every ring. Depth is expressed only through ambient and iridescence.

**Design test.** When an on-screen attention meter competes with more filaments resolving in the player's light cone as Attention rises, choose the filaments.

**Alternative rejected.** Shifting the palette per depth ring. It gives strong depth identity, but it would break the flow-coded hue vocabulary, and it would compete with the violet and flesh-tone rule below.

### Corollary: When the Game Lies, the Lie Leaks (serves Pillar 4)

This is a binding constraint on Pillar 4's hallucination classes, not a fourth principle.

- **Flesh tones and violet exist nowhere in the sane world.** When either appears, it is the player's sanity and never the location. Every hallucination leaks them somewhere: a fringe, a flicker, a tint at the edge of the light. Subtle is allowed; absent is not.
- **Drift order.** Instruments first (needles disagree with the body of the ship), then the light lies (the cone seems to reach further than it does, shadows with no occluder, temperature shifts), then loop hues bleed violet at pipe edges and flesh tones enter.
- **Anchors that never shift.** Character sprites, hand tools, the HUD frame, and the true light radius. A crewmate's own light beam (colour and shape) also stays truthful, per Pillar 1's human channel.

**Design test.** A seamless hallucination vs. one that leaks the sane palette → the leak.

### Constraint Notes

- **Art style.** HD pixel art at 3/4 oblique top-down, with Godot 4.7.2 2D lighting. Readability under light comes from silhouette, hue and motion, not from texture noise. This keeps sprites cheap to author and keeps the lighting doing the visual work.
- **Pipeline consequence.** The lighting-budget spike (a lighting test on D3D12) is the *first* spike, because all three principles depend on 2D lights, occlusion and emission being affordable.
- **Open for the technical artist.** Whether true occlusion at hard falloff, many emissive loops, and a per-client hallucination filter all fit the lighting budget is unmeasured. If they don't, the first thing to cut is the number of simultaneous emitters, not the occlusion rule in Principle 1.

### Reference Touchstones

- **Project Zomboid.** Lived-in detail and a dark world that you move through at a patient pace.
- **Satisfactory.** Legible machinery and flows you can read at a glance.
- **Stellaris.** Dread delivered by systems, not cutscenes.
- **Barotrauma.** A 2D hostile vessel, with failure you can see happening.
- **Beyond the Aquila Rift.** A kind-looking lie, where the wrongness is in what leaks through.
- **Pandorum.** Waking into wrongness aboard a derelict.

### Checklist

For any new asset or visual feature, answer these before approval.
1. Does it make the player spend light to see it (Principle 1)?
2. Does its state live in a moving part or a trail, not an icon (Principle 2)?
3. If it glows, is that glow exposure, and does it carry the right hue (Principle 3)?
4. Does it avoid violet and flesh tones in the sane world (Corollary)?
5. If it is an anchor (character sprite, hand tool, HUD frame, light radius), does it stay unshifted under hallucination (Corollary)?
EOF

input.content:
# UX Alignment Check — Section 7 (ux-designer output, verbatim summary)

## Verdict table
| # | Item | Verdict | Conflict | Section 7 rule (summary) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Dark world vs reading critical state in breach | Supports, needs 3 rules | §3.5 "beam brightest in frame" unsatisfiable next to Paper White text; brightness slider breaks Principle 1 / Pillar 3 | HUD layer exempt from §3.5, glow and ambient; bounded ambient-floor option; a trail-contrast number |
| 2 | Diegetic vs screen-space | Needs a rule | Bible rejects Attention meter and sanity meter; nothing names what is screen-space | Suit vitals, tool state, alarm mark screen-space; ship loops may be diegetic stations; Attention/own sanity in-world with a11y fork |
| 3 | Lying instruments vs low vision / colour-blindness | Conflicts | Stage-1 leak is violet gleam only (~2.9:1 on UI ground, ~1:1 on bezel); invisible to deutan/tritan/low vision; violates §4.0 p2 | Every class-(b) reading leaks on motion + sound as well as hue; anchor list extended to non-visual channels |
| 4 | Hue-coded loops beyond §4.7 | Conflicts (reduced motion) | Motion is primary backup for Fuel vs Alarm; reduced-motion toggle strips the backbone; only "most" colours have a sound | Reduced-motion keeps static direction shapes; all five loops get running + failing sounds; no global daltonization |
| 5 | Text size / contrast | Supports, needs numbers | Alarm Red 3.3:1 fails as text; Paper White vs Tungsten 1.2:1 so Tungsten-only selection invisible to achromats; HUD text over beam core ≈ 1:1 | Minimums, opaque ground plates, shape-change focus, stroke floors, integer pixel-font scaling |
| 6 | Gamepad navigation of diegetic UI | Needs a rule | World gauges are small oblique targets; web-map filaments off-grid | Proximity focus + one contextual action; mirror card; snap-to-node map; enumerate "partial gamepad" per flow |
| 7 | Co-op crewmate state vs human channel | Conflicts | Crewmate sanity mark is violet fringe only while friendly harm is lethal | Class-(c) victim tell gets motion + audio; voice, text chat, pings, speaker indicator declared anchors; no remote vitals by default |

## Hard requirements
- **HR-1 HUD exemption.** HUD renders on its own layer, excluded from world glow, ambient, occlusion and the §3.5 "beam brightest" rule; never dims/fades with world light, Attention or sanity. Test: at 0% ambient and over the beam core, HUD text ≥ 4.5:1 against its own ground.
- **HR-2 Opaque ground.** Every HUD reading and text sits on an opaque UI-ground plate (`#1C2128`); never over live world pixels or on the bezel. Test: no Hull Grey glyph on `#5C6670`.
- **HR-3 Screen-space set.** Suit O₂, suit integrity, equipped tool + state, Alarm warning mark, suit-sensed local temperature/pressure are screen-space at all times (pod transit and boarding included).
- **HR-4 Alarm Red is never text.** UI: warning-mark glyph only (≥ 3:1), paired with shape and sound.
- **HR-5 Stage-1 lie is tri-modal.** Any class-(b) reading on screen-space or a mirror card carries, besides the fringe-violet gleam (`#B07BE6`, never core), one defined motion signature (e.g. needle settles with none of the micro-jitter honest needles show, or sub-1 Hz glass flicker) and one sound signature. Subtle allowed, absent not. Test: with hue removed and with audio removed in turn, a trained tester identifies the lying instrument above chance.
- **HR-6 Anchor list extended.** Never shift under hallucination: HUD frame geometry/position/scale; input mapping; UI typography, scale and a11y settings; menu/pause/settings layers (no violet or flesh, ever); speaker indicator, text chat, pings; haptics driven by P1 events.
- **HR-7 Class-(c) victim tell is tri-modal.** Low-sanity crewmate mark carries motion in the fringe (outside sprite and beam pixels) and an audible P1 cue in proximity, besides violet. Test: under achromatopsia simulation a tester identifies the below-threshold crewmate before contact.
- **HR-8 Reduced motion preserves the backbone.** Flow direction remains as static chevrons/dashes; Alarm sweep becomes static mark + sound + HUD glyph; trail propagation never suppressed; HR-5 motion signatures slow but do not vanish.
- **HR-9 Loop audio is complete.** All five loops have distinct running and failing sounds; every Tell has an audio component starting no later than its visual. → audio-director.
- **HR-10 No global hue remap.** Colour-blind support is shape/pattern emphasis plus per-element alternates in §4.7; no full-frame daltonization shader.
- **HR-11 Focus is a shape.** Keyboard/gamepad focus changes bezel geometry (thicker chamfer, underline, bracket) in addition to Tungsten accent.
- **HR-12 Minimums (provisional; 1080p @100%).** Critical readings ≥ 24 px; body ≥ 18 px; needle/glyph stroke ≥ 2 px; text ≥ 4.5:1, glyphs ≥ 3:1; UI scale 100–200% in integer steps for bitmap fonts (or vector HUD face). Every critical needle has a numeral beside it. Pending accessibility-specialist tier.
- **HR-13 HUD flicker ceiling.** No HUD element flashes above 3 Hz; no HUD shake, blur, chromatic aberration or scale change under any state.
- **HR-14 Gamepad completeness.** Enumerate gamepad-complete vs keyboard-only flows at MVP (text chat the only permitted keyboard-only item in the core loop). Diegetic instruments: proximity focus, one contextual action, mirror card at HUD size carrying the same reading and HR-5 tells. Web map: snap-to-node. Destructive actions: hold-to-confirm.
- **HR-15 Ambient-floor option is bounded.** Low-vision ambient option raises floor to ≤ 6% (provisional; below the 10% stable state), reveals hull geometry only (web, horrors, filaments still only in direct light), does not touch Attention simulation, per-client.

## Recommendations
- R-1 Critical vitals (O₂, alarm) in a compact strip near screen-centre-bottom; full panel at the edge.
- R-2 Confirm with game-designer that character animation state counts as an anchor (gives honest O₂ tell: breathing, stumble).
- R-3 Classify hand-tool readings (scanner) — likely instruments per Pillar 4(d).
- R-4 State explicitly that web map and menus are a human instrument that never lies.
- R-5 Design a world-space ping as a human-channel anchor (deaf/HoH, no-mic crews).
- R-6 Captions: if world audio is P1 ground truth, captions name sources precisely; if phantom audio can be hallucinated, audio needs its own leak equivalent to violet. Blocking for deaf/HoH support.
- R-7 The TD's true-value debug overlay is never exposed as an accessibility option.

## Decisions taken (autonomous, recommended options)
1. Attention accessibility indicator: off-by-default a11y glyph (screen-space filament-count), honest, under accessibility settings only.
2. Crewmate sanity mark: world mark + redundancy (violet fringe + fringe motion + P1 suit sound), no roster flag.
3. Critical vitals: centre-bottom strip, full panel at edge.
4. Low-vision ambient: bounded floor boost per HR-15.

## Open questions by owner
- game-designer: Is "heat" the coolant loop or a room-temperature P1 consequence? Does the boarder receive home-ship telemetry on a derelict — instrument or anchor? Are world sounds (incl. phantom-entity audio) ground truth or hallucinable? Does sprite animation state count as an anchor? Are scanner readings instruments? Is carried weight (class d field check) an honest physical or an instrument numeral?
- audio-director: HR-9 loop sounds; HR-5/HR-7 sound signatures; audio leak equivalent if audio can lie.
- accessibility-specialist: set HR-12 numbers; confirm HR-13 3 Hz and §2.8 sweep against photosensitivity.
- ui-programmer: HUD CanvasLayer excluded from glow/ambient; integer scaling for bitmap fonts; mirror-card feasibility.
- art-director: typography face under integer-scale constraint; HR-7 fringe motion look.
