**Flash thresholds verified against W3C** (WCAG 2.1 SC 2.3.1 and technique G176): a *general flash* is a pair of opposing relative-luminance changes ≥ 10 % of maximum with the darker image below 0.80; a *red flash* is any opposing pair involving a saturated red; content passes with **≤ 3 flashes (opposing pairs) in any one-second period**, or when the concurrently flashing area is below 21,824 px² at 1024×768 (25 % of a 341×256 estimate of a 10° field). Converted to the 640×360 base (my derivation, not W3C): the 10° field ≈ one third of each viewport axis ≈ 213×120 base px, so the small-safe-area exemption is ≈ 6,400 base px² (≈ 80×80 base px). **Treat that as an upper bound** — a fullscreen game at desk or handheld distance fills more visual angle than a 1024×768 web page, so 10° is a smaller fraction of the screen and the real exemption is smaller. QA must not treat 80×80 as safe.

Legibility angular figures: ISO 9241-303 is commonly cited (secondary sources; I could not read the standard text) as 20–22 arcmin character height recommended, 16–18 arcmin acceptable depending on contrast.

---

## 1. Readability at 2× (Steam Deck 1280×800 / 720p)

**Verdict: needs a rule.**

**Analysis.** 7.1 makes the *screen-pixel* floor the contract (21 / 15 px cap height) and the art-px column a derivation; the table has 1080p and 1440p rows only. At a 2× world the 7 / 5 art-px faces render at **14 / 10 screen px** — 67 % of the floor — and the derivation for a 2× HUD (10.5 / 7.5 art px) is not an integer, so no bitmap face at "100 %" can meet it. Angular check on the Deck (7-inch, ≈ 216 PPI, held ≈ 38 cm): 14 px cap ≈ 15 arcmin, 10 px ≈ 11 arcmin — the label floor falls below the commonly cited 16 arcmin minimum. At a **3× HUD** the same screen gives 21 / 15 px ≈ 22 / 16 arcmin, meeting the floor exactly. 8.1 already states the HUD's integer steps are independent of camera zoom; the rule is to make them independent of the *world scale* too.

**Bands.** 8.2 sized the 2 px bands and 1 px separators to survive the single integer zoom-out step from a 3× world (sprites at 67 %). At a 2× world the only step out is 1×: separators become 1 screen px (≈ 1 arcmin on the Deck), below the acuity needed to count four bands. Whether bands read at the *default* 2× on a 7-inch screen (4 px band, 2 px separator ≈ 2 arcmin) is an on-device check for the accessibility-specialist, not a desk verdict. Identity is redundant by design — beam shape (3.2) and the crew-strip glyph (7.5) carry it — so a band failure degrades, it does not break.

**Conflicts to surface, not swallow.**
- 7.0 caps the critical strip at 12 % × 5 % of frame "at 100 % UI scale" and calls exceeding it "the player's explicit accessibility trade". On a 1280×800 screen with the 3× HUD the plate (230×54 px) is ≈ 18 % × 6.8 % **by default**, not by choice. Routed to art-director: re-express the cap relative to a 1080p reference frame, or accept the Deck overage as a platform default.
- HR-12 labels HUD scale "100–200 %" relative to the world scale, so "100 %" is 3× at 1080p and 2× on the Deck — different physical sizes under the same label.

**Rules to add.**
- **C-R1 (hard).** HUD integer multiplier `H` is chosen independently of world scale `W`: `H_default = max(W, 3)` — never below 3 on any display — and the player may raise it in integer steps up to `2 × H_default`. *QA:* at 1280×800, 1280×720, 1366×768, 1920×1080, 2560×1440, 3840×2160 the critical-strip numeral cap height is ≥ 21 screen px and the smallest label ≥ 15 at the default HUD scale.
- **C-R2 (hard).** The HUD layout is authored anchor-relative to the visible viewport edges with the 5 % safe margin measured in HUD pixels, never against an assumed 640×360 HUD canvas; it must survive a fractional logical canvas (1280×800 ÷ 3 = 426.7×266.7) and both `keep` and `expand` aspects. *QA:* no HUD element clipped or overlapping at the six resolutions above in both aspect modes.
- **C-R3 (hard).** Camera zoom-out is unavailable when the resulting world scale would be below 2×. *QA:* at 1280×800 and 1280×720 the zoom-out input is a no-op.
- **C-R4 (recommendation).** Label the HUD scale setting by resulting cap height ("Numerals 21 px / 28 px / 35 px") or absolute multiplier, not a world-relative percentage.
- **C-R5 (recommendation, routed to accessibility-specialist).** Express the 7.1 floor additionally in arcminutes with a per-device-class table (desktop ≥ 60 cm, handheld ≈ 38 cm) so the Deck does not inherit a desk assumption; run the band-count check on a real Deck LCD and OLED.

## 2. Motion comfort

**Verdict: needs a rule** (the existing architecture supports HUD immunity; two conflicts and several gaps remain).

**Analysis.**
- *Smoothing and look-ahead.* 8.4 snaps transforms to the base grid (both passes — under pass B sprites must still land on base-px positions or "sprites on grid" fails). Smoothing plus rounding produces the classic 0/1 px alternation at low pan speed; the hazard is oscillation, not smoothing. Look-ahead shifts the frame on a facing change — motion not proportional to the player's own displacement, the standard vestibular trigger.
- *World shake on hull failure.* Positional, so a vestibular question, not photosensitivity. HR-13 already implies it exists (HUD excluded from camera shake) and 8.4's architecture satisfies HUD immunity **only** if the shake is applied inside the `SubViewport`. **Conflict:** 7.0 anchors interaction prompts (HUD layer) to object screen positions, so under shake they would shake with the object — violating HR-13.
- *4× catch-up.* The kernel's CD-GDD-ALIGN adoption drops lag **beyond** `LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS` (30 ticks); lag ≤ 30 ticks is still repaid at up to 4× (D.5: "repaid at 3/frame"), so a residual of up to 0.5 s of sim time replayed over ≈ 8–10 frames survives the forgiveness. With `tick_alpha` clamped at 1 the presented player position advances 3–4 ticks' worth per frame — a few base px per frame, not a tile — so the camera follow runs at 3–4× normal pan speed for those frames. The forgiveness fixes fairness; the camera still needs a speed rule, and the GDD should not describe catch-up as fully "forgiven".
- *Low-sanity drift.* 2.9 holds energy unchanged and 4.4's drift order (instruments → light → world hue) never names the camera. Nothing currently forbids the Perception Filter from touching the camera transform. A moved or drifting camera would be a lie about the player's own position with no instrument to check it against — the concept's "no lie is unfalsifiable" fails.
- *Already forbidden elsewhere, inherited here:* non-integer zoom (8.1), runtime rotation of human-built geometry (8.4), dim/blur/desaturate on the world (7.4), HUD shake/blur/CA/scale change (HR-13), reduced motion never alters the tick (kernel CR-11).

**Rules to add.**
- **C-R6 (hard).** The camera moves in whole base pixels in the frame it is attached to (see item 7); per-frame displacement is 0 or an integer, and the camera never reverses direction within 100 ms unless the player's own velocity reversed. *QA:* frame-stamp capture of a slow diagonal walk shows no 1-px back-and-forth.
- **C-R7 (hard).** The smooth follow has a **pan-speed ceiling** `CAMERA_MAX_PAN` (provisional: 1.25 × the crewmate's walk speed in base px per frame). If the follow target exceeds that ceiling for more than `N` consecutive frames (provisional 6) or the accumulated follow lag exceeds `K` base px (provisional 24, half a tile), the camera **cuts** to the target — never a fast pan. A single-frame target displacement ≥ 48 base px (teleport, body transfer, pod embark) cuts immediately. Catch-up repayment inside the forgiveness window is covered by the ceiling branch. *QA:* inject a 24-tick hitch while walking; no frame shows camera pan speed above `CAMERA_MAX_PAN`, and the capture shows at most one discontinuity.
- **C-R8 (hard).** World shake is a `Camera2D` offset inside the world `SubViewport`, amplitude ≤ 2 base px, duration bounded per event (provisional ≤ 600 ms), never a post-process offset of the composed frame and never an offset of the `SubViewportContainer`. *QA:* automated diff of the HUD layer across a hull-failure shake is empty.
- **C-R9 (hard).** HUD elements anchored to world positions (interaction prompts) compute screen position from the **unshaken** camera transform. *QA:* a prompt stays still while the world under it shakes.
- **C-R10 (hard).** The Perception Filter may not write camera position, zoom, rotation, offset or any viewport/stretch property; the camera is an anchor alongside the true light radius. *QA:* control-manifest check — the Filter's write set excludes `Camera2D` and `Viewport` properties.
- **C-R11 (hard).** Reduced motion disables look-ahead (camera centres on the player) and sets world-shake amplitude to 0. The information shake carried must land somewhere named: the gauge tremor (7.3), hull-stress hairlines (Failure & Trail), the audio Tell (HR-9) — HR-8's backbone — none of which this setting may suppress. *QA:* with reduced motion on, a hull-failure event still produces the tremor on at least one visible instrument and its audio cue within the same tick window.
- **C-R12 (hard).** Never allowed on the world camera under any state: rotation, non-integer zoom, zoom pulses, FOV punch, blur, chromatic aberration, vignette, or drift not caused by player displacement or an explicit bounded shake event. *QA:* no code path writes `rotation` or a fractional `zoom` on the camera node.
- **C-R13 (recommendation).** Expose look-ahead strength (off / short / default) and shake strength (off / half / full) as separate controls feeding the two parameters reduced motion zeroes.

## 3. Integer scale on odd window sizes

**Verdict: needs a rule.**

**Analysis.** 8.4 fixes `stretch/mode = canvas_items`, `scale_mode = integer`, `aspect = keep` for the spike; 8.10 records `expand` as a post-spike ask. Common odd sizes: 1366×768 (2× with 86×48 px bars under `keep`), 1600×900 (2× with 320×180 px bars — a quarter of the screen), 1680×1050, 3440×1440 (4× with 880 px of side bars). Under `expand` there are no bars and the viewport shows more world at the same integer scale. Comfort: bars are not disruptive on a dark game, but there is a **Principle 1 hazard** — unlit hull sits only 1–2 8-bit steps above true black (8.11 flag 1), so a true-black letterbox bar is nearly indistinguishable from unlit room and may be read as geometry. Readability is unaffected by bars (C-R1 governs the HUD). Under `expand` on ultrawide the bottom-left suit panel sits ≈ 1,700 px from the critical strip — the corner trip 7.0 avoided for the critical strip reappears for the panel.

**Rules to add.**
- **C-R14 (hard).** Settings expose: display mode (exclusive fullscreen / borderless / windowed); resolution (fullscreen); world scale (Auto = largest integer that fits, plus an explicit integer list); HUD scale (integer, floored per C-R1); reading-face scale (continuous); aspect (`keep` / `expand`) once `expand` ships; frame cap and VSync. No non-integer world scale is offered anywhere. *QA:* every control exists, persists across restart, and the world is pixel-exact (uniform N×N blocks in a screenshot) at every option.
- **C-R15 (hard).** Minimum window size is 1280×720 (2× world, 3× HUD fits). Live resize in windowed mode re-derives world and HUD scale and re-anchors the HUD without a reload. *QA:* drag-resize from 1920×1080 to 1366×768; world steps 3→2, HUD stays 3×, nothing clipped.
- **C-R16 (hard).** Letterbox bars render true black and are never part of the world `SubViewport`; the Perception Filter and world shake never touch them. *QA:* bar pixels unchanged across a shake and at sanity stage 3.
- **C-R17 (recommendation, routed to art-director).** Where bars exist, mark the viewport edge with a 1-HUD-px Graphite-lit hairline in the chart-table register so the frame edge is never mistaken for unlit hull — or ship `expand` as the default once the spike confirms it, which removes the bars and the hazard.
- **C-R18 (recommendation, routed to game-designer).** `expand` shows more lit floor on ultrawide — a real information advantage inside a lit room even though the dark is honest. Decide whether that is acceptable or whether the visible field is clamped at 16:9, with an optional "HUD width" setting clamping the HUD to a 16:9 inner frame.

## 4. Dark-by-default screens on bright rooms / monitors

**Verdict: supports** (with one rule to lock it and one flag).

**Analysis.** 8.11 flag 1 condition (i) is what saves Principle 1: web, filaments and horrors are **not drawn** unlit, so no gamma, brightness or monitor setting can reveal them — only direct light does. A full-frame gamma lift therefore cannot break "looking is spending". What it does break: the mood ladder (2.1's 0–10 % ordering compresses), and HUD contrast — a lift on the composed frame lightens Ground `#1C2128` under Paper White and erodes the 4.5 : 1 that HR-1/HR-2 meet by construction. Flag 1 (iv) already says HR-15 and the hull floor are one mechanism, so a bounded step control costs no second path. Steam Deck LCD vs OLED differ in black level by more than the 1–2-step gap, which argues for calibrating rather than guessing.

**Rules to add.**
- **C-R19 (hard).** No full-frame gamma, brightness or contrast post-process exists on the composed frame or the root viewport. The only brightness control the game exposes is the HR-15 ambient-floor step (0 to the bounded ceiling, provisional +3), implemented as the flag-1 hull material raise, so it (a) can never render web-grammar content, (b) never touches the HUD layer, (c) never exceeds the 10 % stable state. *QA:* at the maximum step, a horror and a filament outside direct light are absent from the frame buffer; HUD Ground pixel value is identical at step 0 and step max.
- **C-R20 (hard).** The pipeline guarantees the measured floor is actually output: `hdr_2d` and debanding on (8.4), and the 8.12 step 7 histogram values are the ones the HR-15 control steps from. *QA:* step 7 histogram shows unlit hull 1–2 steps above black at step 0 and exactly N additional steps at step N.
- **C-R21 (recommendation — reframes a user decision; flag to creative-director / user).** A first-boot calibration screen built on the real floor swatches (Void Steel at ring floor, Graphite at +1, +2) that sets the HR-15 step for everyone ("adjust until the right-hand mark is just visible"). This turns the low-vision option into the universal calibration and solves the bright-room case without a gamma curve; the bound is unchanged. HR-15 is currently framed as an accessibility option (user decision 6) — this changes its framing, not its limit.

## 5. Photosensitivity

**Verdict: needs a rule** — one global ceiling at the lighting modifier contract, not per effect.

**Analysis against the verified thresholds.**
| Source | Spec | Rate | Area | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Beacon sweep (2.4, 2.8) | 2–3 s period, single rotating lobe | 0.33–0.5 flashes/s at any point; saturated red so the red-flash rule applies, rate far under 3/s | large | supports |
| Warning mark (7.2) | in beacon phase, ≈ 50 % duty | ≤ 0.5/s | tiny | supports |
| Cryo lamp gutter (2.2) | 0.3–0.5 s dips, ≤ once per 10–20 s | ≤ 0.1/s | large | supports |
| Deployable flicker (3.2, 8.3) | "flickers" — **no frequency or amplitude anywhere in the bible** | undefined | radius 120 base px ≈ 45,000 base px², ≥ 7× the small-safe-area | **needs a rule — the load-bearing one** |
| Power arcing, vent bursts (2.8, 8.13) | transient point lights | undefined; arcing is the classic strobe shape | medium | needs a rule |
| Attention flicker modifier (systems-index 17) | "flicker as a Lighting modifier" | undefined | beam-sized | needs a rule |
| Sanity stage-2 light lies (2.9, 4.4) | cone over-reach, false shadows, warm drift | slow by description; the Corollary permits "a flicker" as a leak | large | needs a rule (bound the leak) |
| HUD (HR-13) | ≤ 3 Hz luminance change | — | — | supports; the positional-tremor exemption and the sweep confirmation stay with the accessibility-specialist — the rules below hold under either outcome |

Multiple sources in one region sum: two deployables plus an arc in a breach room can each be under 3/s while the region exceeds it. The enforcement point already exists — systems-index 6 gives 2D Lighting ownership of final `Light2D` values through a modifier contract that Attention flicker, horror disturbance and Filter decoys submit to.

**Rules to add.**
- **C-R22 (hard).** The lighting modifier contract clamps every light's energy/colour slew so that no light completes more than **3 flashes (opposing pairs of ≥ 10 % relative-luminance change) in any 1 s window**, and no flash pair involving Alarm Red exceeds that rate either (red-flash rule). Modulations below 10 % relative luminance (a deployable "breathing") are unlimited in rate. The clamp applies to all submitters — deployable flicker, gutter, arcing, vent bursts, Attention flicker, horror disturbance, Perception Filter decoys. *QA:* a per-light flash counter on the contract; the 2.8 breach composition (4 beams + beacon + 1 deployable + arcs + vents) runs 60 s with zero violations logged **and zero clamps engaged** — the authored effects already comply.
- **C-R23 (hard).** Regional and frame ceilings: no region of ≈ 213×120 base px (the 10° field estimate) anywhere in the viewport completes more than 3 flashes in any 1 s window from all sources combined; the composed frame's mean luminance obeys the same limit; and no full-frame flash exists under any state (extends 7.3's HUD rule to the world). *QA:* an automated luminance scan (Harding-style, from captured frames, sliding-window per region) of the breach, cryo-wake, crew-loss and stage-3 sanity scenes reports no violations.
- **C-R24 (hard).** Deployable flicker is specified: amplitude and rate inside C-R22 (provisional: ≤ 2 flashes/s, or any rate at < 10 % amplitude), authored once in the deployable light's definition. Routed to art-director / technical-artist for the number; the pipeline rule is that the definition exists and passes the clamp. *QA:* the authored curve passes the C-R22 counter standalone.
- **C-R25 (hard).** Seizure/photosensitivity notice shown at first launch and available in settings, regardless of the ceilings above. *QA:* present on a fresh profile; reachable from settings.
- **C-R26 (hard).** "Reduce flashing" is a toggle **separate** from reduced motion: deployables hold steady, arcing becomes a held glow, the beacon becomes the static mark + sound + HUD glyph of HR-8, the gutter is kept (≤ 0.1/s). It never suppresses trails or the flow backbone (HR-8). *QA:* each listed source behaves as stated with the toggle on and reduced motion off.
- **C-R27 (recommendation).** Build the C-R23 scan into the 8.12 lighting spike as step 11 so the budget shape and the flash ceilings are measured on the same captures.

## 6. Perception Filter full-screen pass

**Verdict: conflicts** — a rule is needed before the material is built.

**Analysis.** 8.10's Materials row places the "full-screen sanity filter" as a `canvas_item` shader on the `SubViewportContainer` (or `BackBufferCopy`). Two structural facts collide with it: (1) the truth-channel anchors — character sprites, hand tools, crewmate beams, trails, the true light radius (Corollary; systems-index 20's tag contract) — live **inside** the `SubViewport`, so an unmasked container shader tints them; (2) the container sits in the root viewport beside the HUD `CanvasLayer` — safe only if the HUD is drawn above and never sampled; a `BackBufferCopy` placed in the root would capture the HUD. Accessibility risks of a per-client pass: deutan players see violet as blue — already tri-modal under HR-5/HR-7, so acceptable *only if the pass cannot also remove the shape/pattern backups*; low-vision players lose contrast if the pass lowers hull below the floor or softens edges; any displacement or blur is both a lens lie (7.4) and a motion-sickness vector; HR-10 forbids global hue remaps, and a stage-3 "surfaces warm toward flesh" tint is one unless bounded to *adding* the reserved hues at the places 4.4 names.

**Rules to add.**
- **C-R28 (hard).** The Filter's screen-wide pass never samples or writes the HUD `CanvasLayer`, the inspect card, menus, text chat, pings, letterbox bars or the debug overlay; it is bound to world `SubViewport` content only. *QA:* HUD-layer pixel diff at sanity stage 0 vs stage 3 is empty.
- **C-R29 (hard).** The pass is multiplied by a **truth-channel mask** rendered with the world (sprites, tools, beams, trails, the true-radius cone edge, the Failure & Trail layer) so anchor pixels are untouched — or the screen-wide effects are decomposed into per-element materials on corruptible nodes only. *QA:* with the pass at maximum, anchor pixels are bit-identical to the pass-disabled frame.
- **C-R30 (hard).** The pass performs no displacement, warp, blur, chromatic aberration, pixelation or resolution change; it writes colour only. Geometry is an anchor — the light-radius edge may not move by one pixel. *QA:* edge-position diff of the beam cone at stage 0 vs stage 3 is zero.
- **C-R31 (hard).** The pass may only **add** violet (edges: cone rim, pipe silhouettes, gauge glass, sprite fringe) and flesh (surfaces and phantom content) per 4.4; it never shifts, desaturates or re-maps sane hues (HR-10), never reduces the luminance contrast between a pipe and its flow marks or between a trail and what it crosses (the trail-contrast number of 7.6), and never lowers hull below the HR-15/flag-1 floor. *QA:* 4.7 pairs re-measured at stage 3 keep their shape backups' contrast within 10 % of stage 0.
- **C-R32 (hard).** The pass obeys C-R22/C-R23 — the Corollary's "a flicker" leak is bounded by the same clamp. *QA:* stage-2/3 scenes pass the C-R23 scan.
- **C-R33 (recommendation).** Pattern-strength (7.4) is applied before the Filter in material order so thickened flow marks are what the Filter tints, never what it erases.

## 7. Camera-induced disorientation in a moving ship

**Verdict: needs a rule** — ship-local frame.

**Analysis.** Systems-index 12 makes the composite ship one physics body with a ship-local frame and characters moving inside a moving body. A **world-frame** camera would sweep the whole interior across the screen while the player stands still — full-field optic flow with no proprioceptive match, the textbook simulator-sickness trigger — and if the ship rotates it rotates the tilemap off-grid, which 8.4 forbids for anything human-built. A **ship-local** camera keeps the interior static on screen; the only exterior view is pod transit (2.5), where the sparse filament field at constant velocity is low-density flow and the state's energy is already "low". Snapping matters too: if the player snaps to the world grid and the floor to the ship grid, they shimmer against each other as the ship moves. Under a ship-local camera, hull shake becomes an explicit bounded effect (C-R8) rather than emergent physics jitter — better for comfort and for HR-13.

**Rules to add.**
- **C-R34 (hard).** During interior play the camera is rigidly attached to the frame of the body the player stands on; the body's world motion is never visible as interior optic flow. *QA:* with the ship under thrust and the player idle, the interior frame is pixel-static.
- **C-R35 (hard).** All pixel snapping (player, props, actors, floor) is performed in the camera's body frame, never in world space. *QA:* no relative 1-px jitter between the crewmate and the floor tile under them while the ship moves.
- **C-R36 (hard).** Transfer of the camera between bodies (detach into a new body, docking, boarding across the seam, pod embark/disembark) is a cut through C-R7's immediate branch, never a pan or blend. *QA:* frame capture of a detach event shows exactly one discontinuity and no interpolated frames.
- **C-R37 (hard).** Pod transit is the only state with exterior optic flow; in it the camera is pod-local with zero lag, flow velocity is constant (no acceleration curves on the camera), and the flow field is the sparse 2.5 filament set. Reduced motion lowers filament density or parallax speed, never the pod's own motion. *QA:* transit capture shows constant-velocity drift and a stationary pod sprite.
- **C-R38 (flag, routed to game-designer and technical-director — ties to kernel open question #3, who owns character position).** The weld-on-moving-ship spike puts two bodies with relative motion in view (home ship and derelict across the seam). The camera follows the body underfoot; the other body moves on screen. Comfort needs that relative motion bounded and, for the grid, relative orientation quantised (dock aligned at 0°/90°) — a design and physics decision, not a pipeline one.

---

## Hard requirements (summary)

| ID | Rule | Item |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C-R1 | HUD multiplier `H_default = max(W, 3)`; never below 3× on any display; integer steps to 2× default | 1 |
| C-R2 | HUD authored anchor-relative to visible viewport, 5 % safe margin, survives fractional canvas and both aspects | 1 |
| C-R3 | No zoom-out below a 2× world | 1 |
| C-R6 | Camera moves in whole base px in its body frame; no oscillation | 2 |
| C-R7 | Pan-speed ceiling on the follow; sustained excess or accumulated lag → cut; ≥ 48 px single-frame → immediate cut (covers catch-up residual) | 2 |
| C-R8 | Shake is a `Camera2D` offset inside the `SubViewport`, ≤ 2 base px, bounded duration | 2 |
| C-R9 | World-anchored HUD prompts use the unshaken camera transform | 2 |
| C-R10 | Perception Filter never writes camera or viewport properties | 2 |
| C-R11 | Reduced motion kills look-ahead and shake; tremor, hairlines, audio carry the information | 2 |
| C-R12 | Never on the world camera: rotation, non-integer zoom, zoom pulse, FOV punch, blur, CA, vignette, uncaused drift | 2 |
| C-R14 | Settings: display mode, resolution, integer world scale, HUD scale, reading scale, aspect, frame cap; no non-integer option | 3 |
| C-R15 | Minimum window 1280×720; live resize re-derives scale and re-anchors | 3 |
| C-R16 | Bars are true black, outside the world, untouched by Filter and shake | 3 |
| C-R19 | No full-frame gamma/brightness; the only brightness control is the bounded HR-15 step on the hull material | 4 |
| C-R20 | Floor output guaranteed (hdr_2d, debanding); HR-15 steps from the step-7 measurement | 4 |
| C-R22 | Lighting modifier contract clamps every light to ≤ 3 flashes (opposing pairs ≥ 10 %) per 1 s, red included | 5 |
| C-R23 | Regional (≈ 213×120 base px) and frame-mean ≤ 3 flashes/s; no full-frame flash; automated scan on four worst scenes | 5 |
| C-R24 | Deployable flicker is specified and passes the clamp | 5 |
| C-R25 | Photosensitivity notice at first launch and in settings | 5 |
| C-R26 | "Reduce flashing" toggle separate from reduced motion; backbone preserved | 5 |
| C-R28 | Filter pass never touches HUD, card, menus, chat, pings, bars, debug overlay | 6 |
| C-R29 | Filter pass masked by a truth-channel mask (or per-element materials) | 6 |
| C-R30 | Filter pass writes colour only — no displacement, blur, CA, pixelation, resolution change | 6 |
| C-R31 | Filter pass only adds violet/flesh at 4.4's places; never remaps/desaturates sane hues or erodes shape/trail contrast; never below the floor | 6 |
| C-R32 | Filter pass obeys C-R22/23 | 6 |
| C-R34 | Interior camera rigid in the body frame | 7 |
| C-R35 | Snapping in the body frame | 7 |
| C-R36 | Body-to-body camera transfer is a cut | 7 |
| C-R37 | Pod transit is the only exterior optic flow; pod-local, constant velocity | 7 |

## Recommendations (summary)

| ID | Recommendation | Routed to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C-R4 | Label HUD scale by cap height or absolute multiplier, not world-relative % | ux (settings spec) |
| C-R5 | Arcminute floor table per device class; on-device Deck band check | accessibility-specialist |
| C-R13 | Separate look-ahead and shake strength controls | ux / settings |
| C-R17 | Viewport-edge hairline when letterboxed, or ship `expand` by default post-spike | art-director |
| C-R18 | Decide whether `expand`'s extra lit floor is acceptable; optional 16:9 HUD clamp | game-designer |
| C-R21 | First-boot floor calibration screen setting the HR-15 step for all players (reframes user decision 6; bound unchanged) | creative-director / user |
| C-R27 | Add the flash scan as 8.12 step 11 | technical-artist |
| C-R33 | Pattern-strength applied before the Filter in material order | technical-artist |

## Conflicts surfaced for the orchestrator (not resolved here)

1. 7.0's critical-strip 12 % × 5 % cap is exceeded **by default** on Steam Deck under the 3× HUD C-R1 requires (art-director).
2. 7.0's world-anchored prompts vs HR-13 under world shake — resolved by C-R9 if adopted.
3. 8.10's full-screen sanity filter on the `SubViewportContainer` vs the Corollary's in-world anchors — resolved by C-R29 if adopted; otherwise the Materials row needs rewording.
4. HR-15 framed as a low-vision option vs C-R21's universal calibration (user decision).
5. The kernel's forgiveness leaves a ≤ 0.5 s, 3–4× residual the camera must absorb (C-R7); the GDD should not describe catch-up as fully "forgiven".
6. Deployable "flicker" has no frequency anywhere in the bible and is the single largest flashing surface in the game (art-director / technical-artist to set, inside C-R22).

Provisional numbers (C-R7's `CAMERA_MAX_PAN`, N, K; C-R8's 600 ms; C-R24's 2 flashes/s) are starting points for the tuning-knobs section, not measured values.

Sources:
- [Understanding SC 2.3.1: Three Flashes or Below Threshold (WCAG 2.1)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/three-flashes-or-below-threshold.html)
- [G176: Keeping the flashing area small enough](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Techniques/general/G176)
- [WCAG 2.1 (definitions of general and red flash threshold)](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG21/)
- [ISO 9241-303:2011 preview (table of contents only)](https://webstore.ansi.org/preview-pages/ISO/preview_ISO+9241-303-2011.pdf)

  ## 1. Readability at 2× (Steam Deck 1280×800 / 720p)
  
  **Verdict: needs a rule.**
  
  **Analysis.** 7.1 makes the *screen-pixel* floor the contract (21 / 15 px cap height) and the art-px column a derivation; the table has 1080p and 1440p rows only. At a 2× world the 7 / 5 art-px faces render at **14 / 10 screen px** — 67 % of the floor — and the derivation for a 2× HUD (10.5 / 7.5 art px) is not an integer, so no bitmap face at "100 %" can meet it. Angular check on the Deck (7-inch, ≈ 216 PPI, held ≈ 38 cm): 14 px cap ≈ 15 arcmin, 10 px ≈ 11 arcmin — the label floor falls below the commonly cited 16 arcmin minimum. At a **3× HUD** the same screen gives 21 / 15 px ≈ 22 / 16 arcmin, meeting the floor exactly. 8.1 already states the HUD's integer steps are independent of camera zoom; the rule is to make them independent of the *world scale* too.
  
  **Bands.** 8.2 sized the 2 px bands and 1 px separators to survive the single integer zoom-out step from a 3× world (sprites at 67 %). At a 2× world the only step out is 1×: separators become 1 screen px (≈ 1 arcmin on the Deck), below the acuity needed to count four bands. Whether bands read at the *default* 2× on a 7-inch screen (4 px band, 2 px separator ≈ 2 arcmin) is an on-device check for the accessibility-specialist, not a desk verdict. Identity is redundant by design — beam shape (3.2) and the crew-strip glyph (7.5) carry it — so a band failure degrades, it does not break.
  
  **Conflicts to surface, not swallow.**
  - 7.0 caps the critical strip at 12 % × 5 % of frame "at 100 % UI scale" and calls exceeding it "the player's explicit accessibility trade". On a 1280×800 screen with the 3× HUD the plate (230×54 px) is ≈ 18 % × 6.8 % **by default**, not by choice. Routed to art-director: re-express the cap relative to a 1080p reference frame, or accept the Deck overage as a platform default.
  - HR-12 labels HUD scale "100–200 %" relative to the world scale, so "100 %" is 3× at 1080p and 2× on the Deck — different physical sizes under the same label.
  
  **Rules to add.**
  - **C-R1 (hard).** HUD integer multiplier `H` is chosen independently of world scale `W`: `H_default = max(W, 3)` — never below 3 on any display — and the player may raise it in integer steps up to `2 × H_default`. *QA:* at 1280×800, 1280×720, 1366×768, 1920×1080, 2560×1440, 3840×2160 the critical-strip numeral cap height is ≥ 21 screen px and the smallest label ≥ 15 at the default HUD scale.
  - **C-R2 (hard).** The HUD layout is authored anchor-relative to the visible viewport edges with the 5 % safe margin measured in HUD pixels, never against an assumed 640×360 HUD canvas; it must survive a fractional logical canvas (1280×800 ÷ 3 = 426.7×266.7) and both `keep` and `expand` aspects. *QA:* no HUD element clipped or overlapping at the six resolutions above in both aspect modes.
  - **C-R3 (hard).** Camera zoom-out is unavailable when the resulting world scale would be below 2×. *QA:* at 1280×800 and 1280×720 the zoom-out input is a no-op.
  - **C-R4 (recommendation).** Label the HUD scale setting by resulting cap height ("Numerals 21 px / 28 px / 35 px") or absolute multiplier, not a world-relative percentage.
  - **C-R5 (recommendation, routed to accessibility-specialist).** Express the 7.1 floor additionally in arcminutes with a per-device-class table (desktop ≥ 60 cm, handheld ≈ 38 cm) so the Deck does not inherit a desk assumption; run the band-count check on a real Deck LCD and OLED.
  
  ## 2. Motion comfort
  
  **Verdict: needs a rule** (the existing architecture supports HUD immunity; two conflicts and several gaps remain).
  
  **Analysis.**
  - *Smoothing and look-ahead.* 8.4 snaps transforms to the base grid (both passes — under pass B sprites must still land on base-px positions or "sprites on grid" fails). Smoothing plus rounding produces the classic 0/1 px alternation at low pan speed; the hazard is oscillation, not smoothing. Look-ahead shifts the frame on a facing change — motion not proportional to the player's own displacement, the standard vestibular trigger.
  - *World shake on hull failure.* Positional, so a vestibular question, not photosensitivity. HR-13 already implies it exists (HUD excluded from camera shake) and 8.4's architecture satisfies HUD immunity **only** if the shake is applied inside the `SubViewport`. **Conflict:** 7.0 anchors interaction prompts (HUD layer) to object screen positions, so under shake they would shake with the object — violating HR-13.
  - *4× catch-up.* The kernel's CD-GDD-ALIGN adoption drops lag **beyond** `LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS` (30 ticks); lag ≤ 30 ticks is still repaid at up to 4× (D.5: "repaid at 3/frame"), so a residual of up to 0.5 s of sim time replayed over ≈ 8–10 frames survives the forgiveness. With `tick_alpha` clamped at 1 the presented player position advances 3–4 ticks' worth per frame — a few base px per frame, not a tile — so the camera follow runs at 3–4× normal pan speed for those frames. The forgiveness fixes fairness; the camera still needs a speed rule, and the GDD should not describe catch-up as fully "forgiven".
  - *Low-sanity drift.* 2.9 holds energy unchanged and 4.4's drift order (instruments → light → world hue) never names the camera. Nothing currently forbids the Perception Filter from touching the camera transform. A moved or drifting camera would be a lie about the player's own position with no instrument to check it against — the concept's "no lie is unfalsifiable" fails.
  - *Already forbidden elsewhere, inherited here:* non-integer zoom (8.1), runtime rotation of human-built geometry (8.4), dim/blur/desaturate on the world (7.4), HUD shake/blur/CA/scale change (HR-13), reduced motion never alters the tick (kernel CR-11).
  
  **Rules to add.**
  - **C-R6 (hard).** The camera moves in whole base pixels in the frame it is attached to (see item 7); per-frame displacement is 0 or an integer, and the camera never reverses direction within 100 ms unless the player's own velocity reversed. *QA:* frame-stamp capture of a slow diagonal walk shows no 1-px back-and-forth.
  - **C-R7 (hard).** The smooth follow has a **pan-speed ceiling** `CAMERA_MAX_PAN` (provisional: 1.25 × the crewmate's walk speed in base px per frame). If the follow target exceeds that ceiling for more than `N` consecutive frames (provisional 6) or the accumulated follow lag exceeds `K` base px (provisional 24, half a tile), the camera **cuts** to the target — never a fast pan. A single-frame target displacement ≥ 48 base px (teleport, body transfer, pod embark) cuts immediately.   - **C-R8 (hard).** World shake is a `Camera2D` offset inside the world `SubViewport`, amplitude ≤ 2 base px, duration bounded per event (provisional ≤ 600 ms), never a post-process offset of the composed frame and never an offset of the `SubViewportContainer`. *QA:* automated diff of the HUD layer across a hull-failure shake is empty.
  - **C-R9 (hard).** HUD elements anchored to world positions (interaction prompts) compute screen position from the **unshaken** camera transform. *QA:* a prompt stays still while the world under it shakes.
  - **C-R10 (hard).** The Perception Filter may not write camera position, zoom, rotation, offset or any viewport/stretch property; the camera is an anchor alongside the true light radius. *QA:* control-manifest check — the Filter's write set excludes `Camera2D` and `Viewport` properties.
  - **C-R11 (hard).** Reduced motion disables look-ahead (camera centres on the player) and sets world-shake amplitude to 0.   ## 4. Dark-by-default screens on bright rooms / monitors
  
  **Verdict: supports** (with one rule to lock it and one flag).
  
  **Analysis.** 8.11 flag 1 condition (i) is what saves Principle 1: web, filaments and horrors are **not drawn** unlit, so no gamma, brightness or monitor setting can reveal them — only direct light does. A full-frame gamma lift therefore cannot break "looking is spending". What it does break: the mood ladder (2.1's 0–10 % ordering compresses), and HUD contrast — a lift on the composed frame lightens Ground `#1C2128` under Paper White and erodes the 4.5 : 1 that HR-1/HR-2 meet by construction. Flag 1 (iv) already says HR-15 and the hull floor are one mechanism, so a bounded step control costs no second path. Steam Deck LCD vs OLED differ in black level by more than the 1–2-step gap, which argues for calibrating rather than guessing.
  
  **Rules to add.**
  - **C-R19 (hard).** No full-frame gamma, brightness or contrast post-process exists on the composed frame or the root viewport. The only brightness control the game exposes is the HR-15 ambient-floor step (0 to the bounded ceiling, provisional +3), implemented as the flag-1 hull material raise, so it (a) can never render web-grammar content, (b) never touches the HUD layer, (c) never exceeds the 10 % stable state. *QA:* at the maximum step, a horror and a filament outside direct light are absent from the frame buffer; HUD Ground pixel value is identical at step 0 and step max.
  - **C-R20 (hard).** The pipeline guarantees the measured floor is actually output: `hdr_2d` and debanding on (8.4), and the 8.12 step 7 histogram values are the ones the HR-15 control steps from. *QA:* step 7 histogram shows unlit hull 1–2 steps above black at step 0 and exactly N additional steps at step N.
  - **C-R21 (recommendation — reframes a user decision; flag to creative-director / user).** A first-boot calibration screen built on the real floor swatches (Void Steel at ring floor, Graphite at +1, +2) that sets the HR-15 step for everyone ("adjust until the right-hand mark is just visible"). This turns the low-vision option into the universal calibration and solves the bright-room case without a gamma curve; the bound is unchanged. HR-15 is currently framed as an accessibility option (user decision 6) — this changes its framing, not its limit.

  ## 6. Perception Filter full-screen pass
  
  **Verdict: conflicts** — a rule is needed before the material is built.
  
  **Analysis.** 8.10's Materials row places the "full-screen sanity filter" as a `canvas_item` shader on the `SubViewportContainer` (or `BackBufferCopy`). Two structural facts collide with it: (1) the truth-channel anchors — character sprites, hand tools, crewmate beams, trails, the true light radius (Corollary; systems-index 20's tag contract) — live **inside** the `SubViewport`, so an unmasked container shader tints them; (2) the container sits in the root viewport beside the HUD `CanvasLayer` — safe only if the HUD is drawn above and never sampled; a `BackBufferCopy` placed in the root would capture the HUD. Accessibility risks of a per-client pass: deutan players see violet as blue — already tri-modal under HR-5/HR-7, so acceptable *only if the pass cannot also remove the shape/pattern backups*; low-vision players lose contrast if the pass lowers hull below the floor or softens edges; any displacement or blur is both a lens lie (7.4) and a motion-sickness vector; HR-10 forbids global hue remaps, and a stage-3 "surfaces warm toward flesh" tint is one unless bounded to *adding* the reserved hues at the places 4.4 names.
  
  **Rules to add.**
  - **C-R28 (hard).** The Filter's screen-wide pass never samples or writes the HUD `CanvasLayer`, the inspect card, menus, text chat, pings, letterbox bars or the debug overlay; it is bound to world `SubViewport` content only. *QA:* HUD-layer pixel diff at sanity stage 0 vs stage 3 is empty.
  - **C-R29 (hard).** The pass is multiplied by a **truth-channel mask** rendered with the world (sprites, tools, beams, trails, the true-radius cone edge, the Failure & Trail layer) so anchor pixels are untouched — or the screen-wide effects are decomposed into per-element materials on corruptible nodes only. *QA:* with the pass at maximum, anchor pixels are bit-identical to the pass-disabled frame.
  - **C-R30 (hard).** The pass performs no displacement, warp, blur, chromatic aberration, pixelation or resolution change; it writes colour only. Geometry is an anchor — the light-radius edge may not move by one pixel. *QA:* edge-position diff of the beam cone at stage 0 vs stage 3 is zero.
  - **C-R31 (hard).** The pass may only **add** violet (edges: cone rim, pipe silhouettes, gauge glass, sprite fringe) and flesh (surfaces and phantom content) per 4.4; it never shifts, desaturates or re-maps sane hues (HR-10), never reduces the luminance contrast between a pipe and its flow marks or between a trail and what it crosses (the trail-contrast number of 7.6), and never lowers hull below the HR-15/flag-1 floor. *QA:* 4.7 pairs re-measured at stage 3 keep their shape backups' contrast within 10 % of stage 0.
  - **C-R32 (hard).** The pass obeys C-R22/C-R23 — the Corollary's "a flicker" leak is bounded by the same clamp. *QA:* stage-2/3 scenes pass the C-R23 scan.
  - **C-R33 (recommendation).** Pattern-strength (7.4) is applied before the Filter in material order so thickened flow marks are what the Filter tints, never what it erases.
  
  ## 7. Camera-induced disorientation in a moving ship
  
  **Verdict: needs a rule** — ship-local frame.
  
  **Analysis.** Systems-index 12 makes the composite ship one physics body with a ship-local frame and characters moving inside a moving body. A **world-frame** camera would sweep the whole interior across the screen while the player stands still — full-field optic flow with no proprioceptive match, the textbook simulator-sickness trigger — and if the ship rotates it rotates the tilemap off-grid, which 8.4 forbids for anything human-built. A **ship-local** camera keeps the interior static on screen; the only exterior view is pod transit (2.5), where the sparse filament field at constant velocity is low-density flow and the state's energy is already "low". Snapping matters too: if the player snaps to the world grid and the floor to the ship grid, they shimmer against each other as the ship moves. Under a ship-local camera, hull shake becomes an explicit bounded effect (C-R8) rather than emergent physics jitter — better for comfort and for HR-13.
  
  **Rules to add.**
  - **C-R34 (hard).** During interior play the camera is rigidly attached to the frame of the body the player stands on; the body's world motion is never visible as interior optic flow. *QA:* with the ship under thrust and the player idle, the interior frame is pixel-static.
  - **C-R35 (hard).** All pixel snapping (player, props, actors, floor) is performed in the camera's body frame, never in world space. *QA:* no relative 1-px jitter between the crewmate and the floor tile under them while the ship moves.
  - **C-R36 (hard).** Transfer of the camera between bodies (detach into a new body, docking, boarding across the seam, pod embark/disembark) is a cut through C-R7's immediate branch, never a pan or blend. *QA:* frame capture of a detach event shows exactly one discontinuity and no interpolated frames.
  - **C-R37 (hard).** Pod transit is the only state with exterior optic flow; in it the camera is pod-local with zero lag, flow velocity is constant (no acceleration curves on the camera), and the flow field is the sparse 2.5 filament set. Reduced motion lowers filament density or parallax speed, never the pod's own motion. *QA:* transit capture shows constant-velocity drift and a stationary pod sprite.
  - **C-R38 (flag, routed to game-designer and technical-director — ties to kernel open question #3, who owns character position).** The weld-on-moving-ship spike puts two bodies with relative motion in view (home ship and derelict across the seam). The camera follows the body underfoot; the other body moves on screen. Comfort needs that relative motion bounded and, for the grid, relative orientation quantised (dock aligned at 0°/90°) — a design and physics decision, not a pipeline one.

  ## 2. Pixel integrity
  
  **Facts `[BIN]`.** `rendering/2d/snap/snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel = false`, `snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel = false`; both exist as `Viewport` members and as `RenderingServer.viewport_set_snap_2d_*` per viewport. `rendering/textures/canvas_textures/default_texture_filter = 1` (LINEAR); `Viewport.canvas_item_default_texture_filter = 1`; `CanvasItem.texture_filter = 0` (`PARENT_NODE`); `CanvasItem.TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST = 1`; `Viewport.gui_snap_controls_to_pixels = true`. `Sprite2D.centered = true`, `offset`. `physics/common/physics_interpolation = false`; `Node.physics_interpolation_mode` {INHERIT, ON, OFF}, `reset_physics_interpolation()`; `SceneTree.physics_interpolation`; `Engine.get_physics_interpolation_fraction()`; `RenderingServer.canvas_item_set_interpolated / canvas_item_transform_physics_interpolation / canvas_item_reset_physics_interpolation`, and the same three for `canvas_light_*` and `canvas_light_occluder_*`. **`get_global_transform_interpolated()` exists on `Node3D` only — not on `Node2D` or `CanvasItem`.**
  
  So the art bible's "2D physics interpolation NOT SOURCEABLE on 4.7" is upgraded: the 2D machinery **exists** in 4.7.2 `[BIN]` (items, lights, occluders). Its behaviour remains NOT SOURCEABLE.
  
  **Constraints and recommendations.**
  
  1. **One interpolator.** The kernel already mandates `tick_alpha` with prev/curr read views (CR-10, D.3) and clamps at 1 (no extrapolation — Pillar 1). Engine `physics_interpolation` and `Camera2D.position_smoothing` are each a *second* interpolator on a clock the kernel does not control. Recommend `physics/common/physics_interpolation = false`, every presentation node with `physics_interpolation_mode = OFF`, and sim-driven motion interpolated only from `tick_alpha`. Decisive `[BIN]` reason: no 2D `get_global_transform_interpolated()`, so a camera (or any script) cannot read where an engine-interpolated body is actually drawn — it would follow the un-interpolated pose and jitter against the sprite. **→ ADR (interpolation clock)**.
  2. **Snap is a floor, not a filter.** Interpolation then snapping can only change the *timing* of one-base-pixel steps, never their size: a body moving 1 base px/tick shows a 3×3 screen block step at 1080p whenever it moves. The GDD must promise "base-pixel steps at interpolated timing", not sub-pixel smoothness. Presentation computes `pos = floor(lerp(prev, curr, tick_alpha))` in base px itself (deterministic, unit-testable, headless), and the viewport snap flags are belt-and-braces. Spike: with both on, check for double-rounding (1-px flicker at .5 boundaries) `[UNV-4.3]`.
  3. **What snap snaps to under pass B is NOT SOURCEABLE** — base px (every N render px) or render px. If render px, pass B puts sprites off-grid relative to the viewport unless presentation floors to base px first — forbidden for human-built art (8.4). Rule 2 makes this moot for sim-driven motion; the spike still has to confirm for `Camera2D` and for tile layers.
  4. **Camera sub-pixel.** The camera's base-px position is floored by the same rule before being written; `Camera2D.limit_*` are `int` `[BIN]` so limits are already integer base px. Whether the engine's `snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel` also snaps the canvas transform the camera produces is NOT SOURCEABLE — flooring the camera manually removes the dependence.
  5. **Half-pixel origins.** `Sprite2D.centered = true` by default `[BIN]`: a texture with an odd dimension centred puts its origin on a .5 → a 1-px wobble under NEAREST (blur under LINEAR). 8.2's cells are even (80×80, 48×48, 96×96) and the foot-centre origin is set via `offset`, so this is satisfied by asset standard; the GDD should state the rule (even cells, or `centered = false` + integer `offset`) so VFX and one-off sprites do not break it.
  6. **Rotated sprites under nearest.** No antialiasing; edges staircase and texels drop/duplicate along the edge. Pass A: a rotated segment resolves on the base grid like everything else. Pass B: angled N×N blocks. Policy is settled in 8.4 (human-built never rotates at runtime; horrors/web quantised to 15°, 12 fps). Section C records it as a testable rule: `rotation == 0` on every node under the environment/pipe/prop/actor groups (lint), 15° quantisation on horror rigs (test). `snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel`'s effect on a rotated quad's corners is NOT SOURCEABLE — 8.12 step 2 judges the rotating segment.
  7. HUD: `gui_snap_controls_to_pixels = true` `[BIN]` on the root; the HUD's integer scale comes from the root stretch (item 1), and `Control.scale` stays `(1,1)`.
  
  **Spike must verify:** proposed **8.12 step 12 "motion integrity"** — a test body moving 1 base px/tick and another moving 0.4 base px/tick (sub-pixel speed), captured at 30, 60, 144 fps: no frame shows a backward step, a doubled step, or a fractional offset; `physics_interpolation` ON vs OFF, measuring camera-vs-sprite jitter in render px; both snap flags on vs off; pass A vs B snap target.

  ## 3. Y-sort and draw calls
  
  **Facts `[BIN]`.** `CanvasItem.y_sort_enabled = false`, `z_index = 0`, `z_as_relative = true`; `RenderingServer.CANVAS_ITEM_Z_MIN/MAX = ±4096`; `TileMapLayer` inherits `Node2D` (so it has `y_sort_enabled`), `rendering_quadrant_size = 16`, `physics_quadrant_size = 16`, `y_sort_origin = 0`, `x_draw_order_reversed = false`; `TileSet.tile_size` default 16×16. `Light2D.range_z_min/max = -1024/1024`, `range_layer_min/max = 0/0`, `range_item_cull_mask = 1`, `shadow_item_cull_mask = 1`; `RenderingServer.MAX_2D_DIRECTIONAL_LIGHTS = 8`. `CanvasLayer.layer = 1`, `follow_viewport_enabled = false`, `custom_viewport`. Measurement: `RenderingServer.get_rendering_info(RENDERING_INFO_TOTAL_DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME = 2)` (whole frame) and `Viewport.get_render_info(RENDER_INFO_TYPE_CANVAS = 2, RENDER_INFO_DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME = 2)` (per viewport — so the world `SubViewport` and the root HUD can be counted separately).
  
  **Cite, don't re-derive:** the draw-call shape is art bible **8.6** (floor `TileMapLayer` ≈ 4; one Y-sorted `Node2D` holding wall-face layer + props + actors + rigs = 50–300 and the single multiplier; wall caps ≈ 4; pipes + emissive 10–40; lights 0 draws, shadows extra; fringe/hallucination ≤ 10; ≤ 12 live `GPUParticles2D`; HUD 20–60) against the 1000 budget; "Y-sort breaks quadrant batching" is `[UNV-4.3]` and the 50–300 number is NOT SOURCEABLE until 8.12 step 5. Art consequences already adopted: floors never Y-sort; wall caps on their own layer above actors; the fallback for a sorted layer over ~300 is per-row `z_index` bands on wall faces, never fewer props.
  
  **Constraints Section C adds.**
  
  1. **Layer stack is a contract.** Record the z/Y-sort stack as named layers with their mechanism, e.g. floor layer (no sort, z 0) → trails/stains (z +1) → one Y-sorted `Node2D` (z +10; wall faces, props, actors, horrors sorted by `y_sort_origin`/foot) → wall caps (z +20) → pipes/emissive (z +30) → fringe/hallucination (per-item material) — exact numbers are the implementation's **→ ADR**. The `z_index` band fallback must stay inside every `Light2D`'s `range_z_min/max` (default ±1024 `[BIN]`) or lights stop affecting banded items; bands therefore stay well under 1024 (behaviour `[UNV-4.3]`, numbers `[BIN]`).
  2. **HUD is in a different viewport, not just a different layer.** `CanvasLayer` on the root (8.11 flag 3) is outside the world `SubViewport`, so world lights, glow, `CanvasModulate`, the sanity filter on the container and the camera transform cannot reach it by construction. The GDD can promise HR-1/HR-6/HR-13 structurally. Trade-off: anything that *must* mix (a diegetic HUD element lit by the world) cannot live there — it goes in the world.
  3. **Y-sort origin.** `y_sort_origin` on `TileMapLayer` and a child's position are the sort key `[UNV-4.3]`; 8.2's projection (wall footprint 24 px deep, face hanging 72 px below the cap) means wall faces sort by the *footprint's* south edge, so the wall-face layer's `y_sort_origin` is set to the footprint depth, not 0. Test in step 5: a crewmate standing just south of a wall is drawn over its face; just north, behind it.
  4. **Lights and masks.** `range_item_cull_mask`/`shadow_item_cull_mask` default to layer 1 `[BIN]` and `CanvasItem.light_mask = 1` `[BIN]`: if the item is lit when the two masks share a bit `[UNV-4.3]`, the unshaded emissive overlay and fringe sprites go on a light-mask bit the beams do not light (6.2 "unshaded"); the HUD needs none because it is in another viewport. 8.12 step 4 checks the mask behaviour.
  5. **Budget measurement is per viewport.** Record draw calls as world + HUD separately with `Viewport.get_render_info` so the HUD's 20–60 is never confused with the sorted layer's number.

  ## 4. Camera
  
  **Facts `[BIN]` — exhaustive `Camera2D` member list:** `anchor_mode = 1` (DRAG_CENTER), `custom_viewport`, `drag_bottom/left/right/top_margin = 0.2`, `drag_horizontal/vertical_enabled = false`, `drag_horizontal/vertical_offset = 0.0`, `editor_draw_drag_margin/limits/screen`, `enabled = true`, `ignore_rotation = true`, `limit_bottom/left/right/top: int = ±10 000 000`, `limit_enabled = true`, `limit_smoothed = false`, `offset`, `position_smoothing_enabled = false`, `position_smoothing_speed = 5.0`, `process_callback = 1` (IDLE), `rotation_smoothing_enabled/speed`, `zoom: Vector2 = (1,1)`. Methods: `align()`, `force_update_scroll()`, `get_screen_center_position()`, `get_target_position()`, `reset_smoothing()`. **There is no pixel-snap member — confirmed by the exhaustive list**, so snapping is the viewport's flags plus presentation flooring (item 2).
  
  **Constraints and recommendations.**
  
  1. **Zoom is N, not `Camera2D.zoom`.** 8.1's zoom-out step ("at 1080p the single step out is 2×, sprites at 67 %") is a change of the world's integer scale factor N (3→2) with more base pixels in view (960×540), not a camera zoom: `Camera2D.zoom = (2/3, 2/3)` would be fractional and `(0.5, 0.5)` would drop every other texel under nearest. Rule: **`Camera2D.zoom` stays `(1,1)` always**; zoom-out is implemented as the world `SubViewport` showing `(W/N', H/N')` base px for the smaller integer N' (pass A: `size`; pass B: `size_2d_override`) **while the HUD stays at N** (8.1: "the frame grows, the world does not"). That is two integer scales in one window — **the same wiring question as pass B** (item 1 constraint 4): under one root `integer` stretch the container would draw a 960×540 texture into a 640×360 base rect, a fractional container scale that is only integer in render px if the engine composes the chain before sampling (NOT SOURCEABLE). Zoom-out therefore shares pass B's candidate wirings (i)/(ii) and is folded into proposed step 11. The brief's "zoom as integer Vector2" should be reframed: integer `zoom` values ≥ 1 zoom *in* — the direction of this convention flipped between Godot 3 and 4 and is `[UNV-4.3]`, checked in step 11 — and are not what 8.1 asks for. Game-designer flag already in 8.12 ("integer zoom steps only"). **→ ADR**.
  2. **Camera is a top-level presentation node, never a child of the body.** `process_callback` default IDLE `[BIN]` means the camera updates in `_process`; a camera parented to a `CharacterBody2D` inherits the body's transform on the engine's clock, not the kernel's (and its rotation unless `ignore_rotation`, default true `[BIN]`), and no 2D API exposes an interpolated global transform (`get_global_transform_interpolated()` is `Node3D`-only `[BIN]`). The camera script reads the Body read view (prev/curr) and `tick_alpha`, composes **ship(α) × local(α)** exactly as the actor's presentation node does, floors to base px, writes `global_position`. If the two compose differently the camera lags the sprite by up to a tick. `Node.process_priority` `[BIN]` orders the camera after the actor presentation within `_process` (behaviour `[UNV-4.3]`, step 12).
  3. **`position_smoothing_enabled` stays false** — second interpolator (item 2). If designers want lag/ease, it is applied to the *target* in base px by the presentation script and floored afterward, so the camera still lands on whole base px every frame. `limit_smoothed` likewise false.
  4. **Limits** are `int` base px `[BIN]`; with the world in ship-local coordinates the limits are the loaded section's bounding rect and are set by a `PROJECTOR` when sections weld/detach (kernel CR-10 class), never by the camera itself.
  5. **`drag_*` margins** (default 0.2, disabled `[BIN]`): usable, but the drag window is in viewport fractions, so the resulting camera position is fractional and must be floored (rule 2 above); with `anchor_mode = DRAG_CENTER` and a 640×360 view the margins are 128×72 base px. The frame is tight (13.3 × 7.5 tiles, 8.2); recommend starting with drag off and a hard follow, adding margins only if the spike shows readable framing.
  6. **Transform hierarchy and the moving ship.** If the ship's world-space transform rotates, every human-built interior sprite rotates off-grid under nearest sampling — forbidden by 8.4. Two consistent resolutions, neither Section C's to pick: (a) **render in the ship-local frame** — the world `SubViewport`'s canvas *is* the ship frame, the ship's motion appears only on the exterior/background layer (`Parallax2D` / `ParallaxBackground` exist `[BIN]`), the interior never rotates; (b) `ignore_rotation = false` so the camera rotates with the ship and the interior stays axis-aligned in screen space while the exterior rotates. (a) is cheaper and avoids the question of what snapping does to a rotated canvas transform (NOT SOURCEABLE). Dependency question for the Ship Body GDD (kernel C.3 #6, Open Question 3). **→ ADR**.
  
  **Spike must verify (proposed 8.12 step 12):** camera following a body on a translating ship section at 144 fps — zero render-px disagreement between camera and sprite each frame; `get_screen_center_position()` is integer base px; limits clamp without fractional residue; `drag` margins + floor produce no 1-px oscillation at rest.

  ## 6. Frame pacing
  
  **Facts `[BIN]`.** `physics/common/physics_ticks_per_second = 60`, `max_physics_steps_per_frame = 8`, `physics_jitter_fix = 0.5`, `physics/common/physics_interpolation = false`; `application/run/max_fps = 0`, `delta_smoothing = true`, `low_processor_mode = false`; `display/window/vsync/vsync_mode = 1` (ENABLED) with `DisplayServer.VSYNC_{DISABLED=0, ENABLED=1, ADAPTIVE=2, MAILBOX=3}`, `window_set_vsync_mode`, `screen_get_refresh_rate`; `rendering/rendering_device/vsync/frame_queue_size = 2`, `swapchain_image_count = 3`; `Engine.get_physics_interpolation_fraction()`, `is_in_physics_frame()`, `get_physics_frames()`, `get_process_frames()`, `get_frames_per_second()`; `SceneTree.physics_frame` / `process_frame` signals; `Node.process_priority`, `process_physics_priority`.
  
  `_process`/`_physics_process` ordering within a frame is **silent in REF** (kernel D.4 says so and makes the "same-frame" best case spike-conditional).
  
  **Constraints and recommendations.**
  
  1. **The sim is fps-independent by construction and the GDD says so as a test**: identical `state_hash` after a scripted 10-s input replay at `max_fps` 30, 60, 144 and 0 (kernel G3 determinism + CR-11). Presentation reads last-committed state at render rate and never causes a tick.
  2. **Who drives the tick is an ADR the pacing promises depend on.** Kernel D.4 assumes the tick is driven by the physics callback (60 Hz; `max_physics_steps_per_frame = 8` `[BIN]` — if it caps catch-up at 8 ticks/frame `[UNV-4.3]`, the engine stops catching up below 7.5 fps; step 13 checks); kernel D.5 defines a kernel-side accumulator with its own `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME`. Two accumulators drift; one must be the clock. If the physics callback drives, `physics_jitter_fix` (default **0.5**, non-zero `[BIN]`) alters per-step timing in a way NOT SOURCEABLE here — recommend **0** pending the spike, since a fixed-tick kernel that forbids wall-clock reads (H9) should not receive engine-smoothed steps. `delta_smoothing = true` `[BIN]` affects `_process` delta only `[UNV-4.3]`; harmless to presentation, irrelevant to the sim. **→ ADR (tick driver)**.
  3. **Promise at 30 fps render:** two ticks per frame, sim unchanged; `tick_alpha` clamps at 1 so nothing extrapolates; input-to-pixel worst case 50 ms (kernel D.4); motion shows every second tick's pose — 2-base-px steps for a 1 px/tick body, which is honest, not smoothed.
  4. **Promise at 144 fps render:** ticks occur on ~42 % of frames; without interpolation 58 % of frames would repeat a pose (visible judder); with `tick_alpha` interpolation + base-px flooring, the camera and sprites step one base px at the interpolated instant, never twice in a frame and never backward. No sub-base-pixel motion exists at any fps (item 2 rule 2). Input latency is unchanged by fps above 60 except `L_render` shrinks to ≤ 6.9 ms.
  5. **V-sync defaults:** ship `VSYNC_ENABLED` (engine default `[BIN]`); expose `MAILBOX` as the "uncapped, no tearing" option and `DISABLED` + `max_fps` for benchmarking; never `ADAPTIVE` by default (behaviour on Windows D3D12 vs Vulkan NOT SOURCEABLE). `max_fps = 0` default `[BIN]`; a user-facing cap of 30/60/120/144/240/0 is a Settings-slice item. On the Deck, 40 Hz or 90 Hz panels are not multiples of 60: the interpolation path is what keeps motion even there — spike at 40 and 90 fps caps.
  6. **Pause and reduced motion** never alter the tick (CR-11); `SceneTree.paused` `[BIN]` must not be the kernel's pause (H10 — the kernel is scene-tree independent), so the pipeline root maps game pause to kernel `PAUSED` and the engine's `paused` only to presentation nodes if at all. **→ ADR** (part of tick driver).
  
  **Spike must verify (proposed 8.12 step 13 "pacing"):** `state_hash` equality across fps caps; frames-with-repeated-pose count at 144 fps with and without interpolation; `physics_jitter_fix` 0 vs 0.5 effect on tick timing (log `get_physics_frames()` vs wall clock); same-frame `_physics_process` → `_process` ordering (kernel D.4 best case); 40/90 fps caps; the `max_physics_steps_per_frame` cap semantics.

  ## 7. Gotchas from the pinned reference, and the three likely mistakes
  
  **From `[REF]` (breaking-changes.md, rendering.md, current-best-practices.md):**
  
  - **4.6 glow reworked — glow processes *before* tonemapping, screen blend.** No pre-4.6 glow tuning transfers; `glow_hdr_threshold` must be re-found. 8.12 step 8 tests the fringe (`#B07BE6` must not bloom; running-loop emissive must). Section C records glow as per-`Viewport` (`use_hdr_2d` is a `Viewport` member `[BIN]`) and world-only.
  - **D3D12 default on Windows since 4.6 `[REF]` vs `rendering/rendering_device/driver.windows = "vulkan"` `[BIN]`.** Not reconciled by either source. The GDD must not assume a driver: 8.12 step 1 prints `get_current_rendering_driver_name()` / `get_current_rendering_method()` `[BIN]` and the recorded driver goes into 8.4 and the ADR. V-sync and swap-chain behaviour (item 6) is driver-dependent and is measured on whichever driver the binary picks, plus the other once.
  - **4.7 `CanvasItem` lines without AA feather, thinner `[REF]`.** Hairlines, filaments, seams, debug camera limits are sprites or `draw_rect`, never `draw_line` width 1 (8.4 already); debug overlays that use `draw_line` need explicit width ≥ 1 base px.
  - **HDR 2D off by default** (`rendering/viewport/hdr_2d = false` `[BIN]`): set on the project *and* on the world `SubViewport` (`use_hdr_2d`), never on the root (the HUD must stay SDR-exact for the 4.6 palette). HDR *output* (4.7 `[REF]`) is a separate feature, off.
  - **`default_texture_filter` default LINEAR** (`= 1` `[BIN]`, `Viewport.canvas_item_default_texture_filter = 1` `[BIN]`): three places to set NEAREST — project setting, world `SubViewport` member, `SubViewportContainer.texture_filter`; the HUD inherits the project default through the root. **Two NEAREST enums with different numbering `[BIN]`:** `Viewport.DEFAULT_CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST = 0` (project setting and `SubViewport` member) but `CanvasItem.TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST = 1` (container, sprites, `CanvasTexture`) — `texture_filter = 0` on a `CanvasItem` is `PARENT_NODE`, not NEAREST. The startup assertion compares the right enum per target.
  - Also from REF, non-rendering but biting Section C's code: 4.7 typed-return overrides need an explicit `return` on every path; `is_class()` takes `StringName`; mouse/keyboard device IDs are `DEVICE_ID_MOUSE/KEYBOARD`, not 0 (the pipeline root's input-coordinate mapping must not test `device == 0`).

  5. **`drag_*` margins** (default 0.2, disabled `[BIN]`): usable, but the drag window is in viewport fractions, so the resulting camera position is fractional and must be floored (rule 2 above); with `anchor_mode = DRAG_CENTER` and a 640×360 view the margins are 128×72 base px. The frame is tight (13.3 × 7.5 tiles, 8.2); recommend starting with drag off and a hard follow, adding margins only if the spike shows readable framing.
  6. **Transform hierarchy and the moving ship.** If the ship's world-space transform rotates, every human-built interior sprite rotates off-grid under nearest sampling — forbidden by 8.4. Two consistent resolutions, neither Section C's to pick: (a) **render in the ship-local frame** — the world `SubViewport`'s canvas *is* the ship frame, the ship's motion appears only on the exterior/background layer (`Parallax2D` / `ParallaxBackground` exist `[BIN]`), the interior never rotates; (b) `ignore_rotation = false` so the camera rotates with the ship and the interior stays axis-aligned in screen space while the exterior rotates. (a) is cheaper and avoids the question of what snapping does to a rotated canvas transform (NOT SOURCEABLE). Dependency question for the Ship Body GDD (kernel C.3 #6, Open Question 3). **→ ADR**.
  
  **Spike must verify (proposed 8.12 step 12):** camera following a body on a translating ship section at 144 fps — zero render-px disagreement between camera and sprite each frame; `get_screen_center_position()` is integer base px; limits clamp without fractional residue; `drag` margins + floor produce no 1-px oscillation at rest.
  
  ---
  
  ## 5. Resolution and window handling
  
  **Facts `[BIN]`.** `display/window/size/mode = 0` (WINDOWED), `borderless = false`, `resizable = true`, `window_width/height_override = 0`, `initial_position_type = 1`, `display/window/dpi/allow_hidpi = true`, `display/window/hdr/request_hdr_output = false`. `Window.mode` {WINDOWED, MINIMIZED, MAXIMIZED, FULLSCREEN=3, EXCLUSIVE_FULLSCREEN=4}, `Window.FLAG_BORDERLESS = 1`, `min_size/max_size`, `unresizable`. Signals/notifications: `Viewport.size_changed`, `Window.dpi_changed`, `Node.NOTIFICATION_WM_SIZE_CHANGED = 1008`, `NOTIFICATION_WM_DPI_CHANGE = 1009`, `NOTIFICATION_WM_OUTPUT_MAX_LINEAR_VALUE_CHANGED = 1013` (HDR output, 4.7). `DisplayServer.screen_get_dpi/scale/max_scale/size/usable_rect/refresh_rate`, `window_set_mode`, `window_set_flag`, `window_set_size`.
  
  **Arithmetic if `integer` + `keep` behave as their names say `[UNV-4.3]` — the engine's actual handling of the remainder is NOT SOURCEABLE:**
  
  | Window | N | Content | Remainder under `keep` | Under `expand` at same N |

  | 1280×720 | 2 | 1280×720 | none | — |
  | 1280×800 (Steam Deck) | 2 | 1280×720 | 80 px (40 top + 40 bottom) | 640×**400** base (+40 rows) |
  | 1366×768 | 2 | 1280×720 | 86 wide, 48 tall | 683×384 base |
  | 1365×768 (odd width) | 2 | 1280×720 | 85 wide, 48 tall | 682.5 wide → what `expand` does with a non-integer base is NOT SOURCEABLE |
  | 1600×900 | 2 | 1280×720 | 320×180 | 800×450 base |

  **Constraints and recommendations.**
  
  1. **Spike starts at `keep`** (8.1, 8.10): the remainder is expected to be a letterbox filled with the clear colour `[UNV-4.3]`; what the engine actually draws there, whether the HUD anchors to the 640×360 content rect or the window, and what `expand` yields at odd windows are NOT SOURCEABLE. The GDD promises: **every window size yields a square N×N base pixel; non-integer multiples are letterboxed, never fractionally scaled**; `expand` is a post-spike ask that must keep N integer and the base size integer.
  2. **Steam Deck** 1280×800: N = 2 either way; `expand` gives +40 base rows (8.1's preference). `allow_hidpi = true` default `[BIN]` — what hidpi does on the Deck's Linux session and on Windows ≥ 125 % scaling is NOT SOURCEABLE; the spike logs `screen_get_scale()`, `screen_get_dpi()` and `get_final_transform()` on each target. The GDD should state N is derived from the window's *pixel* size, never from DPI, and that `content_scale_factor` stays 1.0.
  3. **Fullscreen/borderless.** Default `MODE_FULLSCREEN` (3, borderless window covering the screen) rather than `EXCLUSIVE_FULLSCREEN` (4) for Alt-Tab safety `[UNV-4.3]`; both exist `[BIN]`. A mode change fires `size_changed` → recompute N, resize the `SubViewport` under pass B, re-anchor the HUD. The GDD promises: a resize never produces a frame with a fractional transform (spike: screenshot the first frame after each mode change).
  4. **Resize handling owner.** One presentation node (the "pipeline root") owns `size_changed`/`dpi_changed` and is the only writer of `SubViewport.size`, `size_2d_override`, HUD anchors and camera limits in view units. **→ ADR** (with the pass B wiring).
  5. **HDR output** (4.7 `[REF]`) stays off (`request_hdr_output = false` `[BIN]`) through MVP; `hdr_2d` (internal HDR for glow) is a different setting and is on (8.4).

  ---
  
  ## 6. Frame pacing
  
  **Facts `[BIN]`.** `physics/common/physics_ticks_per_second = 60`, `max_physics_steps_per_frame = 8`, `physics_jitter_fix = 0.5`, `physics/common/physics_interpolation = false`; `application/run/max_fps = 0`, `delta_smoothing = true`, `low_processor_mode = false`; `display/window/vsync/vsync_mode = 1` (ENABLED) with `DisplayServer.VSYNC_{DISABLED=0, ENABLED=1, ADAPTIVE=2, MAILBOX=3}`, `window_set_vsync_mode`, `screen_get_refresh_rate`; `rendering/rendering_device/vsync/frame_queue_size = 2`, `swapchain_image_count = 3`; `Engine.get_physics_interpolation_fraction()`, `is_in_physics_frame()`, `get_physics_frames()`, `get_process_frames()`, `get_frames_per_second()`; `SceneTree.physics_frame` / `process_frame` signals; `Node.process_priority`, `process_physics_priority`.
  
  `_process`/`_physics_process` ordering within a frame is **silent in REF** (kernel D.4 says so and makes the "same-frame" best case spike-conditional).
  
  **Constraints and recommendations.**
  
  1. **The sim is fps-independent by construction and the GDD says so as a test**: identical `state_hash` after a scripted 10-s input replay at `max_fps` 30, 60, 144 and 0 (kernel G3 determinism + CR-11). Presentation reads last-committed state at render rate and never causes a tick.
  2. **Who drives the tick is an ADR the pacing promises depend on.** Kernel D.4 assumes the tick is driven by the physics callback (60 Hz; `max_physics_steps_per_frame = 8` `[BIN]` — if it caps catch-up at 8 ticks/frame `[UNV-4.3]`, the engine stops catching up below 7.5 fps; step 13 checks); kernel D.5 defines a kernel-side accumulator with its own `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME`. Two accumulators drift; one must be the clock. If the physics callback drives, `physics_jitter_fix` (default **0.5**, non-zero `[BIN]`) alters per-step timing in a way NOT SOURCEABLE here — recommend **0** pending the spike, since a fixed-tick kernel that forbids wall-clock reads (H9) should not receive engine-smoothed steps. `delta_smoothing = true` `[BIN]` affects `_process` delta only `[UNV-4.3]`; harmless to presentation, irrelevant to the sim. **→ ADR (tick driver)**.
  3. **Promise at 30 fps render:** two ticks per frame, sim unchanged; `tick_alpha` clamps at 1 so nothing extrapolates; input-to-pixel worst case 50 ms (kernel D.4); motion shows every second tick's pose — 2-base-px steps for a 1 px/tick body, which is honest, not smoothed.
  4. **Promise at 144 fps render:** ticks occur on ~42 % of frames; without interpolation 58 % of frames would repeat a pose (visible judder); with `tick_alpha` interpolation + base-px flooring, the camera and sprites step one base px at the interpolated instant, never twice in a frame and never backward. No sub-base-pixel motion exists at any fps (item 2 rule 2). Input latency is unchanged by fps above 60 except `L_render` shrinks to ≤ 6.9 ms.
  5. **V-sync defaults:** ship `VSYNC_ENABLED` (engine default `[BIN]`); expose `MAILBOX` as the "uncapped, no tearing" option and `DISABLED` + `max_fps` for benchmarking; never `ADAPTIVE` by default (behaviour on Windows D3D12 vs Vulkan NOT SOURCEABLE). `max_fps = 0` default `[BIN]`; a user-facing cap of 30/60/120/144/240/0 is a Settings-slice item.   6. **Pause and reduced motion** never alter the tick (CR-11); `SceneTree.paused` `[BIN]` must not be the kernel's pause (H10 — the kernel is scene-tree independent), so the pipeline root maps game pause to kernel `PAUSED` and the engine's `paused` only to presentation nodes if at all. **→ ADR** (part of tick driver).

  ## 7. Gotchas from the pinned reference, and the three likely mistakes

The GDD must not assume a driver: 8.12 step 1 prints `get_current_rendering_driver_name()` / `get_current_rendering_method()` `[BIN]` and the recorded driver goes into 8.4 and the ADR.   - **HDR 2D off by default** (`rendering/viewport/hdr_2d = false` `[BIN]`): set on the project *and* on the world `SubViewport` (`use_hdr_2d`), never on the root (the HUD must stay SDR-exact for the 4.6 palette). HDR *output* (4.7 `[REF]`) is a separate feature, off.

  ---
  
  ## Consolidated "becomes an ADR" list
  
  1. **Interpolation clock** — kernel `tick_alpha` is the only interpolator; engine `physics_interpolation` off; `position_smoothing` off; prev/curr read views compose ship × local. (Items 2, 4, 6.)
  2. **Tick driver** — physics callback (kernel D.4) vs kernel accumulator (D.5); `physics_jitter_fix` value; mapping of game pause to kernel `PAUSED` vs `SceneTree.paused`. (Item 6.)
  3. **Pass A vs pass B, zoom-out, and `SubViewport` wiring** — which root stretch mode pass B and zoom-out need; who writes `SubViewport.size` on resize; container filter. (Items 1, 4, 5; decided by 8.12 step 2 + proposed step 11.)
  4. **Camera driver** — top-level presentation node, floor-to-base-px, limits set by a `PROJECTOR`, zoom via N not `Camera2D.zoom`, ship-local frame vs rotating camera (dependency on Ship Body GDD). (Item 4.)
  5. **Window/resolution policy** — `keep` for spike, `expand` post-spike; fullscreen mode default; resize owner. (Item 5.)
  6. **Layer stack** — named z bands, Y-sort node contents, `y_sort_origin`, light masks, `range_z` bounds. (Item 3.)

  - **Step 11 "stretch and window"** — the window sizes in item 5 × three modes; remainder; HUD anchoring; `expand` at odd sizes; Deck DPI; pass B wiring (i)/(ii); zoom-out N' with HUD at N; `Camera2D.zoom` direction.
  - **Step 12 "motion integrity"** — scripted bodies at 1 and 0.4 base px/tick, ship translating, at 30/60/144 fps; snap flags on/off; `physics_interpolation` on/off; camera-vs-sprite jitter in render px; `process_priority` ordering.
  - **Step 13 "pacing"** — `state_hash` across fps caps; repeated-pose frames at 144 fps; `physics_jitter_fix` 0 vs 0.5; `_physics_process` → `_process` same-frame ordering; 40/90 fps caps; `max_physics_steps_per_frame` semantics.
  
  ## Findings the caller is least likely to have already
  
  - `get_global_transform_interpolated()` is `Node3D`-only in 4.7.2 `[BIN]` — the decisive reason to keep engine physics interpolation off in 2D and own interpolation via `tick_alpha`.
  - The 2D physics-interpolation machinery (`canvas_item_*`, `canvas_light_*`, `canvas_light_occluder_*` interpolation on `RenderingServer`) **exists** in 4.7.2 `[BIN]`; the art bible's NOT SOURCEABLE on existence can be upgraded, behaviour still unmeasured.

  - Kernel D.4 (tick in the physics callback) and D.5 (kernel accumulator) describe two accumulators; the frame-pacing promises depend on which one is the clock.
  - Zoom-out per 8.1 is a change of N with the HUD fixed, which is the same two-scales-in-one-window wiring problem as pass B; neither is resolvable from the class dump.
  - `physics_jitter_fix` defaults to 0.5 (non-zero) `[BIN]`; two differently numbered NEAREST enums (`Viewport` 0 vs `CanvasItem` 1) `[BIN]`.

A durable copy of this text is at `C:\Users\dasbl\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\D--the-synaptic-sea-2d\e887ccb9-1186-40d9-9566-5eacccbd9b44\scratchpad\section-c-engine-notes.md`.

The reference covers **none** of: stretch/scale modes, SubViewport, Camera2D, 2D snapping, texture filtering, physics interpolation, V-sync, `_process`/`_physics_process` ordering.
