Three parts, and the control-manifest lines that separate them.** (a) The **Input Adapter** reads devices, quantises, and submits `PLAYER`-origin commands as peer 1 acting on the entity the binding table binds to PlayerId 1 (CR-7). It writes no block, ever; it may write only its own local state (raw aim, last-acknowledged intent, hold timers, active device). (b) The **Controller Sim** registers `controller.state` (`SIM`, `persist = true`, `persist_scope = WORLD`, `scope = PER_PLAYER` keyed by PlayerId for the local seat's actor record, `repl_hint = SHARED_SUMMARY`), the command types `set_move_intent`, `set_aim`, and the hook `controller.step` (divisor 1, `after: suit.vitals`). It writes its block only in `apply` and inside its hook (CR-9); it may not submit `PLAYER`-origin commands (CR-3) — only the Adapter submits. (c) The **Avatar Presenter** reads `body.state` (position prev/curr), `controller.state` (facing, gait, locomotion state, hand point), `emitter.state` (beam lit, shape), and `tick_alpha`; for the *local* avatar only it also reads the Adapter's raw aim. It writes CanvasItem / Light2D / AnimatedSprite properties and nothing else. *Rationale.* The brief's manifest line "controller submits via `INPUT_SURFACE` only; never writes blocks" is true of the Adapter and false of the Controller Sim; naming both "the controller" would read as "this system has no block", and then facing and gait would end up as presentation state that co-op cannot replicate and a save cannot restore. *Alternative rejected:* fold the Controller Sim into Ship Body (one "character" block) — rejected because intent and facing are seat semantics (what the player asked for, readable by Interaction, Attention and the HUD) while position is a physics fact (kernel G3's determinism limit); keeping them apart lets the replay test exclude physics without losing the input record.

Input model: actions, intents, commands.** The game reads **named actions** (`StringName`, rebindable, Settings & Input Rebinding), never raw keys or `device == 0` (4.7: `InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_MOUSE` / `DEVICE_ID_KEYBOARD`; identify by event type). **→ ADR** (InputMap actions vs a custom binding layer; edge detection by event vs polling).
  
  | Action | Kind | Default (KB+M / pad) | What the Adapter submits |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `move_up/down/left/right` | continuous | WASD / left stick | part of `set_move_intent` |
  | `run` | hold (toggle offered in Settings) | Shift / L3 | part of `set_move_intent` (`gait`) |
  | aim | continuous | mouse cursor / right stick | `set_aim` (quantised); raw aim kept locally |
  | `beam_toggle` | press | F / Y | `toggle_beam` (owner: Emitter State) |
  | `interact` | press; hold for destructive verbs | E / A | `interact {target}` or the verb Interaction names; hold-to-confirm runs locally (PC-6) |
  | `tool_use` | hold = channel | LMB / RT | `begin_cut` / `begin_weld` / `begin_patch` on press, `cancel_channel` on release (owner: Interaction or Assembly) |
  | `tool_1..4`, `tool_next/prev` | press | 1–4, scroll / LB, RB, d-pad | `equip_tool` (owner: Suit & Equipment) |
  | `drop` | press | G / B (held while carrying) | `drop` (owner: Interaction) |
  | `inspect` | press | R / X | Interaction's inspect verb (HR-14 mirror card) |
  | `zoom_in/out` | press | wheel / d-pad up-down | no command — pipeline C6 consumes it (PC-16) |
  | `pause` / `chart_table` | press | Esc, Tab / Start, Select | host-local control-plane or menu (PC-16) |
  | `cancel` | press | Esc / B | `cancel_channel` if channelling; closes menus otherwise |

  | Knob | Value | px/s at 60 Hz | tiles/s | Why |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `v_walk` | **2 px/tick** | 120 | 2.5 | Deliberate but not tedious: a 13-tile default field crosses in ≈ 5 s; the boarding rhythm's pace is set by doors and reading, not by a slow walk. 1 px/tick (1.25 tiles/s) recorded as the alternative for the MVP playtest if the boarding rhythm reads as hurried |

  | `v_carry` | **1 px/tick** | 60 | 1.25 | A module at chest height halves the walk: extraction under rising Attention is the sortie's tension ("weigh a module against the noise of taking it") and the slowdown is *seen* (carry-walk cycle), never a hidden stat |
  | `v_max` | = `v_run` = 3 px/tick | 180 | — | Read by the pipeline's G check |

  *Acceleration, stopping, turning.* **Instant** start, instant stop, instant facing change: `ACCEL_TICKS` = 0, `DECEL_TICKS` = 0 at MVP. *Rationale:* any ramp passes through non-integer px/tick (1→2→3 over three ticks is the one integer-only ramp and is offered as the fallback knob `RUN_RAMP_TICKS` ∈ {0, 3}); stiff-weighted bodies (5.2) do not ease; and Pillar 2's escape — "a horror enters the cone, I leave" — must cost zero ticks of wind-up. Walk ↔ run switches at the next tick. Positions are always integer base px at commit, so a stop is always *on the pixel grid*; there is **no tile snapping** on stop (a snap is an uncaused motion the player did not make, and C-R's "never reverses unless the player did" extends to the body).
  
  *Diagonals.* Cardinal moves are exactly `v` px/tick per axis. For diagonals the Body integrates `v/√2` per axis with a **sub-pixel residue held in Body's block** (Bresenham-style; position is committed as integers each tick), so diagonal speed equals cardinal speed and the per-axis step pattern is a regular 7-of-10. The residue is zeroed in `post_restore` together with `previous := current` (pipeline C5, routed to every owner of a moving read view — Body is that owner). *Alternatives rejected:* √2-inflated diagonals (the classic diagonal-sprint exploit, and a 41 % speed bonus for free); integer diagonal pairs ((1,1) is 71 % of walk, (2,2) is 141 % — neither is honest).
  
  *Collision contract (Body's to implement, this GDD's to require).* The actor is a kinematic capsule at the feet (≈ 20 × 12 base px, foot-centred, placeholder for Body's GDD); walls, closed doors, props and other actors block; sliding along a wall is permitted; no pushing of actors by actors at MVP. The actor is carried with the deck: welds, detaches and body transfers are Body's and never produce an uncaused interior motion in the frame the player is in (pipeline C2 ii).
  
  **PC-4. Facing: five drawn, three mirrored, derived from aim when the beam is lit.** "Beam held" in the brief means **lit** (`toggle_beam` is a toggle command, CR-4), not a button held. Rules, in priority order:
  1. **Staggered / downed / dead**: facing frozen.
  2. **Channelling**: facing locked to the target's octant for the channel's duration (the work loop is two-handed and tool-forward, 5.2); aim may still move and the beam follows it from the locked hand point.
  3. **Running**: facing = movement direction regardless of the beam. *Rationale:* the run cycle is a forward lean of the whole figure; a lean sideways to its motion reads as the horror's asymmetry (3.2 negation rule). The beam is engine light rotating 360° from the hand point (5.6), so a runner's light may trail behind them — honest and tense.
  4. **Beam lit, walking or stationary**: facing = aim octant (with `FACING_HYSTERESIS_DEG` = 4° at the 22.5° boundaries). The body translates in any of the 8 directions while facing the aim; the single walk cycle plays for the facing (side-steps and back-steps use the same cycle — accepted; the art budget has no strafe sets, 5.7). Back-pedal speed is full `v_walk` (`BACKPEDAL_FACTOR` = 1.0; any other value breaks whole-px cadence, so if the gameplay-programmer wants a penalty it must be "walk only" or an integer).
  5. **Beam unlit, moving**: facing = movement direction.
  6. **Beam unlit, stationary**: facing holds its last value.
  
  Mirroring: SW, W, NW are the SE, E, NE sheets x-flipped; the hand point's x is negated; the tool changes hands (accepted, 5.6). *Alternative rejected:* facing always from aim (Zomboid-style) — in the dark the player's aim is meaningless to anyone else and the body turning toward nothing visible invites the "where is it looking" misread; the beam-lit rule makes *looking* and *lighting* the same act (5.2: "looking at something is lighting it").
  
  **PC-5. Aim and the beam.** *Sources.* Mouse: raw aim = direction from the actor's **floored hand point** to the cursor's world position obtained through the pipeline's mouse-to-world (C11), so zoom level never changes aim; inside `AIM_MOUSE_DEADZONE_PX` = 8 base px of the hand point the aim holds its last value. Gamepad: raw aim = right-stick direction beyond `STICK_DEADZONE`; when the stick is released the aim **holds** (the beam does not swing to the movement direction — a sweep is a decision the player makes, Pillar 3; ux-designer may offer "aim follows movement when idle" as an option, default off). *Two consumers of aim:* the **raw aim** is read locally by the Avatar Presenter (beam `Light2D` rotation, continuous — lights may rotate off-grid, PR-4 rule 5) and by the camera look-ahead (pipeline C4, regardless of lit state); the **committed aim** (5° quantum, ≤ 1 tick late) is what Emitter State orients the beam emitter by for the exposure query, what Interaction uses for target preference, and what co-op replicates. A ≤ 5° / ≤ 1-tick divergence between the drawn and simulated cone is accepted; the identity channel (Pillar 1) is shape and colour, which come from the replicated loadout, never from aim.
  
  *Beam shapes are a loadout, not an input.* The four shapes (wide, narrow, split, fan — art bible 3.2, 8.3) are a per-player `Suit & Equipment` loadout fact; the Adapter has no "change shape" action. One `beam_toggle` action submits **`toggle_beam`** (owner: Emitter State; actor = the player's beam emitter ID, bound to the seat). The beam is an emitter like any other for Attention (Emitter State's exposure query), which is what makes "go dark" a real strategy.
  
  *Acknowledgement vs the anchor (resolves a CR-4 / Pillar 1 collision).* The beam is a human-channel anchor that may never lie. If the local `Light2D` lit on the press and the sim then rejected (`beam charge empty`), the beam would have flickered once on the one object that may not. Rule: **the toggle's sound and the hand's switch animation play immediately; the light itself changes only on the committed state** (≤ 17 ms later, imperceptible against a 3-screen-px cone edge). The Avatar Presenter never predicts beam state.
  
  *Hand point.* The beam's origin is `floor(pos) + hand_offset[facing][animation]` — per facing **and per animation** (carry-walk holds the module at chest height and the lamp hand rises; work and stagger move it too), tabulated from the sheets in Section D, using the same floored position as the sprite (PR-4 rule 2) so light origin and sprite never disagree. The Controller Sim publishes the current hand point in its read view so that when the Perception Filter substitutes a horror rig for a crewmate (class c, art bible 5.0) the beam still originates at the *true* hand point.
  
  **PC-6. Interaction reach, targeting, prompts, hold-to-confirm.** *Reach* is a sector from the actor's foot origin: radius `REACH_PX` = 72 base px (1.5 tiles — covers the adjacent ring including diagonals at 68 px) and half-angle `REACH_HALF_ANGLE_DEG` = 70° about the **facing** (which is the aim when the beam is lit). Objects behind the player are never candidates. *Targeting:* a candidate must be in reach, in the arc, and **lit** (Emitter State's exposure query above the technical-artist's threshold); mouse picks the candidate under the cursor if any, else the nearest in the arc; gamepad uses **proximity focus** — one candidate, chosen by angular distance to the committed aim then by distance — and one contextual action (HR-14). Prompts (`E · Cut`) are drawn only for the candidate, only when lit (art bible 7.0), by the HUD through `world_to_hud`; an off-screen candidate has no prompt (C9). **Decision (art bible 7.0 leaves it to the game-designer): an action is possible only on a lit object.** Interaction's `validate` calls the same exposure query the prompt uses, so the prompt never lies by omission. *Rationale:* "what you light, you can read" must also be "what you light, you can touch", or working in the dark becomes a free Attention dodge and "go dark" degenerates into the dominant strategy (Sirlin); light has to cost Attention to make darkness a trade. Exceptions: `drop` of the module you carry, `toggle_beam`, and the inspect card of an instrument already lit. *Hold-to-confirm* (HR-14, destructive verbs: section cut, module removal, drop into void — the list is Interaction's): a **local** hold of `HOLD_CONFIRM_TICKS` = 36 (0.6 s) measured in render time by the Adapter, then one command; the sim never sees a partial hold; the HUD draws the linear bar (7.3). It is distinct from a channel (PC-7): short, local, and completes into a single command rather than accruing in the sim.
  
  **PC-7. Channels (cut / weld / patch).** Press `tool_use` on a valid candidate → the Adapter submits `begin_<verb> {target}` (`coalesce = NONE`; owner Interaction, with Assembly behind it for weld/cut). The owner's `validate` requires: candidate lit and in reach, `controller.state.dir == NONE`, not carrying, not staggered/downed. **Progress is sim state in the owner's block**, accrued per tick by the owner's hook; the Controller Sim only records `channel_ref` and locks facing (PC-4 rule 2). *Interrupts:* (i) **release** → the Adapter submits `cancel_channel`; (ii) **movement** — the owner's hook reads `controller.state.dir` and aborts when it becomes non-`NONE` (sim-side, so identical in `MIRROR`; the 8-way dead-zone already filters stick drift); (iii) **stagger / downed** — the Controller Sim clears `channel_ref` and the owner aborts on seeing it; (iv) **target invalidated** (power drops mid-cut, the section detaches) — the owner aborts and reports it through state change, never through the command result (CR-5). The player keeps control of the body at all times: a channel never locks movement, movement cancels the channel. *Rationale:* Dread Before Chaos needs "I can leave now" to be true in every state; a locked weld with a horror entering the cone is a cheap death. **Pause:** the tick stops, progress freezes, the hold survives if the button is still down on resume (PC-2 resync). Whether progress persists on the target after an abort is the owner's rule; this GDD recommends a short persistence (Assembly/Interaction to set; placeholder reference durations only for feel validation, not owned here: cut 4 s = 240 ticks, weld 6 s = 360, patch 3 s = 180).
  
  **PC-8. Carrying.** `pickup` (Interaction) on a module → `controller.state.carry_ref` set; `drop` clears it. While carrying: gait forced to `v_carry` (**no run while carrying** — there is no carry-run cycle in the sheet budget and a sprinting module is the wrong image); `tool_use` and `interact` channels are rejected `BUSY` (hands full) — `drop` first; the beam **stays available** (recommended; the hand point shifts to the carry table). The alternative — beam off while carrying, so extraction is blind — is a strong Pillar 3 lever and is recorded as an open question for the user rather than decided here, because it changes the sortie's difficulty curve more than any other single rule in this section. Stagger does **not** drop the module (stagger is brief); downed does.
  
  **PC-9. Honest body states: stagger, downed, dead — driven by the sim, never by a stat.** The Controller Sim consumes one value from Suit & Equipment's read view (`after: suit.vitals`, divisor 6 — a read up to 5 ticks old is tolerated): `vitals.state ∈ {OK, STRAINED, CRITICAL, FAILED}`, derived by Suit from O₂, temperature and suit integrity (thresholds are Suit's / systems-designer's). Rules: **OK / STRAINED** — no locomotion effect (rime and visor fog are Suit-driven overlays the Presenter draws; they are information, not penalties). **Entering CRITICAL** → one **stagger** (`STAGGER_TICKS` = 30 = 0.5 s; input ignored; channel cleared; no displacement — a stagger is animation plus input lock, not a physics impulse), then **walk only** until the state clears (the `run` action does nothing; the HUD breath/warmth reading and the visor fog are the readable reason). **FAILED** → **downed** (`down` 6-frame animation, input ignored, carry dropped); in MVP solo, downed → **dead** after `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` = 1800 (30 s) unless `vitals.state` leaves FAILED; dead hands the actor to Save/Load's MVP death stub (`request_restore` — the controller never calls the control plane). In VS-B a crewmate's revive verb (Interaction) returns downed → idle. External stagger sources (a venting loop's recoil, art bible 5.2) arrive as a `SYSTEM`-origin `stagger` command from the owning system at T+1 (CR-9 path b). *Why no continuous speed penalty:* the concept's secondary design test (−10 % move speed vs a false gauge → the gauge) is explicit that invisible stat debuffs are the wrong tool; a state the body *shows* — fog, rime, stagger, walk-only — is a channel of truth a crewmate can read in their beam (5.3).
  
  **PC-10. The two rhythms in the controller.** Nothing in this system changes between boarding, the Tell and breach: no adrenaline, no speed buff, no reduced noise, no "panic" input changes. **The breach is frantic because of what moves, not because the body changes** (art bible 2.8). Running is allowed everywhere and is **noisy**: the Controller Sim's hook pushes a noise stimulus to Attention's intake each tick the actor moves — `NOISE_WALK` = 1, `NOISE_RUN` = 4, `NOISE_CARRY` = 1 (placeholder stimulus units; Attention's intake is undesigned, kernel C.3 #4). Running is 1.5× faster and 4× louder per tick, so ≈ 2.7× louder per tile: running never dominates walking for stealth and is a real trade in a retreat. Tool noise belongs to the tool (Suit / Interaction). The beam's exposure is Emitter State's.
  
  **PC-11. The human channel; the controller never renders.** The crewmate sprite and its beam (shape and colour) are inviolable anchors (Pillar 1; art bible 5.0). This system draws nothing: the Avatar Presenter is a `PRESENTATION` node reading committed state, and the Perception Filter may substitute the whole body for a horror rig (5.0) but never edits pixels, never moves the hand point, never touches the beam. Remote crewmates are drawn by the same Presenter from `MIRROR` state (PC-17), so a friend's body is the same object on every client.
  
  **PC-12. What the player cannot do.** No jump, no dodge-roll, no vault, no lean/peek (camera C9), no melee or attack input (anti-pillar: not a combat game — the friendly-harm act is an Interaction verb on a crewmate target under Sanity's gate, reached through `tool_use`, never a dedicated button), no auto-aim or aim assist of any kind, no acrobatics, no acceleration tricks. **No crouch (decided).** *Rationale:* restraint in this game is *light and noise* (Pillar 3), not posture; a crouch with lower noise would be a free dodge that every player holds permanently (Sirlin: a dominant strategy that is not a decision); the sheet budget has no crouch set; and a curled crewmate drifts toward the horror grammar 5.2 forbids. Walking and turning the beam off *are* the quiet stance. No sprint-by-stick-deflection (PC-3).
  
  **PC-13. Input device switching.** The **last device that produced an event is active**; prompts and the hand rail switch glyph sets on the HUD. Godot merges devices per action, so a `tool_use` held on a pad survives touching the mouse. Switching aim source never jumps the beam: a mouse move takes aim from the cursor; a stick deflection takes it from the stick; a stick release holds. The cursor is hidden while the pad is active (ux-designer confirms). Every flow in the core loop is **gamepad-complete** (HR-14): move, run, aim, beam, interact, tool use, tool select, drop, inspect (mirror card), zoom, pause, chart table (snap-to-node is Chart Table's); text chat is the only keyboard-only item (VS-B).
  
  **PC-14. Position ownership — recommendation (provisional, kernel Open Question 3 / pipeline Open Question 3).** **Adopt the proposal: Ship Body owns ship-local kinematic position; the Controller Sim owns intent, gait, facing, locomotion state, carry and channel references.** Contract: `controller.step` writes `dir`, `gait_effective`, `facing`, `loco_state`; `body.integrate` (`after: controller.step`) reads them, integrates `v(gait_effective) × unit(dir)` with collision and the diagonal residue, and commits integer `pos_prev / pos_curr` in the body frame; it also exposes `blocked` (moved less than requested) for the Presenter's footstep audio, nothing more. *Why Body:* the composite welded ship and the moving-platform problem are Body's (systems index high-risk row); an actor must transfer between bodies (pod hop, detach) which Body already tracks; physics-derived positions are *inputs* under G3 and keeping them in Body's block lets the replay test exclude exactly one block. *Why not Controller:* it would duplicate the physics projection and put a `PROJECTOR` concern inside an input system. Marked **provisional** until the technical-director's ruling in the weld spike.
  
  **PC-15. Hook order and timing.** `controller.step` (divisor 1, `after: suit.vitals`) → `body.integrate` (divisor 1, `after: controller.step`) → `emitter.place` (divisor 1, `after: body.integrate`; positions the beam emitter at the hand point for the exposure query) → Attention (divisor 6) reads the noise channel. Input-to-effect: an intent submitted during frame N is applied at the next tick's P2 and integrated in P3 of the same tick; the Presenter shows it at the next render (≤ 17 ms + render latency, kernel CR-1).
  
  **PC-16. Inputs this system owns but does not consume.** `zoom_in/out` are player inputs (pipeline C1) owned here as actions and consumed by the pipeline; `pause` calls the host-local control plane (CR-15) through the menu, never from the Controller Sim; `chart_table` opens a UI that is itself an `INPUT_SURFACE`. In `PAUSED` the Adapter stops submitting intents (they would be rejected immediately) and resyncs on resume (PC-2).
  
  **PC-17. Save, restore and co-op seams.** `controller.state` persists (`WORLD`): on restore, `dir = NONE`, `channel_ref = none`, `loco_state` as saved except `CHANNELLING → IDLE` and `STAGGERED → IDLE`; `carry_ref` restored. Body sets `previous := current` and zeroes the residue in `post_restore` (pipeline C5). In VS-B the Adapter of a guest submits identically and the host's Controller Sim applies; remote crewmates' `controller.state` and `body.state` replicate as `SHARED_SUMMARY` and the Presenter draws them from `MIRROR` views with the committed (5°-quantised) aim for their beam rotation. Nothing in the Presenter branches on `HOST`/`MIRROR` (CR-10).
  
  ---
  
  ### States and Transitions
  
  Locomotion states live in `controller.state.loco_state`. "Interrupts channel" means the Controller Sim clears `channel_ref` and the channel owner aborts.
  
  | State | Entered by | Movement | Aim / beam | Channel | Carry | Animation (art bible 5.2/5.7) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | `IDLE` | `dir == NONE` and no other state | none | aim free; facing per PC-4 | may begin | may be carrying (carry-idle = carry-walk frame 0 held) | idle 6 (or carry frame 0) |
  | `WALK` | `dir != NONE`, gait WALK or forced walk | `v_walk` | aim free; facing per PC-4 | **interrupts** | if carrying → `CARRY_WALK` | walk 8 |
  | `RUN` | `dir != NONE`, gait RUN, not carrying, vitals < CRITICAL | `v_run` | aim free; facing = movement | **interrupts** | n/a | run 8 |
  | `CARRY_WALK` | `dir != NONE` and carrying | `v_carry` | aim free (beam allowed, PC-8) | n/a (BUSY) | yes | carry-walk 8 |
  | `CHANNELLING` | `begin_*` `Applied` | none (any `dir` → abort) | aim free; facing locked to target | in progress | no | work 6 |
  | `STAGGERED` | CRITICAL entry edge; `SYSTEM` `stagger` | none; input ignored `STAGGER_TICKS` | frozen | **interrupts** | kept | stagger 4 |
  | `DOWNED` | vitals FAILED | none; input ignored | frozen; beam state unchanged | **interrupts** | dropped | down 6 |
  | `DEAD` | `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` elapsed (solo MVP) | none | beam off (Emitter State on actor death) | n/a | n/a | down last frame; hand-off to Save/Load |
  | `IN_POD` | `pod_hop` `Applied` (body transfer) | none; locomotion ignored | none | n/a | module travels with the pod (Boarding & Salvage) | not drawn; pod is its own body |
  | `MENU` (Adapter-local, not a sim state) | pause / chart table open | Adapter sends `NONE` before opening; no intents while open | raw aim frozen | survives pause if held | — | sim state unchanged |
  
  **Transitions** (every pair not listed is invalid and is reported to diagnostics, never silently applied):
  
  | From | Trigger | To |
  |---|---|---|
  | `IDLE` | `dir != NONE` | `WALK` / `RUN` / `CARRY_WALK` by gait and carry |
  | `WALK` / `RUN` / `CARRY_WALK` | `dir == NONE` | `IDLE` |
  | `WALK` ↔ `RUN` | gait change, while moving, not carrying, vitals < CRITICAL | the other |
  | `RUN` | pickup `Applied`, or vitals → CRITICAL | `CARRY_WALK` / `WALK` (next tick) |
  | `IDLE` | `begin_*` `Applied` | `CHANNELLING` |
  | `CHANNELLING` | `cancel_channel` `Applied`; `dir != NONE`; owner abort (target invalid); channel complete | `IDLE` |
  | any except `DOWNED`/`DEAD`/`IN_POD` | CRITICAL entry edge or `SYSTEM` `stagger` | `STAGGERED` |
  | `STAGGERED` | `STAGGER_TICKS` elapsed | `IDLE` (then re-evaluates `dir` next tick) |
  | any except `DEAD`/`IN_POD` | vitals FAILED | `DOWNED` |
  | `DOWNED` | vitals leaves FAILED (solo) or revive `Applied` (VS-B) | `IDLE` |
  | `DOWNED` | `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` elapsed | `DEAD` |
  | `DEAD` | Save/Load `request_restore` | (block restored; `IDLE`) |
  | `IDLE` / `WALK` | `pod_hop` `Applied` at the pod console | `IN_POD` |
  | `IN_POD` | arrival body transfer complete (Transit hook) | `IDLE` |
  | any | `LOADING → RUNNING` | as restored (PC-17) |
  
  **What interrupts a channel:** release of `tool_use`; any non-`NONE` move intent; stagger; downed; target invalidation by the owner; a body transfer; a restore. A pause does not.
  
  ---
  
  ### Interactions with Other Systems
  
  | # | System | Direction | Contract | Status |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | **Command & Simulation Layer** (kernel) | both | Adapter submits as `INPUT_SURFACE`; Controller Sim registers `controller.state`, two intent types (`coalesce = LATEST_PER_ACTOR_PER_TICK`, `max_age` 30) and hook `controller.step`; consumes result events (STALE resync), `tick_alpha`, binding table (seat → actor); honours CR-16 pause (no intents while paused; resync on resume) | firm (kernel GDD C.3 row 2) |
  | 2 | **Ship Body & Interior Physics** | Controller → Body (intent); Body → Presenter (position) | Body owns ship-local integer position, collision, diagonal residue, `previous := current` in `post_restore`; reads `dir`, `gait_effective`; hook `after: controller.step`. **Provisional** — recommendation PC-14, pending TD ruling | provisional |
  | 3 | **Suit & Equipment** | Suit → Controller | `vitals.state` {OK, STRAINED, CRITICAL, FAILED} drives stagger / walk-only / downed; beam shape and tool loadout; `equip_tool` command owner; rime/fog overlays are Suit's thresholds | provisional (Suit undesigned) |
  | 4 | **Emitter State & Light-Exposure Query** | Adapter → Emitter (`toggle_beam`); Controller → Emitter (committed aim, hand point) | The beam is an emitter; `emitter.place` `after: body.integrate`; the light changes only on committed state (PC-5); exposure query gates prompts and actions (PC-6) | provisional |
  | 5 | **Interaction System** | Adapter → Interaction (verbs); Interaction → Controller (reads `dir`, `carry_ref`, reach) | Reach sector (72 px / 70°), lit-only rule, proximity focus, hold-to-confirm primitive; channel begin/cancel; `BUSY` when carrying or moving; phantom-target question is Interaction's (kernel Open Question 14) | provisional |
  | 6 | **Attention System** | Controller → Attention | Noise stimulus per tick by gait (`NOISE_WALK/RUN/CARRY`), via Attention's intake mutator (CR-9 a) — units are Attention's to define | provisional |
  | 7 | **Modular Ship Assembly** | Assembly → Controller (abort), Controller → Assembly (`dir`) | Weld/cut channels accrue in Assembly's block; abort on movement read from `controller.state`; facing lock for the work loop | provisional |
  | 8 | **Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera** | Controller → Pipeline | Follow target = the local seat's actor (committed + previous position via Body's view, `tick_alpha`); **local raw aim** for look-ahead regardless of beam state; `v_walk/v_run/v_max` in whole px/tick (2/3/3) for the G check; zoom actions owned here, consumed there; mouse-to-world via C11. Matches the pipeline's Dependencies row ("follow target … facing/beam direction for any look-ahead; `tick_alpha` interpolation of the sprite") | firm |
  | 9 | **HUD & Suit Layer** | Controller → HUD | Hand rail (tool + keybind glyphs by active device), tool state, hold-to-confirm bar, prompts at `world_to_hud(target)`; walk-only reason surfaced by the breath/warmth readings, never a text banner | provisional |
  | 10 | **Settings & Input Rebinding** | Settings → Adapter | All actions rebindable; run hold/toggle; aim-follows-movement option; cursor hide; gamepad completeness enumeration (HR-14) — the Adapter reads actions by `StringName` only | provisional |
  | 11 | **Co-op Session & Replication (VS-B)** | Session → kernel → Controller | Guest Adapters submit identically; `controller.state` `SHARED_SUMMARY`; remote bodies drawn from `MIRROR` views with committed aim; no shared camera | seam only in MVP |
  | 12 | **Save/Load & Versioned Format** | via kernel registry | `controller.state` `WORLD`-scoped; restore rules PC-17; death stub consumes `DEAD` | firm (contract) |
  | 13 | **Perception Filter** | Filter reads Controller/Body views | May substitute a whole body for a horror rig; may never move the hand point, edit pixels, or touch the beam (PC-11) | firm (pillar) |
  | 14 | **Web Map & Transit** | Transit → Controller | `pod_hop` → `IN_POD` → arrival body transfer; no pod steering at MVP (abstracted hop) | provisional |
  
  ---
  
  ### Numeric quantities introduced (for Section D)
  
  | Name | Value | Unit | Category | Notes |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `v_walk` | 2 (120 px/s) | base px/tick | feel | alt 1 for playtest |
  | `v_run` | 3 (180 px/s) | base px/tick | feel | hard cap from inner-box invariant (< 200 px/s) |
  | `v_carry` | 1 (60 px/s) | base px/tick | feel/gate | |
  | `v_max` | = `v_run` | — | derived | pipeline G check |
  | `ACCEL_TICKS`, `DECEL_TICKS` | 0 | ticks | feel | `RUN_RAMP_TICKS` ∈ {0, 3} fallback |
  | `BACKPEDAL_FACTOR` | 1.0 | — | feel | integer-only alternatives |
  | `STICK_DEADZONE` | 0.25 | fraction | feel | |
  | `DIR_HYSTERESIS_DEG` | 4 | degrees | feel | 8-way stick quantisation |
  | `AIM_QUANTUM_DEG` | 5 | degrees | curve | sends per sweep vs sim cone accuracy |
  | `AIM_MOUSE_DEADZONE_PX` | 8 | base px | feel | |
  | `FACING_HYSTERESIS_DEG` | 4 | degrees | feel | |
  | `REACH_PX` | 72 | base px | gate | 1.5 tiles |
  | `REACH_HALF_ANGLE_DEG` | 70 | degrees | gate | |
  | `HOLD_CONFIRM_TICKS` | 36 (0.6 s) | render-time ticks-equivalent | gate | local, HR-14 |
  | `STAGGER_TICKS` | 30 (0.5 s) | ticks | feel | |
  | `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` | 1800 (30 s) | ticks | gate | solo MVP placeholder |
  | `NOISE_WALK` / `NOISE_RUN` / `NOISE_CARRY` | 1 / 4 / 1 | Attention stimulus units per tick | curve | placeholders; ratio is the design |
  | channel durations (not owned) | cut 240 / weld 360 / patch 180 | ticks | reference only | Interaction / Assembly set them |
  | capsule (not owned) | ≈ 20 × 12 | base px | reference | Body's GDD |
  | `hand_offset[facing][animation]` | table | base px | feel | from sheets, Section D |
  
  ### Routed corrections and open items
  - **Pipeline GDD:** (a) the operative `v_max` bound is **< 200 px/s** (inner-box invariant), not 266; (b) placeholders 90/150 are non-integer px/tick and are superseded by 120/180; (c) **zoom-in breaks the inner-box invariant** regardless of speeds — at 1080p k = 4 the field is 480×270, `0.30·270 = 81 < 32.4 + 72`; the pipeline must decide whether `L_MAX` scales with the field or the clamp is accepted when zoomed in (post-dates the user's zoom-ladder decision).
  - **User decision needed:** beam available while carrying (recommended) vs beam off while carrying (strong Pillar 3 lever).
  - **Technical-director:** ratify PC-14 (Body owns position).

  # Section C assessment — Player Controller & Input (feel, accessibility, input UX)
  
  **Scope note.** MVP is single-player (game-concept MVP Definition). Co-op, text chat, pings, voice and the crew strip are VS-B; the Settings & Input Rebinding screen is Alpha (systems-index #42) with hooks from MVP (render GDD UI Requirements). Every rule below is tier-tagged. Default key letters are recommendations; the *model* (every action rebindable, conflicts detected, device-aware prompts, mapping as an HR-6 anchor) is the requirement.
  
  Sources read: `D:\the-synaptic-sea-2d\design\gdd\game-concept.md`, `D:\the-synaptic-sea-2d\design\art\art-bible.md` (3.2, 5.1–5.7, 7.0–7.7), `D:\the-synaptic-sea-2d\design\gdd\pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md` (Game Feel, UI Requirements, zoom edge cases, OQ4), `D:\the-synaptic-sea-2d\design\gdd\command-simulation-layer.md` (CR-4, CR-5, CR-7, CR-15, CR-16, Edge Cases line 622, Game Feel, OQ3), `D:\the-synaptic-sea-2d\design\gdd\systems-index.md`.
  
  ---
  
  ## 1. Default bindings and the rebinding model
  
  **Verdict: needs a rule.** No source assigns keys. The sources constrain: HR-6 (input mapping is an anchor no game state may shift), 7.2 (keycap glyph grammar, PlayStation-symbol exception), HR-14 (gamepad completeness), CR-4 (intents vs commands; coalescing), render GDD OQ4 (zoom ladder: integer in/out, `k ∈ [1, k_auto+2]`, persistent, cut per step, Zomboid-style — supersedes the States table's hold-to-zoom).
  
  **Targeting model, singular (hard).** One focus model on every device: **aim-weighted proximity focus among lit interactables within reach** — the lit interactable nearest the aim ray from the hand point, inside reach. Mouse and stick both produce an aim direction; neither is a cursor that can click an unlit object (7.0 prompts are drawn only for lit objects; the game-designer still owns whether an unlit object can be acted on). One prompt rule, one acceptance set, and a mouse player who cannot click what a gamepad player cannot focus.
  
  **Interact is a button, not a verb (hard).** The interact binding submits whichever command type Interaction declares for the focused object (`begin_cut`, `begin_weld`, `begin_patch`, `interact`, `pickup`, `use_item` — CR-4). The controller never chooses the verb and never checks world preconditions.
  
  | Action | Keyboard/mouse default | Gamepad default | Command (CR-4) | Coalesce | Tier |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Move | WASD | Left stick | `set_move_intent` | LATEST_PER_ACTOR_PER_TICK | MVP |
  | Aim | Mouse position → direction from hand point (cursor confined in play) | Right stick (direction) | `set_aim` | LATEST | MVP |
  | Beam toggle | F | Y | `toggle_beam` | NONE | MVP |
  | Interact / contextual action | E (alias: LMB) | A | per focus (Interaction's type) | NONE | MVP |
  | Cancel channel | X (hold-mode: release of E/LMB also cancels) | B | `cancel_channel` | NONE | MVP |
  | Run | Shift (hold; toggle option) | LT (hold; toggle option) | run flag inside `set_move_intent` | LATEST | MVP |
  | Carry / drop | G (pickup if focus is carriable and hands empty; drop if carrying) | X | `pickup` / `drop` | NONE | MVP |
  | Tool select (hand rail) | 1–6 direct; Tab cycles next | RB next / LB previous | equip command (Suit & Equipment's) | NONE | MVP |
  | Zoom in / out (ladder) | Mouse wheel up/down; `=` / `-` | D-pad up / down | presentation only (camera), two edge-triggered actions | — | MVP |
  | Inspect | R (alias: RMB) — press opens, press again/cancel closes | RT | presentation (inspect card) | — | binding reserved MVP; card itself is In-World Instruments' call (art bible 7.6 OQ) |
  | Chart table / pause | Escape | Start/Menu | control plane `request_pause` in solo (CR-15/16); overlay only in co-op | — | MVP |
  | Text chat | Enter | — (keyboard-only, HR-14) | Chat's | — | VS-B |
  | Ping | V (alias: MMB) | D-pad left | Chat/Pings' | NONE | VS-B |
  | Reveal crewmate name | H (press, shows ~2 s) | D-pad right | presentation | — | VS-B |
  | Push-to-talk | T (hold; open-mic option) | — / rebindable | Voice's | — | VS-B |
  | L3 / R3 / View | unbound by default (stick clicks are a motor risk) | — | — | — | — |
  
  The first conflict the model must catch: Zomboid-style zoom takes the wheel, so tool cycling is Tab, not wheel.
  
  **Input contexts (hard, MVP).** `gameplay`, `chart_table`, `inspect_card`, `chat` (VS-B — Enter captures the keyboard and WASD become letters). Entering any non-`gameplay` context sends a zero `set_move_intent`, clears the run latch, and sends `cancel_channel` for any hold-mode channel (the release can no longer be seen). This matters most in co-op, where the chart table is an overlay with the sim running (CR-16): a player must never keep walking while a UI has their keys. The mouse cursor is confined to the window (`MOUSE_MODE_CONFINED`) in `gameplay` so aim direction is always defined, and released in UI contexts; whether a cursor is *drawn* in play is the HUD's/art-director's (a drawn cursor is a screen-space mark that is not an instrument — routed).
  
  **Rebinding model (Alpha UI; MVP data).**
  - MVP: the action map ships as data (one Godot InputMap action per row, per device), and prompts resolve from that map, so Alpha adds only the screen.
  - Every row rebindable per device (keyboard, mouse buttons, gamepad); aim *source* selectable: mouse / right stick / "follows movement" (keyboard-only and one-stick play).
  - Conflict detection per context: the same physical input bound to two actions in one context is a conflict, shown inline on the row ("Also: Cut") with a swap offered; never silently overwritten; cross-context reuse is allowed (A = interact in play, confirm in menus).
  - A profile with no bound path to the chart table is refused (no lock-out).
  - Presets: default; left-hand (arrows / IJKL); one-hand-left keyboard (aim follows movement); one-hand-right (mouse + numpad); gamepad default; gamepad southpaw (sticks swapped).
  - Device-aware prompts: glyph = the binding on the active device, 7.2 keycap grammar; PlayStation symbol inside the keycap; an unbound action's prompt shows "—" in the keycap, never hides the verb.
  - Anchor (HR-6): no sanity, Attention, breach or scar state may alter bindings, swap axes, invert, or change deadzones. Lint-able: the input adapter never requests a Sanity, Attention or `PERCEPTION_OUT` view.
  
  ---
  
  ## 2. Gamepad completeness at MVP
  
  **Verdict: supports (HR-14), needs the enumeration and the aim rule.**
  
  **Gamepad-complete at MVP:** boot and title; chart table (pick target, pause, save/load, settings — bracket focus snapping node-to-node, 7.4); move and run; aim and beam; interact channels (cut/weld/patch) via A on the focused lit object; carry/drop; tool select; inspect card (if it ships); zoom ladder; abstracted pod hop (a chart-table action); hold-to-confirm destructive actions (cut-away section, delete save) on the 7.3 linear bar.
  **Keyboard-only at MVP:** none. **Keyboard-only at VS-B:** text chat (HR-14's single permitted item).
  
  **Aim rule (hard).** Right stick is an absolute direction from the hand point, not a cursor. Comfort permitted: radial deadzone (default 0.20, range 0.10–0.35) with **scaled radial** remapping (not axial), outer deadzone 0.90, response curve exponent 1.0 default (range 1.0–2.0). Comfort forbidden: any magnetism, snap, slow-down or widening near targets (render GDD anti-target "auto-aim"), and any **input-side aim smoothing** by default — the camera already eases look-ahead from *local raw* aim (τ 0.40 s, slew 144 px/s); smoothing stacked under it reads as lag. Stick released: **hold last aim** (default); option "aim follows movement when the stick is idle" (also the one-stick mode).
  
  **Raw vs quantised aim (hard, MVP).** The *local* beam `Light2D` renders from local raw aim in the same frame, exactly as look-ahead does (presentation reads raw aim; a mouse sweep is continuous, never 128 discrete beam angles). The adapter submits `set_aim` on change at a **1/128-turn quantum** (≈ 2.8°), coalesced LATEST per tick; the committed value is authoritative for facing (item 5) and for what other clients render (VS-B may coarsen the replicated value; it must not coarsen facing below the hysteresis below).
  
  ---
  
  ## 3. Accessibility
  
  **Verdict: needs a rule** (sources forbid hidden meters and shake but say nothing about hold vs toggle).
  
  - **Run: hold default, toggle option (MVP, hard).** The toggle auto-clears when move intent has been zero for `RUN_LATCH_CLEAR` ticks (default 30, range 15–60), on channel start, and on entering a UI context. Why: run is an Attention stimulus; a latched run on the next step is a trap the player did not choose.
  - **Channels: hold default, toggle option (MVP, hard).** Hold mode: press sends `begin_*`, release sends `cancel_channel`. Toggle mode: press begins; cancel on second press, on the cancel binding, or on movement intent (game-designer confirms walk-away cancels). Both are adapter policy over the same commands; the sim never knows which mode is on.
  - **One-handed layouts (Alpha UI; MVP must not preclude).** Keyboard-only aim must exist (aim follows movement) or a one-handed preset cannot play. Mouse-only play is out of scope; flagged.
  - **Latency (MVP, hard).** Acknowledgement same frame; effect ≤ 1 tick + 1 render frame (kernel Game Feel). The adapter polls at render rate and submits intents on quantised change. A press is never dropped by presentation: edge-triggered inputs are `coalesce = NONE`; a press during a cut or `RESCALING` frame still submits. No "queue the next action" buffer at MVP — `BUSY` is an honest rejection.
  - **`STALE` resubmit (MVP, hard; kernel Edge Cases line 622).** On `Rejected(STALE)` for a coalescing type, the adapter immediately resubmits its current value, bypassing the quantised-change filter for one send.
  - **No QTEs (hard).** No timed single-input prompts, no mashing, no input whose window is shorter than a hold-to-confirm. Breach is time pressure in the world, never a prompt.
  - **Hold-to-confirm (MVP, hard).** 7.3 linear bar with needle-mark, never radial. `CONFIRM_HOLD` default 0.8 s (range 0.6–1.2); release before completion drains the bar at 2× rate; the bar is on the focused control's plate. **Tap-to-confirm option:** two taps — first arms (bracket thickens, label changes to "Confirm?"), second within `ARM_WINDOW` 3 s confirms; never a single tap, or the destructive guard vanishes.
  - **Flicker ceiling (HR-13).** Any armed/rejected pulse the controller drives stays ≤ 3 Hz; nothing on the HUD shakes.
  - **Haptics (hard, HR-6).** Driven by P1 events only; a master toggle; never by Attention, sanity or the Perception Filter.
  
  ---
  
  ## 4. Comfort
  
  **Run is noisy, with no meter (verdict: supports, needs a rule).** Self-tells already in the sources: the 5.2 run has a whole-figure forward lean (a visible self-tell); the camera lags ≈ 0.6 tile at run speed (render GDD) so the frame itself changes; Attention rising is shown at the cone edge (2.7 filaments, dust) and heard first (HR-9). Rule: **the player's own running footsteps must be audible and distinct from walking at all times** (louder, faster, plus suit-pack rattle — the audio-director owns the sound; this owns that it exists). For deaf/HoH players the lean is the visual channel and captions name it under the R-6 policy ("your footsteps, running"). No meter, no screen effect.
  
  **Device switching (hard, MVP).** Mapping is an anchor; only the *prompt glyph set* and the *aim source* follow the device.
  - **Glyph device** = the device of the last *button or key* press (axes need no prompt, and keying on axis motion would flip glyphs constantly under the mixed input permitted below), with 250 ms hysteresis. Glyphs swap in ≤ 1 frame, silently: no popup, no toast, no mode.
  - **Aim source** = the last aim axis with qualifying input (mouse motion > 4 px, or stick beyond deadzone). Switching to the stick holds the last mouse aim until the stick deflects; switching to the mouse adopts the mouse direction on the first qualifying motion (never a snap to facing).
  - The HR-11 focus bracket appears on keyboard/gamepad navigation and hides on mouse motion; menus keep the last focused item. Mixed input (keyboard move + stick aim) is permitted.
  
  ---
  
  ## 5. Facing and the five drawn facings
  
  **Verdict: supports (5.6), needs a derivation rule.** 5.6 already dissolves the lag question: the beam is 360° engine light from a per-facing hand point; the sprite is 8-way. With the local beam rendered from raw aim (item 2) the mouse never waits for the sprite or the tick. 5.2's stiff style has no turn frames, so a snap is in-style.
  
  Rules (MVP, hard):
  - **Facing derives from committed aim every tick, no easing.** The change applies mid-animation-cycle with the frame index preserved (never waiting for a cycle boundary — that is the one thing that would read as lag).
  - **Hysteresis in quanta:** facing switches only when aim leaves the current 45° sector by `FACING_HYST` aim quanta (default 2 quanta ≈ 5.6°, range 1–3), so a cursor on a boundary never chatters. Lives in the Controller's derivation, not the adapter.
  - **Aim-live → face aim; aim idle → face movement; both idle → hold.** On mouse, aim is always live (absolute position relative to the body), so facing follows the cursor and backpedalling exists. On gamepad, a centred stick holds the last aim (item 2) unless the follow-movement option is on.
  - **Beam state does not change the rule.** The render GDD reads look-ahead from aim regardless of beam lit state; facing must agree with where the frame leans. *Flag for game-designer:* confirm "face aim when the beam is off" — a different answer would make body and camera disagree.
  - **Reduced motion:** look-ahead is zeroed there, so beam direction and facing become the *only* aim confirmation the body gives — the immediacy rule is load-bearing, not polish.
  - Hand-point jumps at a facing change (largest on the E↔W mirror, where the tool changes hands) are accepted per 5.6; the beam direction stays continuous across them.
  - Facing is Controller-owned `SIM` state (kernel OQ3's proposal) because other clients place the beam origin from it.
  
  ---
  
  ## 6. Channel feedback
  
  **Verdict: supports (CR-4/CR-5), needs the presentation rule and two conflicts resolved.** Conflicts: CR-4's "progress ring" is a radial wipe, forbidden by 7.3 — progress is a **linear bar with needle-mark**; CR-5's "shake" as rejection feedback is forbidden by HR-13 (and jolt is 0 at MVP) — rejection is never shake.
  
  | Moment | Must see | Must hear | Source |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Start | Same-frame ack: work loop begins, tool forward; the object's prompt plate changes from `E · Cut` to the linear bar at 0 | tool start sound, same frame | CR-4 ack rule; 5.2 work loop |
  | Confirmed (next tick) | bar begins advancing; in-world P1 evidence begins (cut line, weld bead, sparks) | tool running loop | CR-5 `Applied` |
  | Progress | bar advances honestly; the world shows the work | continuous tool sound | P1 |
  | Cancel (player) | ack same frame: hand drops, bar drains ~150 ms; partial work stays visible in the world if progress persists (game-designer) | "stopped" cue | `cancel_channel` |
  | Abort (world: power drop, light lost) | arrives as channel-state change, not a result; bar holds then drains; the cause is visible in the world (the trail, the beam out) | a distinct "interrupted" cue | CR-5 abort clause |
  | Completion | bar settles full (7.3 settle); hand returns; object changes state in the world; prompt shows the next verb or disappears | completion sound | `Applied` |
  | Rejection, immediate class | ack withdrawn: hand stops, bar removed, prompt verb goes Graphite lit for 300 ms; a short chart-table-register tooltip ("Too far") is allowed | short "no" tool cue; never shake | CR-5 |
  
  **Rejection classes (hard).** *Immediate* reasons falsify nothing and may be shown at once: `OUT_OF_RANGE`, `BUSY`, `INVALID_TARGET`, `ACTOR_NOT_OWNED`, `PAUSED`, kernel admission reasons. *Deferred* reasons could be a free lie-detector (`PRECONDITION` on a device perceived broken but actually working — class (b), MVP). The kernel rejects these at P2 from SIM truth, so the result reaches the controller within one tick; **the controller does not withdraw the ack on a `Rejected` whose reason Interaction flags as deferred** — it keeps the work loop and bar running and withdraws only when Interaction's channel state signals the reveal (Interaction owns the deferred-channel state and the time it charges). The same-frame ack therefore **never encodes success**, only "I tried". QA rule: the ack frame for a command that will be applied and for one that will be deferred-rejected must be pixel- and sound-identical.
  
  **Flag for art-director / HUD:** the channel bar needs a declared home. Proposal: on the object's prompt plate (chart-table register, anchor — it is the player's own hand's work, not the object's state, so it is not a reading and cannot lie).
  
  ---
  
  ## 7. Co-op bodies (VS-B)
  
  **Verdict: supports (3.2, 5.1, 5.5, 7.5), one gap.** A crewmate is their beam shape and band count, confirmed by voice; no name tags (7.5). **Gap: self-identity.** The crew strip shows crewmates; nothing on the HUD tells the player *their own* beam shape and band count. Rule: the player's own identity glyph (beam shape + bands, Tungsten fixture) sits on the suit panel as an anchor, so they can match themselves in a room of four beams. Secondary self-cues: the camera holds the local body in the central 60 % of frame; the local beam responds to local raw aim this frame.
  
  Decisions 7.5 hands to this role, made here:
  - **Hold-to-reveal name: yes.** A press (not a hold) shows names for ~2 s over crewmates inside the viewer's light, chart-table register, anchor, never for unlit crewmates.
  - **Pings: exist at VS-B,** mark a thing (never locate a crewmate), **lit objects only** (answering the Principle 1 question 7.5 left open), chamfered Tungsten-fixture mark, chart-table register, anchor, never hero-sized.
  
  **The controller must never (hard):** issue or acknowledge input for an actor the local seat is not bound to (the kernel rejects `ACTOR_NOT_OWNED`; presentation must not ack it first); provide any shared, assisted or remote control of a crewmate; route a dead player's input anywhere but camera and chart table until the binding table rebinds them (a body transfer is a cut; input during the cut frame is dropped without ack); check sanity for friendly harm (Interaction's validate on `SIM` sanity); alter mapping, aim, deadzone or facing per sanity, Attention or the Perception Filter; fake the speaker indicator or text chat (HR-6 anchors).
  
  ---
  
  ## Hard requirements
  
  1. (MVP) One focus model on all devices: aim-weighted proximity among lit interactables within reach; the controller never chooses the verb.
  2. (MVP) Every action in the table is an InputMap action; every one rebindable per device; conflicts detected per context (`gameplay`, `chart_table`, `inspect_card`, `chat`) and never silently overwritten; no profile without a chart-table path. (Alpha: the screen.)
  3. (MVP) Input mapping, deadzones and aim source are HR-6 anchors: no game state reads into or alters them; the adapter never requests a Sanity, Attention or `PERCEPTION_OUT` view.
  4. (MVP) Entering any non-gameplay context sends zero move intent, clears the run latch and cancels hold-mode channels; cursor confined in play, released in UI.
  5. (MVP) Gamepad-complete flows as enumerated in item 2; keyboard-only set is empty at MVP and exactly {text chat} at VS-B.
  6. (MVP) Right-stick aim: radial deadzone, scaled remap, no magnetism, no input-side smoothing by default; stick released holds last aim.
  7. (MVP) Local beam renders from local raw aim in the same frame; `set_aim` is quantised at 1/128 turn and committed aim is authoritative for facing and remote rendering.
  8. (MVP) Run and channels: hold default with a toggle option; run toggle auto-clears on stop, on channel start and on UI entry.
  9. (MVP) Ack same frame; effect ≤ 1 tick + 1 frame; presses never dropped by presentation; `STALE` on a coalescing type triggers an immediate resubmit.
  10. (MVP) No QTEs. Hold-to-confirm on the 7.3 linear bar, 0.8 s default; tap-to-confirm is two-tap arm/confirm.
  11. (MVP) Own running footsteps audible and distinct from walking; no Attention meter under any setting.
  12. (MVP) Device switch: glyphs follow the last button/key device, aim source follows the last aim axis; silent, ≤ 1 frame, 250 ms hysteresis; no popup.
  13. (MVP) Facing derives from committed aim every tick, no easing, mid-cycle, with 2-quanta sector hysteresis; aim-live → aim, aim idle → movement; beam state does not change it.
  14. (MVP) Channel feedback per the table; progress is a linear bar, never a ring; rejection is never shake; the ack never encodes success; on a deferred-class `Rejected` the ack is held until Interaction's reveal.
  15. (MVP) Zoom ladder bound as two edge-triggered actions (not a hold), a cut per step, works under reduced motion.
  16. (MVP) Chart table binding does not assume pause: solo = `request_pause`; co-op = overlay with the sim running (CR-16).
  17. (MVP) Nothing the controller drives on the HUD pulses above 3 Hz or shakes (HR-13); haptics from P1 events only.
  18. (VS-B) No shared or assisted control; input only for the bound actor; the controller never checks sanity; own identity glyph on the suit panel.
  
  ## Recommendations
  
  - (MVP) The default letters and buttons in the table; L3/R3/View unbound by default.
  - (MVP) Tab cycles tools; wheel is zoom (the first conflict the model catches).
  - (MVP) Inspect as a press-toggle that auto-closes when the instrument leaves reach or goes unlit; binding reserved even if the card is deferred.
  - (MVP) Channel bar lives on the object's prompt plate as an anchor (art-director to confirm).
  - (MVP) Tuning knobs with ranges: `RUN_LATCH_CLEAR` 30 ticks (15–60); aim quantum 1/128 turn; `FACING_HYST` 2 quanta (1–3); deadzone 0.20 (0.10–0.35), outer 0.90; curve exponent 1.0 (1.0–2.0); `CONFIRM_HOLD` 0.8 s (0.6–1.2); `ARM_WINDOW` 3 s; device hysteresis 250 ms; mouse-motion threshold 4 px.
  - (Alpha) Presets: left-hand, one-hand-left (aim follows movement), one-hand-right, southpaw.
  - (VS-B) Press-to-reveal names (~2 s, lit only); pings on lit objects only; push-to-talk on T with open-mic option.
  
  ## Routed questions (one line each)
  
  - game-designer: does the body face aim when the beam is off (must match the camera's look-ahead rule)? Does movement cancel a channel? Does partial channel progress persist? Can unlit objects be acted on?
  - Interaction System: which domain reasons are immediate vs deferred; how `PRECONDITION` on a perceived-broken device is charged before reveal (the deferred-channel state the controller waits on).
  - In-World Instruments: does the inspect card ship at MVP (art bible 7.6)?
  - art-director / HUD: home of the channel bar; own-identity glyph on the suit panel; whether a cursor is drawn in play.
  - audio-director: run footstep signature; "stopped" vs "interrupted" vs "no" cues.
  - accessibility-specialist: captions naming the player's own run; one-hand presets review; the Attention-channel gap (7.6 item 15) is unchanged by anything here.
  - Co-op Session (VS-B): whether replicated aim may be coarsened below 1/128 turn (never below facing hysteresis).

content.thinking:
The primary draft is in GDD shape now. I'm noting disagreements with the gameplay-programmer: on position ownership, I'll go with the primary's take that Body owns it (matching the kernel proposal) over Controller-owns-as-one-block, though I'll flag it provisional for TD review; diagonal residue is fine since both are Bresenham-ish; and the run ramp still needs resolving since gameplay wants an integer-only ramp of 6 ticks at walk speed before running.

I'll settle on RUN_RAMP_TICKS = 6 with a 0–12 range, since the walk-speed ramp doesn't actually block the "escape must cost zero wind-up" pillar — 100ms at walk speed still lets you leave. For input buffering, I'm siding with the primary's no-buffer approach (tap during channel → BUSY) since it's simpler and keeps the sim honest, with ACTION_BUFFER_TICKS defaulting to 0 as a knob rather than gameplay's 6-tick local buffer. On facing, I'm adopting the primary's more considered 6-rule priority system (running favors movement facing, beam lit favors aim) over gameplay's always-facing-from-aim-with-reversed-backpedal approach.

For backpedaling, I'll keep primary's rule that the same animation cycle plays, but adopt gameplay's reversed-frame-order idea as a presenter-level detail rather than a core mechanic. Both sides agree beam light only changes on commit. For v_carry I'm taking primary's 1 px/tick over gameplay's 2, since it's the more visible design lever.

For collision shapes, I'm noting the discrepancy between gameplay's 16×8 foot box and primary's 20×12 capsule placeholder, deferring to Body's spec while recording both. Aim threshold is agreed at 5° by both, and I'm adopting gameplay's additions of a settle-send and rate limit. I'm also adopting adapter sampling happening in the physics callback before the step, and noting that hand-rolled collision (no CharacterBody2D) is a hard constraint from Body's ADR that needs to be routed as a requirement. The zoom-in inner-box issue goes to the pipeline as an open consistency question, and the beam-while-carrying question needs a user decision.

Since gameplay has a lever available for the recommended beam state, I'll take that as the default and flag it for the next user touchpoint.
