  **Scope note.** MVP is single-player (game-concept MVP Definition). Co-op, text chat, pings, voice and the crew strip are VS-B; the Settings & Input Rebinding screen is Alpha (systems-index #42) with hooks from MVP (render GDD UI Requirements). Every rule below is tier-tagged. Default key letters are recommendations; the *model* (every action rebindable, conflicts detected, device-aware prompts, mapping as an HR-6 anchor) is the requirement.
  
  Sources read: `D:\the-synaptic-sea-2d\design\gdd\game-concept.md`, `D:\the-synaptic-sea-2d\design\art\art-bible.md` (3.2, 5.1–5.7, 7.0–7.7), `D:\the-synaptic-sea-2d\design\gdd\pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md` (Game Feel, UI Requirements, zoom edge cases, OQ4), `D:\the-synaptic-sea-2d\design\gdd\command-simulation-layer.md` (CR-4, CR-5, CR-7, CR-15, CR-16, Edge Cases line 622, Game Feel, OQ3), `D:\the-synaptic-sea-2d\design\gdd\systems-index.md`.
  
  ---
  
  ## 1. Default bindings and the rebinding model
  
  **Verdict: needs a rule.** No source assigns keys. The sources constrain: HR-6 (input mapping is an anchor no game state may shift), 7.2 (keycap glyph grammar, PlayStation-symbol exception), HR-14 (gamepad completeness), CR-4 (intents vs commands; coalescing), render GDD OQ4 (zoom ladder: integer in/out, `k ∈ [1, k_auto+2]`, persistent, cut per step, Zomboid-style — supersedes the States table's hold-to-zoom).
  
  **Targeting model, singular (hard).** One focus model on every device: **aim-weighted proximity focus among lit interactables within reach** — the lit interactable nearest the aim ray from the hand point, inside reach. Mouse and stick both produce an aim direction; neither is a cursor that can click an unlit object (7.0 prompts are drawn only for lit objects; the game-designer still owns whether an unlit object can be acted on). One prompt rule, one acceptance set, and a mouse player who cannot click what a gamepad player cannot focus.
  
  **Interact is a button, not a verb (hard).** The interact binding submits whichever command type Interaction declares for the focused object (`begin_cut`, `begin_weld`, `begin_patch`, `interact`, `pickup`, `use_item` — CR-4). The controller never chooses the verb and never checks world preconditions.
  
  | Action | Keyboard/mouse default | Gamepad default | Command (CR-4) | Coalesce | Tier |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Move | WASD | Left stick | `set_move_intent` | LATEST_PER_ACTOR_PER_TICK | MVP |
  | Aim | Mouse position → direction from hand point (cursor confined in play) | Right stick (direction) | `set_aim` | LATEST | MVP |
  | Beam toggle | F | Y | `toggle_beam` | NONE | MVP |
  | Interact / contextual action | E (alias: LMB) | A | per focus (Interaction's type) | NONE | MVP |
  | Cancel channel | X (hold-mode: release of E/LMB also cancels) | B | `cancel_channel` | NONE | MVP |
  | Run | Shift (hold; toggle option) | LT (hold; toggle option) | run flag inside `set_move_intent` | LATEST | MVP |
  | Carry / drop | G (pickup if focus is carriable and hands empty; drop if carrying) | X | `pickup` / `drop` | NONE | MVP |
  | Tool select (hand rail) | 1–6 direct; Tab cycles next | RB next / LB previous | equip command (Suit & Equipment's) | NONE | MVP |
  | Zoom in / out (ladder) | Mouse wheel up/down; `=` / `-` | D-pad up / down | presentation only (camera), two edge-triggered actions | — | MVP |
  | Inspect | R (alias: RMB) — press opens, press again/cancel closes | RT | presentation (inspect card) | — | binding reserved MVP; card itself is In-World Instruments' call (art bible 7.6 OQ) |
  | Chart table / pause | Escape | Start/Menu | control plane `request_pause` in solo (CR-15/16); overlay only in co-op | — | MVP |
  | Text chat | Enter | — (keyboard-only, HR-14) | Chat's | — | VS-B |
  | Ping | V (alias: MMB) | D-pad left | Chat/Pings' | NONE | VS-B |
  | Reveal crewmate name | H (press, shows ~2 s) | D-pad right | presentation | — | VS-B |
  | Push-to-talk | T (hold; open-mic option) | — / rebindable | Voice's | — | VS-B |
  | L3 / R3 / View | unbound by default (stick clicks are a motor risk) | — | — | — | — |
  
  The first conflict the model must catch: Zomboid-style zoom takes the wheel, so tool cycling is Tab, not wheel.
  
  **Input contexts (hard, MVP).** `gameplay`, `chart_table`, `inspect_card`, `chat` (VS-B — Enter captures the keyboard and WASD become letters). Entering any non-`gameplay` context sends a zero `set_move_intent`, clears the run latch, and sends `cancel_channel` for any hold-mode channel (the release can no longer be seen). This matters most in co-op, where the chart table is an overlay with the sim running (CR-16): a player must never keep walking while a UI has their keys. The mouse cursor is confined to the window (`MOUSE_MODE_CONFINED`) in `gameplay` so aim direction is always defined, and released in UI contexts; whether a cursor is *drawn* in play is the HUD's/art-director's (a drawn cursor is a screen-space mark that is not an instrument — routed).
  
  **Rebinding model (Alpha UI; MVP data).**
  - MVP: the action map ships as data (one Godot InputMap action per row, per device), and prompts resolve from that map, so Alpha adds only the screen.
  - Every row rebindable per device (keyboard, mouse buttons, gamepad); aim *source* selectable: mouse / right stick / "follows movement" (keyboard-only and one-stick play).
  - Conflict detection per context: the same physical input bound to two actions in one context is a conflict, shown inline on the row ("Also: Cut") with a swap offered; never silently overwritten; cross-context reuse is allowed (A = interact in play, confirm in menus).
  - A profile with no bound path to the chart table is refused (no lock-out).
  - Presets: default; left-hand (arrows / IJKL); one-hand-left keyboard (aim follows movement); one-hand-right (mouse + numpad); gamepad default; gamepad southpaw (sticks swapped).
  - Device-aware prompts: glyph = the binding on the active device, 7.2 keycap grammar; PlayStation symbol inside the keycap; an unbound action's prompt shows "—" in the keycap, never hides the verb.
  - Anchor (HR-6): no sanity, Attention, breach or scar state may alter bindings, swap axes, invert, or change deadzones. Lint-able: the input adapter never requests a Sanity, Attention or `PERCEPTION_OUT` view.
  
  ---
  
  ## 2. Gamepad completeness at MVP
  
  **Verdict: supports (HR-14), needs the enumeration and the aim rule.**
  
  **Gamepad-complete at MVP:** boot and title; chart table (pick target, pause, save/load, settings — bracket focus snapping node-to-node, 7.4); move and run; aim and beam; interact channels (cut/weld/patch) via A on the focused lit object; carry/drop; tool select; inspect card (if it ships); zoom ladder; abstracted pod hop (a chart-table action); hold-to-confirm destructive actions (cut-away section, delete save) on the 7.3 linear bar.
  **Keyboard-only at MVP:** none. **Keyboard-only at VS-B:** text chat (HR-14's single permitted item).
  
  **Aim rule (hard).** Right stick is an absolute direction from the hand point, not a cursor. Comfort permitted: radial deadzone (default 0.20, range 0.10–0.35) with **scaled radial** remapping (not axial), outer deadzone 0.90, response curve exponent 1.0 default (range 1.0–2.0). Comfort forbidden: any magnetism, snap, slow-down or widening near targets (render GDD anti-target "auto-aim"), and any **input-side aim smoothing** by default — the camera already eases look-ahead from *local raw* aim (τ 0.40 s, slew 144 px/s); smoothing stacked under it reads as lag. Stick released: **hold last aim** (default); option "aim follows movement when the stick is idle" (also the one-stick mode).
  
  **Raw vs quantised aim (hard, MVP).** The *local* beam `Light2D` renders from local raw aim in the same frame, exactly as look-ahead does (presentation reads raw aim; a mouse sweep is continuous, never 128 discrete beam angles). The adapter submits `set_aim` on change at a **1/128-turn quantum** (≈ 2.8°), coalesced LATEST per tick; the committed value is authoritative for facing (item 5) and for what other clients render (VS-B may coarsen the replicated value; it must not coarsen facing below the hysteresis below).
  
  ---
  
  ## 3. Accessibility
  
  **Verdict: needs a rule** (sources forbid hidden meters and shake but say nothing about hold vs toggle).
  
  - **Run: hold default, toggle option (MVP, hard).** The toggle auto-clears when move intent has been zero for `RUN_LATCH_CLEAR` ticks (default 30, range 15–60), on channel start, and on entering a UI context. Why: run is an Attention stimulus; a latched run on the next step is a trap the player did not choose.
  - **Channels: hold default, toggle option (MVP, hard).** Hold mode: press sends `begin_*`, release sends `cancel_channel`. Toggle mode: press begins; cancel on second press, on the cancel binding, or on movement intent (game-designer confirms walk-away cancels). Both are adapter policy over the same commands; the sim never knows which mode is on.
  - **One-handed layouts (Alpha UI; MVP must not preclude).** Keyboard-only aim must exist (aim follows movement) or a one-handed preset cannot play. Mouse-only play is out of scope; flagged.
  - **Latency (MVP, hard).** Acknowledgement same frame; effect ≤ 1 tick + 1 render frame (kernel Game Feel). The adapter polls at render rate and submits intents on quantised change. A press is never dropped by presentation: edge-triggered inputs are `coalesce = NONE`; a press during a cut or `RESCALING` frame still submits. No "queue the next action" buffer at MVP — `BUSY` is an honest rejection.
  - **`STALE` resubmit (MVP, hard; kernel Edge Cases line 622).** On `Rejected(STALE)` for a coalescing type, the adapter immediately resubmits its current value, bypassing the quantised-change filter for one send.
  - **No QTEs (hard).** No timed single-input prompts, no mashing, no input whose window is shorter than a hold-to-confirm. Breach is time pressure in the world, never a prompt.
  - **Hold-to-confirm (MVP, hard).** 7.3 linear bar with needle-mark, never radial. `CONFIRM_HOLD` default 0.8 s (range 0.6–1.2); release before completion drains the bar at 2× rate; the bar is on the focused control's plate. **Tap-to-confirm option:** two taps — first arms (bracket thickens, label changes to "Confirm?"), second within `ARM_WINDOW` 3 s confirms; never a single tap, or the destructive guard vanishes.
  - **Flicker ceiling (HR-13).** Any armed/rejected pulse the controller drives stays ≤ 3 Hz; nothing on the HUD shakes.
  - **Haptics (hard, HR-6).** Driven by P1 events only; a master toggle; never by Attention, sanity or the Perception Filter.
  
  ---
  
  ## 4. Comfort
  
  **Run is noisy, with no meter (verdict: supports, needs a rule).** Self-tells already in the sources: the 5.2 run has a whole-figure forward lean (a visible self-tell); the camera lags ≈ 0.6 tile at run speed (render GDD) so the frame itself changes; Attention rising is shown at the cone edge (2.7 filaments, dust) and heard first (HR-9). Rule: **the player's own running footsteps must be audible and distinct from walking at all times** (louder, faster, plus suit-pack rattle — the audio-director owns the sound; this owns that it exists). For deaf/HoH players the lean is the visual channel and captions name it under the R-6 policy ("your footsteps, running"). No meter, no screen effect.
  
  **Device switching (hard, MVP).** Mapping is an anchor; only the *prompt glyph set* and the *aim source* follow the device.
  - **Glyph device** = the device of the last *button or key* press (axes need no prompt, and keying on axis motion would flip glyphs constantly under the mixed input permitted below), with 250 ms hysteresis. Glyphs swap in ≤ 1 frame, silently: no popup, no toast, no mode.
  - **Aim source** = the last aim axis with qualifying input (mouse motion > 4 px, or stick beyond deadzone). Switching to the stick holds the last mouse aim until the stick deflects; switching to the mouse adopts the mouse direction on the first qualifying motion (never a snap to facing).
  - The HR-11 focus bracket appears on keyboard/gamepad navigation and hides on mouse motion; menus keep the last focused item. Mixed input (keyboard move + stick aim) is permitted.
  
  ---
  
  ## 5. Facing and the five drawn facings
  
  **Verdict: supports (5.6), needs a derivation rule.** 5.6 already dissolves the lag question: the beam is 360° engine light from a per-facing hand point; the sprite is 8-way. With the local beam rendered from raw aim (item 2) the mouse never waits for the sprite or the tick. 5.2's stiff style has no turn frames, so a snap is in-style.
  
  Rules (MVP, hard):
  - **Facing derives from committed aim every tick, no easing.** The change applies mid-animation-cycle with the frame index preserved (never waiting for a cycle boundary — that is the one thing that would read as lag).
  - **Hysteresis in quanta:** facing switches only when aim leaves the current 45° sector by `FACING_HYST` aim quanta (default 2 quanta ≈ 5.6°, range 1–3), so a cursor on a boundary never chatters. Lives in the Controller's derivation, not the adapter.
  - **Aim-live → face aim; aim idle → face movement; both idle → hold.** On mouse, aim is always live (absolute position relative to the body), so facing follows the cursor and backpedalling exists. On gamepad, a centred stick holds the last aim (item 2) unless the follow-movement option is on.
  - **Beam state does not change the rule.** The render GDD reads look-ahead from aim regardless of beam lit state; facing must agree with where the frame leans. *Flag for game-designer:* confirm "face aim when the beam is off" — a different answer would make body and camera disagree.
  - **Reduced motion:** look-ahead is zeroed there, so beam direction and facing become the *only* aim confirmation the body gives — the immediacy rule is load-bearing, not polish.
  - Hand-point jumps at a facing change (largest on the E↔W mirror, where the tool changes hands) are accepted per 5.6; the beam direction stays continuous across them.
  - Facing is Controller-owned `SIM` state (kernel OQ3's proposal) because other clients place the beam origin from it.
  
  ---
  
  ## 6. Channel feedback
  
  **Verdict: supports (CR-4/CR-5), needs the presentation rule and two conflicts resolved.** Conflicts: CR-4's "progress ring" is a radial wipe, forbidden by 7.3 — progress is a **linear bar with needle-mark**; CR-5's "shake" as rejection feedback is forbidden by HR-13 (and jolt is 0 at MVP) — rejection is never shake.
  
  | Moment | Must see | Must hear | Source |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Start | Same-frame ack: work loop begins, tool forward; the object's prompt plate changes from `E · Cut` to the linear bar at 0 | tool start sound, same frame | CR-4 ack rule; 5.2 work loop |
  | Confirmed (next tick) | bar begins advancing; in-world P1 evidence begins (cut line, weld bead, sparks) | tool running loop | CR-5 `Applied` |
  | Progress | bar advances honestly; the world shows the work | continuous tool sound | P1 |
  | Cancel (player) | ack same frame: hand drops, bar drains ~150 ms; partial work stays visible in the world if progress persists (game-designer) | "stopped" cue | `cancel_channel` |
  | Abort (world: power drop, light lost) | arrives as channel-state change, not a result; bar holds then drains; the cause is visible in the world (the trail, the beam out) | a distinct "interrupted" cue | CR-5 abort clause |
  | Completion | bar settles full (7.3 settle); hand returns; object changes state in the world; prompt shows the next verb or disappears | completion sound | `Applied` |
  | Rejection, immediate class | ack withdrawn: hand stops, bar removed, prompt verb goes Graphite lit for 300 ms; a short chart-table-register tooltip ("Too far") is allowed | short "no" tool cue; never shake | CR-5 |
  
  **Rejection classes (hard).** *Immediate* reasons falsify nothing and may be shown at once: `OUT_OF_RANGE`, `BUSY`, `INVALID_TARGET`, `ACTOR_NOT_OWNED`, `PAUSED`, kernel admission reasons. *Deferred* reasons could be a free lie-detector (`PRECONDITION` on a device perceived broken but actually working — class (b), MVP). The kernel rejects these at P2 from SIM truth, so the result reaches the controller within one tick; **the controller does not withdraw the ack on a `Rejected` whose reason Interaction flags as deferred** — it keeps the work loop and bar running and withdraws only when Interaction's channel state signals the reveal (Interaction owns the deferred-channel state and the time it charges). The same-frame ack therefore **never encodes success**, only "I tried". QA rule: the ack frame for a command that will be applied and for one that will be deferred-rejected must be pixel- and sound-identical.
  
  **Flag for art-director / HUD:** the channel bar needs a declared home. Proposal: on the object's prompt plate (chart-table register, anchor — it is the player's own hand's work, not the object's state, so it is not a reading and cannot lie).
  
  ---
  
  ## 7. Co-op bodies (VS-B)
  
  **Verdict: supports (3.2, 5.1, 5.5, 7.5), one gap.** A crewmate is their beam shape and band count, confirmed by voice; no name tags (7.5). **Gap: self-identity.** The crew strip shows crewmates; nothing on the HUD tells the player *their own* beam shape and band count. Rule: the player's own identity glyph (beam shape + bands, Tungsten fixture) sits on the suit panel as an anchor, so they can match themselves in a room of four beams. Secondary self-cues: the camera holds the local body in the central 60 % of frame; the local beam responds to local raw aim this frame.
  
  Decisions 7.5 hands to this role, made here:
  - **Hold-to-reveal name: yes.** A press (not a hold) shows names for ~2 s over crewmates inside the viewer's light, chart-table register, anchor, never for unlit crewmates.
  - **Pings: exist at VS-B,** mark a thing (never locate a crewmate), **lit objects only** (answering the Principle 1 question 7.5 left open), chamfered Tungsten-fixture mark, chart-table register, anchor, never hero-sized.
  
  **The controller must never (hard):** issue or acknowledge input for an actor the local seat is not bound to (the kernel rejects `ACTOR_NOT_OWNED`; presentation must not ack it first); provide any shared, assisted or remote control of a crewmate; route a dead player's input anywhere but camera and chart table until the binding table rebinds them (a body transfer is a cut; input during the cut frame is dropped without ack); check sanity for friendly harm (Interaction's validate on `SIM` sanity); alter mapping, aim, deadzone or facing per sanity, Attention or the Perception Filter; fake the speaker indicator or text chat (HR-6 anchors).
  
  ---
  
  ## Hard requirements
  
  1. (MVP) One focus model on all devices: aim-weighted proximity among lit interactables within reach; the controller never chooses the verb.
  2. (MVP) Every action in the table is an InputMap action; every one rebindable per device; conflicts detected per context (`gameplay`, `chart_table`, `inspect_card`, `chat`) and never silently overwritten; no profile without a chart-table path. (Alpha: the screen.)
  3. (MVP) Input mapping, deadzones and aim source are HR-6 anchors: no game state reads into or alters them; the adapter never requests a Sanity, Attention or `PERCEPTION_OUT` view.
  4. (MVP) Entering any non-gameplay context sends zero move intent, clears the run latch and cancels hold-mode channels; cursor confined in play, released in UI.
  5. (MVP) Gamepad-complete flows as enumerated in item 2; keyboard-only set is empty at MVP and exactly {text chat} at VS-B.
  6. (MVP) Right-stick aim: radial deadzone, scaled remap, no magnetism, no input-side smoothing by default; stick released holds last aim.
  7. (MVP) Local beam renders from local raw aim in the same frame; `set_aim` is quantised at 1/128 turn and committed aim is authoritative for facing and remote rendering.
  8. (MVP) Run and channels: hold default with a toggle option; run toggle auto-clears on stop, on channel start and on UI entry.
  9. (MVP) Ack same frame; effect ≤ 1 tick + 1 frame; presses never dropped by presentation; `STALE` on a coalescing type triggers an immediate resubmit.
  10. (MVP) No QTEs. Hold-to-confirm on the 7.3 linear bar, 0.8 s default; tap-to-confirm is two-tap arm/confirm.
  11. (MVP) Own running footsteps audible and distinct from walking; no Attention meter under any setting.
  12. (MVP) Device switch: glyphs follow the last button/key device, aim source follows the last aim axis; silent, ≤ 1 frame, 250 ms hysteresis; no popup.
  13. (MVP) Facing derives from committed aim every tick, no easing, mid-cycle, with 2-quanta sector hysteresis; aim-live → aim, aim idle → movement; beam state does not change it.
  14. (MVP) Channel feedback per the table; progress is a linear bar, never a ring; rejection is never shake; the ack never encodes success; on a deferred-class `Rejected` the ack is held until Interaction's reveal.
  15. (MVP) Zoom ladder bound as two edge-triggered actions (not a hold), a cut per step, works under reduced motion.
  16. (MVP) Chart table binding does not assume pause: solo = `request_pause`; co-op = overlay with the sim running (CR-16).
  17. (MVP) Nothing the controller drives on the HUD pulses above 3 Hz or shakes (HR-13); haptics from P1 events only.
  18. (VS-B) No shared or assisted control; input only for the bound actor; the controller never checks sanity; own identity glyph on the suit panel.
  
  ## Recommendations
  
  - (MVP) The default letters and buttons in the table; L3/R3/View unbound by default.
  - (MVP) Tab cycles tools; wheel is zoom (the first conflict the model catches).
  - (MVP) Inspect as a press-toggle that auto-closes when the instrument leaves reach or goes unlit; binding reserved even if the card is deferred.
  - (MVP) Channel bar lives on the object's prompt plate as an anchor (art-director to confirm).
  - (MVP) Tuning knobs with ranges: `RUN_LATCH_CLEAR` 30 ticks (15–60); aim quantum 1/128 turn; `FACING_HYST` 2 quanta (1–3); deadzone 0.20 (0.10–0.35), outer 0.90; curve exponent 1.0 (1.0–2.0); `CONFIRM_HOLD` 0.8 s (0.6–1.2); `ARM_WINDOW` 3 s; device hysteresis 250 ms; mouse-motion threshold 4 px.
  - (Alpha) Presets: left-hand, one-hand-left (aim follows movement), one-hand-right, southpaw.
  - (VS-B) Press-to-reveal names (~2 s, lit only); pings on lit objects only; push-to-talk on T with open-mic option.
  
  ## Routed questions (one line each)
  
  - game-designer: does the body face aim when the beam is off (must match the camera's look-ahead rule)? Does movement cancel a channel? Does partial channel progress persist? Can unlit objects be acted on?
  - Interaction System: which domain reasons are immediate vs deferred; how `PRECONDITION` on a perceived-broken device is charged before reveal (the deferred-channel state the controller waits on).
  - In-World Instruments: does the inspect card ship at MVP (art bible 7.6)?
  - art-director / HUD: home of the channel bar; own-identity glyph on the suit panel; whether a cursor is drawn in play.
  - audio-director: run footstep signature; "stopped" vs "interrupted" vs "no" cues.

The mouse cursor is confined to the window (`MOUSE_MODE_CONFINED`) in `gameplay` so aim direction is always defined, and released in UI contexts; whether a cursor is *drawn* in play is the HUD's/art-director's (a drawn cursor is a screen-space mark that is not an instrument — routed).

---

## 2. Gamepad completeness at MVP

**Verdict: supports (HR-14), needs the enumeration and the aim rule.**

**Gamepad-complete at MVP:** boot and title; chart table (pick target, pause, save/load, settings — bracket focus snapping node-to-node, 7.4); move and run; aim and beam; interact channels (cut/weld/patch) via A on the focused lit object; carry/drop; tool select; inspect card (if it ships); zoom ladder; abstracted pod hop (a chart-table action); hold-to-confirm destructive actions (cut-away section, delete save) on the 7.3 linear bar.
**Keyboard-only at MVP:** none. **Keyboard-only at VS-B:** text chat (HR-14's single permitted item).

**Aim rule (hard).** Right stick is an absolute direction from the hand point, not a cursor. Comfort permitted: radial deadzone (default 0.20, range 0.10–0.35) with **scaled radial** remapping (not axial), outer deadzone 0.90, response curve exponent 1.0 default (range 1.0–2.0). Comfort forbidden: any magnetism, snap, slow-down or widening near targets (render GDD anti-target "auto-aim"), and any **input-side aim smoothing** by default — the camera already eases look-ahead from *local raw* aim (τ 0.40 s, slew 144 px/s); smoothing stacked under it reads as lag. Stick released: **hold last aim** (default); option "aim follows movement when the stick is idle" (also the one-stick mode).

**Raw vs quantised aim (hard, MVP).** The *local* beam `Light2D` renders from local raw aim in the same frame, exactly as look-ahead does (presentation reads raw aim; a mouse sweep is continuous, never 128 discrete beam angles). The adapter submits `set_aim` on change at a **1/128-turn quantum** (≈ 2.8°), coalesced LATEST per tick; the committed value is authoritative for facing (item 5) and for what other clients render (VS-B may coarsen the replicated value; it must not coarsen facing below the hysteresis below).

---

## 3. Accessibility

**Verdict: needs a rule** (sources forbid hidden meters and shake but say nothing about hold vs toggle).

- **Run: hold default, toggle option (MVP, hard).** The toggle auto-clears when move intent has been zero for `RUN_LATCH_CLEAR` ticks (default 30, range 15–60), on channel start, and on entering a UI context. Why: run is an Attention stimulus; a latched run on the next step is a trap the player did not choose.
- **Channels: hold default, toggle option (MVP, hard).** Hold mode: press sends `begin_*`, release sends `cancel_channel`. Toggle mode: press begins; cancel on second press, on the cancel binding, or on movement intent (game-designer confirms walk-away cancels). Both are adapter policy over the same commands; the sim never knows which mode is on.
- **One-handed layouts (Alpha UI; MVP must not preclude).** Keyboard-only aim must exist (aim follows movement) or a one-handed preset cannot play. Mouse-only play is out of scope; flagged.
- **Latency (MVP, hard).** Acknowledgement same frame; effect ≤ 1 tick + 1 render frame (kernel Game Feel). The adapter polls at render rate and submits intents on quantised change. A press is never dropped by presentation: edge-triggered inputs are `coalesce = NONE`; a press during a cut or `RESCALING` frame still submits. No "queue the next action" buffer at MVP — `BUSY` is an honest rejection.
- **`STALE` resubmit (MVP, hard; kernel Edge Cases line 622).** On `Rejected(STALE)` for a coalescing type, the adapter immediately resubmits its current value, bypassing the quantised-change filter for one send.
- **No QTEs (hard).** No timed single-input prompts, no mashing, no input whose window is shorter than a hold-to-confirm. Breach is time pressure in the world, never a prompt.
- **Hold-to-confirm (MVP, hard).** 7.3 linear bar with needle-mark, never radial. `CONFIRM_HOLD` default 0.8 s (range 0.6–1.2); release before completion drains the bar at 2× rate; the bar is on the focused control's plate. **Tap-to-confirm option:** two taps — first arms (bracket thickens, label changes to "Confirm?"), second within `ARM_WINDOW` 3 s confirms; never a single tap, or the destructive guard vanishes.
- **Flicker ceiling (HR-13).** Any armed/rejected pulse the controller drives stays ≤ 3 Hz; nothing on the HUD shakes.
- **Haptics (hard, HR-6).** Driven by P1 events only; a master toggle; never by Attention, sanity or the Perception Filter.

---

## 4. Comfort

**Run is noisy, with no meter (verdict: supports, needs a rule).** Self-tells already in the sources: the 5.2 run has a whole-figure forward lean (a visible self-tell); the camera lags ≈ 0.6 tile at run speed (render GDD) so the frame itself changes; Attention rising is shown at the cone edge (2.7 filaments, dust) and heard first (HR-9). Rule: **the player's own running footsteps must be audible and distinct from walking at all times** (louder, faster, plus suit-pack rattle — the audio-director owns the sound; this owns that it exists). For deaf/HoH players the lean is the visual channel and captions name it under the R-6 policy ("your footsteps, running"). No meter, no screen effect.

**Device switching (hard, MVP).** Mapping is an anchor; only the *prompt glyph set* and the *aim source* follow the device.
- **Glyph device** = the device of the last *button or key* press (axes need no prompt, and keying on axis motion would flip glyphs constantly under the mixed input permitted below), with 250 ms hysteresis. Glyphs swap in ≤ 1 frame, silently: no popup, no toast, no mode.
- **Aim source** = the last aim axis with qualifying input (mouse motion > 4 px, or stick beyond deadzone). Switching to the stick holds the last mouse aim until the stick deflects; switching to the mouse adopts the mouse direction on the first qualifying motion (never a snap to facing).
- The HR-11 focus bracket appears on keyboard/gamepad navigation and hides on mouse motion; menus keep the last focused item. Mixed input (keyboard move + stick aim) is permitted.

---

## 5. Facing and the five drawn facings

**Verdict: supports (5.6), needs a derivation rule.** 5.6 already dissolves the lag question: the beam is 360° engine light from a per-facing hand point; the sprite is 8-way. With the local beam rendered from raw aim (item 2) the mouse never waits for the sprite or the tick. 5.2's stiff style has no turn frames, so a snap is in-style.

Rules (MVP, hard):
- **Facing derives from committed aim every tick, no easing.** The change applies mid-animation-cycle with the frame index preserved (never waiting for a cycle boundary — that is the one thing that would read as lag).
- **Hysteresis in quanta:** facing switches only when aim leaves the current 45° sector by `FACING_HYST` aim quanta (default 2 quanta ≈ 5.6°, range 1–3), so a cursor on a boundary never chatters. Lives in the Controller's derivation, not the adapter.
- **Aim-live → face aim; aim idle → face movement; both idle → hold.** On mouse, aim is always live (absolute position relative to the body), so facing follows the cursor and backpedalling exists. On gamepad, a centred stick holds the last aim (item 2) unless the follow-movement option is on.
- **Beam state does not change the rule.** The render GDD reads look-ahead from aim regardless of beam lit state; facing must agree with where the frame leans. *Flag for game-designer:* confirm "face aim when the beam is off" — a different answer would make body and camera disagree.
- **Reduced motion:** look-ahead is zeroed there, so beam direction and facing become the *only* aim confirmation the body gives — the immediacy rule is load-bearing, not polish.
- Hand-point jumps at a facing change (largest on the E↔W mirror, where the tool changes hands) are accepted per 5.6; the beam direction stays continuous across them.
- Facing is Controller-owned `SIM` state (kernel OQ3's proposal) because other clients place the beam origin from it.

---

## 6. Channel feedback

**Verdict: supports (CR-4/CR-5), needs the presentation rule and two conflicts resolved.** Conflicts: CR-4's "progress ring" is a radial wipe, forbidden by 7.3 — progress is a **linear bar with needle-mark**; CR-5's "shake" as rejection feedback is forbidden by HR-13 (and jolt is 0 at MVP) — rejection is never shake.

| Moment | Must see | Must hear | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Start | Same-frame ack: work loop begins, tool forward; the object's prompt plate changes from `E · Cut` to the linear bar at 0 | tool start sound, same frame | CR-4 ack rule; 5.2 work loop |
| Confirmed (next tick) | bar begins advancing; in-world P1 evidence begins (cut line, weld bead, sparks) | tool running loop | CR-5 `Applied` |
| Progress | bar advances honestly; the world shows the work | continuous tool sound | P1 |
| Cancel (player) | ack same frame: hand drops, bar drains ~150 ms; partial work stays visible in the world if progress persists (game-designer) | "stopped" cue | `cancel_channel` |
| Abort (world: power drop, light lost) | arrives as channel-state change, not a result; bar holds then drains; the cause is visible in the world (the trail, the beam out) | a distinct "interrupted" cue | CR-5 abort clause |
| Completion | bar settles full (7.3 settle); hand returns; object changes state in the world; prompt shows the next verb or disappears | completion sound | `Applied` |
| Rejection, immediate class | ack withdrawn: hand stops, bar removed, prompt verb goes Graphite lit for 300 ms; a short chart-table-register tooltip ("Too far") is allowed | short "no" tool cue; never shake | CR-5 |

**Rejection classes (hard).** *Immediate* reasons falsify nothing and may be shown at once: `OUT_OF_RANGE`, `BUSY`, `INVALID_TARGET`, `ACTOR_NOT_OWNED`, `PAUSED`, kernel admission reasons. *Deferred* reasons could be a free lie-detector (`PRECONDITION` on a device perceived broken but actually working — class (b), MVP). The kernel rejects these at P2 from SIM truth, so the result reaches the controller within one tick; **the controller does not withdraw the ack on a `Rejected` whose reason Interaction flags as deferred** — it keeps the work loop and bar running and withdraws only when Interaction's channel state signals the reveal (Interaction owns the deferred-channel state and the time it charges). The same-frame ack therefore **never encodes success**, only "I tried". QA rule: the ack frame for a command that will be applied and for one that will be deferred-rejected must be pixel- and sound-identical.

**Flag for art-director / HUD:** the channel bar needs a declared home. Proposal: on the object's prompt plate (chart-table register, anchor — it is the player's own hand's work, not the object's state, so it is not a reading and cannot lie).

---

## 7. Co-op bodies (VS-B)

**Verdict: supports (3.2, 5.1, 5.5, 7.5), one gap.** A crewmate is their beam shape and band count, confirmed by voice; no name tags (7.5). **Gap: self-identity.** The crew strip shows crewmates; nothing on the HUD tells the player *their own* beam shape and band count. Rule: the player's own identity glyph (beam shape + bands, Tungsten fixture) sits on the suit panel as an anchor, so they can match themselves in a room of four beams. Secondary self-cues: the camera holds the local body in the central 60 % of frame; the local beam responds to local raw aim this frame.

Decisions 7.5 hands to this role, made here:
- **Hold-to-reveal name: yes.** A press (not a hold) shows names for ~2 s over crewmates inside the viewer's light, chart-table register, anchor, never for unlit crewmates.
- **Pings: exist at VS-B,** mark a thing (never locate a crewmate), **lit objects only** (answering the Principle 1 question 7.5 left open), chamfered Tungsten-fixture mark, chart-table register, anchor, never hero-sized.

**The controller must never (hard):** issue or acknowledge input for an actor the local seat is not bound to (the kernel rejects `ACTOR_NOT_OWNED`; presentation must not ack it first); provide any shared, assisted or remote control of a crewmate; route a dead player's input anywhere but camera and chart table until the binding table rebinds them (a body transfer is a cut; input during the cut frame is dropped without ack); check sanity for friendly harm (Interaction's validate on `SIM` sanity); alter mapping, aim, deadzone or facing per sanity, Attention or the Perception Filter; fake the speaker indicator or text chat (HR-6 anchors).

---

## Hard requirements

1. (MVP) One focus model on all devices: aim-weighted proximity among lit interactables within reach; the controller never chooses the verb.
2. (MVP) Every action in the table is an InputMap action; every one rebindable per device; conflicts detected per context (`gameplay`, `chart_table`, `inspect_card`, `chat`) and never silently overwritten; no profile without a chart-table path. (Alpha: the screen.)
3. (MVP) Input mapping, deadzones and aim source are HR-6 anchors: no game state reads into or alters them; the adapter never requests a Sanity, Attention or `PERCEPTION_OUT` view.
4. (MVP) Entering any non-gameplay context sends zero move intent, clears the run latch and cancels hold-mode channels; cursor confined in play, released in UI.
5. (MVP) Gamepad-complete flows as enumerated in item 2; keyboard-only set is empty at MVP and exactly {text chat} at VS-B.
6. (MVP) Right-stick aim: radial deadzone, scaled remap, no magnetism, no input-side smoothing by default; stick released holds last aim.
7. (MVP) Local beam renders from local raw aim in the same frame; `set_aim` is quantised at 1/128 turn and committed aim is authoritative for facing and remote rendering.
8. (MVP) Run and channels: hold default with a toggle option; run toggle auto-clears on stop, on channel start and on UI entry.
9. (MVP) Ack same frame; effect ≤ 1 tick + 1 frame; presses never dropped by presentation; `STALE` on a coalescing type triggers an immediate resubmit.
10. (MVP) No QTEs. Hold-to-confirm on the 7.3 linear bar, 0.8 s default; tap-to-confirm is two-tap arm/confirm.
11. (MVP) Own running footsteps audible and distinct from walking; no Attention meter under any setting.
12. (MVP) Device switch: glyphs follow the last button/key device, aim source follows the last aim axis; silent, ≤ 1 frame, 250 ms hysteresis; no popup.
13. (MVP) Facing derives from committed aim every tick, no easing, mid-cycle, with 2-quanta sector hysteresis; aim-live → aim, aim idle → movement; beam state does not change it.
14. (MVP) Channel feedback per the table; progress is a linear bar, never a ring; rejection is never shake; the ack never encodes success; on a deferred-class `Rejected` the ack is held until Interaction's reveal.
15. (MVP) Zoom ladder bound as two edge-triggered actions (not a hold), a cut per step, works under reduced motion.
16. (MVP) Chart table binding does not assume pause: solo = `request_pause`; co-op = overlay with the sim running (CR-16).
17. (MVP) Nothing the controller drives on the HUD pulses above 3 Hz or shakes (HR-13); haptics from P1 events only.
18. (VS-B) No shared or assisted control; input only for the bound actor; the controller never checks sanity; own identity glyph on the suit panel.

## Recommendations

- (MVP) The default letters and buttons in the table; L3/R3/View unbound by default.
- (MVP) Tab cycles tools; wheel is zoom (the first conflict the model catches).
- (MVP) Inspect as a press-toggle that auto-closes when the instrument leaves reach or goes unlit; binding reserved even if the card is deferred.
- (MVP) Channel bar lives on the object's prompt plate as an anchor (art-director to confirm).
- (MVP) Tuning knobs with ranges: `RUN_LATCH_CLEAR` 30 ticks (15–60); aim quantum 1/128 turn; `FACING_HYST` 2 quanta (1–3); deadzone 0.20 (0.10–0.35), outer 0.90; curve exponent 1.0 (1.0–2.0); `CONFIRM_HOLD` 0.8 s (0.6–1.2); `ARM_WINDOW` 3 s; device hysteresis 250 ms; mouse-motion threshold 4 px.
- (Alpha) Presets: left-hand, one-hand-left (aim follows movement), one-hand-right, southpaw.
- (VS-B) Press-to-reveal names (~2 s, lit only); pings on lit objects only; push-to-talk on T with open-mic option.

## Routed questions (one line each)

- game-designer: does the body face aim when the beam is off (must match the camera's look-ahead rule)? Does movement cancel a channel? Does partial channel progress persist? Can unlit objects be acted on?
- Interaction System: which domain reasons are immediate vs deferred; how `PRECONDITION` on a perceived-broken device is charged before reveal (the deferred-channel state the controller waits on).
- In-World Instruments: does the inspect card ship at MVP (art bible 7.6)?
- art-director / HUD: home of the channel bar; own-identity glyph on the suit panel; whether a cursor is drawn in play.
- audio-director: run footstep signature; "stopped" vs "interrupted" vs "no" cues.
- accessibility-specialist: captions naming the player's own run; one-hand presets review; the Attention-channel gap (7.6 item 15) is unchanged by anything here.
- Co-op Session (VS-B): whether replicated aim may be coarsened below 1/128 turn (never below facing hysteresis).

  **Keyboard-only at MVP:** none. **Keyboard-only at VS-B:** text chat (HR-14's single permitted item).
  
  **Aim rule (hard).** Right stick is an absolute direction from the hand point, not a cursor. Comfort permitted: radial deadzone (default 0.20, range 0.10–0.35) with **scaled radial** remapping (not axial), outer deadzone 0.90, response curve exponent 1.0 default (range 1.0–2.0). Comfort forbidden: any magnetism, snap, slow-down or widening near targets (render GDD anti-target "auto-aim"), and any **input-side aim smoothing** by default — the camera already eases look-ahead from *local raw* aim (τ 0.40 s, slew 144 px/s); smoothing stacked under it reads as lag. Stick released: **hold last aim** (default); option "aim follows movement when the stick is idle" (also the one-stick mode).
  
  **Raw vs quantised aim (hard, MVP).** The *local* beam `Light2D` renders from local raw aim in the same frame, exactly as look-ahead does (presentation reads raw aim; a mouse sweep is continuous, never 128 discrete beam angles). The adapter submits `set_aim` on change at a **1/128-turn quantum** (≈ 2.8°), coalesced LATEST per tick; the committed value is authoritative for facing (item 5) and for what other clients render (VS-B may coarsen the replicated value; it must not coarsen facing below the hysteresis below).
  
  ---
  
  ## 3. Accessibility

  - **Run: hold default, toggle option (MVP, hard).** The toggle auto-clears when move intent has been zero for `RUN_LATCH_CLEAR` ticks (default 30, range 15–60), on channel start, and on entering a UI context. Why: run is an Attention stimulus; a latched run on the next step is a trap the player did not choose.
  - **Channels: hold default, toggle option (MVP, hard).** Hold mode: press sends `begin_*`, release sends `cancel_channel`. Toggle mode: press begins; cancel on second press, on the cancel binding, or on movement intent (game-designer confirms walk-away cancels). Both are adapter policy over the same commands; the sim never knows which mode is on.
  - **One-handed layouts (Alpha UI; MVP must not preclude).** Keyboard-only aim must exist (aim follows movement) or a one-handed preset cannot play. Mouse-only play is out of scope; flagged.
  - **Latency (MVP, hard).** Acknowledgement same frame; effect ≤ 1 tick + 1 render frame (kernel Game Feel). The adapter polls at render rate and submits intents on quantised change. A press is never dropped by presentation: edge-triggered inputs are `coalesce = NONE`; a press during a cut or `RESCALING` frame still submits. No "queue the next action" buffer at MVP — `BUSY` is an honest rejection.
  - **`STALE` resubmit (MVP, hard; kernel Edge Cases line 622).** On `Rejected(STALE)` for a coalescing type, the adapter immediately resubmits its current value, bypassing the quantised-change filter for one send.
  - **No QTEs (hard).** No timed single-input prompts, no mashing, no input whose window is shorter than a hold-to-confirm. Breach is time pressure in the world, never a prompt.
  - **Hold-to-confirm (MVP, hard).** 7.3 linear bar with needle-mark, never radial. `CONFIRM_HOLD` default 0.8 s (range 0.6–1.2); release before completion drains the bar at 2× rate; the bar is on the focused control's plate. **Tap-to-confirm option:** two taps — first arms (bracket thickens, label changes to "Confirm?"), second within `ARM_WINDOW` 3 s confirms; never a single tap, or the destructive guard vanishes.
  - **Flicker ceiling (HR-13).** Any armed/rejected pulse the controller drives stays ≤ 3 Hz; nothing on the HUD shakes.
  - **Haptics (hard, HR-6).** Driven by P1 events only; a master toggle; never by Attention, sanity or the Perception Filter.
  
  ---
  
  ## 4. Comfort
  
  **Run is noisy, with no meter (verdict: supports, needs a rule).** Self-tells already in the sources: the 5.2 run has a whole-figure forward lean (a visible self-tell); the camera lags ≈ 0.6 tile at run speed (render GDD) so the frame itself changes; Attention rising is shown at the cone edge (2.7 filaments, dust) and heard first (HR-9). Rule: **the player's own running footsteps must be audible and distinct from walking at all times** (louder, faster, plus suit-pack rattle — the audio-director owns the sound; this owns that it exists). For deaf/HoH players the lean is the visual channel and captions name it under the R-6 policy ("your footsteps, running"). No meter, no screen effect.
  
  **Device switching (hard, MVP).** Mapping is an anchor; only the *prompt glyph set* and the *aim source* follow the device.
  - **Glyph device** = the device of the last *button or key* press (axes need no prompt, and keying on axis motion would flip glyphs constantly under the mixed input permitted below), with 250 ms hysteresis. Glyphs swap in ≤ 1 frame, silently: no popup, no toast, no mode.
  - **Aim source** = the last aim axis with qualifying input (mouse motion > 4 px, or stick beyond deadzone). Switching to the stick holds the last mouse aim until the stick deflects; switching to the mouse adopts the mouse direction on the first qualifying motion (never a snap to facing).
  - The HR-11 focus bracket appears on keyboard/gamepad navigation and hides on mouse motion; menus keep the last focused item. Mixed input (keyboard move + stick aim) is permitted.
  
  ---
  
  ## 5. Facing and the five drawn facings
  
  **Verdict: supports (5.6), needs a derivation rule.** 5.6 already dissolves the lag question: the beam is 360° engine light from a per-facing hand point; the sprite is 8-way. With the local beam rendered from raw aim (item 2) the mouse never waits for the sprite or the tick. 5.2's stiff style has no turn frames, so a snap is in-style.
  
  Rules (MVP, hard):
  - **Facing derives from committed aim every tick, no easing.** The change applies mid-animation-cycle with the frame index preserved (never waiting for a cycle boundary — that is the one thing that would read as lag).
  - **Hysteresis in quanta:** facing switches only when aim leaves the current 45° sector by `FACING_HYST` aim quanta (default 2 quanta ≈ 5.6°, range 1–3), so a cursor on a boundary never chatters. Lives in the Controller's derivation, not the adapter.
  - **Aim-live → face aim; aim idle → face movement; both idle → hold.** On mouse, aim is always live (absolute position relative to the body), so facing follows the cursor and backpedalling exists. On gamepad, a centred stick holds the last aim (item 2) unless the follow-movement option is on.
  - **Beam state does not change the rule.** The render GDD reads look-ahead from aim regardless of beam lit state; facing must agree with where the frame leans. *Flag for game-designer:* confirm "face aim when the beam is off" — a different answer would make body and camera disagree.
  - **Reduced motion:** look-ahead is zeroed there, so beam direction and facing become the *only* aim confirmation the body gives — the immediacy rule is load-bearing, not polish.
  - Hand-point jumps at a facing change (largest on the E↔W mirror, where the tool changes hands) are accepted per 5.6; the beam direction stays continuous across them.
  - Facing is Controller-owned `SIM` state (kernel OQ3's proposal) because other clients place the beam origin from it.
  
  ---
  
  ## 6. Channel feedback
  
  **Verdict: supports (CR-4/CR-5), needs the presentation rule and two conflicts resolved.** Conflicts: CR-4's "progress ring" is a radial wipe, forbidden by 7.3 — progress is a **linear bar with needle-mark**; CR-5's "shake" as rejection feedback is forbidden by HR-13 (and jolt is 0 at MVP) — rejection is never shake.
  
  | Moment | Must see | Must hear | Source |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Start | Same-frame ack: work loop begins, tool forward; the object's prompt plate changes from `E · Cut` to the linear bar at 0 | tool start sound, same frame | CR-4 ack rule; 5.2 work loop |
  | Confirmed (next tick) | bar begins advancing; in-world P1 evidence begins (cut line, weld bead, sparks) | tool running loop | CR-5 `Applied` |
  | Progress | bar advances honestly; the world shows the work | continuous tool sound | P1 |
  | Cancel (player) | ack same frame: hand drops, bar drains ~150 ms; partial work stays visible in the world if progress persists (game-designer) | "stopped" cue | `cancel_channel` |
  | Abort (world: power drop, light lost) | arrives as channel-state change, not a result; bar holds then drains; the cause is visible in the world (the trail, the beam out) | a distinct "interrupted" cue | CR-5 abort clause |
  | Completion | bar settles full (7.3 settle); hand returns; object changes state in the world; prompt shows the next verb or disappears | completion sound | `Applied` |
  | Rejection, immediate class | ack withdrawn: hand stops, bar removed, prompt verb goes Graphite lit for 300 ms; a short chart-table-register tooltip ("Too far") is allowed | short "no" tool cue; never shake | CR-5 |

The same-frame ack therefore **never encodes success**, only "I tried". QA rule: the ack frame for a command that will be applied and for one that will be deferred-rejected must be pixel- and sound-identical.
  
  **Flag for art-director / HUD:** the channel bar needs a declared home. Proposal: on the object's prompt plate (chart-table register, anchor — it is the player's own hand's work, not the object's state, so it is not a reading and cannot lie).
  
  ---
  
  ## 7. Co-op bodies (VS-B)
  
  **Verdict: supports (3.2, 5.1, 5.5, 7.5), one gap.** A crewmate is their beam shape and band count, confirmed by voice; no name tags (7.5). **Gap: self-identity.** The crew strip shows crewmates; nothing on the HUD tells the player *their own* beam shape and band count. Rule: the player's own identity glyph (beam shape + bands, Tungsten fixture) sits on the suit panel as an anchor, so they can match themselves in a room of four beams. Secondary self-cues: the camera holds the local body in the central 60 % of frame; the local beam responds to local raw aim this frame.

  - **Hold-to-reveal name: yes.** A press (not a hold) shows names for ~2 s over crewmates inside the viewer's light, chart-table register, anchor, never for unlit crewmates.
  - **Pings: exist at VS-B,** mark a thing (never locate a crewmate), **lit objects only** (answering the Principle 1 question 7.5 left open), chamfered Tungsten-fixture mark, chart-table register, anchor, never hero-sized.

  2. (MVP) Every action in the table is an InputMap action; every one rebindable per device; conflicts detected per context (`gameplay`, `chart_table`, `inspect_card`, `chat`) and never silently overwritten; no profile without a chart-table path. (Alpha: the screen.)

input.message:
Produce the FINAL Section C by merging your PC-1..PC-17 draft with the two supporting inputs summarised below (all DECIDED by the orchestrator, autonomous mode, logged 2026-10-26 — integrate as rules, not options). Write to `C:\Users\dasbl\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\D--the-synaptic-sea-2d\e887ccb9-1186-40d9-9566-5eacccbd9b44\scratchpad\s-c-pc-final.md` as four blocks `=== CORE RULES ===`, `=== STATES ===`, `=== INTERACTIONS ===`, `=== QUANTITIES ===` (ready-to-paste bodies, no top-level heading; keep PC-n numbering, add rules as needed), and reply with a short summary plus anything you could not reconcile. Keep: your three-part structure (Adapter / Controller Sim / Presenter), Body owns position (PC-14, provisional for TD), v_walk 2 / v_run 3 / v_carry 1 px/tick, lit-only actions, no crouch/jump/dodge, two-rhythms invariance, noise stimuli, PC-17 seams, and your zoom-in inner-box finding (route to the pipeline GDD).

GAMEPLAY-PROGRAMMER (mechanisms adopted): the avatar has NO physics body — Body integrates a hand-rolled integer kinematic step: `pos: Vector2i` + `sub: Vector2i` in 1/256-px fixed point (an 8-entry integer unit table, diagonal = 181/256), axis-separated 1-px AABB sweeps against the Layout PROJECTOR's integer footprint rectangles (walls 24 px deep per the up-screen convention, closed door leaves, props, machinery), x-then-y every tick, sliding falls out of axis separation, `sub` reset to zero on stop; foot box 16×8 base px (not a 20×12 capsule) — state both as Body's to confirm; the avatar's position is then a pure function of the command stream and layout, so G3 replay needs no physics observations; diagonals normalised to cardinal magnitude (un-normalised run diagonals would exceed the camera's pan ceiling and cut every diagonal sprint); RUN_RAMP_TICKS = 6 at walk speed then run (integer-only, does not block escape) — replaces your instant start; STOP_DECEL_TICKS 0 (range 0–3); the Adapter samples input in the physics callback immediately before `Kernel.step()` (so an intent applies at the next tick's P2 and integrates in P3 of the same tick); `set_aim` stored as `aim_angle: int` in 1/4096-turn units, sent when the quantised value differs by ≥ 1/128 turn (2.8°) OR the source changed OR a settle condition (inside threshold for 6 ticks and differing at all), rate-limited to one per 3 ticks; `set_move_intent {octant 0..8, run}` on change only with 5° octant hysteresis; immediate acknowledgement pre-plays body and sound only, never the effect (light changes on committed state — your PC-5 stands); a `seq → pre-play token` map lets a late result cancel the right pre-play; animation is distance-driven: `odometer` integer accumulated from pixels actually moved (post-collision), frame = floor(odometer/stride) mod 8, STRIDE_WALK 10 / STRIDE_RUN 15 px (12 fps both), presenter writes only frame index, flip_h, integer position, overlay visibility, light position (no scale/rotation/skew — lint); backpedal plays the walk cycle REVERSED when dot(move, facing) < 0 (zero extra frames); hand point rides `floor(interp_pos) + HAND_POINT[facing]`, mirrored `(−x, y)`, art asked to keep |x| ≤ 6 px; stagger/down read from Suit's `locomotion_cap`; `LocomotionStep.step(state, intent, collide: Callable)` as a pure RefCounted for headless tests (list its 12 tests in Interactions or route to Section H); the camera's SECOND inequality `v_max·τ + L_MAX ≤ 108` makes 3 px/tick the integer ceiling (your 200 px/s finding — same conclusion; cite both); NO input buffering (ACTION_BUFFER_TICKS 0 — honest BUSY; your rule stands).

UX-DESIGNER (hard requirements adopted): ONE focus model on all devices — aim-weighted proximity among LIT interactables within reach; the Adapter never chooses the verb (interact is a button; Interaction declares the command type per focused object); the full default-binding table (WASD / left stick; mouse / right stick aim; F / Y beam; E (alias LMB) / A interact; X / B cancel; Shift / LT run, hold default + toggle option with RUN_LATCH_CLEAR 30 ticks auto-clearing on stop, channel start and UI entry; G / X carry-drop; 1–6 + Tab cycle / RB-LB tools — wheel is ZOOM (the first conflict the model catches); wheel or =/− / d-pad up-down zoom ladder as two edge-triggered actions; R (alias RMB) / RT inspect; Esc / Start chart table-pause; L3/R3/View unbound); input CONTEXTS `gameplay / chart_table / inspect_card / chat` — entering a non-gameplay context sends zero move intent, clears the run latch and cancels hold-mode channels; cursor confined in play, released in UI; rebinding model (every action per device, conflicts detected per context and never silently overwritten, no profile without a chart-table path, presets incl. one-handed with aim-follows-movement) as MVP data with the Alpha screen; mapping, deadzones and aim source are HR-6 anchors — the Adapter never requests a Sanity, Attention or PERCEPTION_OUT view; right-stick aim: radial deadzone 0.20 (0.10–0.35) scaled-radial, outer 0.90, curve exponent 1.0, NO magnetism/snap/slow-down and NO input-side smoothing by default, released stick holds last aim (option: follows movement); move deadzone 0.25; the LOCAL beam renders from local raw aim in the same frame; FACING: derives from committed aim every tick, no easing, mid-cycle, 2-quanta sector hysteresis; aim-live → face aim (so mouse players face the cursor and backpedal), aim idle → face movement, both idle → hold; BEAM STATE DOES NOT CHANGE THE FACING RULE (this replaces your "beam lit" condition in PC-4 rules 4–5 — the camera already leans into aim regardless of beam state, and body and camera must agree); keep your rules 1 (frozen), 2 (channel lock) and 3 (running → movement facing); channels: hold default with a toggle option, movement cancels, both modes are Adapter policy over the same commands; no QTEs; hold-to-confirm on the art bible 7.3 LINEAR bar (never a ring — this corrects the kernel's "progress ring" wording) CONFIRM_HOLD 0.8 s (0.6–1.2), release drains at 2×, tap-to-confirm option = two-tap arm/confirm within 3 s; REJECTION CLASSES: immediate reasons (OUT_OF_RANGE, BUSY, INVALID_TARGET, ACTOR_NOT_OWNED, PAUSED, admission) withdraw the ack at once; deferred reasons (PRECONDITION on a perceived-broken device — the free-lie-detector case) do NOT withdraw the ack — the work loop and bar continue until Interaction's channel state signals the reveal; the ack frame for a command that will be applied and one that will be deferred-rejected must be pixel- and sound-identical; rejection is never shake; channel feedback table (start / confirmed / progress / cancel / abort / completion / rejection) with sounds routed to audio-director; own running footsteps audible and distinct from walking (no meter); device switching: glyphs follow the last button/key device with 250 ms hysteresis, aim source follows the last aim axis, silent, ≤ 1 frame, mixed input permitted, bracket shows on key/pad nav and hides on mouse motion; STALE resubmit (your PC-2 resync stands); haptics from P1 events only; VS-B: no shared/assisted control, own identity glyph on the suit panel, press-to-reveal names ~2 s lit-only, pings mark lit things only; chart-table binding = `request_pause` solo, overlay in co-op.

Also record in QUANTITIES: every knob above with defaults and ranges. In Interactions add rows/notes for: Interaction (immediate vs deferred reason classes are its to declare; movement cancels channels — confirmed; partial progress persistence is its rule), HUD (channel bar on the object's prompt plate as an anchor — art-director to confirm; own-identity glyph), audio-director (footstep signatures; stopped/interrupted/no cues), accessibility-specialist (one-hand presets; captions naming own run), In-World Instruments (inspect card at MVP?), Co-op (replicated aim may not be coarsened below facing hysteresis). Keep the "beam while carrying" question for the user (recommended: available).

Section C's three inputs are complete; the UX designer's key contributions are a unified cross-device focus model, input contexts that suppress movement/hold-channels during UI focus, and a two-tier ack rule preventing same-frame acknowledgements from leaking success info. I'm resolving the one real conflict—whether body faces aim with beam off—by having facing follow live aim (except while running) for consistency with the camera, and sending the merge back to the primary.

## Visual/Audio Requirements

The Controller Sim draws nothing; the **Avatar Presenter** (a `PRESENTATION` node, PC-1) does, and it is the one place in the game where the art bible's crewmate rules become runtime requirements:

- **Sheets** (art bible 5.6, 5.7): five drawn facings (S, SE, E, NE, N) and three mirrored by `flip_h`; animations idle 6, walk 8, run 8, work 6, carry-walk 8, stagger 4, down 6; the tool is a separate sprite layer that flips with the body (the tool changes hands on a mirror — accepted); scar and vital overlays follow a per-frame offset table; the helmet's four trim bands are a palette swap, never frames.
- **Cadence** (PC-15): distance-driven at a fixed 12 fps — `STRIDE_WALK` 10 px, `STRIDE_RUN` 15 px, `STRIDE_CARRY` 5 px per frame — from an integer odometer of pixels actually moved, so feet never slide against a wall; backpedal plays the walk cycle reversed. Idle breathes the pack 2–3 px as drawn frames at ~0.5 Hz on `present_time`. *Flag for art-director*: fixed 12 fps with a 15-px run stride, versus a speed-scaled 18 fps run.
- **Stiff-weighted** (5.2): the Presenter writes only frame index, `flip_h`, integer position, overlay visibility and the beam light's position and rotation — never `scale`, `rotation`, `skew` or tweened offsets on the body (lint). Exaggeration only in stagger frames. The run's forward lean is drawn, not computed.
- **Honest body states** (5.3): rime on the plates, visor fog, the stagger and the down animation are overlays and states driven only by Suit's simulation read view; they are a channel of truth and are never used for anything the simulation does not confirm. Sanity is never drawn on the body (no self-tell).
- **Hand point** (PC-5): `HAND_POINT[facing][animation]` from the sheets, mirrored `(−x, y)`, with `|x| ≤ 6` base px so the beam's origin jumps less than an eighth of a tile on a mirror; the beam light rotates freely off-grid from that integer origin.
- **Audio** (routed to audio-director; this GDD owns that they exist): the player's own footsteps audible and distinct between walk and run (louder, faster, suit-pack rattle) — the only Attention feedback for running, since there is no meter; tool start / running / stopped / interrupted / "no" cues (PC-9 channel table); the toggle's click plays on the press while the light changes on commit; haptics from P1 events only. Captions name the player's own run for deaf/HoH players (art bible R-6 policy).

> 📌 **Asset Spec** — the crewmate sheets, tool layer, overlays and hand-point tables are defined here and in art bible 5.7. After the art bible is approved (it is), run `/asset-spec system:player-controller-input` to produce per-asset specs and generation prompts.

input.new_string:
## Game Feel

The target is **a body that is heavy, immediate and the same in every rhythm**. Barotrauma's tempo, your own legs.

- **Immediacy.** Input is sampled in the physics callback immediately before the kernel steps, so an intent applies at the next tick and integrates the first pixel in that same tick; the body moves within ≤ 17 ms plus one render frame. Acknowledgement of a press (hand raise, tool click, footstep cadence) is same-frame; the *effect* (the light, the progress bar) follows the committed state a tick later. The ack never encodes success.
- **Weight without lag.** Walk starts and stops instantly (there is no integer-only ramp at 2 px/tick that would be visible); run ramps for six ticks at walk speed before leaning into 3 px/tick; stops clear the sub-pixel remainder so the first step after a stop is never a 2-px lurch. No deceleration slide, no tile snap — both would be uncaused motion.
- **Speeds** (provisional until the pacing spike and the MVP playtest): walk 2 px/tick (2.5 tiles/s — a 13-tile frame crossed in ~5 s), run 3 px/tick (3.75 tiles/s, the integer ceiling the camera's inner box allows), carry 1 px/tick. Diagonals are normalised to cardinal magnitude; the 1,1,2 / 2,2,2,3 step cadences are what a 144 Hz display will show, and the motion-integrity spike judges them.
- **Facing snaps, the beam flows.** The sprite snaps between eight facings from committed aim with a small hysteresis and preserves the frame index mid-cycle, so a mouse player never waits for a turn; the beam light rotates continuously from local raw aim in the same frame. The hand-point jump on a mirror is accepted and bounded.
- **Rhythm independence.** Nothing in the controller changes between boarding, the Tell and breach — no adrenaline, no speed buff, no reduced noise. Identical input, vitals and load produce identical motion in every state and at every sanity level (acceptance criterion). Running is 1.5× faster and about 2.7× louder per tile: a real trade in a retreat.
- **The body tells the truth.** Stagger is an input lock and animation, never a physics shove; walk-only at CRITICAL vitals is read off the visor fog and the breath reading, never a banner. Rejections are honest and never shake the frame.
- **Comfort.** Run and channels are hold by default with toggle options; the run latch clears on stop, channel start and UI entry; hold-to-confirm 0.8 s on a linear bar with a two-tap option; right-stick aim has a scaled radial deadzone and no magnetism, snap or smoothing; device switching is silent and sub-frame.

*Anti-targets*: analog speed from stick deflection, crouch, jump, dodge, aim assist, auto-vault or auto-step, a breach-only handling change, a channel that locks the feet, QTEs.

input.new_string:
## UI Requirements

The controller has no screens of its own but defines what three HUD and settings surfaces must show:

1. **Prompts and the channel bar** (HUD & Suit Layer, In-World Instruments): one prompt for the single focused lit candidate, drawn at `world_to_hud(target)` through the unjolted camera transform, keybind glyph in the active device's keycap grammar (art bible 7.2) plus the verb Interaction declares; it never clamps to the frame edge and never exists for an unlit object. On channel start the prompt plate becomes the **linear** progress bar with needle-mark (art bible 7.3 — never a ring, which corrects the kernel GDD's "progress ring" wording); the bar fills from committed progress, drains ~150 ms on cancel, holds then drains on a world abort, settles full on completion. Hold-to-confirm uses the same bar on the focused control's plate (0.8 s fill, 2× drain; the two-tap option thickens the bracket and relabels "Confirm?"). The home of the channel bar (object's prompt plate, as an anchor) is routed to the art-director to confirm.
2. **The hand rail** (HUD & Suit Layer): tool glyphs from the hand-tool sprites (art bible 7.2), the bound tool in Tungsten fixture, keybind/button glyphs that swap with the active device in ≤ 1 frame with 250 ms hysteresis and no popup; the carry state; at VS-B the player's **own identity glyph** (beam shape + band count) on the suit panel so they can find themselves among four beams.
3. **Settings & Input Rebinding** (Alpha screen; MVP data): every action in the PC-2 table rebindable per device, conflicts detected per input context and shown inline with a swap, no profile without a path to the chart table; presets (default, left-hand, one-hand-left with aim-follows-movement, one-hand-right, gamepad default, southpaw); run hold/toggle; channel hold/toggle; tap-to-confirm; aim source (mouse / right stick / follows movement); stick deadzones and curve exponent; cursor hide on gamepad; haptics master toggle. Bindings, deadzones and aim source are HR-6 anchors: no game state may read or alter them.

> **📌 UX Flag — Player Controller & Input**: this system has UI requirements (prompts and channel bar, hand rail, rebinding). In Pre-Production, run `/ux-design` for the HUD prompt/bar spec and the rebinding screen before writing epics; stories should cite `design/ux/hud.md` and `design/ux/settings.md`, not this GDD directly. ## Visual/Audio Requirements

The Controller Sim draws nothing; the **Avatar Presenter** (a `PRESENTATION` node, PC-1) does, and it is the one place in the game where the art bible's crewmate rules become runtime requirements:

- **Sheets** (art bible 5.6, 5.7): five drawn facings (S, SE, E, NE, N) and three mirrored by `flip_h`; animations idle 6, walk 8, run 8, work 6, carry-walk 8, stagger 4, down 6; the tool is a separate sprite layer that flips with the body (the tool changes hands on a mirror — accepted); scar and vital overlays follow a per-frame offset table; the helmet's four trim bands are a palette swap, never frames.
- **Cadence** (PC-15): distance-driven at a fixed 12 fps — `STRIDE_WALK` 10 px, `STRIDE_RUN` 15 px, `STRIDE_CARRY` 5 px per frame — from an integer odometer of pixels actually moved, so feet never slide against a wall; backpedal plays the walk cycle reversed. Idle breathes the pack 2–3 px as drawn frames at ~0.5 Hz on `present_time`. *Flag for art-director*: fixed 12 fps with a 15-px run stride, versus a speed-scaled 18 fps run.
- **Stiff-weighted** (5.2): the Presenter writes only frame index, `flip_h`, integer position, overlay visibility and the beam light's position and rotation — never `scale`, `rotation`, `skew` or tweened offsets on the body (lint). Exaggeration only in stagger frames. The run's forward lean is drawn, not computed.
- **Honest body states** (5.3): rime on the plates, visor fog, the stagger and the down animation are overlays and states driven only by Suit's simulation read view; they are a channel of truth and are never used for anything the simulation does not confirm. Sanity is never drawn on the body (no self-tell).
- **Hand point** (PC-5): `HAND_POINT[facing][animation]` from the sheets, mirrored `(−x, y)`, with `|x| ≤ 6` base px so the beam's origin jumps less than an eighth of a tile on a mirror; the beam light rotates freely off-grid from that integer origin.
- **Audio** (routed to audio-director; this GDD owns that they exist): the player's own footsteps audible and distinct between walk and run (louder, faster, suit-pack rattle) — the only Attention feedback for running, since there is no meter; tool start / running / stopped / interrupted / "no" cues (PC-9 channel table); the toggle's click plays on the press while the light changes on commit; haptics from P1 events only. ## Game Feel

The target is **a body that is heavy, immediate and the same in every rhythm**. Barotrauma's tempo, your own legs.

- **Immediacy.** Input is sampled in the physics callback immediately before the kernel steps, so an intent applies at the next tick and integrates the first pixel in that same tick; the body moves within ≤ 17 ms plus one render frame. Acknowledgement of a press (hand raise, tool click, footstep cadence) is same-frame; the *effect* (the light, the progress bar) follows the committed state a tick later. The ack never encodes success.
- **Weight without lag.** Walk starts and stops instantly (there is no integer-only ramp at 2 px/tick that would be visible); run ramps for six ticks at walk speed before leaning into 3 px/tick; stops clear the sub-pixel remainder so the first step after a stop is never a 2-px lurch. No deceleration slide, no tile snap — both would be uncaused motion.
- **Speeds** (provisional until the pacing spike and the MVP playtest): walk 2 px/tick (2.5 tiles/s — a 13-tile frame crossed in ~5 s), run 3 px/tick (3.75 tiles/s, the integer ceiling the camera's inner box allows), carry 1 px/tick. Diagonals are normalised to cardinal magnitude; the 1,1,2 / 2,2,2,3 step cadences are what a 144 Hz display will show, and the motion-integrity spike judges them.
- **Facing snaps, the beam flows.** The sprite snaps between eight facings from committed aim with a small hysteresis and preserves the frame index mid-cycle, so a mouse player never waits for a turn; the beam light rotates continuously from local raw aim in the same frame. The hand-point jump on a mirror is accepted and bounded.
- **Rhythm independence.** Nothing in the controller changes between boarding, the Tell and breach — no adrenaline, no speed buff, no reduced noise. Identical input, vitals and load produce identical motion in every state and at every sanity level (acceptance criterion). Running is 1.5× faster and about 2.7× louder per tile: a real trade in a retreat.
- **The body tells the truth.** Stagger is an input lock and animation, never a physics shove; walk-only at CRITICAL vitals is read off the visor fog and the breath reading, never a banner. Rejections are honest and never shake the frame.
- **Comfort.** Run and channels are hold by default with toggle options; the run latch clears on stop, channel start and UI entry; hold-to-confirm 0.8 s on a linear bar with a two-tap option; right-stick aim has a scaled radial deadzone and no magnetism, snap or smoothing; device switching is silent and sub-frame.

*Anti-targets*: analog speed from stick deflection, crouch, jump, dodge, aim assist, auto-vault or auto-step, a breach-only handling change, a channel that locks the feet, QTEs.
