## Visual/Audio Requirements

The Controller Sim draws nothing; the **Avatar Presenter** (a `PRESENTATION` node, PC-1) does, and it is the one place in the game where the art bible's crewmate rules become runtime requirements:

- **Sheets** (art bible 5.6, 5.7): five drawn facings (S, SE, E, NE, N) and three mirrored by `flip_h`; animations idle 6, walk 8, run 8, work 6, carry-walk 8, stagger 4, down 6; the tool is a separate sprite layer that flips with the body (the tool changes hands on a mirror — accepted); scar and vital overlays follow a per-frame offset table; the helmet's four trim bands are a palette swap, never frames.
- **Cadence** (PC-15): distance-driven at a fixed 12 fps — `STRIDE_WALK` 10 px, `STRIDE_RUN` 15 px, `STRIDE_CARRY` 5 px per frame — from an integer odometer of pixels actually moved, so feet never slide against a wall; backpedal plays the walk cycle reversed. Idle breathes the pack 2–3 px as drawn frames at ~0.5 Hz on `present_time`. *Flag for art-director*: fixed 12 fps with a 15-px run stride, versus a speed-scaled 18 fps run.
- **Stiff-weighted** (5.2): the Presenter writes only frame index, `flip_h`, integer position, overlay visibility and the beam light's position and rotation — never `scale`, `rotation`, `skew` or tweened offsets on the body (lint). Exaggeration only in stagger frames. The run's forward lean is drawn, not computed.
- **Honest body states** (5.3): rime on the plates, visor fog, the stagger and the down animation are overlays and states driven only by Suit's simulation read view; they are a channel of truth and are never used for anything the simulation does not confirm. Sanity is never drawn on the body (no self-tell).
- **Hand point** (PC-5): `HAND_POINT[facing][animation]` from the sheets, mirrored `(−x, y)`, with `|x| ≤ 6` base px so the beam's origin jumps less than an eighth of a tile on a mirror; the beam light rotates freely off-grid from that integer origin.
- **Audio** (routed to audio-director; this GDD owns that they exist): the player's own footsteps audible and distinct between walk and run (louder, faster, suit-pack rattle) — the only Attention feedback for running, since there is no meter; tool start / running / stopped / interrupted / "no" cues (PC-9 channel table); the toggle's click plays on the press while the light changes on commit; haptics from P1 events only. Captions name the player's own run for deaf/HoH players (art bible R-6 policy).

> 📌 **Asset Spec** — the crewmate sheets, tool layer, overlays and hand-point tables are defined here and in art bible 5.7. After the art bible is approved (it is), run `/asset-spec system:player-controller-input` to produce per-asset specs and generation prompts.

## Game Feel

The target is **a body that is heavy, immediate and the same in every rhythm**. Barotrauma's tempo, your own legs.

- **Immediacy.** Input is sampled in the physics callback immediately before the kernel steps, so an intent applies at the next tick and integrates the first pixel in that same tick; the body moves within ≤ 17 ms plus one render frame. Acknowledgement of a press (hand raise, tool click, footstep cadence) is same-frame; the *effect* (the light, the progress bar) follows the committed state a tick later. The ack never encodes success.
- **Weight without lag.** Walk starts and stops instantly (there is no integer-only ramp at 2 px/tick that would be visible); run ramps for six ticks at walk speed before leaning into 3 px/tick; stops clear the sub-pixel remainder so the first step after a stop is never a 2-px lurch. No deceleration slide, no tile snap — both would be uncaused motion.
- **Speeds** (provisional until the pacing spike and the MVP playtest): walk 2 px/tick (2.5 tiles/s — a 13-tile frame crossed in ~5 s), run 3 px/tick (3.75 tiles/s, the integer ceiling the camera's inner box allows), carry 1 px/tick. Diagonals are normalised to cardinal magnitude; the 1,1,2 / 2,2,2,3 step cadences are what a 144 Hz display will show, and the motion-integrity spike judges them.
- **Facing snaps, the beam flows.** The sprite snaps between eight facings from committed aim with a small hysteresis and preserves the frame index mid-cycle, so a mouse player never waits for a turn; the beam light rotates continuously from local raw aim in the same frame. The hand-point jump on a mirror is accepted and bounded.
- **Rhythm independence.** Nothing in the controller changes between boarding, the Tell and breach — no adrenaline, no speed buff, no reduced noise. Identical input, vitals and load produce identical motion in every state and at every sanity level (acceptance criterion). Running is 1.5× faster and about 2.7× louder per tile: a real trade in a retreat.
- **The body tells the truth.** Stagger is an input lock and animation, never a physics shove; walk-only at CRITICAL vitals is read off the visor fog and the breath reading, never a banner. Rejections are honest and never shake the frame.
- **Comfort.** Run and channels are hold by default with toggle options; the run latch clears on stop, channel start and UI entry; hold-to-confirm 0.8 s on a linear bar with a two-tap option; right-stick aim has a scaled radial deadzone and no magnetism, snap or smoothing; device switching is silent and sub-frame.

*Anti-targets*: analog speed from stick deflection, crouch, jump, dodge, aim assist, auto-vault or auto-step, a breach-only handling change, a channel that locks the feet, QTEs.

## UI Requirements

The controller has no screens of its own but defines what three HUD and settings surfaces must show:

1. **Prompts and the channel bar** (HUD & Suit Layer, In-World Instruments): one prompt for the single focused lit candidate, drawn at `world_to_hud(target)` through the unjolted camera transform, keybind glyph in the active device's keycap grammar (art bible 7.2) plus the verb Interaction declares; it never clamps to the frame edge and never exists for an unlit object. On channel start the prompt plate becomes the **linear** progress bar with needle-mark (art bible 7.3 — never a ring, which corrects the kernel GDD's "progress ring" wording); the bar fills from committed progress, drains ~150 ms on cancel, holds then drains on a world abort, settles full on completion. Hold-to-confirm uses the same bar on the focused control's plate (0.8 s fill, 2× drain; the two-tap option thickens the bracket and relabels "Confirm?"). The home of the channel bar (object's prompt plate, as an anchor) is routed to the art-director to confirm.
2. **The hand rail** (HUD & Suit Layer): tool glyphs from the hand-tool sprites (art bible 7.2), the bound tool in Tungsten fixture, keybind/button glyphs that swap with the active device in ≤ 1 frame with 250 ms hysteresis and no popup; the carry state; at VS-B the player's **own identity glyph** (beam shape + band count) on the suit panel so they can find themselves among four beams.
3. **Settings & Input Rebinding** (Alpha screen; MVP data): every action in the PC-2 table rebindable per device, conflicts detected per input context and shown inline with a swap, no profile without a path to the chart table; presets (default, left-hand, one-hand-left with aim-follows-movement, one-hand-right, gamepad default, southpaw); run hold/toggle; channel hold/toggle; tap-to-confirm; aim source (mouse / right stick / follows movement); stick deadzones and curve exponent; cursor hide on gamepad; haptics master toggle. Bindings, deadzones and aim source are HR-6 anchors: no game state may read or alter them.

> **📌 UX Flag — Player Controller & Input**: this system has UI requirements (prompts and channel bar, hand rail, rebinding). In Pre-Production, run `/ux-design` for the HUD prompt/bar spec and the rebinding screen before writing epics; stories should cite `design/ux/hud.md` and `design/ux/settings.md`, not this GDD directly. Noted for the systems index.

content.text:
Open Questions is written; five sections remain (Formulas, Edge Cases, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria, Summary), and all five are blocked on the systems-designer's D/E/G draft, which is still running. The moment it lands I'll splice the three, send the qa-lead the criteria brief, then write the Summary and run the alignment gate. Nothing else is independent to start.

One thing you can decide meanwhile (Open Question 2): should the **beam stay available while carrying a module** (recommended — the hand point shifts to the carry table), or go **off while carrying** so extraction under rising Attention happens in the dark? It's the single rule that most changes the sortie's difficulty curve.

message.content: I'm sorry....beam?

content.text:
Fair — I've been using the art bible's shorthand. "The beam" is the player's **flashlight**: the cone of light from the hand-held lamp on the suit. The art bible made it the game's hero shape — your flashlight *is* your eye (you can only see what you light), it's your identity in co-op (each crewmate has a distinctive cone shape, like a signature, that hallucinations can never fake), and it's also your exposure, since the web notices light.

So the open question in plain terms: **when you're carrying a salvaged module in both hands, can you still have your flashlight on?**

- **Yes, flashlight stays on** (recommended): the lamp is on the suit, so carrying shifts where the light comes from but doesn't switch it off. Extraction stays readable.
- **No, carrying means hands full, light off**: you haul salvage back to the ship in the dark, feeling your way, with the web's attention rising. Much harder, very tense, and it makes every pickup a real decision.

Which do you want?

message.content: Ohhh, yes yes.  Much like Pandorum, the light should be in the front shirt pocket area, so it's hands-free.  There will be throwable glowsticks like Pandorum as well.

content.thinking:
The user decided the lamp is chest-mounted Pandorum-style, hands-free, so the beam is always available regardless of what's being carried. Glowsticks fit as deployable lights matching the existing art bible description, but I need to treat them as a Suit/Interaction item and update the beam origin point from hand to chest across the relevant art bible sections.

This resolves the mirror-jump concern since a chest point mirrors symmetrically, and facing still comes from aim/torso direction with the beam now bobbing at the chest instead of shaking in the hand. I'm routing these corrections through the controller GDD (changing hand point to chest point in several bullets) and the render pipeline dependencies, flagging all the amended art bible sections for the art director, while also checking that glowsticks' omnidirectional, steady glow still matches the deployables description.

Glowsticks don't flicker, which was supposed to be the deployable's distinguishing trait against the beam, so I need to flag their colour too—chemical green isn't in the current palette reserved for Tungsten-family hues, so that's an open question for the art director. Since glowsticks are throwable, they'd need a physics arc in a 1:1 pixel projection, which pushes this into Suit & Equipment/Interaction scope rather than pure art; I'll log this as a minor user decision and add it to Open Questions before applying the edits.

content.text: That settles it cleanly, and it simplifies the design: a **chest-mounted lamp** means the flashlight is always on when you want it — carrying, welding, cutting, nothing takes it away — and the light's origin is the suit's chest point, which also removes the awkward "lamp jumps hands when the sprite mirrors" problem the specialists were working around. **Throwable glowsticks** slot into the art bible's existing "deployable lights" category (the omnidirectional lights you drop or throw to light a room without standing in it). Recording both as your decisions, updating the controller GDD, and routing the art-bible amendments (it currently says the beam comes from the *hand*).

    line=m.group(1)
    s=s.replace(line, line.rstrip()+" *Decided (amendment 9): the pad default is aim-follows-movement until the first right-stick input, so the lamp follows the walk direction until the player chooses to aim.*",1)

rep('## Summary\n\n[To be designed]\n\n> **Quick reference** — Layer: `Core` · Priority: `MVP` · Key deps: `Command & Simulation Layer`, `Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera`',
    "## Summary\n\nThe Player Controller & Input is the crewmate's body and hands: it turns keyboard, mouse or gamepad input into the two things the simulation accepts — intents (where I am walking, where my chest lamp points, whether I am running) and commands (cut, weld, pick up, drop, throw a glowstick) — and turns the simulation's answer back into a stiff, heavy, honest body on screen. The body is the same in the quiet boarding rhythm and the frantic breach: no adrenaline, no speed change, nothing that lets a player read the danger off their controls instead of off the world. Movement is whole-pixel integer kinematics with no physics body; the lamp is chest-mounted and hands-free; every acknowledgement is immediate and never encodes success; the sprite, its tools and its beam are anchors a hallucination can never edit. print("placeholders:",s.count('[To be designed]'),"| GIVEN:",s.count('**GIVEN**'),"| formulas:",s.count('is defined as'),"| ## headings:",len(re.findall(r'^## ',s,re.M)),"| bytes:",len(s.encode('utf-8')),"| |x|<=6 fixed:",n)
EOF

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\dasbl\.claude\skills\consistency-check

=== CCGS Config (resolved: local->yaml->legacy->default; use as-is) ===
automation: autonomous (project.yaml)
workflow: full (rigor:full)
system_overrides: none
=== end ===



# Consistency Check

Detects cross-document inconsistencies by comparing all GDDs against the
entity registry (`design/registry/entities.yaml`). Uses a grep-first approach:
reads the registry once, then targets only the GDD sections that mention
registered names — no full document reads unless a conflict needs investigation.

**This skill is the write-time safety net.** It catches what `/design-system`'s
per-section checks may have missed and what `/review-all-gdds`'s holistic review
catches too late.

**When to run:**
- After writing each new GDD (before moving to the next system)
- Before `/review-all-gdds` (so that skill starts with a clean baseline)
- Before `/create-architecture` (inconsistencies poison downstream ADRs)
- On demand: `/consistency-check entity:[name]` to check one entity specifically

**Output:** Conflict report + optional registry corrections

---

Every `AskUserQuestion` call follows `.claude/docs/automation-modes.md`
(collaborative asks always · guided major-only · autonomous logs and proceeds;
`automation_always_ask` categories always prompt).

**`workflow`** (see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`), applied per GDD at its
**effective** tier — the `system_overrides` row for that GDD's system (its
filename stem) when the block lists one, else the project value:
- `full` — full entity-registry cross-check against all GDD sections.
- `standard` — cross-check against the required sections only. The report's
  Scope line says so, and each value stated for a registered name outside those
  sections is listed as not checked at this tier (Phase 3 applies this).
- `minimal` — not meaningful (no GDDs to check).

## Phase 1: Parse Arguments and Load Registry

**Modes:**
- No argument / `full` — check all registered entries against all GDDs
- `since-last-review` — check only GDDs modified since the last review report
- `entity:<name>` — check one specific entity across all GDDs
- `item:<name>` — check one specific item across all GDDs

**Load the registry:**

```
Read path="design/registry/entities.yaml"
```

If the file does not exist or has no entries:
> "Entity registry is empty. Run `/design-system` to write GDDs — the registry
> is populated automatically after each GDD is completed. Nothing to check yet."

Verdict: **NOT ASSESSED — entity registry empty**. Stop: nothing was compared,
so there is no PASS to give and nothing to write.

Build four lookup tables from the registry:
- **entity_map**: `{ name → { source, attributes, referenced_by } }`
- **item_map**: `{ name → { source, value_gold, weight, ... } }`
- **formula_map**: `{ name → { source, variables, output_range } }`
- **constant_map**: `{ name → { source, value, unit } }`

Count total registered entries. Report:
```
Registry loaded: [N] entities, [N] items, [N] formulas, [N] constants
Scope: [full | since-last-review | entity:name]
```

For `entity:<name>` or `item:<name>`, if the registry has no entry by that name
the verdict is **NOT ASSESSED — `<name>` is not in the registry**: list the
closest registered names and stop. Checking an unregistered name compares
nothing, and that is not a PASS.

---

## Phase 2: Locate In-Scope GDDs

```
Glob pattern="design/gdd/*.md"
```

Exclude the docs that live in `design/gdd/` but are not system GDDs:
`game-concept.md`, `systems-index.md`, `game-pillars.md`, `gameplay-tags.md`,
`entity-registry.md`, `fixture-swap-ledger.md`, `sound-bible.md` and any
`gdd-cross-review-*.md` (the report `/review-all-gdds` writes here).

For `since-last-review` mode:
```bash
git log --name-only --pretty=format: -- design/gdd/ | grep "\.md$" | sort -u
```
Limit to GDDs modified since the most recent `design/gdd/gdd-cross-review-*.md`
file's creation date.

Report the in-scope GDD list before scanning. **If the list is empty** — no system
GDDs exist, or `since-last-review` found none changed — the verdict is
**NOT ASSESSED — no GDDs in scope**: say which filter produced zero, and stop.
A scan of nothing finds no conflicts, and that is not a PASS.

---

## Phase 3: Grep-First Conflict Scan

For each registered entry, grep every in-scope GDD for the entry's name.
Do NOT do full reads — extract only the matching lines and their immediate
context (-C 3 lines).

This is the core optimization: instead of reading 10 GDDs × 400 lines each
(4,000 lines), you grep 50 entity names × 10 GDDs (50 targeted searches,
each returning ~10 lines on a hit).

**In a GDD whose effective tier is `standard`, compare only hits under a
required section.** The effective tier is per GDD: `system_overrides.<stem>`
replaces the project tier for that GDD in either direction (a `full` row makes
every section compared). Grep each such GDD once for `^## ` to get its headings
and line numbers, and file every name hit under the nearest heading above it:
only hits under Overview, Detailed Rules / Detailed Design, Formulas, Edge
Cases, Dependencies or Acceptance Criteria are compared — plus Tuning Knobs when
`project.yaml` sets `workflow_overrides.tuning_knobs: true` (read that flag
once; it only ever adds the section). Any other hit (Tuning Knobs without the
flag, Player Fantasy, any other section) raises no finding and is not logged;
list each one that states a value (name, GDD, section) on the report's
`Not checked at this tier` line.

### 3a: Entity Scan

For each entity in entity_map:

```
Grep pattern="[entity_name]" glob="design/gdd/*.md" output_mode="content" -C 3
```

For each GDD hit, extract the values mentioned near the entity name:
- any numeric attributes (counts, costs, durations, ranges, rates)
- any categorical attributes (types, tiers, categories)
- any derived values (totals, outputs, results)
- any other attributes registered in entity_map

Compare extracted values against the registry entry.

**Conflict detection:**
- Registry says `[entity_name].[attribute] = [value_A]`. GDD says `[entity_name] has [value_B]`. → **CONFLICT**
- Registry says `[item_name].[attribute] = [value_A]`. GDD says `[item_name] is [value_B]`. → **CONFLICT**
- GDD mentions `[entity_name]` but doesn't specify the attribute. → **NOTE** (no conflict, just unverifiable)

### 3b: Item Scan

For each item in item_map, grep all GDDs for the item name. Extract:
- sell price / value / gold value
- weight
- stack rules (stackable / non-stackable)
- category

Compare against registry entry values.

### 3c: Formula Scan

For each formula in formula_map, grep all GDDs for the formula name. Extract:
- variable names mentioned near the formula
- output range or cap values mentioned

Compare against registry entry:
- Different variable names → **CONFLICT**
- Output range stated differently → **CONFLICT**

### 3d: Constant Scan

For each constant in constant_map, grep all GDDs for the constant name. Extract:
- Any numeric value mentioned near the constant name

Compare against registry value:
- Different number → **CONFLICT**

---

## Phase 4: Deep Investigation (Conflicts Only)

For each conflict found in Phase 3, do a targeted full-section read of the
conflicting GDD to get precise context:

```
Read path="design/gdd/[conflicting_gdd].md"
```
(Or use Grep with wider context if the file is large)

Confirm the conflict with full context. Determine:
1. **Which GDD is correct?** Check the `source:` field in the registry — the
   source GDD is the authoritative owner. Any other GDD that contradicts it
   is the one that needs updating.
2. **Is the registry itself out of date?** If the source GDD was updated after
   the registry entry was written (check git log), the registry may be stale.
3. **Is this a genuine design change?** If the conflict represents an intentional
   design decision, the resolution is: update the source GDD, update the registry,
   then fix all other GDDs.

For each conflict, classify:
- **🔴 CONFLICT** — same named entity/item/formula/constant with different values
  in different GDDs. Must resolve before architecture begins.
- **⚠️ STALE REGISTRY** — source GDD value changed but registry not updated.
  Registry needs updating; other GDDs may be correct already.
- **ℹ️ UNVERIFIABLE** — entity mentioned but no comparable attribute stated.
  Not a conflict; just noting the reference.

---

## Phase 5: Output Report

```
## Consistency Check Report
Date: [date]
Registry entries checked: [N entities, N items, N formulas, N constants]
GDDs scanned: [N] ([list names])
Scope: [all GDD sections | required sections only — workflow: standard | per GDD — name each GDD whose effective tier differs, and its tier]
Not checked at this tier: [each value stated outside the required sections (name, GDD, section) — or "none"; omit when every GDD is at `full`]

---

### Conflicts Found (must resolve before architecture)

🔴 [Entity/Item/Formula/Constant Name]
   Registry (source: [gdd]): [attribute] = [value]
   Conflict in [other_gdd].md: [attribute] = [different_value]
   → Resolution needed: [which doc to change and to what]

---

### Stale Registry Entries (registry behind the GDD)

⚠️ [Entry Name]
   Registry says: [value] (written [date])
   Source GDD now says: [new value]
   → Update registry entry to match source GDD, then check referenced_by docs.

---

### Unverifiable References (no conflict, informational)

ℹ️ [gdd].md mentions [entity_name] but states no comparable attributes.
   No conflict detected. No action required.

---

### Clean Entries (no issues found)

✅ [N] registry entries verified across all GDDs with no conflicts.

---

Verdict: PASS | CONFLICTS FOUND | NOT ASSESSED
```

**Verdict:**
- **CONFLICTS FOUND** — one or more conflicts detected. List resolution steps.
- **NOT ASSESSED** — nothing was compared: the entity registry is empty or the

Detects cross-document inconsistencies by comparing all GDDs against the
entity registry (`design/registry/entities.yaml`). Uses a grep-first approach:
reads the registry once, then targets only the GDD sections that mention
registered names — no full document reads unless a conflict needs investigation.

**This skill is the write-time safety net.** It catches what `/design-system`'s
per-section checks may have missed and what `/review-all-gdds`'s holistic review
catches too late.

**When to run:**
- After writing each new GDD (before moving to the next system)
- Before `/review-all-gdds` (so that skill starts with a clean baseline)
- Before `/create-architecture` (inconsistencies poison downstream ADRs)
- On demand: `/consistency-check entity:[name]` to check one entity specifically

**Output:** Conflict report + optional registry corrections

---

Every `AskUserQuestion` call follows `.claude/docs/automation-modes.md`
(collaborative asks always · guided major-only · autonomous logs and proceeds;
`automation_always_ask` categories always prompt).

**`workflow`** (see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`), applied per GDD at its
**effective** tier — the `system_overrides` row for that GDD's system (its
filename stem) when the block lists one, else the project value:
- `full` — full entity-registry cross-check against all GDD sections.
- `standard` — cross-check against the required sections only. The report's
  Scope line says so, and each value stated for a registered name outside those
  sections is listed as not checked at this tier (Phase 3 applies this).
- `minimal` — not meaningful (no GDDs to check).

## Phase 1: Parse Arguments and Load Registry

**Modes:**
- No argument / `full` — check all registered entries against all GDDs
- `since-last-review` — check only GDDs modified since the last review report
- `entity:<name>` — check one specific entity across all GDDs
- `item:<name>` — check one specific item across all GDDs

**Load the registry:**

```
Read path="design/registry/entities.yaml"
```

If the file does not exist or has no entries:
> "Entity registry is empty. Run `/design-system` to write GDDs — the registry
> is populated automatically after each GDD is completed. Nothing to check yet."

Verdict: **NOT ASSESSED — entity registry empty**. Stop: nothing was compared,
so there is no PASS to give and nothing to write.

Build four lookup tables from the registry:
- **entity_map**: `{ name → { source, attributes, referenced_by } }`
- **item_map**: `{ name → { source, value_gold, weight, ... } }`
- **formula_map**: `{ name → { source, variables, output_range } }`
- **constant_map**: `{ name → { source, value, unit } }`

Count total registered entries. Report:
```
Registry loaded: [N] entities, [N] items, [N] formulas, [N] constants
Scope: [full | since-last-review | entity:name]
```

For `entity:<name>` or `item:<name>`, if the registry has no entry by that name
the verdict is **NOT ASSESSED — `<name>` is not in the registry**: list the
closest registered names and stop. Checking an unregistered name compares
nothing, and that is not a PASS.

---

## Phase 2: Locate In-Scope GDDs

```
Glob pattern="design/gdd/*.md"
```

Exclude the docs that live in `design/gdd/` but are not system GDDs:
`game-concept.md`, `systems-index.md`, `game-pillars.md`, `gameplay-tags.md`,
`entity-registry.md`, `fixture-swap-ledger.md`, `sound-bible.md` and any
`gdd-cross-review-*.md` (the report `/review-all-gdds` writes here).

For `since-last-review` mode:
```bash

```
Limit to GDDs modified since the most recent `design/gdd/gdd-cross-review-*.md`
file's creation date.

Report the in-scope GDD list before scanning. **If the list is empty** — no system
GDDs exist, or `since-last-review` found none changed — the verdict is
**NOT ASSESSED — no GDDs in scope**: say which filter produced zero, and stop.
A scan of nothing finds no conflicts, and that is not a PASS.

---

## Phase 3: Grep-First Conflict Scan

For each registered entry, grep every in-scope GDD for the entry's name.
Do NOT do full reads — extract only the matching lines and their immediate
context (-C 3 lines).

This is the core optimization: instead of reading 10 GDDs × 400 lines each
(4,000 lines), you grep 50 entity names × 10 GDDs (50 targeted searches,
each returning ~10 lines on a hit).

**In a GDD whose effective tier is `standard`, compare only hits under a
required section.** The effective tier is per GDD: `system_overrides.<stem>`
replaces the project tier for that GDD in either direction (a `full` row makes
every section compared). Grep each such GDD once for `^## ` to get its headings
and line numbers, and file every name hit under the nearest heading above it:
only hits under Overview, Detailed Rules / Detailed Design, Formulas, Edge
Cases, Dependencies or Acceptance Criteria are compared — plus Tuning Knobs when
`project.yaml` sets `workflow_overrides.tuning_knobs: true` (read that flag
once; it only ever adds the section). Any other hit (Tuning Knobs without the
flag, Player Fantasy, any other section) raises no finding and is not logged;
list each one that states a value (name, GDD, section) on the report's
`Not checked at this tier` line.

### 3a: Entity Scan

For each entity in entity_map:

```
Grep pattern="[entity_name]" glob="design/gdd/*.md" output_mode="content" -C 3
```

For each GDD hit, extract the values mentioned near the entity name:
- any numeric attributes (counts, costs, durations, ranges, rates)
- any categorical attributes (types, tiers, categories)
- any derived values (totals, outputs, results)
- any other attributes registered in entity_map

Compare extracted values against the registry entry.

**Conflict detection:**
- Registry says `[entity_name].[attribute] = [value_A]`. GDD says `[entity_name] has [value_B]`. → **CONFLICT**
- Registry says `[item_name].[attribute] = [value_A]`. GDD says `[item_name] is [value_B]`. → **CONFLICT**
- GDD mentions `[entity_name]` but doesn't specify the attribute. → **NOTE** (no conflict, just unverifiable)

### 3b: Item Scan

For each item in item_map, grep all GDDs for the item name. Extract:
- sell price / value / gold value
- weight
- stack rules (stackable / non-stackable)
- category

Compare against registry entry values.

### 3c: Formula Scan

For each formula in formula_map, grep all GDDs for the formula name. Extract:
- variable names mentioned near the formula
- output range or cap values mentioned

Compare against registry entry:
- Different variable names → **CONFLICT**
- Output range stated differently → **CONFLICT**

### 3d: Constant Scan

For each constant in constant_map, grep all GDDs for the constant name. Extract:
- Any numeric value mentioned near the constant name

Compare against registry value:
- Different number → **CONFLICT**

---

## Phase 4: Deep Investigation (Conflicts Only)

For each conflict found in Phase 3, do a targeted full-section read of the
conflicting GDD to get precise context:

```
Read path="design/gdd/[conflicting_gdd].md"
```
(Or use Grep with wider context if the file is large)

Confirm the conflict with full context. Determine:
1. **Which GDD is correct?** Check the `source:` field in the registry — the
   source GDD is the authoritative owner. Any other GDD that contradicts it
   is the one that needs updating.
2. **Is the registry itself out of date?** If the source GDD was updated after
   the registry entry was written (check git log), the registry may be stale.
3. **Is this a genuine design change?** If the conflict represents an intentional
   design decision, the resolution is: update the source GDD, update the registry,
   then fix all other GDDs.

For each conflict, classify:
- **🔴 CONFLICT** — same named entity/item/formula/constant with different values
  in different GDDs. Must resolve before architecture begins.
- **⚠️ STALE REGISTRY** — source GDD value changed but registry not updated.
  Registry needs updating; other GDDs may be correct already.
- **ℹ️ UNVERIFIABLE** — entity mentioned but no comparable attribute stated.
  Not a conflict; just noting the reference.

---

## Phase 5: Output Report

```

Date: [date]
Registry entries checked: [N entities, N items, N formulas, N constants]
GDDs scanned: [N] ([list names])
Scope: [all GDD sections | required sections only — workflow: standard | per GDD — name each GDD whose effective tier differs, and its tier]
Not checked at this tier: [each value stated outside the required sections (name, GDD, section) — or "none"; omit when every GDD is at `full`]

---

### Conflicts Found (must resolve before architecture)

🔴 [Entity/Item/Formula/Constant Name]

---

### Stale Registry Entries (registry behind the GDD)

⚠️ [Entry Name]
   Registry says: [value] (written [date])
   Source GDD now says: [new value]
   → Update registry entry to match source GDD, then check referenced_by docs.

---

### Unverifiable References (no conflict, informational)

ℹ️ [gdd].md mentions [entity_name] but states no comparable attributes.
   No conflict detected. No action required.

---

### Clean Entries (no issues found)

✅ [N] registry entries verified across all GDDs with no conflicts.

---

Verdict: PASS | CONFLICTS FOUND | NOT ASSESSED
```

**Verdict:**

You are the art-director applying three routed amendments IN PLACE to `D:\the-synaptic-sea-2d\design\art\art-bible.md` (approved AD-ART-BIBLE 2026-10-25; a backup exists). Do not touch the header lines. Nothing else changes.

  Line numbers: kernel = command-simulation-layer.md, render = pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md, controller = player-controller-input.md.
  
  ### Conflicts (🔴)
  
  **C1. Render placeholder speeds vs the controller and registry (known item a). Confirmed.**
  - Render says 90 / 150 / 150 px/s at lines 819, 876, 926 and others, and re-run needed at 636, 712, 909, 923, 926, 1036.
  - Registry V_WALK is 2 px/tick (120 px/s) and V_RUN is 3 px/tick (180 px/s). The controller states 120/180 at lines 92, 245, 246.

  - The inner-box inequality `0.30·L_h > v_max·τ + L_MAX` binds at v_max < 200 px/s (controller 92, 718; registry `speed_ceiling`).
  
  **C3. Kernel "progress ring" vs linear bar (known item c). Confirmed.**
  - Kernel line 85 says "a progress ring starting". Kernel line 745 says "progress ring beginning" and "a ring that begins a tick later".
  - Controller 127, 201, 843 and art bible 7.3 require a linear bar, never a ring.

  - Kernel line 194: "`set_move_intent`, `set_aim`, facing; ...".
  - Registry `facing_from_aim` and the controller derive facing from aim.
  - Kernel 194 and 958 also say "Controller owns intent and facing". That is acceptable, because facing is a controller-derived state rather than a command.
  
  **C5. Hand point as the beam origin in the render GDD (known item e). Confirmed at 4 passages.**
  - Render 112 says "the beam's hand point". Render 289 says "5-facing sprite and hand point" and "its hand point must obey". Render 432 says "Where the hand points".
  - Render 1072 carries a blanket note that these read as the chest point. It is a note, not a rewrite, so the text still states hand point.
  - Kernel: no hand-point or chest-point mention (0 hits).
  - Registry `chest_point` and controller 155 (user decision 2026-10-26) make the chest point the beam origin.
  
  **C6. Render zoom rule is still hold-to-step, not the ladder (known item f). Confirmed. The zoom-ladder decision is only partly applied in place.**
  - Render C6 at line 160 still has the heading "one integer step out, hold-to-step" and the body "**hold** ... **release to return**".
  - Line 160's own tail already says zoom-in is offered up to `k_auto + 2`, so the paragraph contradicts itself.
  - States table row 274 `ZOOMED_OUT` has entry condition "zoom input **held**" and exit "on **release**". Row 272 `FOLLOWING` has "`ZOOMED_OUT` on release".
  - Tuning row 796: "hold-to-step; cut".
  - Edge case 672: "zoomed out (a resize during a zoom hold) ... the hold persists", and `diag.zoom_held`.
  - Acceptance criteria 917, 938, 957, 958, 961 refer to a zoom hold, held zoom or release. The same applies to lines 81, 150 and 289 ("zoom hold", "zoom-hold input binding"). Line 289 also conflicts with controller PC-16, which gives two edge-triggered inputs, `zoom_in` and `zoom_out`.

  - Registry `zoom_out_k` also holds the old rule; see Stale.
  
  **C7. Zoom-in field breaks the inner-box invariant (unresolved, cross-GDD; not a listed item).**
  - Render line 244 allows zoom-in up to `k_auto + 2`, so the field is 480×270 at 1080p, k = 4.

  - Render's Section G invariant is asserted only "at the default field" (render 821, controller 793).
  - This is not fixable by text substitution. It needs a design decision: scale L_MAX with the field, or accept the clamp zoomed in. Controller 268 and 1119 already route it to the pipeline GDD, and the render GDD does not yet address it.
  
  ### Confirmed non-conflicts (items g to j)
  
  - **(g) LAG_CUT 24 vs 48.** The rule is 48 everywhere:
    - Render 158, 275, 494, 689, 805, 836, 934, 952.
    - Controller 263, 269, 738, 1068.
    - Registry 48.
    - The "24 px" at render 246 and 310, and controller 269 and 1057, are explicitly history or counterfactual.
    - The "24 px" at render 124, 126, 720, 787 and 810 is wall footprint or `BAND_H`, unrelated.
    - Controller 103 and 218 say "24 px deep" walls, which is also unrelated.
  - **(h) LOOKAHEAD_PX.** All GDDs state 72 px (1.5 tiles) as the rule. The 96 px / 2.0 tiles at render 156 and 800 is a recorded rejected alternative, and the 2.5-tile range is the range's top. No conflict.

  - `FOLLOW_TAU` and `LOOKAHEAD_PX` need a coupling comment. With V_RUN 3, τ ≤ 0.20 and L ≤ 75 are operative, narrower than the 0.10–0.30 and 48–120 ranges.

  - Controller line 1094 (d) and lines 201, 208, 853, 854, 1119: "corrections routed back" entries. They become resolved once C1 to C4 are applied.

import re
log = []
def patch(path, pairs, note=None):
    s = open(path, encoding='utf-8').read()
    for a, b in pairs:
        n = s.count(a)
        if n == 1: s = s.replace(a, b, 1); log.append(f"ok   {path[-40:]}: {a[:45]}")
        else: log.append(f"SKIP ({n}) {path[-40:]}: {a[:45]}")
    if note:
        i = s.index(note[0]); s = s[:i] + note[1] + s[i:]
    open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(s)

R = 'design/gdd/pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md'
patch(R, [
 ("| 90 / 150 / 150 px/s placeholders |", "| 120 / 180 / 180 px/s (2 / 3 / 3 px/tick; Player Controller GDD, registry V_WALK / V_RUN) |"),
 ("`v_max > LAG_CUT / τ_follow` (266 px/s) breaks the invariant", "`v_max ≥ 200 px/s` breaks the inner-box invariant `0.30·L_h > v_max·τ_follow + L_MAX` (binds first); `v_max > LAG_CUT / τ_follow` (266 px/s) breaks the lag-cut invariant"),
 ("if Player Controller raises `v_max` past 266 px/s at `τ = 0.18`, Section G's check fails the build", "if Player Controller raises `v_max` to 200 px/s or more at `τ = 0.18` and `L_MAX = 72`, Section G's inner-box check fails the build (the inner-box invariant binds before the 266 px/s lag-cut bound)"),
 ("with the build invariant `v_max < LAG_CUT / τ_follow`;", "with the build invariants `v_max < LAG_CUT / τ_follow` (266 px/s) and, binding, `v_max·τ_follow + L_MAX ≤ 0.30·L_h` (< 200 px/s);"),
 ("including the camera and the beam's hand point (which uses the same rounded position as the sprite", "including the camera and the beam's chest point (which uses the same rounded position as the sprite"),
 ("the 5-facing sprite and hand point as a Y-sort item", "the 5-facing sprite and per-facing chest point (beam origin) as a Y-sort item"),
 ("its hand point must obey (same rounded position)", "its chest point must obey (same rounded position)"),
 ("| Where the hand points |", "| Where the chest-mounted beam points |"),
 ("**C6. Zoom: one integer step out, hold-to-step, cut not tween.**", "**C6. Zoom: integer ladder in both directions, persistent, cut not tween.**"),
 ("to step out to `k_out = ceil(k / 2)`, **release to return** (game-designer)", "with `zoom_in` / `zoom_out` (edge-triggered; persistent, reset to default on re-wake) to step `k` through the integer ladder `[1, k_auto + 2]` (user decision 2026-10-26, supersedes the game-designer's hold-to-step-out)"),
 ("zoom input **held** in any state where `k ≥ 3`", "`zoom_out` pressed while `k > 1` (ladder; persistent)"),
 ("hold-to-step; cut; HUD unchanged", "ladder step; cut; HUD unchanged"),
], note=("### States and Transitions", "> **Decided (orchestrator, consistency check 2026-10-26) — zoom-in vs the inner-box invariant (C7):** the look-ahead bound scales with the visible field, `L_MAX_eff = LOOKAHEAD_PX × field_h / 360` (72 → 54 px at k = 4, 36 px at k = 5), so `v_max·τ_follow + L_MAX_eff ≤ 0.30·field_h` holds at every ladder step and running is never clamped by zoom; Section G's invariant is asserted at every reachable `field_h`, not only the default. Registry `camera_lookahead` and `speed_ceiling` carry the scaling.\n\n"))

K = 'design/gdd/command-simulation-layer.md'
patch(K, [
 ("a hand animation, a progress ring starting", "a hand animation, a linear progress bar starting"),
 ("tool sound, hand animation start, progress ring beginning", "tool sound, hand animation start, linear progress bar beginning"),
 ("the only visible effect of the command path is a ring that begins a tick later", "the only visible effect of the command path is a bar that begins a tick later"),
 ("`set_move_intent`, `set_aim`, facing; `coalesce = LATEST_PER_ACTOR_PER_TICK`", "`set_move_intent`, `set_aim` (facing is derived from aim by the Controller, not an intent); `coalesce = LATEST_PER_ACTOR_PER_TICK`"),
])

# Registry
Y = 'design/registry/entities.yaml'; s = open(Y, encoding='utf-8').read()
R_SRC = 'design/gdd/pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md'; C_SRC = 'design/gdd/player-controller-input.md'
def entry_block(name):
    i = s.index(f"  - name: {name}\n"); j = s.find("\n  - name: ", i + 1)
    if j < 0: j = s.find("\n# ", i + 1)
    return i, (j if j > 0 else len(s))
def add_ref(name, src):
    global s
    i, j = entry_block(name); blk = s[i:j]
    if src in blk: return
    if "referenced_by: []" in blk: blk2 = blk.replace("referenced_by: []", f"referenced_by:\n      - {src}", 1)
    else: blk2 = blk.replace("    referenced_by:\n", f"    referenced_by:\n      - {src}\n", 1)
    s = s[:i] + blk2 + s[j:]; log.append(f"ref  {name} += {src[-30:]}")
def set_attr(name, key, val, comment):
    global s
    i, j = entry_block(name); blk = s[i:j]
    blk2 = re.sub(rf"(      {re.escape(key)}: )[^\n]*", rf"\g<1>{val}", blk, count=1)
    blk2 = re.sub(r"    revised: [^\n]*", "    revised: 2026-10-26", blk2, count=1)
    blk2 = blk2.rstrip("\n") + f"\n    # {comment}\n"
    s = s[:i] + blk2 + s[j:]; log.append(f"attr {name}.{key}")
set_attr("zoom_out_k", "expression", "k steps through the integer ladder [1, k_auto + 2] via zoom_in / zoom_out; visible field = (W/k, H/k) base px", "was: k_out = ceil(k/2) single step out — superseded by user decision 2026-10-26 (zoom ladder both directions)")
set_attr("zoom_out_k", "output", "integer ladder in both directions, persistent, cut per step, reset to default on re-wake", "was: integer step only, hold-to-step-back")
set_attr("camera_lookahead", "output", "<= 72 px default at field_h 360; L_MAX_eff = LOOKAHEAD_PX * field_h / 360 at other zoom steps; range 48-120", "L_MAX scales with the field so the inner-box invariant holds at every ladder step (consistency check 2026-10-26)")
set_attr("speed_ceiling", "expression", "v_ceil = min(ceil(LAG_CUT/(FOLLOW_TAU*TICK_RATE)) - 1, floor((0.30*field_h - L_MAX_eff)/(FOLLOW_TAU*TICK_RATE))) with L_MAX_eff = LOOKAHEAD_PX*field_h/360", "asserted at every reachable field_h, not only the default (consistency check 2026-10-26)")
set_attr("camera_cut_predicates", "variables", "T_PAN 0.10 s, LAG_CUT 48 px, JUMP_CUT 48 px; invariants LAG_CUT > v_max*FOLLOW_TAU and 0.30*field_h > v_max*FOLLOW_TAU + L_MAX_eff (binds at < 200 px/s at the default field)", "second invariant added (consistency check 2026-10-26)")
set_attr("FOLLOW_TAU", "value", "0.18", "with V_RUN 3 the operative ceiling is tau <= 0.20 (controller D.2); the 0.10-0.30 range is the pipeline's")
set_attr("LOOKAHEAD_PX", "value", "72", "with V_RUN 3 the operative ceiling is L <= 75 at the default field (controller D.2); range 48-120 is the pipeline's")
for name, src in [("speed_ceiling", R_SRC), ("camera_lookahead", R_SRC), ("camera_lookahead", C_SRC), ("V_WALK", R_SRC), ("V_RUN", R_SRC), ("chest_point", R_SRC), ("V_WALK", C_SRC), ("V_RUN", C_SRC), ("zoom_out_k", C_SRC)]:
    add_ref(name, src)
s = s.replace('last_updated: "2026-10-26"', 'last_updated: "2026-10-26"', 1)
open(Y, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(s)
print("\n".join(log))

import re
p = 'design/gdd/pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md'; s = open(p, encoding='utf-8').read()
def rep(a, b, must=True):
    global s
    if a in s: s = s.replace(a, b, 1); return True
    assert not must, a[:80]
    return False
log = []
# 1. Header + Overview over-claim
log.append(rep("> **Implements Pillar**: The World Never Lies (P1 — true occlusion, honest light radius, no mask or vignette); The Web Watches (P3 — light is rendered as the spent resource it is)",
    "> **Implements Pillar**: The World Never Lies (P1 — no mask, vignette, fog or full-frame gamma between a lit pixel and the screen); Dread Before Chaos and Sanity Rewrites Reality (P2/P4 — no uncaused pixel motion, so tremor and glide stay readable and the frame is an anchor the Filter cannot move); The Web Watches (P3 — the camera never reads world state, and the web's drift stays readable on a grid that does not crawl)"))
log.append(rep("the edge of their own light is the true edge of a real light, never a mask;", "the edge of their own light is drawn as Lighting computes it, never softened or extended by a mask;"))
# 2. Jolt trigger list → C7's single list
n = len(re.findall(r'an impact on the hull, a vent burst, a detach', s)); s = re.sub(r'an impact on the hull, a vent burst, a detach', 'hull section separation, docking contact, a detach (the single trigger list; hull impact and vent bursts are deferred to the VS-A decision, Open Question 14)', s); log.append(f"jolt triggers x{n}")
log.append(rep("| 14 | **Jolt knob at VS-A**: whether a bounded physical jolt (≤ 2 base px, decayed, hull separation / docking / detach only) is adopted once the HUD-still-over-moving-world read is tested; the ≤ 8 Hz positional alternation needs the accessibility-specialist's confirmation alongside 7.3's tremor | game-designer, accessibility-specialist | VS-A |",
    "| 14 | **Jolt knob at VS-A**: whether a bounded physical jolt (≤ 2 base px, decayed, hull separation / docking / detach only — hull impact and vent bursts deferred) is adopted once the HUD-still-over-moving-world read is tested. *Creative-director note*: if adopted, prefer a single decayed displacement over D.11's ±alternation — an oscillating frame shares 7.3's tremor grammar and would make a real gauge tremor ambiguous during the jolt window (Player Fantasy design test 1). The accessibility-specialist confirms whatever form survives | game-designer, creative-director, accessibility-specialist | VS-A |"))
# 3a Game Feel lag
log.append(rep("any follow failure (pan-speed ceiling exceeded, lag over half a tile, a 48-px jump) are cuts.", "any follow failure (pan-speed ceiling exceeded, lag over one tile — `LAG_CUT` 48 px, a 48-px jump) are cuts."))
# 3b reduced motion wording
log.append(rep("Reduced motion disables look-ahead and zeroes the jolt and nothing else; \"reduce flashing\" is a separate toggle. Neither alters the tick.",
    "Reduced motion disables look-ahead, zeroes the jolt and applies the HR-8 world-effect reductions listed in PR-14 and Tuning Knobs (static direction shapes, static alarm mark); it never suppresses trails, tremor, hairlines or audio. \"Reduce flashing\" is a separate toggle. Neither alters the tick."))
# 3c look-ahead rationale with superseded 24 px
m = re.search(r'72 \+ 24[^\n]{0,40}96[^\n]{0,30}108', s)
if m: s = s.replace(m.group(0), "72 px look-ahead + 27 px steady-state lag at `v_max` (`v_max·τ_follow`) = 99 px, inside the ±108 px inner box — the build invariant `LAG_CUT > v_max·τ_follow` is what guarantees this", 1); log.append("3c rationale fixed")
else: log.append("3c pattern not found")
# 3d UI Requirements settings: hide jolt strength until VS-A; look-ahead strength added via amendment note
log.append(rep("look-ahead strength (off / short / default), jolt strength (off / half / full), reduce flashing", "look-ahead strength (off / short / default; added to PR-14 by the amendment note below), reduce flashing (jolt strength is hidden until the VS-A jolt decision — a setting for a feature that ships at 0 is not exposed)"))
# 3e duplicate specialists line: remove the second occurrence
first = s.find("*Specialists consulted:"); second = s.find("*Specialists consulted", first + 10)
if second != -1:
    end = s.find("\n", second); s = s[:second] + s[end+1:]; log.append("dup specialists line removed")
# 4. zoom decision wording → awaiting ratification
log.append(rep("> **Decided (orchestrator, 2026-10-26)** — *zoom-out on 2× displays*:", "> **Decided (orchestrator, 2026-10-26); creative director concurs; awaiting user ratification** — *zoom-out on 2× displays*:"))
# 5. expand ruling + OQ9 owners + amendment note additions (PR-14 look-ahead setting; expand recommendation)
i = s.index('### States and Transitions')
s = s[:i] + "> **Creative-director recommendation (CD-GDD-ALIGN, 2026-10-26), awaiting user ratification** — *`expand` aspect on wide displays*: accept `expand` with the 960×540 cap after spike step 11. The extra width shows honest void in every dark state; the extra lit floor appears mainly in the stable home-ship state where there is no threat; there is no competitive stake (anti-pillar); and a third of the screen black at 1600×900 is the worse experience. Recorded as an Edge Case under window handling. Also adopted: the Settings surface (PR-14) includes **look-ahead strength** (off / short / default); jolt strength is not exposed until the VS-A jolt decision.\n\n" + s[i:]
log.append(rep("| 9 | **`expand` aspect post-spike**: whether the extra lit floor it shows on ultrawide is an acceptable information advantage, and whether a 16:9 HUD clamp is wanted | game-designer, art-director | After spike step 11 |",
    "| 9 | **`expand` aspect post-spike**: whether the extra lit floor it shows on ultrawide is an acceptable information advantage, and whether a 16:9 HUD clamp is wanted. *Creative-director recommendation*: accept `expand` with the 960×540 cap (see the note before States and Transitions). **User ratifies** | user, creative-director, game-designer, art-director | After spike step 11 |"))
log.append(rep("| 4 | **Zoom on 2× displays — on-device acuity.** Decided: the hold-to-step zoom stays available on 2× worlds (to 1×).", "| 4 | **Zoom on 2× displays.** Decided by the orchestrator, creative director concurs, **user ratification pending** (a 1× Deck zoom shows ~4× the default field, the largest framing change in the game): the hold-to-step zoom stays available on 2× worlds (to 1×)."))
# Edge case for expand information gap
j = s.index('\n## Dependencies'); s = s[:j] + "\n- **If the window is wider than 16:9 and `expand` is enabled**: the visible base field widens up to the 960×540 cap at the same integer `k`; the extra columns show whatever is there — honest void in every dark state, and extra lit floor only where loops are running (chiefly the stable home-ship). No information the beam has not paid for is revealed, because unlit geometry remains at the ambient floor and web content is never drawn unlit. Diagnostics record the expanded base size. *(Creative-director recommendation; user ratification pending — Open Question 9.)*\n" + s[j:]
# header gate line
log.append(rep("> **Implements Pillar**:", "> **Creative Director Review (CD-GDD-ALIGN)**: REVISED 2026-10-26 — five consistency/authority items applied; re-check pending\n> **Implements Pillar**:"))
open(p, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(s)
print(log)

skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\dasbl\.claude\skills\consistency-check

=== CCGS Config (resolved: local->yaml->legacy->default; use as-is) ===
automation: autonomous (project.yaml)
workflow: full (rigor:full)

=== end ===



# Consistency Check

Detects cross-document inconsistencies by comparing all GDDs against the
entity registry (`design/registry/entities.yaml`). Uses a grep-first approach:
reads the registry once, then targets only the GDD sections that mention
registered names — no full document reads unless a conflict needs investigation.

**This skill is the write-time safety net.** It catches what `/design-system`'s
per-section checks may have missed and what `/review-all-gdds`'s holistic review
catches too late.

**When to run:**
- After writing each new GDD (before moving to the next system)
- Before `/review-all-gdds` (so that skill starts with a clean baseline)
- Before `/create-architecture` (inconsistencies poison downstream ADRs)
- On demand: `/consistency-check entity:[name]` to check one entity specifically

**Output:** Conflict report + optional registry corrections

---

Every `AskUserQuestion` call follows `.claude/docs/automation-modes.md`
(collaborative asks always · guided major-only · autonomous logs and proceeds;
`automation_always_ask` categories always prompt).

**`workflow`** (see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`), applied per GDD at its
**effective** tier — the `system_overrides` row for that GDD's system (its
filename stem) when the block lists one, else the project value:
- `full` — full entity-registry cross-check against all GDD sections.
- `standard` — cross-check against the required sections only. The report's
  Scope line says so, and each value stated for a registered name outside those
  sections is listed as not checked at this tier (Phase 3 applies this).
- `minimal` — not meaningful (no GDDs to check).

## Phase 1: Parse Arguments and Load Registry

**Modes:**
- No argument / `full` — check all registered entries against all GDDs
- `since-last-review` — check only GDDs modified since the last review report
- `entity:<name>` — check one specific entity across all GDDs
- `item:<name>` — check one specific item across all GDDs

**Load the registry:**

```
Read path="design/registry/entities.yaml"
```

If the file does not exist or has no entries:
> "Entity registry is empty. Run `/design-system` to write GDDs — the registry
> is populated automatically after each GDD is completed. Nothing to check yet."

Verdict: **NOT ASSESSED — entity registry empty**. Stop: nothing was compared,
so there is no PASS to give and nothing to write.

Build four lookup tables from the registry:
- **entity_map**: `{ name → { source, attributes, referenced_by } }`
- **item_map**: `{ name → { source, value_gold, weight, ... } }`
- **formula_map**: `{ name → { source, variables, output_range } }`
- **constant_map**: `{ name → { source, value, unit } }`

Count total registered entries. Report:
```
Registry loaded: [N] entities, [N] items, [N] formulas, [N] constants
Scope: [full | since-last-review | entity:name]
```

For `entity:<name>` or `item:<name>`, if the registry has no entry by that name
the verdict is **NOT ASSESSED — `<name>` is not in the registry**: list the
closest registered names and stop. Checking an unregistered name compares
nothing, and that is not a PASS.

---

## Phase 2: Locate In-Scope GDDs

```
Glob pattern="design/gdd/*.md"
```

Exclude the docs that live in `design/gdd/` but are not system GDDs:
`game-concept.md`, `systems-index.md`, `game-pillars.md`, `gameplay-tags.md`,
`entity-registry.md`, `fixture-swap-ledger.md`, `sound-bible.md` and any
`gdd-cross-review-*.md` (the report `/review-all-gdds` writes here).

For `since-last-review` mode:
```bash
git log --name-only --pretty=format: -- design/gdd/ | grep "\.md$" | sort -u
```
Limit to GDDs modified since the most recent `design/gdd/gdd-cross-review-*.md`
file's creation date.

Report the in-scope GDD list before scanning. **If the list is empty** — no system
GDDs exist, or `since-last-review` found none changed — the verdict is
**NOT ASSESSED — no GDDs in scope**: say which filter produced zero, and stop.
A scan of nothing finds no conflicts, and that is not a PASS.

---

## Phase 3: Grep-First Conflict Scan

For each registered entry, grep every in-scope GDD for the entry's name.
Do NOT do full reads — extract only the matching lines and their immediate
context (-C 3 lines).

This is the core optimization: instead of reading 10 GDDs × 400 lines each
(4,000 lines), you grep 50 entity names × 10 GDDs (50 targeted searches,
each returning ~10 lines on a hit).

**In a GDD whose effective tier is `standard`, compare only hits under a
required section.** The effective tier is per GDD: `system_overrides.<stem>`
replaces the project tier for that GDD in either direction (a `full` row makes
every section compared). Grep each such GDD once for `^## ` to get its headings
and line numbers, and file every name hit under the nearest heading above it:
only hits under Overview, Detailed Rules / Detailed Design, Formulas, Edge
Cases, Dependencies or Acceptance Criteria are compared — plus Tuning Knobs when
`project.yaml` sets `workflow_overrides.tuning_knobs: true` (read that flag
once; it only ever adds the section). Any other hit (Tuning Knobs without the
flag, Player Fantasy, any other section) raises no finding and is not logged;
list each one that states a value (name, GDD, section) on the report's
`Not checked at this tier` line.

### 3a: Entity Scan

For each entity in entity_map:

```
Grep pattern="[entity_name]" glob="design/gdd/*.md" output_mode="content" -C 3
```

For each GDD hit, extract the values mentioned near the entity name:
- any numeric attributes (counts, costs, durations, ranges, rates)
- any categorical attributes (types, tiers, categories)
- any derived values (totals, outputs, results)
- any other attributes registered in entity_map

Compare extracted values against the registry entry.

**Conflict detection:**
- Registry says `[entity_name].[attribute] = [value_A]`. GDD says `[entity_name] has [value_B]`. → **CONFLICT**
- Registry says `[item_name].[attribute] = [value_A]`. GDD says `[item_name] is [value_B]`. → **CONFLICT**
- GDD mentions `[entity_name]` but doesn't specify the attribute. → **NOTE** (no conflict, just unverifiable)

### 3b: Item Scan

For each item in item_map, grep all GDDs for the item name. Extract:
- sell price / value / gold value
- weight
- stack rules (stackable / non-stackable)
- category

Compare against registry entry values.

### 3c: Formula Scan

For each formula in formula_map, grep all GDDs for the formula name. Extract:
- variable names mentioned near the formula
- output range or cap values mentioned

Compare against registry entry:
- Different variable names → **CONFLICT**
- Output range stated differently → **CONFLICT**

### 3d: Constant Scan

For each constant in constant_map, grep all GDDs for the constant name. Extract:
- Any numeric value mentioned near the constant name

Compare against registry value:
- Different number → **CONFLICT**

---

## Phase 4: Deep Investigation (Conflicts Only)

For each conflict found in Phase 3, do a targeted full-section read of the
conflicting GDD to get precise context:

```
Read path="design/gdd/[conflicting_gdd].md"
```
(Or use Grep with wider context if the file is large)

Confirm the conflict with full context. Determine:
1. **Which GDD is correct?** Check the `source:` field in the registry — the
   source GDD is the authoritative owner. Any other GDD that contradicts it
   is the one that needs updating.
2. **Is the registry itself out of date?** If the source GDD was updated after
   the registry entry was written (check git log), the registry may be stale.
3. **Is this a genuine design change?** If the conflict represents an intentional
   design decision, the resolution is: update the source GDD, update the registry,
   then fix all other GDDs.

For each conflict, classify:
- **🔴 CONFLICT** — same named entity/item/formula/constant with different values
  in different GDDs. Must resolve before architecture begins.
- **⚠️ STALE REGISTRY** — source GDD value changed but registry not updated.
  Registry needs updating; other GDDs may be correct already.
- **ℹ️ UNVERIFIABLE** — entity mentioned but no comparable attribute stated.
  Not a conflict; just noting the reference.

---

## Phase 5: Output Report

```
## Consistency Check Report
Date: [date]
Registry entries checked: [N entities, N items, N formulas, N constants]
GDDs scanned: [N] ([list names])
Scope: [all GDD sections | required sections only — workflow: standard | per GDD — name each GDD whose effective tier differs, and its tier]
Not checked at this tier: [each value stated outside the required sections (name, GDD, section) — or "none"; omit when every GDD is at `full`]

---

### Conflicts Found (must resolve before architecture)

🔴 [Entity/Item/Formula/Constant Name]
   Registry (source: [gdd]): [attribute] = [value]
   Conflict in [other_gdd].md: [attribute] = [different_value]
   → Resolution needed: [which doc to change and to what]

---

### Stale Registry Entries (registry behind the GDD)

⚠️ [Entry Name]
   Registry says: [value] (written [date])
   Source GDD now says: [new value]
   → Update registry entry to match source GDD, then check referenced_by docs.

---

### Unverifiable References (no conflict, informational)

ℹ️ [gdd].md mentions [entity_name] but states no comparable attributes.
   No conflict detected. No action required.

---

### Clean Entries (no issues found)

✅ [N] registry entries verified across all GDDs with no conflicts.

---

Verdict: PASS | CONFLICTS FOUND | NOT ASSESSED
```

**Verdict:**
- **CONFLICTS FOUND** — one or more conflicts detected. List resolution steps.
- **NOT ASSESSED** — nothing was compared: the entity registry is empty or the
  named entity is not in it (Phase 1), or no GDDs were in scope (Phase 2). Say
  which.
- **PASS** — no conflicts. Registry and GDDs agree on all checked values, across at least one GDD.

---

## Phase 6: Registry Corrections

**Re-read before you write.** Phase 1 read the registry before the scans, and
another skill or session may have changed it since. Before each Edit, read the
current `design/registry/entities.yaml`, find the entry in its section, and
anchor the Edit on the entry's current text, never on what Phase 1 saw. Append
a new entry after the last existing entry of its section.

If stale registry entries were found, ask:
> "May I update `design/registry/entities.yaml` to fix the [N] stale entries?"

For each stale entry:
- Update the `value` / attribute field
- Set `revised:` to today's date
- Add a YAML comment with the old value: `# was: [old_value] before [date]`

If new entries were found in GDDs that are not in the registry, ask:
> "Found [N] entities/items mentioned in GDDs that aren't in the registry yet.
> May I add them to `design/registry/entities.yaml`?"

Only add entries that appear in more than one GDD (true cross-system facts).

**Never delete registry entries.** Set `status: deprecated` if an entry is removed
from all GDDs.

After writing: Verdict: **COMPLETE** — consistency check finished.
If conflicts remain unresolved: Verdict: **BLOCKED** — [N] conflicts need manual resolution before architecture begins.

### 6b: Append to Reflexion Log

If any 🔴 CONFLICT entries were found (regardless of whether they were resolved),
ask: "May I append [N] entries to `docs/consistency-failures.md` (creating it if
absent)?" On yes, append an entry for each conflict; on no, say the conflicts
were not logged.

```markdown
### [YYYY-MM-DD] — /consistency-check — 🔴 CONFLICT
**Domain**: [system domain(s) involved]
**Documents involved**: [source GDD] vs [conflicting GDD]
**What happened**: [specific conflict — entity name, attribute, differing values]
**Resolution**: [how it was fixed, or "Unresolved — manual action needed"]
**Pattern**: [generalised lesson, e.g. "Item values defined in combat GDD were not
referenced in economy GDD before authoring — always check entities.yaml first"]
```

If `docs/consistency-failures.md` does not exist, create it with this header before appending:

```markdown
# Consistency Failure Log

<!-- Auto-maintained by /consistency-check. Do not edit manually. -->
<!-- One entry per detected conflict, in chronological order. -->

| Date | GDD A | GDD B | Conflict Type | Status |
|------|-------|-------|---------------|--------|
```

Then append the new conflict entries. Never skip logging on your own — a missing file is not a reason to lose conflict history; only the user's "no" is.

---

## Phase 7: Session State and Closing

Silently append to `production/session-state/active.md` (create the file if it does not exist):

```
<!-- CONSISTENCY-CHECK: [date] | GDDs checked: [N] | Conflicts found: [N] | Log: docs/consistency-failures.md -->
```

> **Point at `docs/consistency-failures.md` — the file Phase 6 actually appends
> to.** A breadcrumb is a pointer left for a future session to follow. One that
> names a file nothing writes sends that session looking for conflict history it
> will never find, and nothing errors along the way. Never invent a report
> filename here.

Then close with an `AskUserQuestion` widget:

- **Prompt**: "Consistency check complete — [N] conflicts found. What next?"
- **Options**:
  - `[A] Fix the highest-priority conflict now`
  - `[B] Run /design-review on the most conflicted GDD`
  - `[C] Stop here`

In collaborative and guided modes, never end the skill with plain text — always
close with this widget. In autonomous mode, print the findings and recommended
next step, then record via `log_decision` (no widget).

---

## Recovery / Reference

- **If PASS**: Run `/review-all-gdds` for holistic design-theory review, or
  `/create-architecture` if all MVP GDDs are complete.
- **If CONFLICTS FOUND**: Fix the flagged GDDs, then re-run
  `/consistency-check` to confirm resolution.
- **If STALE REGISTRY**: Update the registry (Phase 6), then re-run to verify.
- Run `/consistency-check` after writing each new GDD to catch issues early,
  not at architecture time.

# Design System

When this skill is invoked:

## 1. Parse Arguments & Validate

**Read `references/1-parse-arguments.md` now and follow it** — this phase's steps are in that file, not here. Read it again if the conversation was compacted or resumed during this phase.

## 2. Gather Context (Read Phase)

**Read `references/2-gather-context.md` now and follow it** — this phase's steps are in that file, not here. Read it again if the conversation was compacted or resumed during this phase.

## 3. Create File Skeleton

**Read `references/3-file-skeleton.md` now and follow it** — this phase's steps are in that file, not here. Read it again if the conversation was compacted or resumed during this phase.

## 4. Section-by-Section Design

**Read `references/4-section-design.md` now and follow it** — this phase's steps are in that file, not here. Read it again if the conversation was compacted or resumed during this phase.

## 5. Post-Design Validation

**Read `references/5-post-design.md` now and follow it** — this phase's steps are in that file, not here. Read it again if the conversation was compacted or resumed during this phase.

## 6. Specialist Agent Routing

This skill delegates to specialist agents for domain expertise. The main session
orchestrates the overall flow; agents provide expert content.

**Rows here are finer-grained than the nine `Category` values on purpose** — the
right specialist for combat is not the right specialist for pathfinding, and both
are `Gameplay`. Resolve in two steps: take the system's `Category` from
`systems-index.md`, then pick the row within it that matches what the system
actually does. Every category has at least one row, so nothing falls through.

| `Category` | Rows below to choose from |
|---|---|
| `Gameplay` | Combat/damage/health · AI/pathfinding/behavior · Animation/character movement · Character systems · Camera/input/controls |
| `Core` | Foundation/Infrastructure · Camera/input/controls |
| `Persistence` | Foundation/Infrastructure |
| `Economy` | Economy/loot/crafting |
| `Progression` | Progression/XP/skills |
| `UI` | UI systems · Visual effects (when the system is HUD-adjacent VFX) |
| `Audio` | Audio systems |
| `Narrative` | Dialogue/quests/lore |
| `Meta` | Foundation/Infrastructure (analytics, tutorial plumbing) · UI systems (accessibility options screens) |

If two rows fit, spawn the union of their Primary agents and say why.

| System type | Primary Agent | Supporting Agent(s) |
|----------------|---------------|---------------------|
| **Foundation/Infrastructure** (event bus, save/load, scene mgmt, service locator) | `systems-designer` | `gameplay-programmer` (feasibility), `engine-programmer` (engine integration) |
| Combat, damage, health | `game-designer` | `systems-designer` (formulas), `ai-programmer` (enemy AI), `art-director` (hit feedback visual direction, VFX intent) |
| Economy, loot, crafting | `economy-designer` | `systems-designer` (curves), `game-designer` (loops) |
| Progression, XP, skills | `game-designer` | `systems-designer` (curves), `economy-designer` (sinks) |
| Dialogue, quests, lore | `game-designer` | `narrative-director` (story), `writer` (content), `art-director` (character visual profiles, cinematic tone) |
| UI systems (HUD, menus) | `game-designer` | `ux-designer` (flows), `ui-programmer` (feasibility), `art-director` (visual style direction), `technical-artist` (render/shader constraints) |
| Audio systems | `game-designer` | `audio-director` (direction), `sound-designer` (specs) |
| AI, pathfinding, behavior | `game-designer` | `ai-programmer` (implementation), `systems-designer` (scoring) |
| Level/world systems | `game-designer` | `level-designer` (spatial), `world-builder` (lore) |
| Camera, input, controls | `game-designer` | `ux-designer` (feel), `gameplay-programmer` (feasibility) |
| Animation, character movement | `game-designer` | `art-director` (animation style, pose language), `technical-artist` (rig/blend constraints), `gameplay-programmer` (feel) |
| Visual effects, particles, shaders | `game-designer` | `art-director` (VFX visual direction), `technical-artist` (performance budget, shader complexity), `systems-designer` (trigger/state integration) |
| Character systems (stats, archetypes) | `game-designer` | `art-director` (character visual archetype), `narrative-director` (character arc alignment), `systems-designer` (stat formulas) |

**When delegating via the `Agent` tool**:
- Provide: system name, game concept summary, dependency GDD excerpts, the specific
  section being worked on, and what question needs expert input
- The agent returns analysis/proposals to the main session
- The main session presents the agent's output to the user via `AskUserQuestion`
- The user decides; the main session writes to file
- Agents do NOT write to files directly — the main session owns all file writes

---

## 7. Recovery & Resume

If the session is interrupted (compaction, crash, new session):

1. Read `production/session-state/active.md` — it records the current system and
   which sections are complete
2. Read `design/gdd/[system-name].md` — sections with real content are done;
   sections with `[To be designed]` still need work
3. Resume from the next incomplete section — no need to re-discuss completed ones

This is why incremental writing matters: every approved section survives any
disruption.

---

## Collaborative Protocol

**In `collaborative` mode (the default).** For `guided` and `autonomous`
modes, see the per-mode rules in `.claude/docs/automation-modes.md` — the
"Never" lines below describe what collaborative mode requires, not what
applies universally.

This skill follows the collaborative design principle at every step:

1. **Question -> Options -> Decision -> Draft -> Approval** for every section
2. **AskUserQuestion** at every decision point (Explain -> Capture pattern):
   - Phase 2: "Ready to start, or need more context?"
   - Phase 3: "May I create the skeleton?"
   - Phase 4 (each section): Design questions, approach options, draft approval
   - Phase 5: "May I update the entity registry? May I update the systems
     index? What's next?" — **not** "Run design review?": §5c forbids offering
     `/design-review` inline, because the reviewing agent must not inherit this
     session's design history. Phase 5c presents the hand-off; it never asks.
3. **"May I write to [filepath]?"** before the skeleton and before each section write
4. **Incremental writing**: Each section is written to file immediately after approval
5. **Session state updates**: After every section write
6. **Cross-referencing**: Every section checks existing GDDs for conflicts
7. **Specialist routing**: Complex sections get expert agent input, presented to
   the user for decision — never written silently

**Never** auto-generate the full GDD and present it as a fait accompli.
**Never** write a section without user approval.
**Never** contradict an existing approved GDD without flagging the conflict.
**Always** show where decisions come from (dependency GDDs, pillars, user choices).

## Context Window Awareness

This is a long-running skill. After writing each section, check if the status line
shows context at or above 70%. If so, append this notice to the response:

> **Context is approaching the limit (≥70%).** Your progress is saved — all approved
> sections are written to `design/gdd/[system-name].md`. When you're ready to continue,
> open a fresh Claude Code session and run `/design-system [system-name]` — it will
> detect which sections are complete and resume from the next one.

---

## Recommended Next Steps

- Run `/design-review design/gdd/[system-name].md` in a **fresh session** to validate the completed GDD independently
- Run `/consistency-check` to verify this GDD's values don't conflict with other GDDs
- Run `/map-systems next` to move to the next highest-priority undesigned system
- Run `/gate-check technical-setup` when all MVP GDDs are authored and reviewed
