input.content:
## Overview

The Life-Support Graph is the ship's circulation written as data: one integer-only simulation block that holds **five loops** — O₂, power, coolant, fuel and integrity — as typed ports on nodes joined by typed edges, plus one atmosphere record (gas amount, temperature) per compartment. It is the physical ground truth the whole game is measured against. Every pipe that leaks, bus that scorches, seam that frosts, scrubber that stalls and hull plate that breaches is a change to this block, made only through its published mutators inside the kernel's write scope; every gauge, trail, hiss, breath-fog and cold-damage tick is a *reading* of it. The Graph is scene-tree free, headless-testable and deterministic (same seed and command stream → identical `state_hash`), serialises as one versioned snapshot, and is the data that co-op will later sync by summary.

The player never operates the Graph as a menu or a schematic. They meet it as a place: a corridor colder than it should be, chevrons crawling slow along a pipe, mist curling from a clamp, a lamp that dims when the scrubber draws. Their verbs — patch, flip a breaker, seal a bulkhead, close a valve, vent, salvage a module, weld a section on, crank by hand — arrive as Interaction commands that call Graph mutators; welding joins another ship's subgraph to this one along a seam. Failures are physical and emergent: a starved scrubber, a frozen pipe or an overloaded cable spreads one hop per propagation run through the quantities it changes, never by script, and every endogenous loss is preceded by a readable physical warning (the fairness gate). The Graph has no notion of a hallucination: it publishes true values only, so a false "fixed" scrubber can be caught by the cold, the thinning air and the hiss the Graph still drives.

Without this system there is no Pillar 1. Without a shared, honest, falsifiable physical state, the hallucination design (Pillar 4) has nothing to lie *against*, the web has no power draw to watch (Pillar 3), and salvage and welding have nothing to act on (Pillar 5). It is the design-order-3 bottleneck with fourteen dependents, and the MVP hypothesis — *the boarding→breach loop over a visible life-support graph is tense for 30+ minutes* — cannot be tested without it.

*Implementation questions raised while designing and deferred to ADRs (→ `/architecture-decision`): struct-of-arrays packed fields vs objects (ADR-LSG-01); the fixed-point unit system (ADR-LSG-02); the explicit one-pass propagation scheme (ADR-LSG-03); append-only topology identity (ADR-LSG-04); snapshot/restore and migration (ADR-LSG-05); dirty-key encoding (ADR-LSG-06); keyed RNG (ADR-LSG-07); stable content type IDs (ADR-LSG-08); and two routed amendments outside this system — the kernel's per-block cached hash (K-1) and Save/Load's binary interchange for 64-bit values (S-1).*

## Player Fantasy

**Framing: indirect, with a direct layer on top.** The player experiences the Graph through its consequences and acts on it through physical verbs; they never see "the Graph". *(creative-director consulted; Framing A adopted with B as its competence and C as its guarantee.)*

> The ship is a body the crew assembled from other ships' corpses, and the Life-Support Graph is its circulation: oxygen, power, coolant, fuel and the hull that holds them. The player never operates the Graph as a menu. They tend the ship: a corridor colder than it should be, chevrons crawling slow along a pipe, frost fanning out from a weld seam, a hiss behind a panel. They go to it with a light and their hands, and they reroute, seal, weld or cut.
>
> Competence is literacy, not optimisation. Every failure leaves a trail along the edge it travels, thickest at its source, so a veteran crew does not run the ship better than a new one; they understand sooner what it is telling them and reach the right seam faster.
>
> And the body never lies. Gauges can be wrong and eyes can be wrong, but the cold, the thin air and the falling pressure in a compartment come from the Graph's true state for every player. When the instruments and the room disagree, the room wins, and the player learns to trust it.

**Anchor moment.** You come back up the pod tube with a salvaged scrubber on your back, and the corridor is colder than you left it. The O₂ pipe along the ceiling is still lit cyan, but its chevrons are crawling slower than they should, and there is a fine white fan of frost on the elbow by the galley. Your own breath hangs in the beam. You set the scrubber down, put your glove on the pipe, and follow the cold back to where it started — the way you would check a sleeping friend's forehead. The emotion is *caretaking under threat*: tenderness and vigilance. The power is not control; it is keeping something alive by attention — the Project Zomboid base you built with your own hands, made precarious (concept, Core Fantasy).

**Pillar alignment.** Pillar 1 verbatim: *"Pipes leak, frost forms, air hisses; the physical world is ground truth. Only instruments and perception can be wrong … A pipe may look fixed, but the room still gets cold, the air still thins, the pressure still drops."* The Graph is that ground truth. Pillar 2 (Dread Before Chaos): every fault has a long, readable tell before it cascades. Pillar 3: keeping the air clean draws power, and power draw is something the web can read. Pillar 4: the Graph is the falsification ground every hallucination is tested against. Pillar 5: salvage and welding act on its nodes; a lost compartment is not a lost ship.

**Design test.** *When a choice makes the ship easier to read from a screen vs. easier to read from the room → choose the room. When a choice rewards running the ship well vs. rewards noticing it is unwell → choose noticing.* Corollaries: a fault persists and spreads until someone goes to it (never times out); a failure's origin is shown by a trail the player follows back along the edge, never by a marker; a hallucinated "fixed" state never quiets the real hiss or warms the real room.

**Under hallucination the fantasy deepens rather than breaks.** Pillar 4 lets the lie extend from the gauge to the sprite — a broken scrubber may render whole and spinning. What cannot change is the consequence channel: compartment temperature, O₂ and pressure, and the frost, mist, scorch, drip and hiss that Failure & Trail and Adaptive Audio render as pure readers of the Graph's true values. The caretaker who can no longer trust their eyes falls back on breath, cold and touch — the oldest reading of a body. Verification costs rise in order: the room itself; a second instrument elsewhere on the ship; a saner crewmate (VS-B); time.

**Reference techniques, taken precisely.** Project Zomboid — the base degrades on its own clock and competence is the routine of noticing (*adopt*); its numeric context-menu condition readouts (*reject*). Barotrauma — repair is a place you go with the right tool; a junction box fails *where it is* (*adopt*); the Status Monitor ship-overview screen (*reject*). Dwarf Fortress fluids — propagation is visible in the medium, not announced (*adopt*). The Long Dark — cold is read from breath vapour before any number (*adopt*). SS13 / Stationeers — precision is something you go and get (*adopt* as the lit inspect card); their gas chemistry (*reject*: five loops, not chemistry). FTL — door-control causality (*adopt*); per-room O₂ shading on a schematic (*reject*). Alien: Isolation — checking costs you (*adopt*). Pandorum — the failing ship as the only reliable narrator (*adopt*).

**What this GDD does not promise (anti-pillar guard rails).**
1. No mastery-by-optimisation: no efficiency, "optimal layout", throughput score, uptime grade or any reward for running loops near capacity. Staying alive is the only payoff.
2. The web is not a puzzle to solve: failures are not authored puzzles with one correct sequence; there is no "solved" state and no completion ping.
3. No schematic, overlay, minimap or ship-status screen. Precision exists only as the lit inspect card of a specific instrument (art bible 7.0), which lies when that gauge lies. The suit's O₂ numeral on the critical strip is the *suit's* reading, not a Graph overlay.
4. No progression from the Graph: nothing unlocks or levels from repairs; better modules come from salvage.
5. No readability in the dark: "What You Light, You Can Read" — unlit compartments are readable only through the body channels (cold, breath, hiss, pressure), never by sprite state.
6. No sixth loop and no "heat loop": heat and pressure are per-compartment atmosphere.
7. No freeform plumbing: rerouting is valves, breakers, hatches, seams and cuts on pre-shaped modules.
8. No guarantee the ship can always be saved. Losing a section or the ship is allowed; the failure contract (Pillar 5) is the safety net, not the Graph.

## Dependencies

**Upstream (this system depends on):**

| Dependency | Nature | Interface and locked facts | Status |
|------------|--------|----------------------------|--------|
| Command & Simulation Layer | Hard | The Graph registers **one** state block `graph.state` (CR-8: `SIM`, `persist`, `WORLD`, `SHARED`, `repl_hint SHARED_SUMMARY`, schema v1) and **three** step hooks at divisor 6 / offset 0 chained by `after:` (`graph.propagate.power` → `.atmo` → `.failure`, CR-3). All writes go through its published mutators inside a kernel `WriteScope` in P2 (CR-9); Class A mutators pair with pure `check_*` used by the owning command's `validate`, Class B mutators clamp and never reject. It registers **no commands of its own** — the verbs live with Interaction, Assembly, Suit. It cites the registered `rng_derive` (keyed counter), `state_hash`, `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS = 256` (confirmed, not set, by D.10), `STEP_BUDGET_MS = 4` (a logging threshold), `TICK_RATE = 60`. Two amendments are **routed** to the kernel owner and are not this GDD's rule: K-1 (per-block cached hash under D.12) and a one-line D.10 clarification (an owner-defined 63-bit key is a valid `counter`). Index row-1 wording "Blocks" → "Block" routed. | Designed (locked) |
| Ship Section & Layout Data Model | Hard (provisional) | Layout owns room identity, polygon, volume `V` (tiles) and `exposed_tiles`; the Graph caches `V` and restores `restore_after: [layout.state]`. Compartments are keyed by Layout `room_id`; sockets reference Graph port ids. Section templates (node/edge lists with explicit numeric type IDs) are Layout/Item-DB data that `instantiate_section` consumes. Cuts happen only along seams, never through a compartment. | Undesigned — contract stated here, flagged provisional |
| Item & Module Database | Hard (provisional) | Module definitions reference this GDD's **port-type IDs** (stable numeric, append-only); `install_module` / `salvage_node` exchange `def_id` and `hp`; the loot roll is Item DB's. Full repair consumes an Item DB part; patch does not. | Undesigned — IDs defined here |
| Art bible | Constraint (hard) | Trail vocabulary (frost, mist, scorch, drip, hiss, hum, flicker) and the per-loop hue/pipe grammar (O₂ Cyan thin round pipe with ring clamps; Power Amber flat bus; Coolant Ice lagged pipe; Fuel Ember thick flanged pipe; Hull Grey plates) are what Failure & Trail renders from this GDD's semantic descriptors; the Graph emits no visuals and names no colours. Diegetic-only readability; no meter, no schematic. | Approved |

**Downstream (systems that depend on this one).** Hard unless marked. All are undesigned except the kernel, so each row is the contract this GDD *offers*; the dependent GDD must repeat it.

## Visual/Audio Requirements

The Graph draws nothing and plays nothing. It owns the **semantics** that Failure & Trail, In-World Instruments and Adaptive Audio render, and it constrains them:

- **Descriptors, not visuals.** Every presentation of a failure is derived from a `FailureDescriptor` (mode, medium, severity 0–4, intensity ‰, anchor ids, acoustic class, `alarm_eligible`). Medium selects the art bible's trail word — O₂ → mist, coolant → frost, power → scorch, fuel → drip, integrity → hairline/buckling — and severity selects the band; the Graph never names a colour, a sprite or a sound.
- **One trail per source, continuous along its edge** (art bible rule). A descriptor carries the source anchor and the edge it travels, so a trail is thickest at the source and never appears at a node without upstream evidence on the connecting edge. An orphan trail is therefore always a hallucination tell.
- **Spatial gradients are presentation.** Atmosphere is per compartment; frost creeping from a leak point is Failure & Trail's interpolation of the true compartment value plus the leak anchor and its age — honest to the Graph, never a per-tile simulation.
- **Lamps dim honestly.** `served_pm` drives lamp brightness under brownout; a lamp never renders brighter than the power it is served (P1).
- **Audio is true-state.** Hiss pitch/rate, hum, ticking and the loop whisper are read from true values; a hallucination may *add* audio but never remove a real hiss, and `alarm_eligible` (severity ≥ 3) is the only state in which an alarm-class sound or the Alarm Red sweep may play — never as the first warning.
- **The first fault the player ever sees** is the seeded coolant frost trail running from the cryo bay leak to the far wall (art bible carried element).

> 📌 **Asset Spec** — no sprites are owned here; the descriptor→trail mapping table is the input to `/asset-spec system:failure-and-trail-system` once that GDD exists.

## Game Feel

The Graph's feel is **slow burn, then cascade, then silence** — and the player should be able to say afterwards exactly why.

- **A body that decays on its own clock.** Left alone, the home-ship develops faults on minute-scale timers (first tell to lethal ≈ 6 min for an O₂ pinhole in a room, ≈ 9 for the ship; 4.5 for a power overload branch; 9 for coolant; 12 for hull fatigue); nothing resolves itself.
- **Long tell, short chaos.** Phases A (tell) and B (spread) are long and readable; C (cascade, propagation ×2) is short; D (loss) is final. The fairness gate guarantees ≥ 8 s of ≥ 2-channel physical warning before any endogenous irreversible loss, so "death is a bitch" is always nameable, never arbitrary.
- **Every fix moves a cost.** Power for air (the scrubber draws, the web watches); air for heat; a sealed door for a stranded room; a weld for a leaky seam; a salvaged battery for a dark ship. Triage of five coupled loops, not a repair list.
- **Derelicts are already dead.** They don't tick until the player brings power; then latent faults wake at half the home-ship's tell time, and a breach skips to cascade.
- **Truncation reads as physical.** Rooms never perfectly equalise (flux rounds to zero on tiny gradients); a faint pressure difference across a nearly-closed hatch is expected, not a bug.
- **Silence is a tell.** When a leak stops hissing, it is because there is nothing left to leak.

*Anti-targets*: self-healing faults, a rate dial that speeds everything, scripted "if A then B" cascades, dice-roll deaths, a status screen.

## UI Requirements

The Graph has no screens. It defines what three diegetic surfaces must be able to show, and forbids a fourth:

1. **In-World Instruments & Inspect View** — gauges read `read_view` at render rate for smooth needles (dirty keys only wake discrete presentation); a lit inspect card shows one instrument's precise reading and nothing else; gauges are per node, so two instruments on different nodes are the player's "second opinion".
2. **Failure & Trail** — trail spawn/despawn and band changes from `F/`, `C/`, `B/` keys; `T`/`SEC/` for structural rebuilds.
3. **HUD & Suit Layer** — the suit O₂ numeral on the critical strip is the suit's reading of compartment atmosphere via Suit, not a Graph overlay.
4. **Forbidden** — any schematic, overlay, minimap, ship-status or loop-summary screen that shows Graph state at a distance. The Debug Overlay (true values) is a development tool and is never shipped as a player surface.

> **📌 UX Flag — Life-Support Graph**: instruments, inspect card and trail legibility need `/ux-design` for In-World Instruments before epics; stories should cite `design/ux/instruments.md`.

## Overview

The Life-Support Graph is the ship's circulation written as data: one integer-only simulation block that holds **five loops** — O₂, power, coolant, fuel and integrity — as typed ports on nodes joined by typed edges, plus one atmosphere record (gas amount, temperature) per compartment. It is the physical ground truth the whole game is measured against. Every pipe that leaks, bus that scorches, seam that frosts, scrubber that stalls and hull plate that breaches is a change to this block, made only through its published mutators inside the kernel's write scope; every gauge, trail, hiss, breath-fog and cold-damage tick is a *reading* of it. The Graph is scene-tree free, headless-testable and deterministic (same seed and command stream → identical `state_hash`), serialises as one versioned snapshot, and is the data that co-op will later sync by summary.

The player never operates the Graph as a menu or a schematic. They meet it as a place: a corridor colder than it should be, chevrons crawling slow along a pipe, mist curling from a clamp, a lamp that dims when the scrubber draws. Their verbs — patch, flip a breaker, seal a bulkhead, close a valve, vent, salvage a module, weld a section on, crank by hand — arrive as Interaction commands that call Graph mutators; welding joins another ship's subgraph to this one along a seam. Failures are physical and emergent: a starved scrubber, a frozen pipe or an overloaded cable spreads one hop per propagation run through the quantities it changes, never by script, and every endogenous loss is preceded by a readable physical warning (the fairness gate). The Graph has no notion of a hallucination: it publishes true values only, so a false "fixed" scrubber can be caught by the cold, the thinning air and the hiss the Graph still drives.

Without this system there is no Pillar 1. Without a shared, honest, falsifiable physical state, the hallucination design (Pillar 4) has nothing to lie *against*, the web has no power draw to watch (Pillar 3), and salvage and welding have nothing to act on (Pillar 5). It is the design-order-3 bottleneck with fourteen dependents, and the MVP hypothesis — *the boarding→breach loop over a visible life-support graph is tense for 30+ minutes* — cannot be tested without it.

*Implementation questions raised while designing and deferred to ADRs (→ `/architecture-decision`): struct-of-arrays packed fields vs objects (ADR-LSG-01); the fixed-point unit system (ADR-LSG-02); the explicit one-pass propagation scheme (ADR-LSG-03); append-only topology identity (ADR-LSG-04); snapshot/restore and migration (ADR-LSG-05); dirty-key encoding (ADR-LSG-06); keyed RNG (ADR-LSG-07); stable content type IDs (ADR-LSG-08); and two routed amendments outside this system — the kernel's per-block cached hash (K-1) and Save/Load's binary interchange for 64-bit values (S-1).*

## Player Fantasy

**Framing: indirect, with a direct layer on top.** The player experiences the Graph through its consequences and acts on it through physical verbs; they never see "the Graph". *(creative-director consulted; Framing A adopted with B as its competence and C as its guarantee.)*

> The ship is a body the crew assembled from other ships' corpses, and the Life-Support Graph is its circulation: oxygen, power, coolant, fuel and the hull that holds them. The player never operates the Graph as a menu. They tend the ship: a corridor colder than it should be, chevrons crawling slow along a pipe, frost fanning out from a weld seam, a hiss behind a panel. They go to it with a light and their hands, and they reroute, seal, weld or cut.
>
> Competence is literacy, not optimisation. Every failure leaves a trail along the edge it travels, thickest at its source, so a veteran crew does not run the ship better than a new one; they understand sooner what it is telling them and reach the right seam faster.
>
> And the body never lies. Gauges can be wrong and eyes can be wrong, but the cold, the thin air and the falling pressure in a compartment come from the Graph's true state for every player. When the instruments and the room disagree, the room wins, and the player learns to trust it.

**Anchor moment.** You come back up the pod tube with a salvaged scrubber on your back, and the corridor is colder than you left it. The O₂ pipe along the ceiling is still lit cyan, but its chevrons are crawling slower than they should, and there is a fine white fan of frost on the elbow by the galley. Your own breath hangs in the beam. You set the scrubber down, put your glove on the pipe, and follow the cold back to where it started — the way you would check a sleeping friend's forehead. The emotion is *caretaking under threat*: tenderness and vigilance. The power is not control; it is keeping something alive by attention — the Project Zomboid base you built with your own hands, made precarious (concept, Core Fantasy).

**Pillar alignment.** Pillar 1 verbatim: *"Pipes leak, frost forms, air hisses; the physical world is ground truth. Only instruments and perception can be wrong … A pipe may look fixed, but the room still gets cold, the air still thins, the pressure still drops."* The Graph is that ground truth. Pillar 2 (Dread Before Chaos): every fault has a long, readable tell before it cascades. Pillar 3: keeping the air clean draws power, and power draw is something the web can read. Pillar 4: the Graph is the falsification ground every hallucination is tested against. Pillar 5: salvage and welding act on its nodes; a lost compartment is not a lost ship.

**Design test.** *When a choice makes the ship easier to read from a screen vs. easier to read from the room → choose the room. When a choice rewards running the ship well vs. rewards noticing it is unwell → choose noticing.* Corollaries: a fault persists and spreads until someone goes to it (never times out); a failure's origin is shown by a trail the player follows back along the edge, never by a marker; a hallucinated "fixed" state never quiets the real hiss or warms the real room.

**Under hallucination the fantasy deepens rather than breaks.** Pillar 4 lets the lie extend from the gauge to the sprite — a broken scrubber may render whole and spinning. What cannot change is the consequence channel: compartment temperature, O₂ and pressure, and the frost, mist, scorch, drip and hiss that Failure & Trail and Adaptive Audio render as pure readers of the Graph's true values. The caretaker who can no longer trust their eyes falls back on breath, cold and touch — the oldest reading of a body. Verification costs rise in order: the room itself; a second instrument elsewhere on the ship; a saner crewmate (VS-B); time.

**Reference techniques, taken precisely.** Project Zomboid — the base degrades on its own clock and competence is the routine of noticing (*adopt*); its numeric context-menu condition readouts (*reject*). Barotrauma — repair is a place you go with the right tool; a junction box fails *where it is* (*adopt*); the Status Monitor ship-overview screen (*reject*). Dwarf Fortress fluids — propagation is visible in the medium, not announced (*adopt*). The Long Dark — cold is read from breath vapour before any number (*adopt*). SS13 / Stationeers — precision is something you go and get (*adopt* as the lit inspect card); their gas chemistry (*reject*: five loops, not chemistry). FTL — door-control causality (*adopt*); per-room O₂ shading on a schematic (*reject*). Alien: Isolation — checking costs you (*adopt*). Pandorum — the failing ship as the only reliable narrator (*adopt*).

**What this GDD does not promise (anti-pillar guard rails).**
1. No mastery-by-optimisation: no efficiency, "optimal layout", throughput score, uptime grade or any reward for running loops near capacity. Staying alive is the only payoff.
2. The web is not a puzzle to solve: failures are not authored puzzles with one correct sequence; there is no "solved" state and no completion ping.
3. No schematic, overlay, minimap or ship-status screen. Precision exists only as the lit inspect card of a specific instrument (art bible 7.0), which lies when that gauge lies. The suit's O₂ numeral on the critical strip is the *suit's* reading, not a Graph overlay.
4. No progression from the Graph: nothing unlocks or levels from repairs; better modules come from salvage.
5. No readability in the dark: "What You Light, You Can Read" — unlit compartments are readable only through the body channels (cold, breath, hiss, pressure), never by sprite state.
6. No sixth loop and no "heat loop": heat and pressure are per-compartment atmosphere.
7. No freeform plumbing: rerouting is valves, breakers, hatches, seams and cuts on pre-shaped modules.
8. No guarantee the ship can always be saved. Losing a section or the ship is allowed; the failure contract (Pillar 5) is the safety net, not the Graph.

## Overview

The Life-Support Graph is the ship's circulation written as data: one integer-only simulation block that holds **five loops** — O₂, power, coolant, fuel and integrity — as typed ports on nodes joined by typed edges, plus one atmosphere record (gas amount, temperature) per compartment. It is the physical ground truth the whole game is measured against. Every pipe that leaks, bus that scorches, seam that frosts, scrubber that stalls and hull plate that breaches is a change to this block, made only through its published mutators inside the kernel's write scope; every gauge, trail, hiss, breath-fog and cold-damage tick is a *reading* of it. The Graph is scene-tree free, headless-testable and deterministic (same seed and command stream → identical `state_hash`), serialises as one versioned snapshot, and is the data that co-op will later sync by summary.

The player never operates the Graph as a menu or a schematic. They meet it as a place: a corridor colder than it should be, chevrons crawling slow along a pipe, mist curling from a clamp, a lamp that dims when the scrubber draws. Their verbs — patch, flip a breaker, seal a bulkhead, close a valve, vent, salvage a module, weld a section on, crank by hand — arrive as Interaction commands that call Graph mutators; welding joins another ship's subgraph to this one along a seam. Failures are physical and emergent: a starved scrubber, a frozen pipe or an overloaded cable spreads one hop per propagation run through the quantities it changes, never by script, and every endogenous loss is preceded by a readable physical warning (the fairness gate). The Graph has no notion of a hallucination: it publishes true values only, so a false "fixed" scrubber can be caught by the cold, the thinning air and the hiss the Graph still drives.

Without this system there is no Pillar 1. Without a shared, honest, falsifiable physical state, the hallucination design (Pillar 4) has nothing to lie *against*, the web has no power draw to watch (Pillar 3), and salvage and welding have nothing to act on (Pillar 5). It is the design-order-3 bottleneck with fourteen dependents, and the MVP hypothesis — *the boarding→breach loop over a visible life-support graph is tense for 30+ minutes* — cannot be tested without it.

*Implementation questions raised while designing and deferred to ADRs (→ `/architecture-decision`): struct-of-arrays packed fields vs objects (ADR-LSG-01); the fixed-point unit system (ADR-LSG-02); the explicit one-pass propagation scheme (ADR-LSG-03); append-only topology identity (ADR-LSG-04); snapshot/restore and migration (ADR-LSG-05); dirty-key encoding (ADR-LSG-06); keyed RNG (ADR-LSG-07); stable content type IDs (ADR-LSG-08); and two routed amendments outside this system — the kernel's per-block cached hash (K-1) and Save/Load's binary interchange for 64-bit values (S-1).*

## Player Fantasy

**Framing: indirect, with a direct layer on top.** The player experiences the Graph through its consequences and acts on it through physical verbs; they never see "the Graph". *(creative-director consulted; Framing A adopted with B as its competence and C as its guarantee.)*

> The ship is a body the crew assembled from other ships' corpses, and the Life-Support Graph is its circulation: oxygen, power, coolant, fuel and the hull that holds them. The player never operates the Graph as a menu. They tend the ship: a corridor colder than it should be, chevrons crawling slow along a pipe, frost fanning out from a weld seam, a hiss behind a panel. They go to it with a light and their hands, and they reroute, seal, weld or cut.
>
> Competence is literacy, not optimisation. Every failure leaves a trail along the edge it travels, thickest at its source, so a veteran crew does not run the ship better than a new one; they understand sooner what it is telling them and reach the right seam faster.
>
> And the body never lies. Gauges can be wrong and eyes can be wrong, but the cold, the thin air and the falling pressure in a compartment come from the Graph's true state for every player. When the instruments and the room disagree, the room wins, and the player learns to trust it.

**Anchor moment.** You come back up the pod tube with a salvaged scrubber on your back, and the corridor is colder than you left it. The O₂ pipe along the ceiling is still lit cyan, but its chevrons are crawling slower than they should, and there is a fine white fan of frost on the elbow by the galley. Your own breath hangs in the beam. You set the scrubber down, put your glove on the pipe, and follow the cold back to where it started — the way you would check a sleeping friend's forehead. The emotion is *caretaking under threat*: tenderness and vigilance. The power is not control; it is keeping something alive by attention — the Project Zomboid base you built with your own hands, made precarious (concept, Core Fantasy).

**Pillar alignment.** Pillar 1 verbatim: *"Pipes leak, frost forms, air hisses; the physical world is ground truth. Pillar 4: the Graph is the falsification ground every hallucination is tested against. Pillar 5: salvage and welding act on its nodes; a lost compartment is not a lost ship.

**Design test.** *When a choice makes the ship easier to read from a screen vs. easier to read from the room → choose the room. **Under hallucination the fantasy deepens rather than breaks.** Pillar 4 lets the lie extend from the gauge to the sprite — a broken scrubber may render whole and spinning. What cannot change is the consequence channel: compartment temperature, O₂ and pressure, and the frost, mist, scorch, drip and hiss that Failure & Trail and Adaptive Audio render as pure readers of the Graph's true values. The caretaker who can no longer trust their eyes falls back on breath, cold and touch — the oldest reading of a body. Verification costs rise in order: the room itself; a second instrument elsewhere on the ship; a saner crewmate (VS-B); time.

**Reference techniques, taken precisely.** Project Zomboid — the base degrades on its own clock and competence is the routine of noticing (*adopt*); its numeric context-menu condition readouts (*reject*). Barotrauma — repair is a place you go with the right tool; a junction box fails *where it is* (*adopt*); the Status Monitor ship-overview screen (*reject*). Dwarf Fortress fluids — propagation is visible in the medium, not announced (*adopt*). The Long Dark — cold is read from breath vapour before any number (*adopt*). SS13 / Stationeers — precision is something you go and get (*adopt* as the lit inspect card); their gas chemistry (*reject*: five loops, not chemistry). FTL — door-control causality (*adopt*); per-room O₂ shading on a schematic (*reject*). Alien: Isolation — checking costs you (*adopt*). Pandorum — the failing ship as the only reliable narrator (*adopt*).

**What this GDD does not promise (anti-pillar guard rails).**
1. No mastery-by-optimisation: no efficiency, "optimal layout", throughput score, uptime grade or any reward for running loops near capacity. Staying alive is the only payoff.
2. The web is not a puzzle to solve: failures are not authored puzzles with one correct sequence; there is no "solved" state and no completion ping.
3. No schematic, overlay, minimap or ship-status screen. Precision exists only as the lit inspect card of a specific instrument (art bible 7.0), which lies when that gauge lies. The suit's O₂ numeral on the critical strip is the *suit's* reading, not a Graph overlay.
4. No progression from the Graph: nothing unlocks or levels from repairs; better modules come from salvage.
5. No readability in the dark: "What You Light, You Can Read" — unlit compartments are readable only through the body channels (cold, breath, hiss, pressure), never by sprite state.
6. No sixth loop and no "heat loop": heat and pressure are per-compartment atmosphere.
7. No freeform plumbing: rerouting is valves, breakers, hatches, seams and cuts on pre-shaped modules.
8. No guarantee the ship can always be saved. Losing a section or the ship is allowed; the failure contract (Pillar 5) is the safety net, not the Graph.

- **A body that decays on its own clock.** Left alone, the home-ship develops faults on minute-scale timers (first tell to lethal ≈ 6 min for an O₂ pinhole in a room, ≈ 9 for the ship; 4.5 for a power overload branch; 9 for coolant; 12 for hull fatigue); nothing resolves itself.
- **Long tell, short chaos.** Phases A (tell) and B (spread) are long and readable; C (cascade, propagation ×2) is short; D (loss) is final. The fairness gate guarantees ≥ 8 s of ≥ 2-channel physical warning before any endogenous irreversible loss, so "death is a bitch" is always nameable, never arbitrary.
- **Every fix moves a cost.** Power for air (the scrubber draws, the web watches); air for heat; a sealed door for a stranded room; a weld for a leaky seam; a salvaged battery for a dark ship. Triage of five coupled loops, not a repair list.
- **Derelicts are already dead.** They don't tick until the player brings power; then latent faults wake at half the home-ship's tell time, and a breach skips to cascade.
- **Truncation reads as physical.** Rooms never perfectly equalise (flux rounds to zero on tiny gradients); a faint pressure difference across a nearly-closed hatch is expected, not a bug.
- **Silence is a tell.** When a leak stops hissing, it is because there is nothing left to leak.

*Anti-targets*: self-healing faults, a rate dial that speeds everything, scripted "if A then B" cascades, dice-roll deaths, a status screen.

## UI Requirements

The Graph has no screens. It defines what three diegetic surfaces must be able to show, and forbids a fourth:

1. **In-World Instruments & Inspect View** — gauges read `read_view` at render rate for smooth needles (dirty keys only wake discrete presentation); a lit inspect card shows one instrument's precise reading and nothing else; gauges are per node, so two instruments on different nodes are the player's "second opinion".
2. **Failure & Trail** — trail spawn/despawn and band changes from `F/`, `C/`, `B/` keys; `T`/`SEC/` for structural rebuilds.
3. **HUD & Suit Layer** — the suit O₂ numeral on the critical strip is the suit's reading of compartment atmosphere via Suit, not a Graph overlay.
4. **Forbidden** — any schematic, overlay, minimap, ship-status or loop-summary screen that shows Graph state at a distance. The Debug Overlay (true values) is a development tool and is never shipped as a player surface.

> **📌 UX Flag — Life-Support Graph**: instruments, inspect card and trail legibility need `/ux-design` for In-World Instruments before epics; stories should cite `design/ux/instruments.md`.

## Overview

The Life-Support Graph is the ship's circulation written as data: one integer-only simulation block that holds **five loops** — O₂, power, coolant, fuel and integrity — as typed ports on nodes joined by typed edges, plus one atmosphere record (gas amount, temperature) per compartment. It is the physical ground truth the whole game is measured against. Every pipe that leaks, bus that scorches, seam that frosts, scrubber that stalls and hull plate that breaches is a change to this block, made only through its published mutators inside the kernel's write scope; every gauge, trail, hiss, breath-fog and cold-damage tick is a *reading* of it. The Graph is scene-tree free, headless-testable and deterministic (same seed and command stream → identical `state_hash`), serialises as one versioned snapshot, and is the data that co-op will later sync by summary.

The player never operates the Graph as a menu or a schematic. They meet it as a place: a corridor colder than it should be, chevrons crawling slow along a pipe, mist curling from a clamp, a lamp that dims when the scrubber draws. Their verbs — patch, flip a breaker, seal a bulkhead, close a valve, vent, salvage a module, weld a section on, crank by hand — arrive as Interaction commands that call Graph mutators; welding joins another ship's subgraph to this one along a seam. Failures are physical and emergent: a starved scrubber, a frozen pipe or an overloaded cable spreads one hop per propagation run through the quantities it changes, never by script, and every endogenous loss is preceded by a readable physical warning (the fairness gate). The Graph has no notion of a hallucination: it publishes true values only, so a false "fixed" scrubber can be caught by the cold, the thinning air and the hiss the Graph still drives.

Without this system there is no Pillar 1. Without a shared, honest, falsifiable physical state, the hallucination design (Pillar 4) has nothing to lie *against*, the web has no power draw to watch (Pillar 3), and salvage and welding have nothing to act on (Pillar 5). It is the design-order-3 bottleneck with fourteen dependents, and the MVP hypothesis — *the boarding→breach loop over a visible life-support graph is tense for 30+ minutes* — cannot be tested without it.

*Implementation questions raised while designing and deferred to ADRs (→ `/architecture-decision`): struct-of-arrays packed fields vs objects (ADR-LSG-01); the fixed-point unit system (ADR-LSG-02); the explicit one-pass propagation scheme (ADR-LSG-03); append-only topology identity (ADR-LSG-04); snapshot/restore and migration (ADR-LSG-05); dirty-key encoding (ADR-LSG-06); keyed RNG (ADR-LSG-07); stable content type IDs (ADR-LSG-08); and two routed amendments outside this system — the kernel's per-block cached hash (K-1) and Save/Load's binary interchange for 64-bit values (S-1).*

## Player Fantasy

**Framing: indirect, with a direct layer on top.** The player experiences the Graph through its consequences and acts on it through physical verbs; they never see "the Graph". *(creative-director consulted; Framing A adopted with B as its competence and C as its guarantee.)*

> The ship is a body the crew assembled from other ships' corpses, and the Life-Support Graph is its circulation: oxygen, power, coolant, fuel and the hull that holds them. The player never operates the Graph as a menu. They tend the ship: a corridor colder than it should be, chevrons crawling slow along a pipe, frost fanning out from a weld seam, a hiss behind a panel. They go to it with a light and their hands, and they reroute, seal, weld or cut.
>
> Competence is literacy, not optimisation. Every failure leaves a trail along the edge it travels, thickest at its source, so a veteran crew does not run the ship better than a new one; they understand sooner what it is telling them and reach the right seam faster.
>
> And the body never lies. Gauges can be wrong and eyes can be wrong, but the cold, the thin air and the falling pressure in a compartment come from the Graph's true state for every player. When the instruments and the room disagree, the room wins, and the player learns to trust it.

**Anchor moment.** You come back up the pod tube with a salvaged scrubber on your back, and the corridor is colder than you left it. The O₂ pipe along the ceiling is still lit cyan, but its chevrons are crawling slower than they should, and there is a fine white fan of frost on the elbow by the galley. Your own breath hangs in the beam. You set the scrubber down, put your glove on the pipe, and follow the cold back to where it started — the way you would check a sleeping friend's forehead. The emotion is *caretaking under threat*: tenderness and vigilance. The power is not control; it is keeping something alive by attention — the Project Zomboid base you built with your own hands, made precarious (concept, Core Fantasy).

**Pillar alignment.** Pillar 1 verbatim: *"Pipes leak, frost forms, air hisses; the physical world is ground truth. Only instruments and perception can be wrong … A pipe may look fixed, but the room still gets cold, the air still thins, the pressure still drops."* The Graph is that ground truth. Pillar 2 (Dread Before Chaos): every fault has a long, readable tell before it cascades. Pillar 3: keeping the air clean draws power, and power draw is something the web can read. Pillar 4: the Graph is the falsification ground every hallucination is tested against. Pillar 5: salvage and welding act on its nodes; a lost compartment is not a lost ship.

**Design test.** *When a choice makes the ship easier to read from a screen vs. easier to read from the room → choose the room. When a choice rewards running the ship well vs. rewards noticing it is unwell → choose noticing.* Corollaries: a fault persists and spreads until someone goes to it (never times out); a failure's origin is shown by a trail the player follows back along the edge, never by a marker; a hallucinated "fixed" state never quiets the real hiss or warms the real room.

**Under hallucination the fantasy deepens rather than breaks.** Pillar 4 lets the lie extend from the gauge to the sprite — a broken scrubber may render whole and spinning. What cannot change is the consequence channel: compartment temperature, O₂ and pressure, and the frost, mist, scorch, drip and hiss that Failure & Trail and Adaptive Audio render as pure readers of the Graph's true values. The caretaker who can no longer trust their eyes falls back on breath, cold and touch — the oldest reading of a body. Verification costs rise in order: the room itself; a second instrument elsewhere on the ship; a saner crewmate (VS-B); time.

**Reference techniques, taken precisely.** Project Zomboid — the base degrades on its own clock and competence is the routine of noticing (*adopt*); its numeric context-menu condition readouts (*reject*). Barotrauma — repair is a place you go with the right tool; a junction box fails *where it is* (*adopt*); the Status Monitor ship-overview screen (*reject*). Dwarf Fortress fluids — propagation is visible in the medium, not announced (*adopt*). The Long Dark — cold is read from breath vapour before any number (*adopt*). SS13 / Stationeers — precision is something you go and get (*adopt* as the lit inspect card); their gas chemistry (*reject*: five loops, not chemistry). FTL — door-control causality (*adopt*); per-room O₂ shading on a schematic (*reject*). Alien: Isolation — checking costs you (*adopt*). Pandorum — the failing ship as the only reliable narrator (*adopt*).

**What this GDD does not promise (anti-pillar guard rails).**
1. No mastery-by-optimisation: no efficiency, "optimal layout", throughput score, uptime grade or any reward for running loops near capacity. Staying alive is the only payoff.
2. The web is not a puzzle to solve: failures are not authored puzzles with one correct sequence; there is no "solved" state and no completion ping.
3. No schematic, overlay, minimap or ship-status screen. Precision exists only as the lit inspect card of a specific instrument (art bible 7.0), which lies when that gauge lies. The suit's O₂ numeral on the critical strip is the *suit's* reading, not a Graph overlay.
4. No progression from the Graph: nothing unlocks or levels from repairs; better modules come from salvage.
5. No readability in the dark: "What You Light, You Can Read" — unlit compartments are readable only through the body channels (cold, breath, hiss, pressure), never by sprite state.
6. No sixth loop and no "heat loop": heat and pressure are per-compartment atmosphere.
7. No freeform plumbing: rerouting is valves, breakers, hatches, seams and cuts on pre-shaped modules.
8. No guarantee the ship can always be saved. Losing a section or the ship is allowed; the failure contract (Pillar 5) is the safety net, not the Graph.

### Core Rules

*Every rule below is a sim rule of the Graph owner module (`src/sim/graph/`), stated so that an implementer can write it and a tester can falsify it. Registry constants are cited by their registered name (`TICK_RATE`, `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS`, `STEP_BUDGET_MS`, `rng_derive`, `state_hash`, `hook_runs_this_tick`, `TILE_PX`); every constant this GDD introduces is written by the registry name it proposes (Section G marks the candidates). Type IDs are explicit, stable, checked unique at boot and never reused (R19). Where a rule records an alternative that was considered and rejected, the rejection is part of the rule: a later change must answer it.*

**LS-1 — One block, one determinism contract.** The Graph is exactly one persisted SIM state block, `graph.state` (owner Graph; `class` SIM; `persist` true; `persist_scope` WORLD; `scope` SHARED; `repl_hint` SHARED_SUMMARY; `schema_version` 1; `restore_after: [layout.state]`), registered by the Graph's composition-root call during BOOTING. **LS-2 — Five loops, no sixth.** Loop ids: `0 NONE` (non-loop couplings), `1 O2`, `2 POWER`, `3 COOLANT`, `4 FUEL`, `5 INTEGRITY`. ## Summary

The Life-Support Graph is the ship's circulation as one integer-only, scene-tree-free simulation block: five loops (O₂, power, coolant, fuel, integrity) as typed ports, nodes and edges, plus a per-compartment atmosphere (gas amount, temperature; pressure and bands derived). It is the physical ground truth every trail, gauge, hiss, breath-fog and cold-damage tick is read from, and the only thing in the game that never lies — hallucinations are tested against it, never written into it. Failures spread one hop per 10 Hz propagation run through the quantities they change, every endogenous loss is preceded by ≥ 8 s of two-channel physical warning, and welding another ship's section joins its subgraph along a seam whose sub-edges start disconnected. Everything that fails, glows, leaks or is salvaged reads or writes it through 18 published mutators and one true-value read view.

> **Quick reference** — Layer: `Core` · Priority: `MVP` · Key deps: `Command & Simulation Layer` (designed; one block `graph.state`, three hooks at divisor 6); `Ship Section & Layout Data Model` and `Item & Module Database` (undesigned — ownership and port-type contracts stated here, provisional); art bible (trail and loop grammar). Depended on by 14 systems (Failure & Trail, Suit, Emitter State, Attention, Interaction, Assembly, Horror, Perception/Instruments, Audio, Save/Load, Sanity, Web Map, Wear, Failure Contract, Co-op, Onboarding).

For the render pipeline, controller, kernel and systems index I grepped their pillar headers and truth-channel lines; I did not read them in full.
  
  Overall: the Player Fantasy matches the core fantasy closely. "Caretaking under threat" and "competence is literacy, not optimisation" are the right reading, and the eight guard rails defend the anti-pillars. I found no violation that needs a redesign. The fixes below are mostly wording, plus one schema hole and one missing witness.
  
  Adversarial questions, short answers:
  (1) Optimisation and solved state: no reward for optimising (D3 and D7 hold). But a quiet "solved" state can be reached after full repair. See #4.
  (2) Fairness gate: it honours "death is a bitch". It only delays a failure by under 2 s and the extra damage is discarded, not forgiven. The default sits below Pillar 2's own number, see #3.
  (3) Weld ruling: it passes. The drama moves to a verb the player chooses, and the seam weep is the weld's own tell. That is more P2-coherent, not sanitised. One gap remains, see #5.
  (4) Hallucination boundary: the prose draws the boundary correctly, but the schema and two lines leave it open. See #1 and #2.
  (5) Tone: Player Fantasy and Overview paragraph 2 are in the game's voice. Game Feel slips into engineering terms in two lines (#7). Core Rules are allowed to be engineering-speak.
  (6) Contradictions: the "orphan trail" line conflicts with the systems index and the render pipeline (#2). I found no other new conflict. The concept's "O₂, heat and power" wording is already flagged in OQ-15.
  
  Concerns:
  1. LS-14 / LS-10 (States). Quote: "OK → DEGRADED … subject descriptor at sev 1". A module losing hp alone (no LEAK or OVERHEAT mode) still has to emit a descriptor, but the `mode` enum has no value for that case, and `medium`/`acoustic` have no NONE. If Failure & Trail renders that descriptor on the truth channel, then "broken reads as fixed" (P4b) is disproved for free on every module, which collapses the verification economy. Fix: add an hp-only mode (e.g. `WORN`) with `medium`/`acoustic` NONE. Then state in LS-14 that COMPARTMENT, EDGE, SEAM and OPENING descriptors and leak or hazard modes are the consequence channel, and that the module-body state (sprite, gauge, inspect card) can be corrupted. Mirror this in LS-22 and in the Player Fantasy hallucination paragraph.
  2. LS-13, Visual/Audio, Dependencies (Perception row). Quotes: "a filter may add or alter sprites and gauges but never remove a hiss"; "a hallucination may *add* audio"; "An orphan trail is therefore always a hallucination tell." Pillar 1 says physical consequences can't be altered at all, and the systems index and render pipeline make trails truth-channel and immune to the Filter. Letting a hallucination add a hiss or an orphan trail is a lie told through the consequence channel. Fix: define the consequence channel as a closed list: trail VFX, the LS-14 acoustic classes at a descriptor anchor, Suit body cues (breath, fog, vignette, shiver), lamp brightness from `served_pm`, and draught. Perception may not remove, alter or add anything on that list. Phantom-entity audio is the Filter's and must not use a witness class. Delete the orphan-trail sentence, or change it to "an orphan trail cannot occur".
  3. LS-13 / D.11 / Game Feel. Quote: "`W_MIN_WARNING_S` = 8". Pillar 2's design test says a "10–30 second escalating tell". The floor sits under the pillar's lower bound, and every Attention or horror breach is EXOGENOUS, so it skips the gate. Fix: (a) raise the default to 10, or add one sentence saying the gate is the sim's own floor and real tells run in minutes (D.15). (b) Add an exported requirement in LS-13 and OQ-2: any non-player exogenous source (M17 RUPTURE/GOUGE/STRESS, M18 from the environment) must be preceded by Attention's or Horror's own 10–30 s P2 tell. "The gate protects against the sim, not against agency" must not read as "Pillar 2 does not apply to horrors".
  4. Game Feel vs D.9. Quote: "Left alone, the home-ship develops faults on minute-scale timers". D.9 applies wear only to LEAK, OVERHEAT, fatigued or patched subjects. After a FULL repair (and plate replacement), the only clock left is fuel, about 4.6 h at the HEALTHY 1020 W load. That is a solved, safe-harbour state, against Pillar 5 "no safe place" and guard rail 2. The D1/D4 countermeasures depend on authored fatigue. Fix: either (a) add a small MVP duty-wear term `W_DUTY` on running machines (scrubber, pump, reactor) to D.9 and LS-25, or (b) rewrite the claim as "decays from its authored faults", name Resource Depletion & Wear (VS) as the owner of P5's no-safe-farm rule, and add an OQ.
  5. LS-15 / D.14 / Edge Cases "seams". Quote: "the warning is diegetic (hiss at the hatch, the gauge)". With hatch `area` 0 there is no flow, so no AIRFLOW descriptor exists. The hiss has nothing in the Graph behind it. A gauge lying about ΔP across a closed hatch can then only be disproved by opening it, which is the lethal act, so P4 "no lie is unfalsifiable" fails. Fix: emit a sev-1 descriptor on a closed OPENING when |ΔP| > `WELD_DP_WARN` (e.g. a seal-strain whistle or creak, rim frost when ΔT is large), and add "pressure across a closed hatch" to the LS-22 witness table. Also state that `surge[]` reaches the player only through diegetic tells and corruptible instruments, never as a number in a weld preview (guard rail 3).
  6. Header "Implements Pillar". It leaves out P2, though the fairness gate is a tempo rule and Player Fantasy and Game Feel both claim P2. It leaves out P4 (the LS-22 falsification ground). It over-claims P5: salvage and weld are Assembly and Item DB verbs, and the Graph is only what they act on. Under the bar applied to the render pipeline: "Implements: P1 (primary); P2 (endogenous warning floor); P4 (falsification ground). Serves: P3 (power-use stimulus); P5 (substrate for salvage, weld and wear)". Also, Player Fantasy line 39 says "a lost compartment is not a lost ship", which misreads P5's failure contract (knowledge persists). Replace it with "salvage and welding act on its nodes; loss is the failure contract's, not the Graph's".
  7. Game Feel (tone). Quotes: "Phases A (tell) and B (spread) … C (cascade, propagation ×2)"; "Truncation reads as physical … flux rounds to zero"; "a breach skips to cascade". These lines are in a player-facing section, and the last one reads as if derelicts skip the tell. Fix: say it in the voice of the place ("a long tell, a spreading wrongness, a short collapse"; "rooms never quite settle; a faint draught at a nearly-shut hatch is real"). For derelicts: "faults that wake run twice as fast — but still warn first."
  
  Recommended order: #1, #2, #5 (the P4 boundary), then #3 and #4, then #6 and #7. No re-gate is needed if the changes stay as worded above.

== 9
> **Implements Pillar**: P1 The World Never Lies (the graph is the physical ground truth every instrument, trail and hallucination is measured against); P3 The Web Watches (power use and light are graph loads the web can read); P5 Deeper Is Richer, Loss Is Not Total (salvage and welding act on graph nodes)
== 39
**Pillar alignment.** Pillar 1 verbatim: *"Pipes leak, frost forms, air hisses; the physical world is ground truth. Only instruments and perception can be wrong … A pipe may look fixed, but the room still gets cold, the air still thins, the pressure still drops."* The Graph is that ground truth. Pillar 2 (Dread Before Chaos): every fault has a long, readable tell before it cascades. Pillar 3: keeping the air clean draws power, and power draw is something the web can read. Pillar 4: the Graph is the falsification ground every hallucination is tested against. Pillar 5: salvage and welding act on its nodes; a lost compartment is not a lost ship.
== 849
| Perception Filter / In-World Instruments | `true_value(kind,id)` and `read_view` — the Filter is the only non-diagnostic reader that may *wrap* a true value; it may add or alter sprites and gauges but never suppress a true descriptor's acoustic or physical channel | nothing (PERCEPTION_OUT never feeds the Graph, CR-12) | PRESENTATION | Yes (Instruments) / **No — add edge (Perception Filter)** |
== 956
- **One trail per source, continuous along its edge** (art bible rule). A descriptor carries the source anchor and the edge it travels, so a trail is thickest at the source and never appears at a node without upstream evidence on the connecting edge. An orphan trail is therefore always a hallucination tell.
== 959
- **Audio is true-state.** Hiss pitch/rate, hum, ticking and the loop whisper are read from true values; a hallucination may *add* audio but never remove a real hiss, and `alarm_eligible` (severity ≥ 3) is the only state in which an alarm-class sound or the Alarm Red sweep may play — never as the first warning.
== 968
- **A body that decays on its own clock.** Left alone, the home-ship develops faults on minute-scale timers (first tell to lethal ≈ 6 min for an O₂ pinhole in a room, ≈ 9 for the ship; 4.5 for a power overload branch; 9 for coolant; 12 for hull fatigue); nothing resolves itself.
== 969
- **Long tell, short chaos.** Phases A (tell) and B (spread) are long and readable; C (cascade, propagation ×2) is short; D (loss) is final. The fairness gate guarantees ≥ 8 s of ≥ 2-channel physical warning before any endogenous irreversible loss, so "death is a bitch" is always nameable, never arbitrary.
== 971
- **Derelicts are already dead.** They don't tick until the player brings power; then latent faults wake at half the home-ship's tell time, and a breach skips to cascade.
== 972
- **Truncation reads as physical.** Rooms never perfectly equalise (flux rounds to zero on tiny gradients); a faint pressure difference across a nearly-closed hatch is expected, not a bug.
== 13 summary snippet
13:every endogenous loss is preceded by ≥ 8 s of two-channel physical warning
969:The fairness gate guarantees ≥ 8 s of ≥ 2-channel physical warning before any endogenous irreversible loss, so "death is a bitch" is always nameable, never arbitrary.

- LS-10 DEGRADED definition (WORN mention).
- LS-11: `10 WORN` entry appended after SCRAM; SEAL_STRAIN cross-reference sentence.
- LS-13: W_MIN_WARNING_S 10 / W_MIN_STEPS 100 / "100 consecutive steps"; new **exported requirement** paragraph (non-player exogenous sources M17 RUPTURE/GOUGE/STRESS and environmental M18 need Attention's/Horror's own 10–30 s Pillar 2 tell; gate protects against the sim, not agency); R17 clause scoped to consequence-channel descriptors (medium ≠ NONE).

- LS-15: diegetic-warning sentence → SEAL_STRAIN; `surge[]` never a number in a weld preview (preview may read `surge[].warn` only).
- LS-22 witness table: new third column "Channel (LS-14)" on every row; new row "Pressure across a closed hatch" (consequence); trailing sentence on WORN having no row.
- LS-25: duty added to the wear list with the 4.2 h arithmetic.
- LS-26: "modes live" list notes WORN and SEAL_STRAIN as live-by-construction non-hazard modes.
- States table: OK→DEGRADED row names WORN; FAILED (forced) row FREEZE ≥ 100 steps; Mode overlays line gains WORN on/off.

- D.9: W_base Derived line gains the duty term; variable table gains `W_DUTY_BP_PER_100` and `duty_pm` rows; Output Range gains the duty paragraph and "at least 10 s"; Example gains the scrubber duty worked case (2 bp → hp 6998 at step 150,100; served_pm 400 → 1 bp).

- D.13 product table: new row `W_DUTY_BP_PER_100 × duty_pm` (6 × 1000).
- D.14: new Derived line (SEAL_STRAIN trigger/clear/hysteresis, surge outlet); variable table gains `HATCH_DT_FROST_MC` and `H_P, H_T` rows and extends WELD_DP_WARN's description; Output Range "(the hiss at the hatch)" → SEAL_STRAIN; Example gains the closed-hatch worked case (850 dkPa / 50,000 mC; 299→295 hysteresis).
- D.15 table: new **DUTY** reference row.
Section E (Edge Cases):
- Fairness gate bullet 1: 100 steps, ρ ≥ 1317, 40+ bp, hold arithmetic (37 steps; arc-flash ~98 steps); forced-mode bullet "100 steps later".
- New bullet under Patch/repair: duty wear at partial served_pm.

input.prompt:
Run a READ-ONLY consistency scan in D:\the-synaptic-sea-2d (the /consistency-check skill's Phase 3-4). Do NOT edit or write any file.

Registry: design/registry/entities.yaml (79 entries: formulas + constants; `source:` is the owner; `referenced_by` lists consumers; comments "# pending referenced_by" name GDDs not yet written — ignore those). In scope: design/gdd/command-simulation-layer.md, design/gdd/pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md, design/gdd/player-controller-input.md, and the NEW design/gdd/life-support-graph.md (254 KB — never read whole; Grep with -C 3 and Read offset/limit). The first three were scanned clean earlier today; focus on what the new GDD adds.

Checks:
1. For every registry entry name, grep all four GDDs; compare stated values to the registry (constants: numbers; formulas: expression/variables/output). Pay special attention to the 29 entries whose source is life-support-graph.md (W_MIN_WARNING_S must be 10 everywhere — "8 s"/"80 steps" is stale; GRAPH_STEP_TICKS 6; GAS_SCALE 1000; band constants COLD_DMG_ONSET_MC -15000 / HEAT_DMG_ONSET_MC 45000 / HYPOXIA_PP 140 / DECOMP_P 400; PATCH_CAP_BP 6000; PATCH_DECAY_S 240; WELD_DP_WARN 300; SEAM_LEAK_INITIAL_BP 10000; MAX_SPREAD_PER_STEP 32; MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP 16; MAX_GRAPH_NODES 4096; W_DUTY_BP_PER_100 2; HATCH_DT_FROST_MC 20000; formulas fairness_gate, atmosphere_derive, power_allocation, seam_at_weld, dirty_key_budget) and to how the Graph GDD cites the kernel's entries (TICK_RATE 60, MAX_DIRTY_KEYS 256 — must be "confirmed", not "set"; STEP_BUDGET_MS 4; rng_derive; state_hash — the Graph must cite the registered forms and present K-1 / D.10-counter as routed amendments, not as its own rule; hook_runs_this_tick; TILE_PX 48).
2. Cross-GDD contract checks: the kernel GDD's Interactions row 1 for the Life-Support Graph vs the Graph GDD's LS-1/Dependencies (block count, hook names `graph.propagate.power/.atmo/.failure` at divisor 6, mutators, read_view, dirty keys); the kernel's CR-3/CR-8/CR-9/CR-12 vs the Graph's claims; the controller GDD's interaction rules (lit-only, channelled, cancel on movement) vs the Graph's verb/mutator table; the render pipeline's truth-channel/Perception Filter rules vs the Graph's "consequence channel vs module-body channel" boundary (LS-14, LS-22); art bible trail vocabulary (frost, mist, scorch, drip) vs the Graph's medium→trail mapping (grep design/art/art-bible.md only for "frost", "mist", "scorch", "drip", "O₂ Cyan").
3. 4. Stale tokens: "8 s" / "80 steps" referring to the gate; "hold-to-step"; "hand point" as beam origin; "Blocks" plural for the Graph in the Graph GDD itself.

Report: (1) entries checked; (2) CONFLICTS each with registry value, file:line, stated value, suggested fix; (3) STALE REGISTRY; (4) stale-token hits with file:line; (5) UNVERIFIABLE notes (brief); (6) verdict PASS / CONFLICTS FOUND. Cite file:line for every finding; be concise.

    s = open(path, encoding='utf-8').read()
    for a, b in pairs:
        n = s.count(a); log.append(f"{'ok ' if n == 1 else 'SKIP(' + str(n) + ')'} {path[-28:]}: {a[:50]}")
        if n == 1: s = s.replace(a, b, 1)
    open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(s)
AM = " *(Amended 2026-10-26 — consistency check, routed from the Life-Support Graph GDD)*"
K = 'design/gdd/command-simulation-layer.md'
patch(K, [
 ("(Suit vitals `after: graph.propagate`). The order is data", "(Suit vitals `after: graph.propagate.atmo` — the Graph registers three chained hooks, see its LS-1" + AM + "). The order is data"),
 ("vitals hook `after: graph.propagate`; pushes noise/power stimuli to Attention", "vitals hook `after: graph.propagate.atmo`" + AM + "; pushes noise/power stimuli to Attention"),
 ("Blocks: topology, flow/failure/atmosphere state (`persist`, `SIM`, `SHARED_SUMMARY`); propagation hook at divisor 6; published mutators for the footprint channel and for Assembly's weld/cut |",
  "One block `graph.state`: topology, flow/failure/atmosphere state (`persist`, `SIM`, `SHARED_SUMMARY`); three chained propagation hooks at divisor 6 (`graph.propagate.power` → `.atmo` → `.failure`); published mutators for the footprint channel and for Assembly's weld/cut" + AM + " |"),
 ("Dirty-key volume on large graphs sets `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS`", "Dirty-key volume on large graphs confirms `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256 (Graph D.10: MVP worst ≈ 38, VS-A worst ≈ 135; never below 128)" + AM),
])
s = open(K, encoding='utf-8').read()
i = s.find("propagation hook at divisor 6", s.find("## Open Questions") if "## Open Questions" in s else 0)
# line 757 variants
for a, b in [("`design/gdd/life-support-graph.md` (not yet written)", "`design/gdd/life-support-graph.md` (designed 2026-10-26)"), ("propagation hook at divisor 6", "three chained propagation hooks at divisor 6")]:
    n = s.count(a); log.append(f"{'ok ' if n >= 1 else 'SKIP(0)'} kernel x{n}: {a[:40]}"); s = s.replace(a, b)
open(K, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(s)

G = 'design/gdd/life-support-graph.md'
patch(G, [
 ("and a one-line D.10 clarification (an owner-defined 63-bit key is a valid `counter`). Index row-1 wording \"Blocks\" → \"Block\" routed.",
  "and a one-line D.10 clarification (an owner-defined 63-bit key is a valid `counter`).  ("**Bidirectional consistency.** The kernel GDD's Interactions row 1 names this system with the same block/hub/mutator shape (wording fix routed).", "X"),  # may not exist; harmless
 ("**Bidirectional consistency.** The kernel GDD's Interactions row 1 names this system with the same block/hook/mutator shape (wording fix routed).",
  "**Bidirectional consistency.** The kernel GDD's Interactions row 1, CR-3 example and Suit row now name this system's one block and three chained hooks (fixed in place at the 2026-10-26 consistency check)."),
 ("- **GIVEN** the MVP weld (home-ship + derelict A),", "- **GIVEN** the MVP weld (home-ship + the section salvaged from derelict A; D.16's 35/45/5 cost row is the derelict-B worst case),"),
])
s = open(G, encoding='utf-8').read()
a = "**LS-26 — The MVP slice (R23) and what waits.**"
if s.count(a) == 1:
    s = s.replace(a, a + " *Mode count note (consistency check 2026-10-26): \"six MVP modes\" are six hazard groups — LEAK, SHORT/OVERLOAD, OVERHEAT/SCRAM, FREEZE, BREACH, STARVE — spanning ids 1–7 and 9; SEVERED (8) is also MVP-live by construction because salvage (V8, M6/M12) produces an `open_end`; WORN (10) and SEAL_STRAIN (26) are non-hazard and live wherever hp or a closed hatch exists.*", 1); log.append("ok LS-26 mode note")
else: log.append(f"SKIP LS-26 anchor x{s.count(a)}")
open(G, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(s)

Y = 'design/registry/entities.yaml'

fix("SEAM_LEAK_INITIAL_BP", "bp — leak imperfection of a fresh seam before wear-in / SEAL_SEAM, scaled by weld quality q", "bp — leak imperfection of a fresh seam, lowered by wear-in / SEAL_SEAM; weld quality q enters through the seam area (D.2), not this value", "'scaled by weld quality q'")

fix("power_allocation", "(brownout shed order: tier 4 lamps/heaters first)", "(brownout shed order: tier 4 'other' first, then tier 3 lamps and HEATER; sat_3 drives lamp brightness)", "'tier 4 lamps/heaters first'")
fix("dirty_key_budget", "keys_per_run <= C_changed + B_changed + N_transitions + F_buckets + L_quanta + S + T + SEC;", "keys_per_run <= C_changed + B_changed + N_transitions + F_buckets + L_quanta + S + T_f (T_f folds T and SEC/<id>);", "8-term sum with SEC separate")
# S4: drop kernel from referenced_by of GRAPH_STEP_TICKS, GRAPH_HOOK_BUDGET_MS, dirty_key_budget
for n in ["GRAPH_STEP_TICKS", "GRAPH_HOOK_BUDGET_MS", "dirty_key_budget"]:
    i, j = blk(n); b = s[i:j]
    b2 = b.replace("      - design/gdd/command-simulation-layer.md\n", "", 1)
    b2 = re.sub(r"    referenced_by:\n(?=    attributes:)", "    referenced_by: []\n", b2)
    if b2 != b: b2 = b2.rstrip("\n") + "\n    # forward reference: the kernel GDD will cite this once the routed hook/budget amendments land\n"; log.append(f"ok reg ref drop {n}")
    s = s[:i] + b2 + s[j:]
open(Y, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(s)
print("\n".join(log))

## Life-Support Graph GDD — complete (design order 3)

`design/gdd/life-support-graph.md` — 254 KB: 26 core rules, 16 formulas, 75 edge cases, 80 tuning knobs, 95 acceptance criteria, 17 open questions. CD-GDD-ALIGN: CONCERNS → REVISED (seven items, no redesign). Consistency check after it: 2 kernel-wording conflicts + 3 stale registry expressions, all fixed in place; registry 79 entries validates; index row 2 Designed (4/26 MVP).

**Design, in one breath.** One integer-only block, five loops (O₂, power, coolant, fuel, integrity) with per-compartment atmosphere; three chained hooks at 10 Hz; failures spread one hop per run through the physics, never by script; 18 mutators, one true-value read view; the Graph knows nothing about hallucinations.

**Decisions you should see (all logged; say so if you want any reversed):**
- **Death is gated by a physical warning.** Any loss the *ship* causes by itself must be preceded by ≥ 10 s of two-channel physical tell (`W_MIN_WARNING_S`, raised from 8 at the CD gate to sit inside Pillar 2's 10–30 s). Player-caused losses and horror attacks are exempt — but horrors must bring their own tell. "Death is a bitch" stays; arbitrary death doesn't.
- **Welding moves nothing.** A fresh seam's hatch, valves and breaker all start disconnected; connecting each is a lit verb with a readable warning (seal-strain creak/whistle at a closed hatch under pressure). The game-designer's "the weld is a hole" moment became "the seam weeps until sealed" — no vacuum-section soft-lock.
- **No safe harbour.** Running machines wear (~4 h duty to the first warning), so a fully repaired ship is quiet, never solved.
- **Fuel is a timer + puddle hazard; fire waits for VS-A.** Coolant minimal. No CO₂, no rate dial.

def rep(a, b):
    global s
    n = s.count(a); log.append(f"{'ok ' if n == 1 else 'SKIP(' + str(n) + ')'} {a[:60]}")
    if n == 1: s = s.replace(a, b, 1)

# 6 header + P5 misread
rep("> **Implements Pillar**: P1 The World Never Lies (the graph is the physical ground truth every instrument, trail and hallucination is measured against); P3 The Web Watches (power use and light are graph loads the web can read); P5 Deeper Is Richer, Loss Is Not Total (salvage and welding act on graph nodes)",
    "> **Implements Pillar**: P1 The World Never Lies (primary — the Graph is the physical ground truth every instrument, trail and hallucination is measured against); P2 Dread Before Chaos (the endogenous warning floor and the minutes-long tells of D.15); P4 Sanity Rewrites Reality (the falsification ground: every gauge quantity has a physical witness driven by the same true value). **Serves**: P3 The Web Watches (power use is a graph load the web can read); P5 Deeper Is Richer, Loss Is Not Total (the substrate salvage, welding and wear act on — the verbs belong to Assembly and Item DB, the failure contract to Pillar 5's own systems)\n> **Creative Director Review (CD-GDD-ALIGN)**: CONCERNS → REVISED 2026-10-26 (seven items applied: WORN descriptor mode with NONE medium; closed consequence-channel list; W_MIN_WARNING_S raised to 10 s with the exogenous-source tell requirement; duty wear W_DUTY so a fully repaired ship is never a safe harbour; closed-hatch pressure witness; header re-scoped; Game Feel re-voiced)")
rep("Pillar 5: salvage and welding act on its nodes; a lost compartment is not a lost ship.",
    "Pillar 5: salvage, welding and wear act on its nodes; loss is the failure contract's business, not the Graph's.")

# 2 consequence channel — Dependencies, Visual/Audio, Player Fantasy
rep("it may add or alter sprites and gauges but never suppress a true descriptor's acoustic or physical channel | nothing (PERCEPTION_OUT never feeds the Graph, CR-12)",
    "it may corrupt the **module-body channel** (sprites, gauges, inspect cards, descriptors in mode `WORN`) but may not remove, alter **or add** anything on the **consequence channel** — a closed list: trail VFX for leak/hazard descriptors; the LS-14 acoustic classes at a descriptor anchor; Suit body cues (breath, visor fog, vignette, shiver); lamp brightness from `served_pm`; draught. Phantom-entity audio is the Filter's own and never uses a witness acoustic class | nothing (PERCEPTION_OUT never feeds the Graph, CR-12)")
rep("so a trail is thickest at the source and never appears at a node without upstream evidence on the connecting edge. An orphan trail is therefore always a hallucination tell.",
    "so a trail is thickest at the source and never appears at a node without upstream evidence on the connecting edge. Trails are on the consequence channel: the Perception Filter can neither remove nor add one, so an orphan trail cannot occur.")
rep("- **Audio is true-state.** Hiss pitch/rate, hum, ticking and the loop whisper are read from true values; a hallucination may *add* audio but never remove a real hiss, and `alarm_eligible`",
    "- **Audio is true-state.** Hiss pitch/rate, hum, ticking and the loop whisper are read from true values and belong to the consequence channel: a hallucination may neither remove a real hiss nor add a hiss, creak or whistle in a witness acoustic class (phantom-entity audio is the Filter's own, in its own classes); `alarm_eligible`")
rep("What cannot change is the consequence channel: compartment temperature, O₂ and pressure, and the frost, mist, scorch, drip and hiss that Failure & Trail and Adaptive Audio render as pure readers of the Graph's true values.",
    "What cannot change is the **consequence channel** — a closed list: compartment temperature, O₂ and pressure as the body feels them; the frost, mist, scorch and drip trails; the hiss, creak and whistle at a descriptor's anchor; lamp brightness; draught. Failure & Trail, Suit and Adaptive Audio render these as pure readers of the Graph's true values, and the Filter may neither remove nor add to them. What *can* lie is the module-body channel: sprites, gauges, inspect cards and a module's own wear state.")

# 3a + 7 Game Feel re-voiced; W_MIN 10
rep("- **A body that decays on its own clock.** Left alone, the home-ship develops faults on minute-scale timers (first tell to lethal ≈ 6 min for an O₂ pinhole in a room, ≈ 9 for the ship; 4.5 for a power overload branch; 9 for coolant; 12 for hull fatigue); nothing resolves itself.",
    "- **A body that decays on its own clock.** Left alone, the home-ship wears: its authored faults run on minute-scale clocks (first tell to lethal ≈ 6 min for an O₂ pinhole in a room, ≈ 9 for the ship; 4.5 for a power overload branch; 9 for coolant; 12 for hull fatigue), and the machines that keep it alive wear a little every hour they run (`W_DUTY`), so a fully repaired ship is quiet, never safe. Nothing resolves itself.")
rep("- **Long tell, short chaos.** Phases A (tell) and B (spread) are long and readable; C (cascade, propagation ×2) is short; D (loss) is final. The fairness gate guarantees ≥ 8 s of ≥ 2-channel physical warning before any endogenous irreversible loss, so \"death is a bitch\" is always nameable, never arbitrary.",
    "- **Long tell, short collapse.** A long tell, a spreading wrongness, a short collapse, then silence. The real tells run in minutes (D.15); the sim's own floor beneath them is `W_MIN_WARNING_S` = 10 s of two-channel physical warning before any loss the ship causes by itself, so \"death is a bitch\" is always nameable, never arbitrary. Horrors and the web have their own tells (Attention, Horror Entities) that must precede anything they do to the ship.")
rep("then latent faults wake at half the home-ship's tell time, and a breach skips to cascade.",
    "then faults that wake run twice as fast — but still warn first; a breach is already past its tell by the time the hull gives.")
rep("- **Truncation reads as physical.** Rooms never perfectly equalise (flux rounds to zero on tiny gradients); a faint pressure difference across a nearly-closed hatch is expected, not a bug.",
    "- **Rooms never quite settle.** A faint draught at a nearly-shut hatch is real and stays; two rooms do not balance to the last breath. Expected, not a bug.")
rep("every endogenous loss is preceded by ≥ 8 s of two-channel physical warning", "every endogenous loss is preceded by ≥ 10 s of two-channel physical warning")
rep("| 2 | **Fairness gate scope — adopted as a hard sim rule (W_MIN_WARNING_S = 8 s, endogenous transitions only; horror kills and player-caused losses exempt).** Confirm the exemption list once Horror Entities and Interaction are designed. | user (confirm), game-designer | Horror Entities GDD |",
    "| 2 | **Fairness gate scope — adopted as a hard sim rule (W_MIN_WARNING_S = 10 s, raised from 8 at CD-GDD-ALIGN to sit inside Pillar 2's 10–30 s tell; endogenous transitions only; player-caused losses exempt).** Exported requirement: any non-player exogenous source (footprint RUPTURE/GOUGE/STRESS, environmental `apply_damage`) must be preceded by Attention's or Horror Entities' own 10–30 s Pillar 2 tell — the gate protects against the sim, not against agency, and Pillar 2 still applies to horrors. Confirm the exemption list once Horror Entities and Interaction are designed. | user (confirm), game-designer | Horror Entities GDD |")
open(G, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(s)
print("\n".join(log))
