## Overview

The Synaptic Sea needs 42 systems. Its mechanical heart is a simulated life-support graph (O2, power, coolant, fuel, integrity) carried by a composite ship that the player grows by welding salvaged sections onto it; around that sit the two rhythms of the core loop (the deliberate boarding rhythm and the frantic breach rhythm), joined by an Attention system the web uses to watch the players, and a Sanity system that rewrites what the players perceive rather than how they perform. The game pillars decide the shape of the list: The World Never Lies puts the graph, trails and lighting in the foundation; Dread Before Chaos and The Web Watches make Attention and the audio tells MVP systems; Sanity Rewrites Reality isolates the Perception Filter from the simulation so a hallucination can never corrupt state; Deeper Is Richer, Loss Is Not Total adds depth rings, depletion and the failure contract at the Vertical Slice.

The tiers follow the producer-adjusted scope in the concept. **MVP** is the single-player loop test (two handmade derelicts, one weld, one Attention threshold, one horror behaviour, one hallucination class, save v1, plus a kill/continue playtest). **Vertical Slice** is split in the concept into VS-A (single-player, procedural derelicts, the shippable fallback) and VS-B (2-player LAN co-op, built only after VS-A is complete); systems marked **(VS-B)** carry the Vertical Slice tier here but must not start before VS-A. **Alpha** adds the depth rings' full content, Steam lobbies, host-owned world carry-over and accessibility settings. The template's Priority Tiers are fixed, so 'Spike phase' (weld, graph, save, lighting budget) is not a tier: it is a prototype pass over four MVP systems (Modular Ship Assembly, Life-Support Graph, Save/Load, 2D Lighting) and is listed under High-Risk Systems.

**System-by-system rationale.** Fixed-column tables cannot carry prose, so each system's scope and the reason for its tier follow here in enumeration order.

- **1. Command & Simulation Layer** (Core, MVP, inferred). Thin kernel only: fixed tick, command dispatch with authority check, a registry of state blocks owned by domain systems, change notification to presentation, and peer/authority identity on every command from day one (single-player is peer 1). Owns no domain state and defines no other system's commands. ADR-first (authority model), with a short technical spec rather than a full player-facing GDD. *Why this tier:* TD-FEASIBILITY B2: authority discipline from day one is what keeps co-op an addition rather than a rewrite. No networking in MVP; this is only the command/state separation.
- **2. Life-Support Graph** (Core, MVP, explicit). Pure-data model of O2, power, coolant, fuel and integrity loops across welded sections: node and port types, edges (seams are edges whose properties Assembly sets at weld time), flows, failure state and propagation, and per-compartment atmosphere (temperature, pressure, O2 — the P1 consequences). Separate from the scene tree so it can be serialized, tested headless and synced by summary. Stays at five loops. *Why this tier:* The core of Pillar 1; MVP hypothesis cannot be tested without it. Everything that fails, glows, leaks or is salvaged reads or writes it.
- **3. Item & Module Database** (Economy, MVP, inferred). Definitions of salvageable modules (scrubber, reactor cell, hull plate, coolant unit, data core), tools, consumables and their dialect and weights; references graph port-type IDs that the Life-Support Graph GDD defines. *Why this tier:* Salvage and welding have nothing to act on without definitions; also feeds save format.
- **4. Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera** (Core, MVP, inferred). 640x360 SubViewport world at integer scale, HUD in the root viewport, nearest filtering, snapping, Y-sort layer shape, camera. Art bible 8.1/8.4. *Why this tier:* Every visual system sits on it; the lighting spike (8.12) starts here.
- **5. Emitter State & Light-Exposure Query** (Core, MVP, inferred). Simulation-side record of every light emitter (fixtures, beams on/off and cone shape, machinery-node lanterns, deployables, power draw), written through commands, plus a geometric light-exposure query (cone test and occluder raycasts on physics shapes) that Attention, Horror Entities and Interaction use. Runs headless; never reads Light2D. *Why this tier:* TD-SYSTEM-BOUNDARY: keeps light a simulation input no hallucination can touch, and lets Attention run headless and on the host for remote players.
- **6. 2D Lighting & Occlusion** (Core, MVP, explicit). Rendering only: reads emitter state and draws Light2D, occluders, ambient floors, the material-level hull floor, the six shadow-casting slots, emission glow and light textures. Owns the final Light2D values through a modifier contract: Attention flicker, horror light disturbance and Perception Filter decoys submit layered modifiers; the Filter may add decoy visuals but never changes the real reveal radius (a pillar anchor). *Why this tier:* Identity-defining and the art bible's first spike: if lighting does not fit the frame budget the whole direction needs a trade-off.
- **7. Player Controller & Input** (Core, MVP, inferred). Movement, 5-facing sprite with mirrored facings, per-facing chest point for the beam (user decision 2026-10-26: chest-mounted lamp), gamepad/keyboard input mapping, stiff-weighted animation states. *Why this tier:* Nothing is playable without a body to light.
- **8. Interaction System** (Gameplay, MVP, inferred). Inspect, cut, weld, open, carry, run a field check; the act-only-on-lit rule uses the light-exposure query (prompts drawn only for lit objects is the UI side, 7.0); hold-to-confirm on destructive actions; proximity focus for gamepad. Falsification checks reach Sanity as commands from here. Also owns the friendly-harm act: tool use against a crewmate is an Interaction command accepted only when Sanity's gate reports the actor below threshold (no dedicated damage or combat system — Anti-Pillar), with no reward path. *Why this tier:* The verb layer for boarding; encodes the 'spend light to act' rule.
- **9. Failure & Trail System** (Gameplay, MVP, explicit). Pure reader: maps graph failure state and footprint sources to physical trail visuals (frost, mist, scorch, drip, hairlines) in the three sizes, writing only CanvasItem/Material/particles. Owns no propagation and no atmosphere — both are Graph state. Tagged as a truth channel: immune to the Perception Filter. *Why this tier:* Pillar 1 made visible; the honest channel every hallucination is checked against.
- **10. Suit & Equipment** (Gameplay, MVP, inferred). Suit vitals (O2, integrity, local temperature and pressure read from the Graph's compartment atmosphere) as a PER_PLAYER block keyed by PlayerId, loadout and tool slots, the chest-mounted lamp (hands-free; the four beam shapes) and deployables — including throwable glowsticks (user decision 2026-10-26) — as emitters, carried modules. Each tool's effect is defined by the system it acts on (cutter/welder: Interaction and Assembly; scanner: Sanity falsification; suppressant: Attention/Horror). *Why this tier:* Personal survival state and the beam are the player's two instruments; the suit layer HUD reads from here.
- **11. Ship Section & Layout Data Model** (Core, MVP, inferred). The runtime section schema shared by authoring, procgen, assembly and save: tile layer reference, collision shapes, sockets, seams, graph-node references, salvage/module slots, and the pure-data ship layout (sections, transforms, welds) that is projected onto the scene tree. *Why this tier:* TD-SYSTEM-BOUNDARY: without a single owner three GDDs would each define a socket; needed before the weld spike.
- **12. Ship Body & Interior Physics** (Core, MVP, inferred). The composite ship as one physics body with a ship-local reference frame; characters and props moving inside a moving body (the moving-platform problem); detach spawns a new body. *Why this tier:* TD-SYSTEM-BOUNDARY: the spike is weld-on-a-moving-ship and nothing owned the motion; needed before the weld spike.
- **13. Modular Ship Assembly** (Gameplay, MVP, explicit). Weld and cut sections as atomic one-tick commands across graph join and layout change: join validation is a pure Graph query; seams set edge properties; cap plates; detach into a new body. Also owns module install/uninstall (cut a scrubber free, install it at home) as a graph mutation distinct from section welding. *Why this tier:* The game's hook and its riskiest build task (producer: the weld is the hardest MVP item); first spike.
- **14. Derelict Authoring (Handmade Kits)** (Gameplay, MVP, explicit). Hand-built Foundry-dialect derelict and spawn ship from the room kit (6.3): tagged sockets, graph nodes, salvage slots, one visible unknown per wreck. *Why this tier:* MVP uses two handmade derelicts; the kit definition is also what procgen later assembles.
- **15. Boarding & Salvage** (Gameplay, MVP, explicit). The boarding rhythm: enter, listen, light, decide, cut a module free, carry it home under rising Attention; field checks for suspect salvage. *Why this tier:* The 5-minute loop. Without it there is no sortie.
- **16. Web Map & Transit** (Gameplay, MVP, explicit). The web world model (derelict list, seeds plus deltas, what is loaded) and the abstracted pod hop between home-ship and target (state 2.5), docking, fuel cost. Full flight is out of scope. Depth Rings extends it at VS; the Chart Table only displays it. *Why this tier:* Connects the two ends of the MVP sortie at minimum cost.
- **17. Attention System** (Gameplay, MVP, explicit). The web's attention. Owns a stimulus-input API (light via the exposure query; noise and power stimuli pushed in by Graph, Suit, Interaction, Assembly and Horrors — never read from Audio), baseline set by depth, and the BREACH STATE MACHINE (calm → tell window → breach → subsiding). Owns the tell-window contract — every breach is preceded by a 10–30 s escalating tell the player could perceive — which Horror Entities, Graph failure injection, Lighting modifiers and Audio must all honour; the contract is a testable acceptance criterion written before Horror and Audio are designed. Its presentation (filaments in the light cone, creaks, flicker as a Lighting modifier) reads attention level plus emitter state. Pillars 2 and 3. *Why this tier:* The hinge between the two rhythms; core hypothesis cannot be tested without it.
- **18. Horror Entities** (Gameplay, MVP, explicit). Segment-rig horrors with creep/unfold/snap behaviours, real occlusion and shadow; writes hidden-entity footprints (branching rime, radial hairlines, light disturbance) into the Graph footprint channel and submits light-disturbance modifiers to Lighting. MVP: one behaviour. *Why this tier:* Gives Attention consequences; MVP minimum is one behaviour.
- **19. Sanity & Hallucination Rules** (Gameplay, MVP, explicit). Per-player sanity, its drift order, the four hallucination classes and their guard rails (inviolable channels, no unfalsifiable lie, system-gated friendly harm, verification cost). Authoritative; writes per-player perception state keyed by a stable PlayerId (seat), never by transport peer ID, from MVP; receives falsification checks as commands from Interaction/Suit. No simulation system ever reads perception state — the friendly-harm gate reads the sanity level, not perception. *Why this tier:* Pillar 4 and the hook. MVP: class (b) false system state only.
- **20. Perception Filter** (Gameplay, MVP, explicit). Per-client perceived-value query/decorator service (displayed value of X for local peer P) plus screen-wide effects: stage-1/2/3 drift, the violet fringe, palette leak, Light2D decoy modifiers. Owns no instrument or HUD nodes — Instruments and HUD ask it and draw the result. Defines the truth-channel/corruptible tag contract on presentation nodes (trails, true reveal radius, crewmate beams, character sprites, HUD frame immune; gauges and machine sprites corruptible). Owns the class-(c) victim tell as a truth-channel element: the below-threshold crewmate's violet fringe with mandatory breathing and the P1 proximity cue (art bible 5.5), rendered for every saner viewer and attributed to the web in logs and scars. Reads simulation state, writes only CanvasItem/Material/Light2D. *Why this tier:* Isolating it keeps hallucinations from touching the simulation (TD rule) and gives the debug overlay something to contrast.
- **21. HUD & Suit Layer** (UI, MVP, explicit). Centre-bottom critical strip, bottom-left suit panel, hand rail, warning mark, tri-modal lying-reading signatures, HR-1..15. *Why this tier:* How the player reads their own body; Section 7 of the art bible specifies it.
- **22. In-World Instruments & Inspect View** (UI, MVP, explicit). Owns the gauge, sight-glass and dial nodes as lit sprites and the inspect view (the same instrument magnified); asks the Perception Filter for the displayed value and draws it with the settle/tremor/glide motion signatures. *Why this tier:* Where class (b) lies live; pairs with the Failure & Trail System as the truth check.
- **23. Chart Table (Web Map & Menus)** (UI, MVP, explicit). The never-lying human instrument: web map, route planning, pause panel, menus. MVP: pick a target, pause, save. *Why this tier:* Needed to start a sortie; the web map grows in later tiers.
- **24. Adaptive Audio & Tells** (Audio, MVP, explicit). Distinct running and failing sound per loop read directly from Graph state (so audio tells can lead visuals), horror and Attention cues, the P1 proximity cue. Must state whether audio can lie: if it can, audio corruption joins the Perception Filter's write set under the same rule; the voice channel is never faked either way. Audio is the only non-visual Attention channel. *Why this tier:* Pillar 2 and the accessibility consequence of 'no Attention indicator': sound carries the weight.
- **25. Save/Load & Versioned Format** (Persistence, MVP, explicit). A versioned state-block registration contract: each domain system registers its serializable state block through the Command kernel's registry, and Save/Load serializes and migrates the set (format version from v1; host-owned). Domain systems depend on this contract, not the reverse. Also owns the MVP death stub: on crew death the game reloads the last save (placeholder, replaced by Failure Contract & Re-wake at VS-A) so no MVP GDD improvises its own. *Why this tier:* A no-win-state game that breaks saves on every module change cannot be played long; versioning is cheapest on day one.
- **26. Debug Overlay (True Values)** (Meta, MVP, inferred). Developer-only overlay showing authoritative values beside the hallucinated ones, to tell deliberate corruption from real desync. Never exposed as an accessibility feature (R-7). *Why this tier:* TD-FEASIBILITY: needed from the start; also the QA instrument for the sanity system.
- **27. Procedural Derelict Generation** (Gameplay, Vertical Slice, explicit). Seeded generator assembling hand-authored kit chunks by grammar: continuity, one trail per source, hero cap, clear path (6.3 rules), salvage placement, one visible unknown. Host sends seed plus deltas. *Why this tier:* VS-A: the point where it becomes a repeatable game rather than a prototype; deliberately after the loop is proven.
- **28. Depth Rings & Scarcity** (Progression, Vertical Slice, explicit). Rings of the web: Attention baseline, ambient and iridescence per ring, salvage value, horror roster. Pillar 5. VS: one ring beyond the spawn ring. Ring access in VS-A is gated by ship capability (pod range, life-support margin) read from the Graph and Assembly, so the shipped fallback has an implicit capability ladder; Ship Capability Progression formalises it at Alpha. *Why this tier:* Gives 'deeper is richer' a mechanism.
- **29. Resource Depletion & Wear** (Economy, Vertical Slice, explicit). Scrubbers and plates degrade; outer-ring salvage runs out, so there is no safe place to farm forever. *Why this tier:* The enforcement mechanism for Pillar 5 the creative-director asked for.
- **30. Knowledge Codex & Logs** (Progression, Vertical Slice, explicit). Decoded web rules, horror tells and recovered logs that persist across crew loss; some rules shift with depth so the web never becomes solvable. Knowledge must change play, not just be stored: a decoded tell becomes recognisable earlier, a learned rule is annotated on the Chart Table, and a recovered log names a deeper wreck on the Web Map (the session hook). Acceptance criterion: every codex entry has a stated effect on play. *Why this tier:* The currency of the failure contract and the Discovery aesthetic.
- **31. Failure Contract & Re-wake** (Progression, Vertical Slice, explicit). Losing the ship or a body costs ship and body, never knowledge; the next crew wakes in the cryo bay knowing more (state 2.10). Owns the cryo-bay fiction as a throughline: re-wake presents the mystery (pod count, pod states, what changes each wake, who else is in the pods and why they keep waking), co-authored with narrative-director, with lore fragments fed through the Knowledge Codex. Includes lethal friendly harm's consequences. The GDD's Player Fantasy section opens with the cryo bay, not a respawn rule. *Why this tier:* Pillar 5's contract; prevents the death spiral.
- **32. Environmental Storytelling Placement** (Narrative, Vertical Slice, explicit). The cause/verb/absence three-sentence verdict per wreck, placed by tagged slots; no bodies, only empty suits. *Why this tier:* Delivers lore without text or cutscenes; makes procgen derelicts read as places.
- **33. Co-op Session & Replication (VS-B)** (Core, Vertical Slice, explicit). Listen-server host-authoritative 2-player LAN: spawner/synchronizers, request validation, summary-state sync of the graph. Built only after VS-A is complete. *Why this tier:* VS-B; gated behind the single-player slice per TD-FEASIBILITY.
- **34. Chat, Voice & Pings (VS-B)** (Core, Vertical Slice, explicit). Voice/proximity, text chat and world pings: the human channel, never hallucinated, with a speaker indicator. *Why this tier:* The costly-check channel Pillar 4 relies on; deaf/HoH and no-mic crews need text and pings.
- **35. Crew Strip HUD (VS-B)** (UI, Vertical Slice, explicit). Identity glyph (beam shape plus stripe count), name, voice activity, location, beam state; no sanity, no vitals, no locators. *Why this tier:* Co-op readability without breaking the human-channel rule.
- **36. Onboarding (Cryo Bay)** (Meta, Vertical Slice, explicit). The first ten minutes: one sealed bay, one failing loop, follow the trail, fix it, watch the gauge agree. Teaches the boarding rhythm and the first Attention threshold. *Why this tier:* A slow-start game dies without it; MVP playtesters get a hand-led version.
- **37. Sanity Scars & Character History** (Progression, Alpha, explicit). Permanent suit-repair-style scars in three slots; how earned, how many, whether guests keep them (open question). *Why this tier:* Gives sanity lasting weight; depends on the failure contract and the guest-carry-over decision.
- **38. Ship Capability Progression** (Progression, Alpha, explicit). Life-support margin, range, hull as the ladder players climb as they graft. *Why this tier:* The Achiever ladder; not needed to test the loop.
- **39. Steam Lobby & NAT** (Core, Alpha, explicit). Steam lobbies and NAT traversal so friends connect over the internet. Needs a technology evaluation first. *Why this tier:* A separate milestone from LAN co-op (TD).
- **40. Host-Owned World & Guest Carry-over** (Persistence, Alpha, explicit). Whose save owns the shared ship; what guests keep; copying a save to let a guest host. Open design question for game-designer and creative-director. *Why this tier:* B1 decision made structural: no live host migration.
- **41. Accessibility Settings** (Meta, Alpha, explicit). UI scale, reading-face scale, HUD opacity floor, reduced motion preserving the backbone, bounded low-vision ambient floor, pattern strength, captions policy (R-6). *Why this tier:* Design starts early because several settings change what other systems must expose.
- **42. Settings & Input Rebinding** (Meta, Alpha, inferred). Graphics, audio, controls, key and button rebinding, gamepad completeness enumeration (HR-14). *Why this tier:* Expected on PC; not needed to test the loop.

**Relationship analysis.** The heaviest dependency roots are listed in the data line below; they are the project's bottlenecks. Command & Simulation Layer sits under almost everything because TD-FEASIBILITY made 'every mutation is an authority-checked request' the rule that keeps co-op additive. The Life-Support Graph is the data every visible system reads. The Item & Module Database is a quiet bottleneck: salvage, welding, save format, depletion and depth rings all need its definitions, so it should be designed early despite looking like content. Lighting is both a Foundation-adjacent technical risk and the carrier of three pillars. The Perception Filter is deliberately a query service with many readers and no simulation writers: it is the isolation that makes Sanity safe. The Emitter State & Light-Exposure Query exists for the mirror-image reason: light must stay a simulation input the Filter cannot touch. UI and Audio systems depend on gameplay systems, never the reverse, so they can be designed after the rules they display.

**Relationship analysis (data).** The four heaviest dependency roots are Command & Simulation Layer (16 dependents), Life-Support Graph (14 dependents), Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera (11 dependents), Item & Module Database (9 dependents).

> **Technical Director Review (TD-SYSTEM-BOUNDARY)**: CONCERNS, revisions applied 2026-10-25 — emitter state split from light rendering; Ship Section & Layout Data Model and Ship Body & Interior Physics added; Save/Load inverted into a state-block contract; Failure & Trail made a pure reader; Item DB sequenced after the Graph; Web Map & Transit owns the world model. GDD-level notes are carried in each system's rationale above.

Instead of rigid waves, I'm sketching a dependency-driven scheduler where each system starts as soon as all its prerequisite GDDs are complete, treating it like a pipeline of per-system promises rather than fixed barrier stages. Writing the scheduler logic...

For the per-system pipeline, I'm weighing whether to separate a "brief" stage (gathering context, dependency contracts, art bible sections, routing specialists) from the actual authoring stage, since a single agent authoring an entire ~250KB GDD in one context may be too much to handle reliably.

Given that token cost isn't really a constraint here, I'm leaning toward: a Sonnet-high brief agent per system that writes out locked facts, provisional contracts for undesigned dependencies, pillar mapping, category routing, and open decisions with recommendations into a scratchpad file, which then feeds the authoring stage.

Next I'm adding an advisor-rulings step where a design-advisor model reviews the brief's decisions, issues explicit rulings, flags any drift, and cross-checks undesigned-dependency assumptions against whatever GDD content has already been written in parallel. Then the actual author agent (Sonnet high) builds the GDD skeleton from the template and fills in sections A through H plus optional ones in order, writing each section to file immediately as it follows the required formats.

Simplest path: make the author agent general-purpose since it needs Bash for log_decision, and have it attempt to spawn specialists via the Agent tool when available, falling back to drafting with its own expertise and flagging if a specialist wasn't consulted. Since workflow agents with agentType general-purpose seem to have access to all tools, I'll build in the specialist consultation step that way.

Actually, I think it's cleaner to make specialist consultation its own deterministic workflow stage with a fan-out: parallel specialist agents draft different section groups into scratchpad files — one handling detailed design, dependencies, and cross-references; another handling formulas, edge cases, and tuning knobs; a qa-lead handling acceptance criteria (which must run after the design/formula stages since it depends on them); and separate agents for player fantasy and visual/audio sections.

But doing the math, that's roughly six agents per system before review, which multiplied across everything balloons to around 250 agents total — technically fine under ultracode but risky in terms of complexity and failure surface. A simpler middle ground might be to have one general-purpose author agent walk through the whole document section by section, writing incrementally, and optionally invoking the Agent tool to consult specialists for specific sections if available, falling back to proceeding solo with a note if not — then letting advisor review and adversarial verification catch gaps afterward.

Earlier GDDs ballooned to 250 KB because multiple specialists contributed, but a single Sonnet author would likely produce something more like 60-120 KB, which is probably more readable anyway — I should aim for thorough density without mandating a specific size. Sonnet's context window easily handles authoring that much output while also reading dependency GDDs section by section, so that's not a real constraint. Then the advisor-review step, run by Fable in session mode, would check the written GDD for drift from the brief and rulings, pillar alignment, and contract consistency with dependency GDDs.

The advisor would also verify format compliance (formula lead-ins, GWT, If-then structures), flag leftover placeholders and registry conflicts, and return a PASS/REVISE verdict with specific actionable corrections — looping back to author-revise for up to two rounds. Next comes cd-gate, which runs the creative-director agentType against cd-gdd-align.md: a CONCERNS verdict triggers an auto-revise pass that applies the flagged items before recording REVISED, while a REJECT triggers a full revision and a single gate re-run. After that, registry-candidates handles the author-side extraction step.

Now I'm working through the merge contention problem: 22 systems writing to entities.yaml in parallel would cause conflicts, so each system should write its candidate entries to its own scratchpad fragment file, with a final serialized stage merging them one at a time and validating after each merge. For cross-system dependencies, where a later system needs a constant from an earlier one not yet merged, I'm considering having brief stages read all the scratchpad fragments directly, or better, merging each fragment into the registry immediately after its GDD completes using a simple JS promise-chain mutex to serialize the writes safely in the single-threaded workflow script.

After the registry merges, I still need a stage to regenerate the index, update systems.py status, refresh session state and design notes, and run registry validation. Finally, I'm planning a consistency-check phase that fans out parallel scanners—one per new GDD—to compare each against the registry and cross-reference the other GDDs.

I want fixes to go through a serial fixer with print-count discipline, since a past lesson warns that consistency checks need a confirming re-scan. Scaling it out, each system needs roughly 7-10 agents across brief, rulings, authoring, advisor review, revisions, CD gate, and registry merge stages, which across 22 systems lands around 200 agents plus ~30 for final consistency — comfortably under the 1000 cap. ## MVP Definition

**Core hypothesis**: The boarding→breach two-rhythm loop, over a visible
life-support graph, is tense and absorbing for a 30+ minute solo session.

**Required for MVP** (single-player):
1. One handmade spawn derelict and one handmade target derelict, with an
   abstracted pod hop between them.
2. Visible O₂ / heat / power graph with propagating, physically rendered
   failures.
3. One weld: attach one section and join its nodes to the graph.
4. Attention with one threshold and one horror behaviour.
5. Sanity as a single hallucination class (false system state), falsifiable by
   the physical world.
6. Save/load v1 with a format version.
7. All state changes through a single command/simulation layer (no networking
   code, no replication).

**Explicitly NOT in MVP**: procedural generation, co-op, multiple horrors,
other hallucination classes, lore, Steam, art at final fidelity, adaptive
audio.

**Kill/continue gate at the end of MVP**: playtest with at least three people
outside the project. If a 30+ minute solo session is not tense and absorbing,
iterate on the loop before any VS-A work. No procgen on an unproven loop.

### Scope Tiers (if budget/time shrinks)

const NAME2SLUG = {}
for (const s of SYSTEMS) NAME2SLUG[s.name] = s.slug
const pathOf = (name) => DESIGNED[name] || ('design/gdd/' + NAME2SLUG[name] + '.md')

// dependency depth (in-workflow deps only) for a safe topological start order
const depth = {}
function depthOf(s) {
  if (depth[s.slug] != null) return depth[s.slug]
  let d = 0
  for (const n of s.deps) if (NAME2SLUG[n]) d = Math.max(d, 1 + depthOf(SYSTEMS.find(x => x.name === n)))
  depth[s.slug] = d
  return d
}
SYSTEMS.forEach(depthOf)
SYSTEMS.sort((a, b) => (depth[a.slug] - depth[b.slug]) || (a.order - b.order))

function sysBlock(s, depStatus) {
  const deps = s.deps.map(n => `  - ${n} -> ${pathOf(n)} [${depStatus[n]}]`).join('\n')
  const dependents = SYSTEMS.filter(x => x.deps.includes(s.name)).map(x => x.name)
  return `SYSTEM: ${s.name} (index row ${s.order}; Category ${s.cat}; Layer ${s.layer}; Priority MVP). GDD path: design/gdd/${s.slug}.md. Stage dir: ${SCR}/${s.slug} (call it <SCR>).
Specialist routing (design-system Section 6, from the index Recommended Design Order): primary ${s.primary}; supporting ${s.support.join(', ')}.
Required extras by category: Visual/Audio ${['Gameplay', 'UI', 'Audio', 'Narrative'].includes(s.cat) ? 'REQUIRED (art-director consulted)' : 'optional (write a real note, not a placeholder)'}; Game Feel ${['Gameplay', 'UI'].includes(s.cat) ? 'REQUIRED' : 'optional (write a real note)'}; Cross-References REQUIRED; UI Requirements and Open Questions always written.
Upstream dependencies (status at the moment this stage started):
${deps}
Downstream dependents among the systems being designed in this run: ${dependents.length ? dependents.join('; ') : 'none in this run'}.
ROUTED THREADS this GDD must carry (decisions already made elsewhere; honour verbatim): ${s.threads}`
}

const REVISE_S = { type: 'object', properties: { applied: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } }, skipped: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } } }, required: ['applied', 'skipped'] }
const GATE_S = { type: 'object', properties: { verdict: { type: 'string', enum: ['APPROVE', 'CONCERNS', 'REJECT', 'NOT ASSESSED'] }, items: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } }, rationale: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['verdict', 'items', 'rationale'] }
const REG_S = { type: 'object', properties: { added: { type: 'number' }, refs_updated: { type: 'number' }, parked: { type: 'number' }, validate_clean: { type: 'boolean' }, header_recorded: { type: 'boolean' }, names_missing_in_gdd: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } } }, required: ['added', 'refs_updated', 'parked', 'validate_clean', 'header_recorded', 'names_missing_in_gdd'] }

// ---- helpers ----
const SON = { model: 'sonnet', effort: 'high' }
async function tryAgent(prompt, opts, tries) {
  for (let i = 0; i < (tries || 2); i++) {
    const r = await agent(i === 0 ? prompt : prompt + '\n\n(RETRY ' + i + ': a previous attempt died; resume from whatever already exists on disk — do not redo finished work.)', opts)
    if (r) return r
  }
  return null
}
let regChain = Promise.resolve()
function serial(fn) { const p = regChain.then(fn, fn); regChain = p.catch(() => {}); return p }

const doneP = {}, resolveDone = {}
for (const s of SYSTEMS) doneP[s.slug] = new Promise(res => { resolveDone[s.slug] = res })
const results = {}

async function runSystem(s) {
  const L = (stage) => ({ label: `${stage}:${s.slug}` })
  const out = { slug: s.slug, name: s.name, status: 'failed', stages: {} }
  try {
    // 0. wait for in-run dependencies
    const depStatus = {}
    for (const n of s.deps) {
      if (DESIGNED[n]) { depStatus[n] = 'designed' ; continue }
      const r = await doneP[NAME2SLUG[n]]
      depStatus[n] = r && r.status === 'done' ? 'designed in this run' : 'FAILED in this run — treat as undesigned; state a provisional contract'
    }
    log(`▶ ${s.name}: dependencies settled, starting brief`)
    const SB = sysBlock(s, depStatus)

    // 1. Brief
    const brief = await tryAgent(`${COMMON}\n\n${SB}\n\nSTAGE 1 — CONTEXT BRIEF (design-system Phase 2, all of 2a-2e). Produce <SCR>/brief.md, the single context document every later stage of this system reads. Do the reads: the index row + rationale bullet + dependency-map entries for this system; the concept pillars, core loop and MVP definition; the registry entries this GDD will own or read (grep every constant/formula whose referenced_by names design/gdd/${s.slug}.md, and every "# pending referenced_by" comment naming it); for EVERY upstream GDD that exists, its Interactions-with-Other-Systems row and its Dependencies / Formulas / Edge Cases / Tuning Knobs / Cross-References sections where they mention this system by name (grep the system name and its obvious short forms, e.g. "Suit", "Attention", "Filter"), quoting the exact contract text with file:line; the Graph GDD's Interactions row and Cross-References for this system even if it is not a direct dependency (it names most MVP systems); the art bible sections that govern this system; the reflexion log entries whose Domain touches this category; the engine reference for this system's domain (VERSION.md + breaking-changes.md; name the modules file or say none exists). Write brief.md with these headings: Mandate (index wording verbatim + why this tier), Pillar mapping (primary / serves, with the design tests), Locked facts (table: fact, value, owner file:line — registry + dependency GDDs), Contracts expected of this system by its dependents (quoted, file:line), Provisional contracts for undesigned or in-flight dependencies, Routed threads (restate each thread and where it lands in the GDD), Past failure patterns (reflexion), Engine feasibility brief (capabilities / constraints / knowledge gaps marked HIGH/MEDIUM / ADRs: none exist yet), Open design decisions (each: point, 2-4 options with pros/cons, recommended option, reason — these are the decisions the Section Cycle would have asked the user), Risks, Scope guard (what this GDD must NOT absorb from neighbours). Be concrete: names, numbers, ids. Return the schema fields; file is the brief path.`, { ...SON, phase: 'Brief', schema: BRIEF_S, ...L('brief') })
    if (!brief) throw new Error('brief failed')
    out.stages.brief = { decisions: brief.decisions.length, undesigned: brief.undesigned_deps }

    // 2. Rulings (advisor, session model)
    const rulings = await agent(`${COMMON}\n\n${SB}\n\nSTAGE 2 — ADVISOR RULINGS. You are the design advisor (the stronger model) standing in for the orchestrator who, in the single-session /design-system run, made numbered rulings that bound every specialist (precedent: the Graph GDD's 24 rulings). Read <SCR>/brief.md fully. For each open decision in it, rule: pick the option, say why in one or two sentences, name the pillar or locked fact that decides it. Verify the brief's locked facts against the files it cites (spot-check at least 8 with Grep: wrong line, wrong value or paraphrase = fix it in the ruling). Check each provisional contract against any sibling GDD that now exists on disk (Glob design/gdd/*.md) and against the registry — if a sibling already decided it, the ruling cites the sibling verbatim. Add guard rails: the three to six ways this specific GDD is most likely to drift (absorbing a neighbour's ownership, restating a locked constant with a new value, inventing a meter/overlay the anti-pillars forbid, adding combat/progression, letting a hallucination touch the consequence channel, describing implementation instead of behaviour, thin sections). State the GDD rule-id prefix to use (2-3 letters, e.g. SL-, IDB-, EM-) and the section-size bar: docs.density thorough, the kernel and Graph GDDs are the bar (numbered rules with names, tables for states and interfaces, every formula with the lead-in + variable table + output range + worked example, 25+ edge cases as If/then, 30+ tuning knobs, 40+ GWT acceptance criteria with (auto)/(lint)/(review)/(manual)/(spike) tags). Write <SCR>/rulings.md: numbered R1..Rn, then Guard rails, then Bar. Return the schema.`, { phase: 'Rulings', schema: RULINGS_S, ...L('rulings') })
    out.stages.rulings = rulings ? rulings.rulings_count : 'advisor unavailable'

    // 3. Specialists (parallel): primary + supporting on C/D/E/G proposals; creative-director on Player Fantasy
    const specPrompt = (role, ask) => `${COMMON}\n\n${SB}\n\nSTAGE 3 — SPECIALIST PROPOSAL as ${role}. Read <SCR>/brief.md and <SCR>/rulings.md first; they bind you. ${ask} Write your proposal to <SCR>/spec-${role}.md with clear headings; mark any claim that conflicts with a locked fact or a ruling as CONFLICT and say which. Be concrete (named rules, numbers, tables, worked examples); no hand-waving; no implementation patterns (those are ADR material — note them as "-> ADR candidate"). Return the schema (file, two-sentence summary, flags = conflicts/risks).`
    const specs = await parallel([
      () => agent(specPrompt(s.primary, `You are the PRIMARY specialist for this system. Propose the Detailed Design: Core Rules (numbered, each with a short name), States and Transitions (table), Interactions with Other Systems (table per dependency and dependent: data in, data out, owner of the interface, hook/mutator/read_view names where the kernel or Graph already fixes them), and the Dependencies table (hard/soft, interface, designed/provisional). Then propose the Formulas this system needs (name, expression, variables with type/range/source, output range, worked example) and the tuning knobs they imply.`), { ...SON, phase: 'Specialists', schema: SPEC_S, agentType: s.primary, ...L('spec-' + s.primary) }),
      ...s.support.map(role => () => agent(specPrompt(role, role === 'art-director'
        ? `You are the art-director. Propose the Visual/Audio Requirements for this system: the VFX, sprite-state and visual feedback requirements for each event this system produces or reads, animation/motion constraints, which art bible principles and sections apply (cite numbers), palette/semantic colour rules it must obey (sanity palette, loop hues, luminance ladder), and the truth-channel / corruptible classification of every visual it emits. Also list the asset types it implies for a later /asset-spec.`
        : role === 'creative-director'
        ? `You are the creative-director. Shape the Player Fantasy: the emotion or power fantasy, the anchor player moment, tone and language that fits the established feeling (quote the pillar text it serves), 2-3 candidate framings with a recommendation, the design test sentence, how the fantasy deepens rather than breaks under hallucination, reference techniques to adopt/reject precisely, and the anti-pillar guard rails this GDD must state.`
        : role === 'qa-lead'
        ? `You are the qa-lead. From the brief's mandate and contracts, propose the acceptance-criteria skeleton: the minimum test set that proves this system, grouped by core rule family, each GIVEN/WHEN/THEN, tagged (auto)/(lint)/(review)/(manual)/(spike), plus the performance budget criteria and the cross-system criteria (dependency contracts verified end to end).`
        : `You are a SUPPORTING specialist (${role}). Review the mandate from your discipline: propose the rules, formulas (with variable tables), edge cases (If [condition]: [exact outcome]), tuning knobs (value, safe range, too-high / too-low behaviour, interactions) and feasibility constraints that the primary specialist is likely to miss; cite engine facts as verified-from-docs or [UNV].`), { ...SON, phase: 'Specialists', schema: SPEC_S, agentType: role, ...L('spec-' + role) })),
      ...(s.support.includes('creative-director') ? [] : [() => agent(specPrompt('creative-director', `You are the creative-director. Shape the Player Fantasy: the emotion or power fantasy, the anchor player moment, tone and language that fits the established feeling (quote the pillar text it serves), 2-3 candidate framings with a recommendation (Category ${s.cat}: ${['Core', 'Persistence', 'Meta'].includes(s.cat) ? 'indirect framing recommended — players feel what it enables' : ['Economy', 'Progression'].includes(s.cat) ? 'both direct and indirect' : 'direct framing recommended'}), the design test sentence, how the fantasy deepens rather than breaks under hallucination, reference techniques to adopt/reject precisely, and the anti-pillar guard rails this GDD must state.`), { phase: 'Specialists', schema: SPEC_S, agentType: 'creative-director', ...L('spec-creative-director') })]),
    ])
    out.stages.specialists = specs.filter(Boolean).map(x => x.file)
    const specFiles = specs.filter(Boolean).map(x => x.file).join(', ') || '(no specialist files — draft from the brief and rulings and note "specialist not consulted — agent unavailable" in each affected section)'

    // 4. Author part 1
    const AUTH_RULES = `AUTHORING RULES (design-system Phase 3-4, full tier, autonomous): create the file from .claude/docs/templates/game-design-document.md if absent (keep its heading set and order exactly; header: Status "In Design", Author "user + ${[s.primary, ...s.support].join(', ')}, creative-director (via /design-system, autonomous; orchestrated run ${DATE})", Last Updated/Verified ${DATE}, Implements Pillar from the brief's pillar mapping as "Pn Name (primary — why); ... **Serves**: ..."). Author each section in order and WRITE IT IMMEDIATELY with Edit, old_string = the heading line + blank line + "[To be designed]" (never the placeholder alone). Read .claude/docs/templates/guidance/game-design-document-guide.md once for section intent. Keep the GDD at behaviour level; implementation choices become "-> ADR candidate" notes. Every locked constant/formula name is used VERBATIM with its registry value. Prefix every rule with the id prefix the rulings set. Provisional assumptions about undesigned or in-flight dependencies are marked "(provisional — <dep> undesigned/in flight)". Log one decision per section approval and one per framing/approach choice (LOGGING). Density: thorough — the kernel and Graph GDDs are the bar; a thin section is bounced by the reviewer. Use the specialist proposals (${specFiles}) as source material: integrate, reconcile, do not paste contradictions; where two specialists disagree, the rulings decide, else pick and say so in a one-line "(orchestrator ruling: ...)" note.`
    let a1 = await tryAgent(`${COMMON}\n\n${SB}\n\nSTAGE 4a — AUTHOR, PART 1. Read <SCR>/brief.md, <SCR>/rulings.md and the specialist files. ${AUTH_RULES}\nWrite, in order: ## Overview (framing: ${['Core', 'Persistence', 'Meta'].includes(s.cat) ? 'data/infrastructure layer with its player impact' : 'both the data layer and its player-facing effect'}; what it is in one sentence, how the player meets it, what the game loses without it; index wording reconciled); ## Player Fantasy (from the creative-director proposal: framing, anchor moment, pillar quote, design test, under-hallucination paragraph, reference techniques adopt/reject, anti-pillar guard rails); ## Detailed Design with ### Core Rules (numbered, named), ### States and Transitions (table: state, entry, exit, transitions, who may cause them), ### Interactions with Other Systems (table per upstream and downstream system: data in, data out, interface owner, exact hook/mutator/read_view/dirty-key names where fixed elsewhere; bidirectional consistency with the dependency GDD's own Interactions row — quote it); ## Dependencies (table: system, direction, hard/soft, interface, status designed/in-flight/undesigned-provisional); ## Cross-References (table: this GDD's reference -> other GDD section/registry name). Leave the remaining sections as placeholders for part 2. Return the schema: sections_written; placeholders_left among YOUR sections (should be none); questions = anything you were unsure of and how you resolved it provisionally (the advisor will rule before part 2 builds on it); assumptions; registry_conflicts (any locked name you needed a different value for — you must NOT have changed the registry value in the text).`, { ...SON, phase: 'Author', schema: AUTHOR_S, ...L('author-1') })
    if (!a1) throw new Error('author part 1 failed')
    let chk = await agent(`Check design/gdd/${s.slug}.md in ${ROOT} (Bash: cd /d/the-synaptic-sea-2d). Do NOT read it whole. Use Grep: (1) pattern "\\[To be designed\\]" with -n and -B 2 to list every placeholder and the "## " or "### " heading nearest above each (report the heading names); (2) count lines matching "^## " ; (3) size in KB via Bash: wc -c. Return the schema: placeholders = headings of sections still holding the placeholder; size_kb; headings = count of "## " lines.`, { model: 'haiku', effort: 'low', phase: 'Author', schema: CHECK_S, ...L('check-1') })
    const part1 = ['Overview', 'Player Fantasy', 'Core Rules', 'States and Transitions', 'Interactions with Other Systems', 'Dependencies', 'Cross-References']
    if (chk && chk.placeholders.some(h => part1.some(p => h.includes(p)))) {
      a1 = await tryAgent(`${COMMON}\n\n${SB}\n\nSTAGE 4a — AUTHOR, PART 1 (RESUME). design/gdd/${s.slug}.md exists but these part-1 sections still hold "[To be designed]": ${chk.placeholders.filter(h => part1.some(p => h.includes(p))).join('; ')}. Read <SCR>/brief.md, <SCR>/rulings.md, the specialist files (${specFiles}) and the sections already written (by heading range). ${AUTH_RULES}\nWrite ONLY the missing part-1 sections. Return the schema.`, { ...SON, phase: 'Author', schema: AUTHOR_S, ...L('author-1-resume') }) || a1
    }
    out.stages.author1 = { questions: a1.questions.length, conflicts: a1.registry_conflicts }

    // 5. Advisor checkpoint
    const cp = await agent(`${COMMON}\n\n${SB}\n\nSTAGE 5 — ADVISOR CHECKPOINT (the mid-point guidance the author cannot ask for). Read <SCR>/brief.md and <SCR>/rulings.md, then the written sections of design/gdd/${s.slug}.md (Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Design, Dependencies, Cross-References — by heading range). The author's questions and assumptions: ${JSON.stringify({ questions: a1.questions, assumptions: a1.assumptions, registry_conflicts: a1.registry_conflicts })}. Rule on every question (binding). Then audit for drift before formulas are built on it: (1) every locked name used with its registry value (grep the registry for each constant/formula the text names); (2) every Interactions row consistent with the dependency GDD's own text (grep the dependency GDD for this system's name and compare hook/mutator/block ids verbatim — an id that does not exist in the owner GDD is a boot-failing error); (3) rulings and guard rails honoured; (4) ownership boundaries (nothing absorbed from Graph/kernel/neighbours); (5) anti-pillars; (6) density (named numbered rules, tables, no vague verbs). Append "## Checkpoint rulings (${DATE})" to <SCR>/rulings.md with the answers and required corrections. Return the schema: ok = no blocking drift; answers; corrections = concrete edits for part 2 to apply FIRST (section, problem, fix text); drift = one-line notes.`, { phase: 'Advise', schema: CHECKPOINT_S, ...L('checkpoint') })
    out.stages.checkpoint = cp ? { ok: cp.ok, corrections: cp.corrections.length } : 'advisor unavailable'
    const cpText = cp ? JSON.stringify(cp.corrections) : '[]'

    // 6. Author part 2a: Formulas, Edge Cases, Tuning Knobs + AC draft
    let a2 = await tryAgent(`${COMMON}\n\n${SB}\n\nSTAGE 6 — AUTHOR, PART 2a. Read <SCR>/brief.md, <SCR>/rulings.md (including the Checkpoint rulings), the specialist files (${specFiles}), and the written sections of design/gdd/${s.slug}.md by heading range. FIRST apply these checkpoint corrections to the existing sections with Edit: ${cpText}. ${AUTH_RULES}\nThen write: ## Formulas — every formula begins exactly "The <name> formula is defined as:" then a backtick expression line, a **Variables:** table with columns Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description, **Output Range:** and **Example:** with real numbers; integer/fixed-point where the kernel's determinism rule applies (anything hashed or replicated); reference dependency formulas by registry name instead of reinventing. ## Edge Cases — 25 or more, each "- **If [condition]**: [exact outcome]. [rationale]", grouped by theme, covering zero/max/out-of-range, simultaneous rules, degenerate strategies, save/restore, hallucination interplay, co-op-later hooks. ## Tuning Knobs — table: knob, default, unit, safe range, too high, too low, interacts with; mark registry candidates with ★ (cross-system facts only); point at the source of truth for knobs another GDD owns instead of duplicating. Then write a DRAFT ## Acceptance Criteria to <SCR>/ac-draft.md (not the GDD): GIVEN/WHEN/THEN, one or more per core rule and per formula, cross-system criteria, performance budget, tags (auto)/(lint)/(review)/(manual)/(spike). Return the schema (questions = anything unresolved for the final review).`, { ...SON, phase: 'Author', schema: AUTHOR_S, ...L('author-2a') })
    if (!a2) throw new Error('author part 2a failed')

    // 7. qa-lead on the AC draft; art-director V/A where required
    const vaRequired = ['Gameplay', 'UI', 'Audio', 'Narrative'].includes(s.cat)
    const post = await parallel([
      () => agent(`${COMMON}\n\n${SB}\n\nSTAGE 7 — QA-LEAD REVIEW of the draft acceptance criteria (design-system Section H delegation). Read <SCR>/ac-draft.md and, by heading range, the GDD's Core Rules, Formulas and Edge Cases in design/gdd/${s.slug}.md. Verify every criterion is independently testable by a QA tester without the GDD, that every core rule and every formula has at least one criterion, that cross-system contracts and the performance budget are covered, and that tags are right. Write <SCR>/ac-review.md: gaps (rule/formula without a criterion), untestable criteria rewritten, missing cross-system criteria, suggested additional criteria. Return the schema.`, { ...SON, phase: 'Specialists', schema: SPEC_S, agentType: 'qa-lead', ...L('qa-lead') }),
      ...(vaRequired && !s.support.includes('art-director') ? [() => agent(`${COMMON}\n\n${SB}\n\nSTAGE 7 — ART-DIRECTOR on Visual/Audio Requirements (REQUIRED for Category ${s.cat}). Read <SCR>/brief.md, <SCR>/rulings.md and, by heading range, the GDD's Core Rules and States in design/gdd/${s.slug}.md; read the art bible sections that apply. Specify: (1) VFX and visual feedback for every event this system produces or reads, (2) animation/motion constraints, (3) which art bible principles and numbered sections apply, (4) palette rules (sanity palette, loop hues, luminance ladder), (5) truth-channel vs corruptible classification of each visual, (6) asset types implied. Write <SCR>/spec-art-director.md. Return the schema.`, { ...SON, phase: 'Specialists', schema: SPEC_S, agentType: 'art-director', ...L('art-director') })] : []),
    ])
    out.stages.post = post.filter(Boolean).map(x => x.file)

    // 8. Author part 2b: AC, extras, Summary
    let a3 = await tryAgent(`${COMMON}\n\n${SB}\n\nSTAGE 8 — AUTHOR, PART 2b (finish). Read <SCR>/rulings.md, <SCR>/ac-draft.md, <SCR>/ac-review.md (if present), the art-director file if present (<SCR>/spec-art-director.md), the audio proposals if any, and the GDD's written sections by heading range. ${AUTH_RULES}\nWrite: ## Acceptance Criteria — the draft with the qa-lead's gaps closed and rewrites applied, grouped under ### sub-headings, 40+ GWT criteria for a system this size, tags on every one, plus a "### Gaps / untestable as written" list if any remain; ## Visual/Audio Requirements — ${vaRequired ? 'REQUIRED: full section from the art-director proposal (events -> VFX/sprite state/audio class; art bible citations; truth-channel classification)' : 'a real note (what is visible/audible, which other GDD renders it, which art bible sections apply) — never a placeholder'}; ## Game Feel — ${['Gameplay', 'UI'].includes(s.cat) ? 'REQUIRED: responsiveness, weight, timing and snap targets as numbers (ticks, px, ms), with the input-to-feedback chain' : 'a real note on what the player feels of this system and which GDD owns the feel'}; ## UI Requirements — what HUD/instrument/menu surfaces this system needs, with the UX flag text "📌 **UX Flag — ${s.name}**: ..." when it has real UI, or an explicit "no UI of its own; surfaces owned by ..." note; ## Open Questions — table: #, question, owner (user / agent / GDD), target (playtest / next GDD / ADR), with the user-decision items first; then ## Summary — 2-3 sentences a stranger can use to decide whether to read this GDD, and replace the Quick reference line's bracketed values (Layer ${s.layer}, Priority MVP, Key deps from the Dependencies table with designed/undesigned notes). Then: the "📌 **Asset Spec**" notice belongs in the Visual/Audio section's last line when that section has real content. Write <SCR>/registry-candidates.yaml: the cross-system facts this GDD introduces (constants with value/unit/range/referenced_by candidates; formulas with expression/variables/output; entities/items with attributes), in the entities.yaml entry layout (see its header comment), each with "source: design/gdd/${s.slug}.md", added/revised ${DATE}; ONLY facts another GDD will read; list separately the EXISTING registry names this GDD references so referenced_by can be extended. Grep the finished file for "[To be designed]" and remove any that remain. Set the header Status to "Designed". Return the schema.`, { ...SON, phase: 'Author', schema: AUTHOR_S, ...L('author-2b') })
    if (!a3) throw new Error('author part 2b failed')
    chk = await agent(`Check design/gdd/${s.slug}.md in ${ROOT} (Bash: cd /d/the-synaptic-sea-2d). Do NOT read it whole. Use Grep: (1) pattern "\\[To be designed\\]" with -n and -B 2 to list every placeholder and the nearest "## " or "### " heading above each; (2) count lines matching "^## "; (3) size in KB via Bash wc -c. Return the schema.`, { model: 'haiku', effort: 'low', phase: 'Author', schema: CHECK_S, ...L('check-2') })
    if (chk && chk.placeholders.length) {
      await tryAgent(`${COMMON}\n\n${SB}\n\nSTAGE 8 — AUTHOR, PART 2b (RESUME). These sections of design/gdd/${s.slug}.md still hold "[To be designed]": ${chk.placeholders.join('; ')}. Read <SCR>/rulings.md and the related stage files in <SCR>, and the GDD by heading range. ${AUTH_RULES}\nWrite ONLY the missing sections, with real content. Return the schema.`, { ...SON, phase: 'Author', schema: AUTHOR_S, ...L('author-2b-resume') })
    }
    out.stages.size_kb = chk ? chk.size_kb : null

    // 9. Final review (advisor) with up to 2 revise rounds
    let rounds = 0, review = null
    for (let r = 0; r < 3; r++) {
      review = await agent(`${COMMON}\n\n${SB}\n\nSTAGE 9 — ADVISOR FINAL REVIEW (round ${r + 1}). Read <SCR>/brief.md and <SCR>/rulings.md, then design/gdd/${s.slug}.md section by section (grep "^## " then Read each range; the file may be 60-200 KB — read every section, in pieces). Judge against: (A) completeness — no "[To be designed]", header complete (Status Designed, Author, dates, Implements Pillar), Summary + Quick reference real; (B) the density bar (thorough): numbered named rules; state table; interaction table with exact ids; every formula with lead-in + Variables table (Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description) + Output Range + Example; 25+ If/then edge cases; 30+ tuning knobs with ranges and failure directions; 40+ GWT criteria with tags; (C) consistency — every registry name used with its registry value (grep each); every hook/mutator/block/read_view id this GDD cites exists verbatim in the owner GDD (grep the owner); every dependency GDD's Interactions row for this system agrees with this GDD's Interactions row; sibling GDDs that already exist and name this system (grep design/gdd/*.md for "${s.name}") are not contradicted; (D) rulings and guard rails honoured, routed threads present, ownership boundaries kept, anti-pillars kept, nothing hallucination-related touches the consequence channel, behaviour level not implementation; (E) the MVP slice is explicit (what is MVP vs later). Severity: blocking = wrong locked value / nonexistent id / missing required section / contradiction with a designed GDD; major = thin section, missing routed thread, unresolved ownership; minor = wording. Verdict PASS only if no blocking and no major items. Each item: section, severity, problem, fix = the exact text or edit to make. Return the schema.`, { phase: 'Advise', schema: REVIEW_S, ...L('review-' + (r + 1)) })
      if (!review) break
      rounds = r + 1
      if (review.verdict === 'PASS' || r === 2) break
      await tryAgent(`${COMMON}\n\n${SB}\n\nSTAGE 10 — REVISE after advisor review round ${r + 1}. Apply every item below to design/gdd/${s.slug}.md with Edit (read the affected section range first; keep heading set and order; locked registry values are never changed — if an item says the GDD has a different value, the GDD text moves to the registry value). Items: ${JSON.stringify(review.items)}. Registry conflicts to resolve the same way: ${JSON.stringify(review.registry_conflicts)}. Update <SCR>/registry-candidates.yaml if an item changed a candidate. Log one decision for the revision pass. Return the schema: applied (item -> what changed), skipped (item -> why, only if impossible).`, { ...SON, phase: 'Author', schema: REVISE_S, ...L('revise-' + (r + 1)) })
    }
    out.stages.review = review ? { verdict: review.verdict, rounds, open: review.items.length } : 'advisor unavailable'

    // 11. CD-GDD-ALIGN gate
    let gate = await agent(`${COMMON}\n\n${SB}\n\nGATE CD-GDD-ALIGN. FIRST read .claude/docs/director-gates/cd-gdd-align.md and follow it. Context: GDD design/gdd/${s.slug}.md (read by heading range; its "## Player Fantasy" section is the system's stated fantasy); pillars in design/gdd/game-concept.md "## Game Pillars"; MDA target aesthetics in "### Target Aesthetics". Review for pillar alignment: does every section serve the stated pillars; do any rules contradict or weaken a pillar or cross an anti-pillar; does the Player Fantasy match the core fantasy. Return the schema: verdict APPROVE / CONCERNS / REJECT / NOT ASSESSED; items = specific sections with the issue and the change that resolves it; rationale.`, { phase: 'Gate', schema: GATE_S, agentType: 'creative-director', ...L('cd-gate') })
    let gateRecord = 'NOT ASSESSED ' + DATE + ' — creative-director agent unavailable'
    if (gate) {
      if (gate.verdict === 'APPROVE') gateRecord = 'APPROVED ' + DATE
      else if (gate.verdict === 'NOT ASSESSED') gateRecord = 'NOT ASSESSED ' + DATE + ' — ' + (gate.items[0] || gate.rationale)
      else {
        const rev = await tryAgent(`${COMMON}\n\n${SB}\n\nSTAGE 12 — APPLY CD-GDD-ALIGN ${gate.verdict} (autonomous mode picks "Revise flagged items"; precedent: the Graph GDD applied all seven concerns). Items: ${JSON.stringify(gate.items)}. Rationale: ${gate.rationale}. Re-run the section cycle for each flagged section of design/gdd/${s.slug}.md: read its range, redraft to resolve the item while keeping locked values and rulings, write with Edit. Log one decision per flagged section. Update <SCR>/registry-candidates.yaml if affected. Return the schema.`, { ...SON, phase: 'Gate', schema: REVISE_S, ...L('cd-revise') })
        if (gate.verdict === 'REJECT') {
          const g2 = await agent(`${COMMON}\n\n${SB}\n\nGATE CD-GDD-ALIGN (re-run after REJECT revisions). FIRST read .claude/docs/director-gates/cd-gdd-align.md and follow it. Previous blockers: ${JSON.stringify(gate.items)}. Review design/gdd/${s.slug}.md by heading range against the pillars in design/gdd/game-concept.md. Return the schema.`, { phase: 'Gate', schema: GATE_S, agentType: 'creative-director', ...L('cd-gate-2') })
          gateRecord = g2 ? (g2.verdict === 'APPROVE' ? 'REJECT → REVISED → APPROVED ' + DATE : g2.verdict === 'REJECT' ? 'REJECT (unresolved) ' + DATE + ' — ' + g2.items.join('; ') : 'REJECT → REVISED ' + DATE + ' (' + g2.verdict + ': ' + g2.items.join('; ') + ')') : 'REJECT → REVISED ' + DATE
          gate = g2 || gate
        } else {
          gateRecord = 'CONCERNS → REVISED ' + DATE + ' (' + gate.items.length + ' items applied' + (rev && rev.skipped.length ? '; skipped: ' + rev.skipped.join('; ') : '') + ')'
        }
      }
    }
    out.stages.gate = gateRecord

    // 13. Registry merge (serialised) + header record
    const reg = await serial(() => tryAgent(`${COMMON}\n\n${SB}\n\nSTAGE 13 — REGISTRY MERGE + HEADER (design-system Phase 5b; runs one system at a time — you hold the lock, be quick and exact). (1) Record the gate in the GDD header: insert the line "> **Creative Director Review (CD-GDD-ALIGN)**: ${gateRecord}" directly after the "> **Implements Pillar**" line of design/gdd/${s.slug}.md (Edit; read the first 15 lines only), make sure Status is "Designed" and Last Updated/Verified are ${DATE}. (2) Read design/registry/entities.yaml's header comment and layout line, and <SCR>/registry-candidates.yaml. (3) For each candidate: grep "  - name: <name>" — if present, do not duplicate: append this GDD's path to its referenced_by (block list) only if the GDD actually reads it, and if the candidate's VALUE differs from the registry's, do NOT change the registry — write the conflict to <SCR>/registry-conflicts.md and fix the GDD text to the registry value; if absent, append the entry after the last entry of its section (constants / formulas / entities / items) with source, referenced_by, attributes, added, revised ${DATE}. referenced_by paths MUST exist on disk (Glob): a path to a GDD not yet written goes into a "    # pending referenced_by (GDD not yet written): <paths>" comment line at the end of the entry instead. (4) For every existing entry whose "# pending referenced_by" comment names design/gdd/${s.slug}.md, now that the file exists: move that path into the real referenced_by list (keep other pending paths in the comment; delete the comment when empty). (5) Run: cd /d/the-synaptic-sea-2d && bash .claude/scripts/registry.sh validate — fix every DUPLICATE / PATH_MISSING / STATUS / LAYOUT row you caused and re-run until clean (print the final counts). (6) For each entry whose source is this GDD, grep the GDD for the exact name; list any name missing. Return the schema.`, { ...SON, phase: 'Registry', schema: REG_S, ...L('registry') }))
    out.stages.registry = reg || 'failed'
    out.status = 'done'
    log(`✔ ${s.name}: done (review ${out.stages.review && out.stages.review.verdict}, gate ${gateRecord.split(' ')[0]}, registry ${reg ? (reg.validate_clean ? 'clean' : 'NOT clean') : 'failed'})`)
  } catch (e) {
    out.error = String(e && e.message || e)
    log(`✖ ${s.name}: FAILED — ${out.error}; dependents proceed treating it as undesigned`)
  } finally {
    results[s.slug] = out
    resolveDone[s.slug](out)
  }
  return out
}

log(`22 systems; start order by dependency depth: ${SYSTEMS.map(s => s.slug + '(d' + depth[s.slug] + ')').join(', ')}`)
await parallel(SYSTEMS.map(s => () => runSystem(s)))

const done = SYSTEMS.filter(s => results[s.slug] && results[s.slug].status === 'done').map(s => s.slug)
const failed = SYSTEMS.filter(s => !results[s.slug] || results[s.slug].status !== 'done').map(s => ({ slug: s.slug, error: results[s.slug] && results[s.slug].error }))
log(`finished: ${done.length} done, ${failed.length} failed`)
return { date: DATE, done, failed, systems: results }

const depth = {}
function depthOf(s) {
  if (depth[s.slug] != null) return depth[s.slug]
  let d = 0
  for (const n of s.deps) if (NAME2SLUG[n]) d = Math.max(d, 1 + depthOf(SYSTEMS.find(x => x.name === n)))

function sysBlock(s, depStatus) {

  const dependents = SYSTEMS.filter(x => x.deps.includes(s.name)).map(x => x.name)
  return `SYSTEM: ${s.name} (index row ${s.order}; Category ${s.cat}; Layer ${s.layer}; Priority MVP). GDD path: design/gdd/${s.slug}.md. Stage dir: ${SCR}/${s.slug} (call it <SCR>).

Required extras by category: Visual/Audio ${['Gameplay', 'UI', 'Audio', 'Narrative'].includes(s.cat) ? 'REQUIRED (art-director consulted)' : 'optional (write a real note, not a placeholder)'}; Game Feel ${['Gameplay', 'UI'].includes(s.cat) ? ${deps}

ROUTED THREADS this GDD must carry (decisions already made elsewhere; honour verbatim): ${s.threads}`
}

log(`22 systems; start order by dependency depth: ${SYSTEMS.map(s => s.slug + '(d' + depth[s.slug] + ')').join(', ')}`)

const done = SYSTEMS.filter(s => results[s.slug] && results[s.slug].status === 'done').map(s => s.slug)

const NAME2SLUG = {}
for (const s of SYSTEMS) NAME2SLUG[s.name] = s.slug
const pathOf = (name) => DESIGNED[name] || ('design/gdd/' + NAME2SLUG[name] + '.md')

// dependency depth (in-workflow deps only) for a safe topological start order
const depth = {}
function depthOf(s) {
  if (depth[s.slug] != null) return depth[s.slug]
  let d = 0
  for (const n of s.deps) if (NAME2SLUG[n]) d = Math.max(d, 1 + depthOf(SYSTEMS.find(x => x.name === n)))
  depth[s.slug] = d
  return d
}
SYSTEMS.forEach(depthOf)
SYSTEMS.sort((a, b) => (depth[a.slug] - depth[b.slug]) || (a.order - b.order))

function sysBlock(s, depStatus) {
  const deps = s.deps.map(n => `  - ${n} -> ${pathOf(n)} [${depStatus[n]}]`).join('\n')
  const dependents = SYSTEMS.filter(x => x.deps.includes(s.name)).map(x => x.name)
  return `SYSTEM: ${s.name} (index row ${s.order}; Category ${s.cat}; Layer ${s.layer}; Priority MVP). GDD path: design/gdd/${s.slug}.md. Stage dir: ${SCR}/${s.slug} (call it <SCR>).
Specialist routing (design-system Section 6, from the index Recommended Design Order): primary ${s.primary}; supporting ${s.support.join(', ')}.
Required extras by category: Visual/Audio ${['Gameplay', 'UI', 'Audio', 'Narrative'].includes(s.cat) ? 'REQUIRED (art-director consulted)' : 'optional (write a real note, not a placeholder)'}; Game Feel ${['Gameplay', 'UI'].includes(s.cat) ? 'REQUIRED' : 'optional (write a real note)'}; Cross-References REQUIRED; UI Requirements and Open Questions always written.
Upstream dependencies (status at the moment this stage started):
${deps}
Downstream dependents among the systems being designed in this run: ${dependents.length ? dependents.join('; ') : 'none in this run'}.
ROUTED THREADS this GDD must carry (decisions already made elsewhere; honour verbatim): ${s.threads}`
}

async function tryAgent(prompt, opts, tries) {
  for (let i = 0; i < (tries || 2); i++) {
    const r = await agent(i === 0 ? prompt : prompt + '\n\n(RETRY ' + i + ': a previous attempt died; resume from whatever already exists on disk — do not redo finished work.)', opts)
    if (r) return r
  }
  return null
}
